Power-Ups and Bonuses: As players progress through the game, they can collect power-ups that enhance their abilities. These may include extra bombs, increased bomb blast radius, temporary invincibility, or other helpful boosts. These items give players an edge and allow them to tackle tougher challenges as they advance. Varied Environments: The game offers a variety of levels set in different environments, each with its own set of challenges. Some levels may feature narrow corridors, while others include large open spaces filled with traps. Each environment requires a different approach, keeping the gameplay fresh and engaging. Increasing Difficulty: As players advance through the game, the levels become more difficult. The puzzles get more intricate, enemies become more numerous and aggressive, and the time limits get stricter. Players must improve their bomb placement strategy and timing to succeed in the later stages of the game. Classic 2D Graphics: Boom Master uses pixelated 2D graphics typical of DOS-era games. The visuals are clear and easy to understand, with distinct enemies, obstacles, and bomb effects. The explosions are visually satisfying, with large, colorful blasts that make each bomb placement feel impactful. Simple Controls: The game features straightforward controls that make it easy for players to dive right in. The player can control movement, place bombs, and interact with the environment using basic keyboard commands. The simplicity of the controls allows the focus to remain on the action and strategy. Sound Effects and Music: Boom Master features an energetic soundtrack and a variety of sound effects, including the satisfying sound of explosions, enemy movements, and item pickups. The audio contributes to the overall excitement and helps immerse players in the explosive action.

name: Boomerang
description: Boomerang is a fast-paced DOS action game that combines quick reflexes, strategy, and puzzle-solving elements. Players control a character who throws boomerangs to solve puzzles, defeat enemies, and navigate through various levels. The game challenges players to think strategically as they use their boomerangs to hit targets, clear obstacles, and progress through increasingly difficult stages. Features: Boomerang Throwing Mechanics: The main feature of Boomerang is the use of a boomerang as the player's primary tool. Players must throw the boomerang to hit enemies, activate switches, and clear obstacles. The boomerang returns after being thrown, and players must catch it to reuse it, adding a layer of timing and precision to the gameplay. Enemies and Obstacles: Throughout the game, players face various enemies that can only be defeated by the boomerang. Some enemies require multiple hits, while others might be immune to certain attacks. Players must also navigate through levels filled with obstacles, such as walls, traps, and other environmental hazards, all while using their boomerang to solve puzzles. Puzzle-Solving: Many levels in Boomerang feature puzzle elements. To advance, players must use their boomerang to hit switches, break walls, or trigger mechanisms. The game challenges players to figure out the best angle and timing for each boomerang throw, as many puzzles require precise actions to complete. Time Limits: Some levels in Boomerang are timed, adding an element of urgency. Players must complete each objective before the time runs out, increasing the challenge. This feature forces players to act quickly and plan their moves efficiently. Power-Ups and Bonuses: As players progress, they can collect power-ups and bonuses that enhance their abilities. These might include boomerangs that travel faster, longer distances, or have special effects. Collecting these items makes the game easier and adds an additional strategic element to the gameplay. Varied Environments: The game features a wide range of environments, each with unique challenges. From caves to forests to enemy-filled castles, each level presents new obstacles and puzzle mechanics. The varied environments keep the gameplay fresh and exciting as players must adapt their strategy to each new setting. Increasing Difficulty: As players progress through the game, the difficulty increases. New types of enemies, more complex puzzles, and more intricate level designs challenge players to think ahead and react quickly. Later levels feature more complicated puzzles and tougher enemies that require careful planning and execution. Simple 2D Graphics: Boomerang features simple yet colorful 2D graphics typical of DOS-era games. The visuals are clear and functional, helping players easily identify enemies, obstacles, and interactive elements within the environment. The boomerang’s flight and return are well-animated, giving a satisfying sense of motion. Sound Effects and Music: The game includes fun sound effects, such as the whoosh of the boomerang flying through the air, enemy reactions, and explosions. The background music is catchy and upbeat, providing an engaging atmosphere as players work their way through each level. Simple Controls: The controls in Boomerang are simple and intuitive. Players can move their character and throw the boomerang using basic keyboard commands. The game’s easy-to-learn controls allow players to focus on strategy and problem-solving.

name: Boppin
description: This game is a bit different from other side-scrolling games published by Apogee. It contains a prominent "adults only" warning, I think mostly due to the cartoon depictions of "seppuku" (suicide). Viewer discretion is advised! But anyways, in the game, all of the other video game villains have become trapped in jewel stones; the gameplay consists of picking up jewels of various colors and matching them up to eliminate them from the playing field, freeing the baddies. Boppin is a fun and fast-paced DOS puzzle game that combines elements of action, strategy, and quick reflexes. Players control a character who must solve puzzles by bouncing objects around the screen to defeat enemies, clear obstacles, and navigate through various levels. The game features a colorful, whimsical design and increasingly difficult challenges that require both skill and creativity. Features: Bouncing Mechanics: The primary gameplay feature of Boppin is the ability to bounce objects (such as balls or blocks) to hit enemies and solve puzzles. Players control the trajectory of these objects, which can bounce off walls, obstacles, and enemies, making it essential to plan each shot carefully to hit targets and trigger certain actions. Puzzle-Solving Gameplay: Each level presents a unique puzzle that players must solve by using the bouncing objects. This might include hitting switches to open doors, triggering traps, or defeating enemies by bouncing objects at them. Some levels also have movable obstacles or platforms that must be manipulated to clear a path. Varied Environments: Boppin offers a variety of levels set in different environments. Each environment has its own set of challenges, with new types of obstacles, enemies, and puzzles to solve. Players will encounter forests, caves, castles, and more, each requiring a different approach to navigating the level and solving its puzzle. Increasing Difficulty: As players progress, the game becomes more challenging. Enemies become more aggressive, puzzles get harder, and the timing required to solve each puzzle becomes more precise. New elements, such as moving platforms and tougher enemies, are introduced, keeping the gameplay fresh and engaging. Enemies and Bosses: Throughout the game, players face a variety of enemies that can only be defeated by hitting them with the bouncing objects. Some enemies are easy to take out, while others require multiple hits or specific strategies. At the end of certain stages, players will face challenging boss battles that require quick thinking and precise aim. Power-Ups and Bonuses: Players can collect power-ups throughout the game that enhance their abilities. These can include extra lives, speed boosts, or special objects that can be used to clear obstacles or defeat enemies more efficiently. The power-ups add an extra layer of strategy to the game, allowing players to make the most of their resources. Simple, Colorful Graphics: Boppin features bright, cartoonish 2D graphics that are both fun and functional. The levels are visually appealing, with clear icons and obstacles that make it easy for players to understand the game mechanics. The colorful and whimsical design helps make the game feel lighthearted and enjoyable. Engaging Soundtrack: The game includes a catchy soundtrack that complements the fun, light tone of the gameplay. The sound effects, including the bounce of objects and the reactions of enemies, add to the immersive experience, making each level feel lively and engaging. User-Friendly Controls: The controls in Boppin are simple and intuitive. Players can move their character, aim, and launch objects using basic keyboard commands. The straightforward control scheme makes it easy for players to focus on solving puzzles and mastering the bouncing mechanics without being bogged down by complex controls.

name: Borderworld
description: Borderworld is an interesting graphical adventure game, or perhaps more accurately a text adventure game including graphics. You are teleported into a mysterious world, which you must explore using a mouse-driven interface, which is a little clunky to use sometimes. Rather than typing, you select your actions from a list, and rather than moving using the arrow keys or typing a command, you click a compass. Borderworld is a DOS-based space strategy and adventure game that combines exploration, tactical combat, and resource management. Set in a vast and mysterious universe, players take on the role of a space explorer who is tasked with navigating a complex system of planets, managing a starship, and interacting with various alien species. The game emphasizes decision-making, strategy, and the management of resources as players work to unravel the mysteries of the galaxy. Features: Space Exploration: The game offers a wide universe filled with different planets, each with unique resources, challenges, and alien civilizations. Players can travel between different star systems, explore unknown worlds, and interact with different species. Each planet offers new opportunities for trade, diplomacy, or combat, providing players with endless exploration possibilities. Tactical Combat: Borderworld features real-time tactical combat, where players command a starship during battles. Players must use their ship’s weapons and abilities wisely to defeat enemy ships, navigate through asteroid fields, or engage in strategic warfare with hostile factions. Combat requires quick decision-making, as players manage shields, weapons, and positioning in battle. Resource Management: As players explore the galaxy, they must gather resources, such as fuel, supplies, and technology. Managing these resources is essential to maintaining the functionality of the starship and ensuring survival. Players can trade with alien factions or complete missions to earn resources, but scarcity can become a major issue, especially in distant sectors of the galaxy. Diplomacy and Factions: The universe of Borderworld is populated by various alien factions, each with its own agenda and motivations. Players can engage in diplomacy, forge alliances, or engage in conflict with these factions. Decisions in diplomatic negotiations can affect the player's reputation, trade opportunities, and access to valuable resources or technology. Story-driven Gameplay: The game offers a rich narrative with branching storylines, where the choices made by the player directly influence the outcome. Players will encounter mysterious quests, ancient artifacts, and political intrigue that drive the game's overarching plot. The story unfolds based on player actions, leading to multiple possible endings and replayability. Ship Customization: Players have the ability to upgrade and customize their starship. From improving weaponry to enhancing shields or adding new systems like cloaking or enhanced sensors, ship customization is key to surviving the challenges that arise in the game. The more resources and technology the player accumulates, the stronger their ship becomes. Multiple Playable Characters: Throughout the game, players can recruit various crew members, each with different skills and specialties. These characters provide valuable assistance in combat, diplomacy, or exploration. Building a strong crew with complementary abilities is crucial to success in the game. 2D Graphics and User Interface: Borderworld features simple 2D graphics typical of many DOS games. The interface includes a star map, ship control systems, and detailed mission logs, all of which help the player manage their spacefaring adventure. The visuals, while not cutting-edge, are functional and convey the game’s atmosphere effectively. Atmospheric Soundtrack: The game’s soundtrack creates an immersive atmosphere with space-themed music and sound effects that accompany the action. From the hum of the starship engines to the booming sounds of combat, the audio helps enhance the sense of being in a vast, dynamic universe. Challenging AI: As players explore the galaxy, they will encounter various hostile factions and enemies. The AI in Borderworld is designed to present a challenge, with enemies that can adapt to the player's tactics and present unique threats. The difficulty gradually increases as players venture into more dangerous areas of space.

name: BOSTON.COM Snowplow Game
description: The BOSTON.COM Snowplow Game is a fun and fast-paced arcade-style game where you take on the role of a snowplow driver tasked with clearing the streets of Boston after a massive Nor'Easter. Your mission is to navigate the city, collect all the snowflakes and peppermints, and clear the streets as quickly as possible—all while racing against the clock. With its charming winter theme and challenging gameplay, this game is perfect for players who enjoy time-based challenges and lighthearted fun. How to Play: Control the Snowplow: Use the arrow keys or WASD to move your snowplow around the city streets. Collect Snowflakes and Peppermints: Drive over snowflakes and peppermints to collect them. These are scattered throughout the streets and are essential for completing each level. Clear the Streets: Plow through snowbanks to clear the streets and create paths to reach all the collectibles. Race Against Time: Complete each level as quickly as possible before time runs out. Avoid Obstacles: Watch out for obstacles like parked cars, traffic cones, and other hazards that can slow you down. Features: Winter Theme: The game is set in a snowy Boston, complete with festive visuals and a cheerful winter atmosphere. Time-Based Challenge: Each level has a time limit, adding urgency and excitement to the gameplay. Simple Controls: Easy-to-learn mechanics make the game accessible for players of all ages. Multiple Levels: The game offers a variety of levels with increasing difficulty, ensuring hours of engaging gameplay. Festive Fun: The inclusion of snowflakes and peppermints adds a playful and seasonal touch.

name: Bottle Cap Match
description: Fun match 3 game with bottle caps. Swap 2 bottle caps to match 3 or more of the same in a row or column. Remove as many bottle caps as indicated. Bottle Cap Match is a colorful and engaging match-3 game featuring a collection of vibrant bottle caps. Your goal is to swap adjacent bottle caps to create matches of three or more of the same type in a row or column. As you successfully match bottle caps, they disappear from the board, and new ones fall into their place. Key Features: Colorful and Eye-Catching Graphics: The game features a visually appealing design with bright and colorful bottle caps. Easy-to-Learn Gameplay: The simple and intuitive controls make it easy for players of all ages to pick up and play. Challenging Levels: As you progress through the game, the levels become increasingly challenging, requiring strategic thinking and quick reflexes. Power-Ups and Combos: Utilize special power-ups and create explosive combos to clear multiple bottle caps at once. Time-Based Challenges: Some levels feature time limits, adding an extra layer of excitement and pressure.

name: Boulder Dash
description: Boulder Dash is a clone of the popular PC game of the same name. It offers gameplay that closely matches that of the original game, as well as VGA graphics and a bunch of levels. Note that the key to begin the game at the title screen / menu is the RIGHT SHIFT key, took awhile slapping pretty much every keyboard button before figuring that out. In any case it plays well enough and captures the feel / aesthetic of the original, which is impressive for a 48k executable file. Boulder Dash is a classic puzzle game that was originally released in 1984 for DOS. It has since been ported to many other platforms and has spawned numerous sequels and spin-offs. The game features a simple but addictive gameplay mechanic. The player controls a character named Rockford, who must dig through a maze of tunnels to collect diamonds and reach the exit. The player must avoid falling rocks and other hazards, such as enemies and deadly gases. Boulder Dash is a challenging game that requires careful planning and quick reflexes. It is a great game for people who enjoy puzzle games and arcade games. Here are some of the key features of Boulder Dash: Simple but addictive gameplay Challenging puzzles Colorful graphics Addictive soundtrack If you want to play Boulder Dash, you can find it on a number of different platforms, including: PC: You can download Boulder Dash from a variety of online sources, such as GOG.com. Mobile: There are several Boulder Dash games available for iOS and Android devices. Emulators: You can emulate the original DOS version of Boulder Dash using a variety of emulators, such as DOSBox.

name: Boulderoid
description: Boulderoid is a remake of the classic Boulder Dash game. It includes maps from the original game as well as other sequels. There are two different graphical tilesets (one approximating the C64 game and another original better looking set) included, and there's a level editor so you can make your own levels. Boulderoid is a DOS game that is a clone of Boulder Dash. It was developed by CodeWraith Software, MacroHead & MicroBrain, and published by MacroHead & MicroBrain in 1994. Key Features: Clone of Boulder Dash: It offers similar gameplay mechanics to Boulder Dash, where you control a character named Rockford and must navigate through mazes, collecting diamonds and avoiding hazards like falling rocks and enemies. Enhanced Graphics: Boulderoid introduced improved graphics compared to the original Boulder Dash, with support for VGA graphics and sound cards. Level Editor: The game included a level editor, allowing players to create their own custom levels and share them with others. Multiple Graphics Modes: Players could choose between two graphics modes: the original style or a more modern "Boulderoid" style. However, due to legal issues with the original creators of Boulder Dash, the development of Boulderoid was halted, and the final version released was 1.15. To play Boulderoid: You can find the game on various online archives and download it to run on a DOS emulator like DOSBox.

name: Bounce
description: The object of the plainly titled Bounce is to collect all of the gems on a particular level and then make it to the exit before time runs out. The game is very colorful and while the controls take a little while to get used to they are very responsive during the game. The difficultly level is rather high, and here, unlike many puzzle game, you'll need quick reflexes to get through the many levels. "Bounce" is a classic arcade-style game that was originally developed for Nokia mobile phones in the early 2000s. The game involves controlling a bouncing ball through various levels, with the goal being to navigate through obstacles and collect items to progress to the next stage. Here's a general description of the game: Game Overview: Platform: Originally a mobile game, but later adapted for other platforms as well. Objective: The main objective of the game is to guide a ball through a series of increasingly challenging levels, avoiding obstacles and collecting items like stars or coins along the way. Players need to jump, bounce, and sometimes use power-ups to overcome obstacles and complete the level. Gameplay Mechanics: The ball automatically bounces, and the player controls its direction by tilting the phone or using arrow keys (depending on the platform). Levels feature various elements such as platforms, walls, springs, and enemies that the player must navigate around or avoid. The player must reach the exit point in each level to progress to the next. Power-ups and Obstacles: There are different power-ups like speed boosts or invincibility that help the player overcome tougher parts of the level. Some levels feature traps and enemies that can harm the ball, requiring careful timing and movement to avoid them.

name: Bounce Ball
description: Bounce Ball is a fun and simple HTML5 game that is typically played in a browser. The game revolves around controlling a ball that bounces around the screen, and the objective is often to guide the ball through obstacles, reach a goal, or collect items while avoiding hazards. Gameplay Overview: Ball Movement: In Bounce Ball, you control a ball that continuously bounces. You can guide its trajectory by moving it left or right using keyboard arrows (or swiping if you’re on mobile). Gravity plays a role in the game, meaning the ball will fall when there’s no support beneath it, making precision in controlling its bounce important. Objective: The core objective in most Bounce Ball games is to reach the goal, typically marked by a platform or a finish line, while avoiding obstacles like spikes, pits, or other hazards. Some versions may also require you to collect items or coins scattered throughout the levels to increase your score. Obstacles: As you progress through different levels, you encounter various obstacles like spikes, moving platforms, spinning traps, and sometimes even enemies. Timing is key to avoiding these obstacles while keeping the ball in motion. Levels: The game typically consists of multiple levels that get progressively harder. As you advance, the levels may have narrower platforms, more frequent obstacles, or faster-moving hazards. Each level may be designed with different backgrounds, platform styles, and challenges, keeping the gameplay fresh and exciting. Physics: Bounce Ball games often rely on basic physics to determine how the ball bounces off platforms, walls, and ceilings. The ball’s bounce height and angle are determined by its velocity and the direction it hits obstacles. Controls: On desktop, players usually use the left and right arrow keys (or A and D) to control the horizontal movement of the ball. For mobile, touch-based controls or tilt mechanisms may be used to control the ball.

name: Bounce Zone
description: Like Pong, but actually somewhat fun to play! There's actually some skill involved here, as you can send the ball firing towards your opponent (the computer ... it's only a one player game) and also move forward and backwards into the foreground. The wire-frame graphics simulate a 3D perspective. Pretty cool, although at a certain point the computer opponent seems to become too difficult to beat. Bounce Zone is a classic DOS game released in 1990 by COMPUTE! Publications, Inc. It's a 3D take on the classic Pong game, adding a new dimension to the gameplay. Key Features: 3D Gameplay: Unlike traditional Pong, Bounce Zone takes place in a 3D rectangular court. Dual-Axis Control: Players control their paddles using two axes, allowing for more complex maneuvers. Bouncing Off Walls and Ceiling: The ball can bounce off not only the walls but also the floor and ceiling, adding a new layer of strategy. First-Person Perspective: The game is played from a first-person perspective, giving players a unique view of the action.

name: Bouncing Babies
description: Bouncing Babies is something of a classic PC game. Not necessarily because it's fun to play, more just because it's old. It play similarly to the Nintendo LCD Game'n'Watch series of handheld games that were popular many years ago. The object is to catch (bounce) the babies falling out of the burning building to lead them to safety. It certainly will test your eye hand coordination but the extremely simple gameplay and very dated graphics will probably get old quickly. Key Features: Simple yet challenging gameplay: The game is easy to learn but becomes increasingly difficult as you progress through the levels. Retro graphics and sound: The game features classic CGA graphics and a simple, catchy soundtrack. Addictive gameplay: The fast-paced action and the satisfaction of saving babies make the game highly addictive. To play Bouncing Babies, you can find it on various online archives and download it to run on a DOS emulator like DOSBox.

name: Bowling
description: Bowling HTML5 games are a fun way to enjoy the sport of bowling right from your browser. These games use HTML5 technology, which allows them to be played on modern browsers without the need for additional plugins like Flash. Whether you're a casual player looking for a quick game or someone who loves sports simulations, HTML5 bowling games offer an enjoyable experience. Core Gameplay Features Controls: Mouse or Touchscreen: Most Bowling HTML5 games are controlled using either a mouse or touchscreen (for mobile versions). You control the ball's direction, speed, and spin before releasing it. On desktop, you click and drag to adjust the ball’s position and spin, then release the ball by clicking or pressing a button. On mobile, you tap or swipe to control the ball’s motion. You can usually control aspects like the angle of the throw, the speed of the ball, and sometimes even apply spin to curve the ball and hit the pins at better angles. Lane and Pins: The game typically features a bowling lane where you roll the ball, and at the end, there are 10 pins arranged in a triangular shape. The objective is to knock down all the pins with the fewest rolls, just like in real bowling. Game Mode: Single Player: Most bowling HTML5 games offer a single-player mode, where you bowl against a computer-generated opponent or just aim for the best score on your own. Multiplayer: Some games allow you to compete with friends or other players online in a multiplayer mode. Scoring: Points are awarded based on the number of pins you knock down with each roll. A perfect game (10 strikes in a row) is the highest score you can achieve, which is 300 points. If you knock down all 10 pins on the first roll (a strike), you get a bonus of the pins you knock down on the next two rolls. If you knock down all 10 pins with the second roll (a spare), you get a bonus of the pins you knock down on the next roll. Customization and Power-ups: Many HTML5 bowling games allow you to customize the ball (color, patterns) or the lane. Some games might include power-ups or special features that make the game more exciting, such as increasing the speed of the ball or adding spin effects to help curve the ball around obstacles or more pins. Graphics and Physics: The graphics in Bowling HTML5 games are often stylized with smooth animations and physics-based simulations. The ball’s movement, spin, and reaction to the pins are based on realistic physics. The game will simulate how the ball travels down the lane and interacts with the pins to ensure it feels realistic and fun.

name: Bowman
description: Bowman is a popular browser-based HTML5 game that involves archery, where players control a bowman and compete against an AI or another player in a battle of accuracy and timing. The game is simple yet challenging, requiring good control over your bow and arrow to hit the target or your opponent while avoiding incoming attacks. Gameplay Features Basic Mechanics: You control a bowman who can shoot arrows. The primary controls usually involve adjusting the angle and power of the shot. The game uses a power meter to determine the strength of your shot. A higher power meter launches the arrow further, while a lower one keeps the arrow closer. Angle: The angle you set will determine the trajectory of the arrow. If the angle is too steep, the arrow might go too high, and if it's too shallow, it may not travel far enough to hit your opponent. Game Modes: Single Player: In single-player mode, you usually face an AI opponent. The AI is programmed with varying difficulty levels, making the game challenging for beginners as well as seasoned players. Two-Player Mode: One of the most engaging aspects of Bowman is its two-player mode, where you can either play on the same device or against another player on different devices. Both players take turns shooting arrows at each other, trying to knock out the opponent. Obstacles and Terrain: Some versions of Bowman feature terrain with hills, walls, or other obstacles that can deflect arrows or affect the trajectory. You will need to account for these environmental factors when shooting. You may also have to adjust your strategy depending on the distance and the level of elevation between your character and the opponent. Health System: In Bowman, players generally have health bars. A single arrow to the head or chest can reduce your health, and once it reaches zero, you lose the game. The goal is to hit your opponent with as many arrows as possible while dodging their shots. Graphics and Sound: The graphics in Bowman are minimalist, with simple 2D visuals that focus on gameplay. Characters are typically stick figures, and the backgrounds are plain to keep the focus on the archery mechanics. The sound is often minimal too, with sounds for shooting arrows, hitting targets, and occasional background music.

name: Boxer Rebellion
description: Boxer Rebellion is a QIX type game where the object is to completely outline the score boxes while avoiding the enemies. Presented in CGA with PC speaker sound effects (quite reasonable for 1982!) this game plays pretty well, and includes nine different levels. It's a little different from QIX but that may make it more enticing to play than a direct clone. The Boxer Rebellion in the context of DOS games likely refers to a game inspired by the historical event of the Boxer Rebellion, which occurred in China between 1899 and 1901. The rebellion was led by a Chinese nationalist movement known as the "Boxers" who sought to expel foreign influence from China, specifically targeting Western missionaries, diplomats, and Chinese Christians. Boxer Rebellion (DOS Game) This game, released in the early '90s, is a strategy and simulation game based on the historical events surrounding the Boxer Rebellion. Players take on the role of a Chinese or foreign faction during the rebellion, trying to control different aspects of the conflict and shape the outcome of the event. Game Overview and Features: Developer: The game was developed by Strategy First and released in 1992. It was available on DOS platforms. Genre: Strategy, Simulation, and Historical Warfare. Setting: The game takes place in China during the Boxer Rebellion. The player can experience the conflict from multiple perspectives, such as leading the Boxers or commanding the foreign military forces that intervened in the rebellion. Gameplay: Factions and Campaign: Players can either lead the Boxers, a Chinese nationalist movement, or the Eight-Nation Alliance, a coalition of foreign powers (including the United States, the United Kingdom, Japan, Russia, Germany, France, Italy, and Austria-Hungary). Each faction has different objectives, strengths, and tactics to employ. The Boxer side seeks to drive out the foreign invaders and restore China to its "traditional" ways, while the foreign powers aim to protect their citizens, interests, and prevent the spread of anti-foreign sentiments. Combat and Strategy: The game is played on a turn-based system where the player must manage resources, troop movements, and battlefield tactics. Battles are tactical, involving infantry, cavalry, and artillery, often set in historically accurate locations such as Beijing or other Chinese towns under siege. The player also needs to manage diplomacy and alliances, with various powers having their own interests in the region.

name: Boxhead 2 Play
description: Boxhead 2 Play is a popular Flash game from the Boxhead series developed by Sean Cooper. This series is well-known for its top-down zombie survival gameplay, where players fight off hordes of zombies using various weapons. In Boxhead 2 Play, the game expands on the original formula by adding co-op multiplayer (with up to two players), new levels, enemies, and weaponry. Key Gameplay Features Gameplay Mechanics: The core gameplay revolves around moving and shooting. You control the character using the arrow keys or W, A, S, D (for movement) and mouse to aim and shoot. The goal is to survive wave after wave of zombies that grow in number and difficulty. You can use a variety of weapons to kill zombies, and the game rewards accuracy and efficiency. Multiplayer (2-Player): The biggest addition to Boxhead 2 Play compared to its predecessors is the multiplayer mode, which allows two players to play on the same screen. Player 1 uses the keyboard for movement and the mouse to aim and shoot. Player 2 uses the arrow keys for movement and W, A, S, D for aiming. Working together with a friend can make the game more manageable and fun, as you strategize to hold off the zombie hordes. Weapons and Power-ups: The game offers a wide range of weapons to help players fight off zombies, including guns, shotguns, machine guns, and even explosives. As you progress through the levels, you can find power-ups or upgrade your weapons. This can be a huge help in managing the larger waves of zombies. Zombies: Boxhead 2 Play features a variety of zombie types, each with different speeds, attack patterns, and strengths. Some zombies are faster and harder to kill, while others might explode upon death, creating dangerous environmental hazards. As you defeat zombies, you collect coins and score points. The more zombies you kill, the more upgrades you unlock. Levels and Maps: The game features several maps with different layouts and challenges. Some maps are closed areas with limited space to move, while others are more open. The environment can be used to your advantage, as you can use walls and other obstacles to help keep zombies at bay. Survival: The main goal in Boxhead 2 Play is to survive as long as possible. There are several rounds, with each round being more difficult than the last. You must constantly manage your ammo, watch out for environmental hazards, and strategize to stay alive. Graphics and Style: Boxhead 2 Play features a simple stick-figure art style, which is a hallmark of the Boxhead series. While the graphics are not overly complex, they are functional and effective, especially when it comes to fast-paced gameplay where you’re focused on the action. The game’s top-down view makes it easy to spot enemies and plan your movements. Difficulty and Replayability: The game has increasing difficulty, with zombies becoming faster and more numerous as you progress through the rounds. There are multiple levels and game modes, including endless waves, which give the game a lot of replay value.

name: Brad Perolis Bomb Seeker
description: Bomb Seeker is a text-mode minesweeper variant which uses a 10x10 grid and 25 bombs, which is a lot higher ratio than you would be used to if you played the popular Windows version of the game. (You know, the one everyone played, that was included with Windows up til Windows 8.) This game uses keyboard controls only, and doesn't offer any options so hopefully you enjoy the default set up. Text-based Input: The game likely used a command-line interface where the player types commands to move through different rooms, defuse bombs, or interact with various objects and clues. Bomb Defusing: The central mechanic involves carefully disarming bombs. You might have to cut wires, enter codes, or solve other puzzles to disable them. Each bomb could have different complexities, and the player would have to read clues and use logical deduction to succeed. Time Pressure: There could be a time limit for each bomb or puzzle, adding urgency and stress to the gameplay. Decision Making: The game might present players with choices that affect the outcome, such as which tools to use or which bomb to tackle first. Wrong decisions could result in the explosion of a bomb or failure to save an area from destruction. Game Interface: Text Mode: The game is most likely played entirely in text mode (characters and symbols on a black screen), where the user interacts with descriptions of rooms, bombs, objects, and other characters. Simple Commands: Commands like "LOOK," "USE," "CUT," or "GO NORTH" would be typical of text-based adventures, and you would type these commands to perform actions. Objective: The player’s ultimate goal is to disarm all the bombs in the given area or safeguard a specific location. Each level or scenario might present increasingly difficult bomb-disposal challenges, with more intricate puzzles to solve. The game likely had various levels with different environments where Brad must navigate through dangerous situations, such as crowded buildings, streets, or military bases, filled with explosive devices.

name: BRAINdead2
description: BRAINdead2 is a simple tile-matching memory game where you turn up two tiles, and if they match, they disappear. If they don't match, they're flipped back over, and you continue until all the tiles have been matched. You can choose from one of three different tilesets, and there is a second game mode where all of the tiles are turned face up, which turns the memory game into a race against the clock. Nothing too impressive or visually stimulating here. The author says they made the game, in part, so that their 5 year old could play it unassisted.

name: Brainjar Blackjack
description: Brainjar Blackjack is a simple and straightforward HTML5 version of the classic card game Blackjack (also known as 21). This online version allows you to play Blackjack in your browser without needing to download any software or plugins. It's a great option for casual players who enjoy card games and want to practice their Blackjack skills. Game Mechanics and Rules Card Values: Number cards (2-10): Their face value (e.g., a 2 is worth 2 points, a 10 is worth 10 points). Face cards (Jack, Queen, King): Each worth 10 points. Ace: Can be worth either 1 point or 11 points, depending on what is more beneficial to the hand. Objective: The goal is to get a hand that totals 21 points, or as close to it as possible, without exceeding 21. If you go over 21, you "bust" and lose the round. You are playing against the dealer. If your hand value is closer to 21 than the dealer's, you win. If the dealer's hand is closer, you lose. If both you and the dealer have the same hand value, it’s a push (a tie). Gameplay: The game usually starts with you and the dealer both being dealt two cards. The dealer’s cards are dealt face up (one card), and the other face down (the hole card). On your turn, you can choose to: Hit: Draw another card to increase the total value of your hand. Stand: Keep your current hand and end your turn. Double Down: Double your initial bet and receive only one more card (typically available only on your first two cards). Split: If your first two cards are of equal value, you can split them into two separate hands, each with its own bet. You will then play each hand separately. Dealer's Turn: After you finish your turn, the dealer reveals their face-down card. The dealer must follow certain rules: they must hit if their total is 16 or less, and they must stand if their total is 17 or more. Winning and Payouts: If you win, you typically receive a 1:1 payout on your bet. If you win with a Blackjack (an Ace and a 10-point card), you receive a 1.5:1 payout. If the dealer busts (exceeds 21), you automatically win the round. If you bust, you lose the round, regardless of the dealer’s hand.

name: BrainStorm Pro
description: BrainStorm Pro is a gravity-based piece-matching game which bears similarity in its gameplay to the Epic Megagames classic game Brix. Both seem inspired by Taito's Puzznic game, although Brix was an obvious clone / rip-off, whereas BrainStorm Pro has its own style while retaining similar gameplay. BrainStorm Pro is a classic DOS puzzle game that challenges players to connect blocks of the same color to clear them from the screen. As you progress through the levels, the puzzles become increasingly complex, requiring strategic thinking and quick reflexes. Key Features: Addictive Gameplay: The simple yet challenging gameplay mechanic keeps you engaged for hours. Colorful Graphics: The game features bright and colorful graphics that are easy on the eyes. Multiple Levels: With 170 levels, there's plenty of content to keep you entertained. Password System: You can save your progress using passwords, allowing you to pick up where you left off.

name: Bratz Babyz Fish Tank
description: "Bratz Babyz Fish Tank" is a Flash-based simulation game that allows players to create and manage their own virtual aquarium. In the game, you can select from various fish species, design the tank's appearance with different backgrounds and decorations, and ensure the well-being of your aquatic pets by feeding them and maintaining the tank's cleanliness. Additionally, the game offers a unique feature where players can breed different fish to create new species, adding an extra layer of engagement. "Bratz Babyz Fish Tank" remains accessible through emulation on certain websites.

name: Brave Bird
description: Brave Bird is a popular and addictive HTML5 game inspired by the classic Flappy Bird. In this game, you control a bird that must navigate through a series of obstacles (usually pipes or walls) without hitting them. The game is simple in concept but challenging due to its precise timing and quick reflexes. Gameplay Mechanics Controls: Tap or Click: The bird flies upward each time you tap or click. If you don’t tap, the bird will start descending due to gravity. The key is to time your taps correctly to keep the bird at the right height to pass through gaps in the obstacles (usually pipes). The game is easy to play but difficult to master, requiring precise control over your bird’s flight path. Obstacles: The main obstacles in Brave Bird are pipes (similar to those in Flappy Bird). These pipes are spaced in such a way that you must maneuver the bird through narrow gaps. The pipes typically appear in pairs—one high and one low—requiring you to navigate through the gap between them. The pipes move from right to left, so your bird must stay in the air long enough to avoid colliding with them. Scoring: Each time you successfully pass through a set of pipes (without hitting them), you earn one point. The objective is to keep flying as long as possible, accumulating as many points as you can. Losing the Game: The game ends when the bird collides with a pipe or the ground. If the bird touches a pipe or the floor, your score is recorded, and you can try again to beat your previous score.

name: Break It
description: Break It is a DOS game from the early 1990s, typically classified as a breakout-style game, a genre made famous by Atari's Pong and later Arkanoid. Multiple Game Modes: Choose from various modes, including single-player challenges, local multiplayer, and online tournaments for endless fun! Dynamic Arenas: Play in a variety of colorful and dynamic arenas, each with unique obstacles and layouts that change the way you strategize. Power-ups: Collect power-ups during matches to gain an advantage, such as speed boosts, shields, or enhanced ball control. Character Customization: Personalize your bumper character with different skins and accessories to stand out on the field. How to Play: Select Your Mode: Choose between single-player, multiplayer, or tournament modes to start your game. Control Your Character: Use the arrow keys or WASD to navigate and bump the ball towards your opponent's goal. Collect Power-ups: Keep an eye out for power-ups on the field to enhance your gameplay. Score Goals: Aim for the opponent's net to score points and win the match! Get ready to bounce into action with BUMPER-BALL! Show off your skills and become the champion of the arena. Let the games begin!

name: Bumpmaze
description: Bumpmaze is a unique and not very fun game where the object is to "bump" the ball until it bounces into a hole. It's one of the earliest offerings from William Soleau before began focusing more on strategy / puzzle games. The ball continually bounces around at 45 degree angles in one of six randomly selected maze layouts, and you guide your "pusher" to try to nudge it where you want it to go.Bumpmaze is a classic DOS-based maze game where players navigate through mazes while avoiding obstacles and trying to reach a specific goal. It’s a puzzle and strategy game that focuses on moving through a grid-like maze, often encountering challenges and needing to figure out the most efficient way to get through. Gameplay Mechanics: Objective: The primary objective of Bumpmaze is to guide your character through a maze, usually filled with walls, obstacles, and traps, while trying to reach the exit. In some versions, you may need to collect items or complete other tasks before the exit becomes accessible. Movement: The player controls a character that moves through a grid-like maze, typically using the arrow keys or a joystick (if using a DOS-compatible controller). The character moves one square at a time, and the maze might be viewed from a top-down or isometric perspective, depending on the specific version. Maze Layout: The mazes in Bumpmaze may have varying difficulty levels, with increasing complexity as the player progresses. Some mazes might feature doors that can only be opened by collecting certain items or solving puzzles in specific ways. Some versions of the game may include teleporters or other types of maze mechanics that add complexity. Bumping Mechanic: The "Bump" part of Bumpmaze refers to a mechanic where players must bump into certain objects or elements in the maze to clear paths, open doors, or disable traps. This mechanic can involve either manually pushing elements or triggering specific actions by moving into them. Some versions might have objects like crates, stones, or other movable elements that players can bump to open new paths or block enemies. Enemies and Hazards: As the player progresses through the maze, there may be enemies or hazards that require quick reflexes or strategic thinking to avoid. Enemies may move in predictable patterns or follow the player, adding an extra layer of challenge. Traps like spikes, pits, or timed doors may add difficulty, requiring players to carefully plan their moves.

name: Bunny Solitaire
description: Tripeaks Solitaire game for Easter. Try to remove all cards by selecting cards that are 1 higher or lower in value than the open card at the bottom.Bunny Solitaire is a cute and engaging variation of the classic Solitaire card game, typically featuring a playful bunny theme. In this version of Solitaire, you may encounter colorful, themed cards and background images related to bunnies, which adds a whimsical touch to the traditional gameplay. Gameplay Mechanics: Objective: The primary goal of Bunny Solitaire is the same as classic Solitaire: to arrange the cards in a specific order, usually from Ace to King, in four suit piles (one for each suit). The game is typically played with a standard deck of 52 cards. The player must use strategy and careful planning to move cards between piles and build sequences. Gameplay Rules: The game starts with a set of face-up and face-down cards placed in various columns. The player needs to create a sequence of descending cards (from King to Ace) in alternating colors (red and black) on the tableau. The tableau consists of columns of cards, and empty spaces can be filled with a King. There are also foundation piles where cards must be placed in ascending order (from Ace to King) by suit. Controls: Drag and Drop: Cards are typically moved by clicking on them and dragging them to the correct position, whether it's within the tableau or into the foundation piles. Click to Reveal: In some versions, face-down cards in the tableau can be revealed by clicking on them. Undo and Restart: Many modern versions include the option to undo moves or restart the game. Bunny Theme: As the name suggests, the game may feature bunny-themed graphics, such as cards decorated with cute bunny illustrations, a bunny character as the main mascot, and a playful background (such as a meadow or bunny-filled forest). Some versions might also feature small animations of bunnies hopping around or performing actions when the player makes a move, adding a whimsical and lighthearted atmosphere. Scoring and Winning: The player earns points for correctly moving cards to the foundation piles, with bonuses for completing all piles in a shorter time. The game is won once all cards have been successfully placed in the four foundation piles in the correct order. Levels and Difficulty: Bunny Solitaire may offer different difficulty levels, such as Easy, Medium, and Hard, which influence the number of face-up cards at the start and the complexity of the tableau arrangement. Some versions include additional challenges, such as a time limit or a set number of moves to complete the game.

name: Burger Shop
description: Can you cook the right Burgers? And add the ingredients in the right order? Serve your burgers as fast as you can.Burger Shop is a popular time-management and restaurant simulation game where players run a burger joint, serving customers quickly and efficiently. The goal is to prepare and serve the correct food orders based on customer requests, which usually include assembling various ingredients to make the right combination of burgers, drinks, fries, and desserts. The game often features multiple levels, increasing difficulty, and the pressure of serving a growing number of customers in a limited time. Gameplay Mechanics: Objective: In Burger Shop, the player is tasked with running a burger restaurant and fulfilling customer orders as quickly as possible. Each customer places an order that requires the player to assemble ingredients such as buns, patties, vegetables, and condiments in the correct order. The goal is to maximize the speed and accuracy of food preparation, serving each customer before they become impatient or leave. Controls: Drag and Drop: The player will usually interact with the game by dragging ingredients to the assembly area to create the burger or other items (like drinks or fries) as per the customer's order. Clicking: Clicking on the kitchen equipment (like grills, fryers, or drink dispensers) to prepare different parts of the meal. Menu: The player can view customer orders on the screen and must prepare the food items accordingly. Game Flow: Customers arrive at the counter and place their orders, which are displayed with a list of ingredients. The player must quickly assemble the correct ingredients and deliver the finished burger or meal to the customer. The game features multiple stations for different tasks: grilling burgers, frying fries, preparing drinks, and assembling burgers. As the game progresses, the orders become more complex, and the number of customers increases, making it more challenging to keep up with the orders. Ingredients and Items: Burgers: A variety of ingredients such as beef patties, chicken patties, lettuce, tomatoes, cheese, ketchup, and mustard are used to create burgers. Sides: French fries, onion rings, and other sides may be prepared for customers. Drinks and Desserts: Customers may also order drinks, ice cream, or other desserts, requiring additional preparation. Each item has a specific preparation step, and some ingredients may require cooking or frying. Levels and Progression: The game typically progresses through different levels, with each level introducing new ingredients, more complex customer orders, or additional stations in the kitchen. As the levels increase, customers become more impatient, and the player must work faster to meet their demands. New equipment may be unlocked as the game progresses, such as upgraded grills, faster fryers, or even automated systems to help with food preparation.

name: Burnt Rubber
description: Burnt Rubber is a simple and violent game where the object is to run over people and animals with your car. Unlike Grand Theft Auto, there are no missions or exploration other than the single screen where you run over as many people/animals until time runs out.Burnt Rubber is a DOS game released in the early 1990s, developed by Titus Interactive. It is a racing game that focuses on fun, arcade-style gameplay, where players control a car and race against AI-controlled opponents on various tracks. The game features a top-down view and uses a simple control scheme, making it accessible to a broad audience. Gameplay Mechanics: Objective: The player controls a car and competes against AI opponents in various races. The goal is to finish each race in the fastest time while avoiding obstacles and managing the car's performance. Players can race on different tracks with varying levels of difficulty and complexity, including turns, jumps, and other challenges. Controls: Keyboard: The game uses simple keyboard controls for steering, accelerating, and braking the car. The player needs to navigate around tight corners and avoid obstacles to maintain a competitive pace. Arrow Keys: Typically used for controlling the car’s movement—left and right for steering, up for accelerating, and down for braking. Spacebar: May be used for other actions like boosting or special abilities, depending on the version of the game. Car and Tracks: Cars: Players have access to a variety of vehicles, each with unique characteristics such as speed, handling, and durability. Players can often choose which car they want to use before starting a race. Tracks: The game features several tracks with varying levels of complexity. Some tracks are straightforward while others are filled with sharp turns, ramps, or obstacles to navigate through. Race Modes: Single Race: A quick, standalone race against AI opponents. Tournament/Championship: A series of races across different tracks, with the player earning points based on their finishing position in each race. The overall champion is determined at the end of the series. Difficulty: The difficulty of the game is determined by the number of AI competitors, the complexity of the tracks, and the car’s performance capabilities. Players can adjust the difficulty for a more challenging experience. Power-ups: In some versions of the game, players can collect or use power-ups that help them during the race, such as boosts to speed, temporary shields, or other advantages to beat the competition. Graphics: The game features 2D graphics with a top-down perspective, typical of many arcade-style racing games of the era. Cars are viewed from above, and tracks are designed with a simple but clear layout, allowing players to focus on navigation and racing tactics.

name: Burrito Bison
description: Burrito Bison is a popular Flash game developed by Juicy Beast Studios, first released in 2011. The game is a fun, action-packed launch game where players control Burrito Bison, a luchador, who is on a mission to escape a candy-themed world by launching himself into the air and smashing through various obstacles. Gameplay Mechanics: Objective: The main goal is to launch Burrito Bison as far as possible by smashing through candy-themed obstacles and enemies. The player earns money and upgrades after each launch to improve Burrito Bison’s abilities and extend the distance he can travel. Controls: Mouse Click: The player clicks at the right time to launch Burrito Bison into the air. The launch timing is crucial for achieving the best trajectory and maximum distance. While in Air: Players can perform additional actions, such as smashing or bouncing off enemies to maintain speed or height. Launching Mechanics: Burrito Bison starts each round being slingshotted into the air. The player must aim and launch him at the right angle to travel as far as possible. During flight, Burrito Bison can hit various candy enemies, such as gummy bears, and bounce off them to maintain momentum. The player must continuously smash through candy enemies and avoid obstacles while collecting gold for upgrades. Enemies and Obstacles: Candy Enemies: The game features a variety of candy-themed enemies, such as gummy bears and jelly beans, which Burrito Bison can either bounce off or destroy. These enemies help the player gain more momentum or speed. Obstacles: Some obstacles can hinder Burrito Bison’s flight, including spikes, walls, or other traps. The goal is to avoid or break through them to continue traveling. Upgrades: After each run, the player earns gold based on the distance traveled and the enemies destroyed. This gold can be used to buy upgrades that improve various aspects of Burrito Bison's abilities: Launch Power: Increases the force of the slingshot to make Burrito Bison travel farther from the start. Speed and Momentum: Upgrades that help maintain or increase speed and boost your distance. Special Abilities: New moves and powers that allow Burrito Bison to smash through enemies or avoid certain obstacles. Game Flow: Each launch starts with Burrito Bison being slingshotted into the air, and the player must time the launch correctly. The goal is to travel as far as possible by bouncing on enemies, using power-ups, and avoiding obstacles. Players repeat this process, trying to outdo their previous distance. The game gets progressively harder with more challenging enemies, tracks, and obstacles. Graphics: Cartoonish and Humorous: The game uses bright, colorful, and exaggerated cartoonish graphics that reflect its whimsical, candy-themed world. Burrito Bison and enemies are drawn in a humorous, fun style, adding to the overall lightheartedness of the game. Sound and Music: Sound Effects: The game has fun sound effects, such as engine noises, bouncing sounds, and the squashing of enemies. These audio cues add to the gameplay experience. Music: The background music is upbeat and energetic, matching the fast-paced, arcade-style action of the game.

name: Bush Shoot-Out
description: "Bush Shoot-Out" is a satirical flash game that places players in the role of a character resembling former U.S. President George W. Bush. The gameplay involves navigating various levels while shooting at targets, including caricatures of political figures and objects, in a humorous and exaggerated style. Players use a variety of weapons and power-ups to rack up points and complete missions, all while facing increasing challenges and obstacles. The game features a cartoonish art style and a lighthearted tone, making it an entertaining, if cheeky, experience. With its mix of action and political satire, "Bush Shoot-Out" offers a playful take on the world of politics, allowing players to engage in over-the-top gameplay while providing a humorous commentary on political events.

name: Bust-a-Move 2: Arcade Edition
description: Bust-a-Move (aka Puzzle Bobble) is an extremely popular series of bubble-matching games which combine a puzzle game's need for strategy with the quick-thinking and reflexes needed for success in an action game. It is popular in arcades as well as home consoles. This demo of Bust-a-Move 2 allows you to experience this conversion of the arcade game for DOS, albeit with no music and limited levels.Bust-a-Move 2: Arcade Edition is a DOS game released in the mid-1990s. It's a classic puzzle game that is part of the Bust-a-Move series (also known as Puzzle Bobble), developed by Taito. The game is widely recognized for its simple yet addictive gameplay, where players shoot bubbles to form matches of three or more, causing them to pop. Gameplay Mechanics: Objective: The main objective in Bust-a-Move 2: Arcade Edition is to clear the screen of bubbles by shooting bubbles from a cannon at the bottom of the screen. Players need to match bubbles of the same color in groups of three or more to make them pop. The game features various levels with different bubble arrangements, and the goal is to clear all bubbles on each level before the screen fills up to the bottom. Controls: Arrow Keys: Used to move the bubble cannon left and right. Spacebar: Shoots the bubble in the direction the cannon is facing. The player must aim carefully to ensure the bubbles match with others of the same color on the screen. Mouse (optional): Some versions may allow players to control the cannon with the mouse to aim and shoot the bubbles. Gameplay Mechanics: Bubbles: Bubbles are arranged in clusters at the top of the screen, and the player controls a cannon that shoots bubbles of different colors. The player must aim the cannon and shoot bubbles to create groups of three or more matching bubbles. When a match is made, the bubbles pop and disappear. The game gradually introduces new patterns of bubble arrangements, making the levels progressively harder. Levels and Progression: Each level starts with a new bubble arrangement, and the player must clear the bubbles before they descend too far toward the bottom of the screen. The game features several levels, and after clearing each one, the player moves on to the next, with the difficulty increasing as new, more complex bubble formations are introduced. The game includes both single-player and two-player modes, where two players can cooperate or compete to clear bubbles. Special Bubbles: Power-ups: In some versions, there are special bubbles that provide power-ups when popped, such as clearing a larger area or changing the color of nearby bubbles. Bomb Bubbles: Some bubble types act as bombs, clearing surrounding bubbles when popped.

name: Butterfly Kyodai
description: Mahjong connect game with butterflies. Connect two halves to create a butterfly. The connecting path cannot have more than two 90 degree angles. Butterfly Kyodai is a fun and engaging HTML-based puzzle game that revolves around matching tiles in pairs to clear the board. It’s a part of the Kyodai Mahjong series, where the player is tasked with solving various tile-matching puzzles. This particular game adds a unique twist by using butterfly-themed tiles. Gameplay Mechanics: Objective: The goal in Butterfly Kyodai is to clear the board by matching pairs of identical butterfly-themed tiles. The game follows the traditional Mahjong-style mechanics but adds a butterfly theme with beautifully designed tiles. You can only match two tiles if they are free, meaning they are not covered by other tiles and can be connected by a line that does not exceed two right-angle turns. Controls: Mouse Click: The player clicks to select tiles, and a valid pair of tiles will automatically disappear from the board. Hint and Shuffle: There are also options to shuffle the tiles or get hints if you’re stuck, although these are typically limited in usage during the game. Tile Matching: Free Tiles: A tile is considered free if it is not blocked by other tiles. You can only match free tiles. Line Connections: The key mechanic is that tiles can be connected by a path with at most two right-angle turns (making an "L" or "Z" shape). If you can connect a pair of tiles through this path, they will be removed from the board. Levels: The game consists of various levels, each with a different arrangement of butterfly tiles. As the player progresses, the layouts become more complex, with more tiles to clear and more difficult paths to navigate. Some levels have additional challenges like limited moves or time constraints, adding an extra layer of difficulty. Power-ups: Shuffle: If you can’t find any more valid pairs, you can shuffle the tiles, which re-randomizes their placement and might give you new matching opportunities. Hint: If you're stuck, you can use the hint button to reveal a pair of tiles that are ready to be matched. Graphics and Design: Butterfly Tiles: The game’s tiles are beautifully designed with butterfly illustrations, making it visually appealing. The colorful tiles contrast nicely with the clean, simple backgrounds of the game. Theme: The overall theme is calming and relaxing, with soothing music and pleasant tile designs. Sound and Music: The game features soothing background music and gentle sound effects when tiles are matched or shuffled. The relaxing audio makes the game ideal for players looking for a casual, stress-free experience. Difficulty Levels: As you advance through the levels, the complexity increases. New patterns of tiles and more blocks to clear mean that you need to plan your moves carefully to find free tiles and match them. The game doesn’t impose a time limit in most levels, but some levels may feature time-based challenges to add variety and difficulty.

name: Butterfly Match 3
description: Match 3 game with Butterflies. Try to remove all colored (light blue) backgrounds by matching 3 or more of the same butterflies.Butterfly Match 3 is a fun and colorful HTML5-based puzzle game that follows the popular Match-3 genre. In this game, players are tasked with matching three or more similar butterfly-themed tiles to clear them from the board and earn points. It offers simple mechanics, but the challenge increases as the player progresses through various levels. Gameplay Mechanics: Objective: The primary goal in Butterfly Match 3 is to swap adjacent tiles to form matches of three or more tiles of the same color or design, often butterflies or related items. When a match is made, the matched tiles are cleared from the board, and new tiles fall into place from the top. Controls: Mouse/Touch Controls: The player clicks (or taps on mobile devices) to select two adjacent tiles and swap them. The goal is to create a line of three or more identical tiles horizontally or vertically. Drag and Drop: Some versions may allow players to click and drag tiles to swap them. Matching Mechanics: Match-3 Rule: To score points, you need to align at least three matching tiles in a row either horizontally or vertically. When this happens, the tiles are removed, and new tiles fall to replace them. Combo Moves: Creating larger matches (more than three tiles) often results in special bonuses or powerful effects, like clearing entire rows or columns. Levels and Progression: Increasing Difficulty: As the player advances through levels, new challenges are introduced, such as restricted tile swaps, limited moves, or tiles that are locked in place. Objectives: Some levels have specific objectives, such as clearing a certain number of butterflies or achieving a target score within a set number of moves. Timer or Moves: Some versions include time limits for each level, while others limit the number of moves available to complete the level’s objective.

name: Byte Bandit
description: Byte Bandit is a simple slot-machine / one-armed-bandit casino type game. You start with $10 virtual dollars, insert your coin(s) and pull the handle.Byte Bandit is a DOS-based game released in the early 1990s. It's an arcade-style action and puzzle game where players take on the role of a digital "bandit" trying to navigate through various computer-themed levels while avoiding or overcoming obstacles. The game is set in a world inside a computer, where the player must perform different tasks, often related to collecting data or manipulating elements of the virtual world. Gameplay Mechanics: Objective: The main goal of Byte Bandit is to navigate through various computer-themed levels, collecting certain items or solving puzzles while avoiding enemies and obstacles. Each level is set up like a "system" within the computer, and the player must figure out how to move past security systems, gather data, and find the exit. Gameplay Style: Action-Puzzle Hybrid: The game is a mix of quick reflexes and puzzle-solving. As the player moves through the levels, they will encounter various challenges such as security firewall2s, hostile programs, or locked areas that require solving puzzles to proceed. Timed Challenges: Some levels feature a time limit, requiring the player to act quickly to avoid being "caught" by the system or to solve a puzzle before time runs out. Controls: Arrow Keys: Used to move the Byte Bandit character around the screen, dodging obstacles and enemies. Action Keys: Depending on the task, you may use specific keys to interact with objects, collect items, or use special abilities. Levels and Progression: The game is structured across multiple levels, with increasing difficulty as the player progresses. Each level involves a new set of challenges or a more complex "computer system" to navigate. Some levels have different objectives, such as collecting all the data packets or breaking into secured areas. Enemies and Obstacles: Security Systems: These can include "firewall2s," which block your progress, and you must find a way around them. There are also hostile computer programs that try to stop you. Hazards: Moving obstacles or traps in the levels will damage or reset your progress, adding a level of strategy and timing to your movements.

name: Búsqueda de Palabras Diaria
description: Everyday a new word search puzzle level in Spanish. Find all the indicated words.Búsqueda de Palabras Diaria is an engaging HTML5 word search game where players are tasked with finding hidden words in a grid of letters. The twist in this game is that it offers daily challenges, providing players with a new word search puzzle each day. This keeps the gameplay fresh and gives players a reason to come back every day to solve the latest puzzle. Gameplay Mechanics: Objective: The objective of Búsqueda de Palabras Diaria is simple: players need to find a list of hidden words within a grid of random letters. The words may be arranged in any direction: horizontally, vertically, diagonally, and even backward. The game provides a daily challenge, with a new puzzle appearing every day. Each day's puzzle comes with a different set of words to find, ensuring a fresh experience each time. Controls: Mouse/Touch: Players click and drag to highlight words in the grid. Once a word is found, it is highlighted in the grid, and the word is removed from the list of words to find. On mobile, players can tap and swipe across the grid to select words. Gameplay Style: Word List: At the beginning of each puzzle, a list of words to find is displayed, typically at the side or bottom of the screen. These words can be related to a specific theme (e.g., animals, food, sports, etc.). Timed or Untimed: Some versions of the game are timed, challenging players to complete the puzzle within a set time limit, while others may be untimed, focusing purely on finding the words at your own pace. Levels and Progression: Daily Challenges: The game offers a new puzzle each day. The difficulty may vary, with some daily challenges being easier and others more complex. Increasing Difficulty: As you progress through the days, the word search grids may become larger, or the list of words to find may become more difficult or more complex. Power-ups and Hints: Hint Feature: If a player is stuck, they can use a hint to reveal part of a hidden word, making it easier to find. Word Highlighting: Some versions of the game will automatically highlight the first few letters of each word to help players get started. Graphics and Design: Clean, Simple Layout: The design is straightforward, with a large grid of letters displayed on the screen and a side or bottom panel showing the word list. Word Highlighting: As players find words, the matching letters are typically highlighted in bright colors, making it clear which words have been completed. Themes: Depending on the version, the game may use different background themes, such as nature, abstract designs, or minimalist designs, to create a visually appealing environment.

name: C-Dogs
description: The sequel to Cyberdogs, C-Dogs improves the original Cyberdogs gameplay formula in some ways. The game involves you taking your character on missions which usually involve shooting anything around using a variety of weapons that can be bought before missions.C-Dogs is a DOS-based top-down action game, often remembered for its engaging multiplayer mode and action-packed gameplay. Originally released in the 1990s, the game was created by the C-Dogs Team and became popular for its fast-paced, arcade-style combat and the ability to play in both single-player and multiplayer modes. Gameplay Mechanics: Objective: In C-Dogs, players control a mercenary armed with various weapons and must complete different combat missions. The primary objective is to navigate through levels, fight enemies, and complete assigned tasks, such as rescuing hostages, destroying enemy bases, or eliminating targets. The game offers both single-player and multiplayer modes, allowing players to either take on missions alone or team up for cooperative gameplay. Controls: Movement: The game uses the arrow keys to move the character around the screen. Shooting: Players shoot in the direction they are facing using a specific key, typically Ctrl or Spacebar. The shooting is done in an eight-directional setup, making the combat dynamic and quick. Weapons: Players can collect different weapons and ammunition, ranging from basic pistols to powerful machine guns, rocket launchers, and explosives. There are also grenades that can be thrown at enemies or obstacles. Menu Navigation: Players can access inventory and mission information using other function keys (like Esc for menus). Gameplay Style: Top-Down Shooter: The game is a top-down shooter, where you navigate the map and face enemies coming at you from various angles. It features fast-paced action, with lots of shooting and dodging. Mission-Based: Each level in the game presents a unique mission that may involve clearing an area of enemies, rescuing hostages, or collecting items. Players are given a set of objectives, and they must complete them while fighting through enemies. Multiplayer Mode: One of the key features of C-Dogs is its local multiplayer mode, where up to four players can compete against each other or cooperate in the same level. This mode adds a layer of fun, allowing for team-based strategies or PvP (player vs. player) battles. Levels and Progression: The game features a series of missions that are organized into different campaigns. Each campaign has a different story or theme, such as taking down a criminal syndicate or infiltrating a military base. Progression: Players advance through the game by completing missions and moving onto more difficult levels with tougher enemies, new environments, and more complex objectives. Weapons and Power-ups: Weapons: The game includes a variety of weapons, such as handguns, rifles, machine guns, rocket launchers, and grenades. Weapons can be picked up in the environment or purchased between missions. Power-ups: Players can find health packs to heal or armor to reduce damage taken. There are also ammunition pickups to reload your weapons. Enemies and Obstacles: Enemy Soldiers: The main enemies are hostile soldiers, but the game features different types of enemies with varying behaviors, such as some that may hide behind cover or others that rush directly at the player. Obstacles: Some levels include obstacles, like walls or doors that can be opened or destroyed. These add an extra layer of strategy to each level, as players need to find ways to overcome environmental challenges.

name: CAAC
description: The game could have been a flight simulation game developed for DOS, where players could control different aircraft, possibly used for training or as a promotional tool by the CAAC. name: Cactus McCoy
description: Cactus McCoy is a platformer flash game developed by Flipline Studios. The game was released in 2011 and is available for free to play online. The game stars Cactus McCoy, a cowboy who is cursed to become a cactus after stealing a cursed emerald. McCoy must now return the emerald to its rightful owner in order to break the curse. The game features a variety of weapons and items that McCoy can use to defeat enemies and solve puzzles. The game also features a variety of different environments, including deserts, caves, and ruins. Cactus McCoy is a fun and challenging game that is suitable for all ages. It is a great way to pass the time and enjoy some classic arcade action.

name: Cadillacs and Dinosaurs
description: Cadillacs and Dinosaurs is a classic arcade game originally released by Capcom in 1993. It was also adapted into a Flash game version for online play, capturing the essence of the original beat-'em-up experience with its action-packed gameplay and quirky characters. Game Description: "Cadillacs and Dinosaurs" is a fast-paced, side-scrolling beat-'em-up flash game that combines the thrills of classic arcade combat with a unique setting: a post-apocalyptic world where dinosaurs roam free, and humans struggle to survive. Players fight through hordes of enemies using a combination of punches, kicks, and special attacks, all while encountering fierce dinosaurs and other wild creatures. In this Flash version, players can enjoy the same dynamic gameplay and characters from the original arcade game, with updated controls and graphics to fit the Flash platform. The game captures the charm and excitement of the 90s arcade action genre, allowing players to experience the thrills of battling alongside their heroes. Gameplay: Playable Characters: Players can choose from several characters from the original game, including: Mack the T-Rex Hunter: A rugged, heroic figure armed with powerful fists and a strong sense of justice. Hannah Dundee: A skilled fighter who uses her agility and combat expertise to take down enemies. Jack Tenrec: A mechanic and environmentalist who fights to protect nature, often using tools and vehicles in combat. Mustapha the Technician: Known for his intelligence and resourcefulness.

name: Cake House
description: Connect 3 or more of the same cake images. Connections can be made in all directions. Baking Equipment: You will need to use various machines in the bakery, such as ovens and mixers, to prepare the cake layers. The game may have a timer for baking, so you must manage time carefully. Decoration Station: Once the cake is baked, it moves to the decoration station, where you can add toppings and frosting to complete the order.

Whether to launch a direct assault or to prepare for a defensive stand are key parts of the gameplay.
