name: Canabalt
description: "Canabalt" is a fast-paced, endless runner flash game where players control a character who is fleeing from a collapsing city. The game features simple one-touch controls, allowing players to jump across rooftops, dodge obstacles, and survive as long as possible. Its minimalist aesthetic, with pixel art graphics and a haunting soundtrack, creates an immersive atmosphere. The gameplay focuses on speed and precision, challenging players to master the timing of their jumps to achieve the highest score. The game's combination of simplicity and intensity has made it a classic in the genre.

name: Candy Bubble

This is done by shooting bubbles from a cannon at the bottom of the screen to match them with the existing bubbles on the playfield. Matching bubbles of the same color will cause them to pop and disappear, allowing for more space to shoot and new bubbles to fall into place. Clicking or tapping will release a bubble from the cannon, aiming it toward other bubbles in the game grid. Aim and Fire: The player must aim their shot carefully. The cannon will show a preview of where the bubble will land, and the player can adjust the aim before shooting. Bubbles of the same color need to connect in groups of at least three to pop and clear them from the board. Levels and Difficulty: Increasing Complexity: As the game progresses, the levels become more intricate, with bubbles arranged in tighter patterns or requiring more precise aiming to clear. Some levels may introduce obstacles like walls or extra-colored bubbles that make the puzzles harder. Multiple Levels: Candy Bubble typically has many levels, offering plenty of gameplay hours. name: Candy Connect

Controls: Mouse or Touchscreen: Players use their mouse or touchscreen to click and drag a line between two matching candies. The line must not pass through other candies or obstacles on the grid. Connection: The player can connect matching candies vertically, horizontally, or diagonally, as long as there are no blockers in the way. Gameplay Style: Match-3 Twist: Instead of swapping candies like in traditional match-3 games, the goal is to connect them in a continuous line. This introduces a layer of strategic thinking, as players must plan their moves to connect and clear groups of candies. Grid-based Puzzles: The game is typically played on a grid, where candies are placed randomly, and players need to find and connect the matching pairs. Limited Moves or Time: Some versions of Candy Connect come with a limited number of moves or a countdown timer. name: Canfield Solitaire
description: Classic Canfield Solitaire game. Move all cards to the 4 foundation piles starting with the initial card in ascending order. On the tableau build down by alternate color. Use the stock (top left) or waste pile (left) for new cards. You can wrap from King to Ace.Canfield Solitaire is a classic and engaging HTML5 solitaire card game based on a variation of Klondike solitaire. It features a more challenging layout and requires players to strategically manage their moves. In Canfield Solitaire, the goal is to arrange all the cards in four foundation piles, starting from Ace to King, all while dealing with a unique deck and setup. Gameplay Mechanics: Objective: The primary goal in Canfield Solitaire is to build four foundation piles, each starting with an Ace and ending with a King, one for each suit (hearts, diamonds, clubs, and spades). Players need to move cards from the tableau (the seven columns of cards) and the stock (remaining cards) to the foundation piles in the correct order. You must play the game using the fewest moves possible to complete all foundation piles. Controls: Mouse or Touchscreen: Players drag and drop cards from the tableau to the foundation piles or move them to other tableau columns. Stock Pile: Cards from the stock pile are drawn one at a time, and can be moved to the tableau or foundation piles. Tableau: The tableau consists of seven piles, where the top card of each pile is visible. The cards are arranged in decreasing order and alternating colors (red and black). Gameplay Style: Deck Layout: The game begins with seven tableau piles. The first pile has one card, the second has two, and so on, up to seven cards in the last pile. Moving Cards: Cards can be moved within the tableau in descending order and alternating colors (red and black). For example, a red 6 can be placed on a black 7. Stock Pile: If there are no more moves available in the tableau, players can draw cards from the stock. The stock will be reshuffled once all cards from it have been dealt. Foundation Piles: The goal is to move cards to the four foundation piles. Aces go at the bottom of each pile, and players need to stack the rest of the cards in ascending order (2, 3, 4, etc.) in matching suits. Levels and Difficulty: Challenging Gameplay: Canfield Solitaire is known for being more challenging than traditional solitaire. The tableau has fewer cards visible at the start, and the stockpile is limited to one draw, making it a game of careful strategy and planning. Limited Moves: Players must be strategic in their card moves, as the game often doesn’t offer the same "easy" hints as traditional Klondike solitaire. Power-ups and Bonuses: Stock Reuse: The deck may offer the option to reshuffle the cards once all cards from the stock have been drawn, but in some versions, this is limited to one reshuffle. No Undo: Most versions of Canfield Solitaire do not allow undoing moves, which requires players to think carefully about each decision. The background is often minimalistic, allowing the focus to remain on the game itself. Sound: Simple sound effects are triggered when cards are moved, matched, or placed in the foundation piles. The game typically includes soft background music that adds to the relaxing atmosphere. name: Capt'n Squiddy's Bootleg Push-Push
description: Capt'n Squiddy's Bootleg Push-Push is a Sokoban variant that is pretty decent overall. Apparently a version of Sokoban called "Push-Push" was available on early Samsung phones, and that's the game that this DOS version attempts to mimic. It plays just like Sokoban: Push blocks on top of X's to beat the level and move on to the next. It has decent graphics and some midi music. There are a lot of levels, and thanks to the Wayback Machine there's a website that gives solutions to all the levels, assuming the levels in this game are all the same as those for the ancient Samsung phone game.

description: This "Special Edition" (aka demo, or limited version of the full game) of Captain Bible in Dome of Darkness presents better production quality than most Christian video games, and it actually has gameplay as well! You of course play Captain Bible, and run around a maze collecting verses to dispel the lies that you encounter.Captain Bible in Dome of Darkness is a DOS action-adventure game released in 1994. Developed by Klein & Partners and published by Knowledge Adventure, the game is an educational title that blends religious themes with gameplay. It was aimed at a Christian audience, specifically targeting younger players, and sought to teach Bible verses and moral lessons through gameplay. Gameplay Mechanics: Objective: In Captain Bible in Dome of Darkness, players control Captain Bible, a hero who is on a mission to stop the forces of darkness that are trying to take over a futuristic city. The game is divided into several levels, each with a specific objective, and players need to use Bible verses to defeat the enemies and solve puzzles. Controls: Mouse or Keyboard: The game is controlled using the keyboard or mouse. Players navigate Captain Bible through the levels, interact with objects, and fight enemies using a combination of Bible-based abilities. Combat: The player uses the Bible verses to defeat enemies or obstacles. In some instances, Captain Bible must "collect" Bible verses by solving puzzles or overcoming challenges. The correct Bible verse allows Captain Bible to unleash a powerful attack or trigger a positive effect. Gameplay Style: Exploration and Puzzle Solving: Players navigate through the "Dome of Darkness," solving puzzles and overcoming obstacles to progress. Puzzles are based around Bible knowledge, with players needing to select the correct Bible verse or passage to solve each puzzle. Learning through Gameplay: The educational aspect is central to the game. Players learn Bible verses and concepts as they progress through different levels. The game aims to teach moral lessons through its storyline and gameplay, focusing on good vs. evil themes, and the power of faith. Battle and Enemies: The game features battles against various dark forces. Captain Bible can use his knowledge of the Bible to "fight" these enemies by quoting appropriate scriptures, which act as a form of attack or defense. Story and Setting: The game's storyline involves Captain Bible entering the Dome of Darkness, a futuristic, dystopian city controlled by evil forces. Players help Captain Bible use his Bible knowledge to dispel the darkness and restore order. The setting features a sci-fi, futuristic cityscape mixed with religious symbolism. Enemies are often referred to as “dark forces” and “evil creatures,” and the game aims to combat these forces with the power of Bible verses.

name: Captain Comic
description: One of my first experiences with 'shareware' way back a couple of months before we'd even purchased our old 2400baud modem ... Anyways, this game was quite innovative back when it was released, with it's smooth scrolling EGA graphics and sound effects. (This was 1989, of course.) It's still a pretty cool game; the enemies and locations are memorable, as is the music.Captain Comic is a DOS platformer game released in 1990, developed and published by Michael A. Berlyn. It’s a fun, colorful side-scrolling action game that combines exploration, puzzle-solving, and platforming. The game features Captain Comic, a quirky hero who must retrieve stolen treasures across several different worlds while navigating tricky obstacles and fighting enemies. Gameplay Mechanics: Objective: In Captain Comic, the player controls the titular hero, Captain Comic, whose mission is to recover stolen treasures that have been scattered across various levels. These treasures include valuable artifacts, and collecting them is key to completing the game. Players must guide Captain Comic through various worlds, avoiding traps and enemies while solving puzzles to access new areas and find hidden treasures. Controls: Keyboard: The game is controlled using the keyboard, where the player moves Captain Comic left or right, jumps, and shoots. The typical keys involve using arrow keys for movement and the space bar for jumping or shooting. Jumping and Shooting: Captain Comic can jump over platforms and obstacles, while his blaster allows him to shoot enemies. It’s important to time jumps and attacks to navigate the levels effectively. Gameplay Style: Platforming: As a traditional platformer, the game focuses heavily on jumping, dodging obstacles, and collecting items. The levels feature platforms that require precise jumps to reach higher areas or avoid dangerous pitfalls. Exploration and Puzzle Solving: Along with navigating the levels, Captain Comic needs to find hidden items or keys to progress through locked doors and uncover treasures. Puzzles are usually straightforward and require exploring different paths to unlock new areas. Enemies and Obstacles: Captain Comic faces various enemies, such as alien creatures, robots, and environmental hazards like spikes. Shooting or avoiding these enemies is key to progressing through the game. Power-ups: Along the way, Captain Comic can collect power-ups like special items that enhance his jumping ability or blaster power, which can make it easier to defeat stronger enemies.

name: Captain Forever
description: Captain Forever is a unique and creative flash game that blends elements of space exploration and ship building. Players take on the role of a customizable spaceship captain tasked with navigating through an endless universe filled with enemy ships and various resources. The game features a distinctive mechanic where players can collect parts from defeated enemies to build and upgrade their own ships. This allows for a high degree of customization, letting players experiment with different configurations and designs to create the ultimate spacecraft. The graphics are retro and charming, with a focus on colorful pixel art. As players progress, they face increasingly challenging foes and environments, encouraging strategic thinking and adaptation. With its addictive gameplay loop and emphasis on creativity, Captain Forever offers a captivating experience for fans of space games and sandbox mechanics.

name: Captain Spleen
description: Captain Spleen is an adventure game, but a strange one. Rather than typing commands or clicking objects, you simple use the cursor keys and Enter/Spacebar to select different options. The story (perhaps inspired by the movie Spaceballs?!) involves paying back a debt. You'll need to travel around the galaxy as the titular "Captain Spleen" to I guess collect money to pay off the debt. There are many locations to visit although there's no guidance about where to go or what to do. The graphics are amateurish but since it sounds like it was one of the author's first games (he calls it "pretty pathetic" on his old website) that's not too surprising!

name: Captain Spleen II
description: This is part two of the mercifully short-lived Captain Spleen series. The first Captain Spleen game is a strange adventure game where you use the keyboard to choose different action options in weird locations. The sequel does a lot of the same, except using the mouse to click on things. There is an odd story that you'll get to follow along with odd drawings and sound effects.Captain Spleen II is a DOS platformer and action game released in 1994. It is the sequel to Captain Spleen, a relatively obscure action game that gained attention for its quirky humor and offbeat gameplay. The game was created by TurboTech and released for PC (DOS) systems. Like its predecessor, Captain Spleen II features humorous gameplay and cartoonish graphics, combined with platforming action and a unique protagonist. Gameplay Mechanics: Objective: In Captain Spleen II, players control Captain Spleen, a quirky, offbeat superhero who must navigate various levels, defeat enemies, and overcome obstacles to complete his mission. The primary objective of the game is to progress through different levels while solving puzzles, avoiding traps, and battling enemies. Captain Spleen is tasked with collecting objects, defeating bosses, and ultimately stopping the evil forces threatening the world. Controls: Keyboard: The game is primarily controlled using the keyboard. Players move Captain Spleen around the screen, jump to avoid obstacles, and perform actions like attacking or interacting with objects. Jumping and Combat: Captain Spleen can jump over platforms and enemy attacks, as well as use various abilities to fight enemies. The game features a simple combat system where Captain Spleen can shoot or perform special moves to defeat foes. Gameplay Style: Platforming: Captain Spleen II is a traditional 2D platformer. Players must jump across platforms, avoid hazards like spikes and enemies, and navigate through varied levels. The game often involves collecting items and power-ups while avoiding or defeating enemies. Exploration and Puzzles: Players will explore different environments, with hidden paths and objects to find. Some levels also feature puzzles, where players need to interact with objects or use specific abilities to progress. Combat: As Captain Spleen moves through each level, he faces a variety of enemies, ranging from basic foes to larger bosses. Players must utilize attacks and strategies to defeat them. Levels and Environments: The game offers several levels, each with its own unique theme and challenges. Levels may include forest areas, caves, and futuristic environments. Some levels feature vertical scrolling, while others may be horizontally-scrolling, offering a variety of gameplay experiences. The game also includes hidden areas and collectibles to encourage exploration. Power-ups and Abilities: Captain Spleen can collect various power-ups and items that improve his abilities, such as increased health, stronger attacks, or temporary shields. As the game progresses, players may gain new abilities that help Captain Spleen navigate through more difficult levels and defeat tougher enemies.

name: Capture the Flag
description: This game was given several glowing reviews upon its initial release (1994/95) and its easy to see why. This shareware game has an interface that is very professionally done and rivals the commercial games of its time. The graphics are clean and functional, and overall the game is very well designed.Capture the Flag is a DOS game released in 1993. It is a simple, yet fun, multiplayer action game that takes inspiration from the classic "capture the flag" sport. In this game, players are divided into two teams, each aiming to capture the opponent's flag while protecting their own. The game is known for its simplicity and fast-paced action, which made it popular among fans of multiplayer games during the early 90s.Gameplay Mechanics: Objective: The primary objective of Capture the Flag is to capture the opposing team's flag while keeping your own flag safe. The game takes place on a large, open map where two teams compete against each other. Players must navigate through the environment, avoid or defeat enemies, and steal the flag from the other team's base. Controls: Keyboard: The game is controlled via the keyboard, where players use the arrow keys or WASD keys to move their character. Other keys are used for actions like shooting or picking up the flag. Multiplayer: The game can be played with two or more players. In a multiplayer mode, players can either play head-to-head on the same computer (with split-screen) or connect over a local area network (LAN) for more intense matches. Gameplay Style: Capture the Flag Gameplay: Players control characters on a top-down or isometric map and must move to the opponent’s base, grab their flag, and return it to their own base. Along the way, players can use weapons and traps to hinder opponents and defend their flag. Team-Based: The game is typically divided into two teams, with each team consisting of multiple players. While one team focuses on attacking and capturing the flag, the other team defends its base and attempts to stop the opposing players. Strategy: The game encourages teamwork and strategic planning. One player might act as a defender, while others are more focused on attacking the enemy and retrieving the flag. Good coordination between teammates is essential for success. Weapons and Items: Players can use various weapons, such as guns or other projectiles, to attack opponents. Some versions of the game might also allow the use of traps or other defensive mechanisms to block or slow down attackers. There may be power-ups or items scattered across the map, which can help players in their mission, such as health packs or speed boosts. Map Design: Arena-Style Levels: The levels in Capture the Flag are typically simple, symmetrical arenas where each team has a base. The map design is key to the gameplay, with obstacles, barriers, and other features that players can use to their advantage. Environmental Hazards: Some maps may feature environmental hazards that can damage players, such as water, pits, or traps that must be avoided. Multiplayer Mode: LAN Play: Capture the Flag was one of the earlier DOS games to feature LAN (Local Area Network) play, allowing players to connect their computers over a network for competitive matches. This multiplayer mode was a key part of the game’s popularity among friends and gaming groups during the early 90s. Split-Screen: For players on the same computer, the game offered a split-screen mode, allowing two players to compete against each other on the same system.

name: Captured by Pirates!
description: Captured by Pirates! is a strategy game where players (2-4, human or CPU controlled) compete to ... win the game? Get money? Destroy all your opponents? It never actually seems to tell you what the object is, but you'll need to strategically place your ships and buy weaponry, as well as look for buried treasure and hope that randomized events don't affect your fleet. Captured by Pirates! is a DOS action-adventure game released in 1992. The game was developed and published by Starlight Software. It is a pirate-themed game where players must navigate a series of dangerous challenges after being captured by pirates. The game blends elements of exploration, strategy, and action as players attempt to escape from the clutches of their pirate captors. Gameplay Mechanics: Objective: In Captured by Pirates!, players take on the role of a character who has been captured by pirates. The main goal is to escape captivity, outwit the pirates, and navigate through various islands and environments to recover treasures and ultimately find a way to escape. The game features different scenarios and challenges, and the player must use their wits, resources, and actions to overcome obstacles, defeat enemies, and find ways to move forward in the game. Controls: Keyboard: The game is controlled using the keyboard. The player moves their character through various environments, interacts with objects, and makes choices in dialogues and situations that affect the game’s outcome. The interface typically includes a command-line input for interaction, where the player types out actions, or selects options from a menu, depending on the version of the game. Gameplay Style: Adventure and Exploration: The game is mostly exploration-focused, with the player navigating through various locations, meeting characters, and solving puzzles. Each location presents different obstacles and challenges that require creative thinking. Combat: There are action elements, such as fighting off pirates or defending against dangers encountered along the way. The combat may involve simple attack commands or selecting the correct items to use in battle. Resource Management: The player must manage resources such as food, weapons, or tools to help in the escape attempt. These resources may be gathered or traded with other characters in the game. Decision-Making: The game’s progress can be influenced by the player’s choices in dialogues and actions, adding an element of strategy and replayability as different choices lead to different outcomes. Story and Progression: Pirate-Themed Narrative: The story revolves around the player’s capture by pirates and the effort to escape. Along the way, the player uncovers pirate treasure, secret maps, and hidden areas. Non-linear Progression: The game allows for some non-linear exploration, as there are multiple routes and ways to solve problems. Some tasks can be solved in different orders, and some puzzles or challenges have several possible solutions. Interactions with NPCs: The player will interact with various non-playable characters (NPCs), including fellow prisoners, pirates, and island inhabitants. These interactions are crucial for progressing through the game.

name: CAR
description: CAR is a generically-named and obscure sidescrolling / driving / shooting / autoscrolling game which is the author's first released software. (He was 14 when this was released.) So it's a little rough around the edges. There is story about your dog being kidnapped by a monster or something, but gameplay involves auto-scrolling from left to right in your super-powered car, blasting things and trying not to die. Action is a LITTLE frantic (that's an understatement) as things fly at you from everywhere.CAR is a DOS game released in 1994 that focuses on vehicular combat. It is a 2D arcade-style action game where players drive around various levels, typically fighting enemies, avoiding obstacles, and using weapons. The game has a simple premise but is quite fun and fast-paced, emphasizing action and speed rather than deep strategy or complex mechanics.

name: Car Park Sort
description: "Car Park Sort" is a fun and challenging puzzle game where players must sort cars by color in a parking lot. The goal is to rearrange the cars so that all cars of the same color are grouped together. The game requires strategic thinking and planning, as players must move cars around without getting stuck. Game Description: Objective: Sort the cars by color so that all cars of the same color are grouped together in the parking lot. Gameplay: The game presents a parking lot with cars of different colors parked in random order. Players can move cars forward or backward within their row, but they cannot move diagonally or jump over other cars. The challenge is to rearrange the cars with the fewest moves possible. Parking Lot Layout: The parking lot is typically a grid with multiple rows and columns. Cars can only move within their row, and players must plan their moves carefully to avoid blocking other cars. Difficulty Levels: The game includes multiple levels, with increasing complexity in the number of cars and colors. Later levels may introduce obstacles, such as blocked parking spots or limited moves. Special Features: Undo Move: Players can undo their last move if they make a mistake. Hint System: Players can use hints to get suggestions for the next move. Move Counter: The game tracks the number of moves, encouraging players to solve the puzzle efficiently.

name: Car Parking
description: Sokoban type of game. Move the crates to the indicated spots (P).Car Parking HTML refers to web-based versions of the classic car parking puzzle games that are playable in modern browsers. These HTML5-based games are designed to work on any device with a web browser (such as desktops, tablets, and smartphones), allowing players to enjoy the game without needing to install anything. Gameplay Mechanics: Objective: The core goal of Car Parking HTML games is to park a car in a specific parking space within a crowded parking lot. Players must maneuver the car by steering, moving forward, and reversing, all while avoiding obstacles like walls, other cars, and barriers. The challenge comes from the limited space and the need to plan movements carefully to avoid collisions and get the car to the right spot. Controls: Arrow Keys or WASD: Players usually control the car's movement using the arrow keys or the WASD keys. One key controls forward movement, while others control turning and reversing the car. In some versions, there may be touch-based controls for mobile devices, where players swipe or tap on the screen to move the car. Gameplay Style: Puzzle and Strategy: As a puzzle game, Car Parking HTML focuses on thinking ahead. Players need to plan their moves carefully, making sure to avoid obstacles and park the car in the designated spot. Limited Movement: Similar to traditional car parking games, players may only be able to move the car in certain directions depending on its surroundings, adding to the challenge. Time Challenges: Some versions may include a time limit, where players must park the car within a set period. Other versions may allow unlimited time but require more precise movements. Levels: Multiple Levels: Most Car Parking HTML games feature multiple levels, each with a more complicated parking layout or more obstacles. As players progress, the difficulty increases, and the puzzles become more intricate. Progression: The game may provide a "level up" system or unlock new cars or locations after successfully completing a certain number of levels. Graphics and Sound: Graphics: The visual style of Car Parking HTML games can vary, but they usually feature clear, simple 2D graphics with a top-down or isometric view of the parking lot. The car and obstacles are often represented in simple but recognizable shapes. Sound: Most HTML5 car parking games feature minimal sound effects, such as engine noises, collision sounds, or background music. The sound is typically non-intrusive, focusing more on the gameplay experience. Difficulty and Replayability: Increasing Difficulty: As players progress through the levels, the game typically becomes harder, with more cars and tighter spaces to navigate. Players must think ahead and manage their car's movements more strategically. Replayability: These games often have high replay value, as players can attempt to achieve the fastest time, complete all levels, or simply enjoy the satisfaction of solving each parking puzzle.

name: Car Parking 2
description: Sokoban type of game with 200 new levels. Move the crates to the indicated spots (P).Car Parking 2 HTML is a web-based puzzle game that is a sequel to the original Car Parking game. This version is typically available in HTML5, meaning it can be played directly in any modern web browser without needing any plugins or downloads. Car Parking 2 expands upon the original gameplay, offering new levels, more complex parking scenarios, and various challenges. Gameplay Mechanics: Objective: The goal of Car Parking 2 remains largely the same as its predecessor: park the car in a designated parking spot within a crowded parking lot, avoiding other cars, walls, and obstacles. The challenge increases with more complex layouts and additional cars or barriers in later levels, requiring strategic planning and precise driving to complete the puzzle. Controls: Keyboard: Arrow keys or WASD keys are used to control the car’s movement: up or W to move forward, down or S to reverse, and left and right to steer. Mouse or Touchscreen (for mobile versions): In some versions, players may use on-screen controls or swipe gestures to maneuver the car. The controls are simple, but the gameplay becomes progressively challenging as more obstacles are introduced. Gameplay Style: Puzzle and Strategy: Like the original game, Car Parking 2 requires careful planning. Players must figure out the correct sequence of movements to park the car without hitting anything or getting blocked by other vehicles. Limited Movement: The parking lot typically features narrow spaces, other cars, or barriers, limiting the player’s ability to move freely, which adds to the puzzle element. Time Limit: Some versions may have time challenges, where players must park the car within a set time limit, while others allow for unlimited time but with a focus on completing the puzzle with as few moves as possible. Levels: Multiple Levels: Car Parking 2 includes a variety of levels, each one presenting a different parking scenario. These levels gradually increase in difficulty as the player progresses. The levels start with simpler configurations, but later stages can feature a more complex arrangement of cars and obstacles that require careful planning and strategy. As the player advances, the parking spaces may become more narrow, more cars may block the way, and new obstacles (like barriers or walls) may be added to the layout.

name: Cardmania
description: Cardmania is a collection of two different games based on the popular Poker and Blackjack card games. The first (and the only one playable in this demo/shareware version) is Pokio, a Poker-like game where you draw cards one at a time and assign each to one of three Poker hands, which begin empty. The goal is to create scoring Poker hands in one or more of them. The other game looks similar to Blackjack, and similarly to Pokio it's sort of like playing several Blackjack hands at once. The game is presented well, with high attention to detail, like having multiple characters you can control, and also different dealers.

name: Cargo Bay
description: Cargo Bay is a Sokoban clone where the object is to push crates on top of transporters. It's jazzed up with a sci-fi theme and a storyline, including different aliens for each set of levels, but it plays the same as Sokoban in the end.Cargo Bay is a DOS game that was released in the early 1990s. It's a simple action-puzzle game that involves the player controlling a vehicle (often a cargo ship or space vehicle) to navigate through various levels, usually involving the delivery of cargo to different locations while avoiding obstacles. Gameplay Mechanics: Objective: The primary objective of Cargo Bay is to navigate a cargo vessel (usually a ship or spaceship) through levels while collecting and delivering cargo to designated locations. The player must avoid obstacles, enemies, and other environmental hazards while attempting to safely deliver goods to the correct destination. The game often requires time management, as some versions may have a time limit for completing levels or challenges related to cargo delivery. Controls: The controls typically involve moving the cargo vehicle up, down, left, or right using the arrow keys or other directional controls. The player must carefully navigate through narrow passages or dangerous areas while ensuring the cargo remains intact. In some versions, additional controls may allow the player to drop or release cargo at the correct locations. Gameplay Style: Puzzle and Action: The game combines action (navigating the vehicle) and puzzle elements (figuring out the best way to maneuver and deliver the cargo). Avoiding Obstacles: As the player progresses, levels introduce more complex layouts with increasing obstacles, such as moving walls, enemy ships, or space debris. Cargo Handling: The player must manage cargo carefully, avoiding damage while moving it through various environments, which often include confined spaces or areas with enemies.

name: Caribbean Slide
description: Enjoy a Caribbean Adventure in this Mahjong Game. Slide two of the same Mahjong tiles next to each other to make them dissappear. Remove all tiles to advance to the next level.Caribbean Slide is a fun and engaging HTML5 puzzle game that challenges players with sliding puzzles, often themed around the Caribbean or tropical islands. The goal is to slide and arrange pieces (or tiles) to form a complete image or path, relying on logic and spatial thinking. This game typically includes vibrant graphics, tropical music, and a relaxing atmosphere. Gameplay Mechanics: Objective: The primary goal in Caribbean Slide is to solve sliding puzzles. The player is presented with an image or path that is broken into several parts, which are shuffled. The player must slide the puzzle pieces around until the image or path is correctly arranged. Some versions of the game may feature specific challenges, like solving puzzles under a time limit or with a limited number of moves. Controls: Mouse/Touch Controls: Players typically slide pieces by clicking or tapping and dragging them to adjacent empty spaces. The game may allow sliding vertically or horizontally depending on the puzzle. In mobile versions, players usually swipe to move the pieces into position. Gameplay Style: Slide Puzzle: The core gameplay revolves around sliding tiles into the correct positions to solve the puzzle. The tiles may depict scenic images of tropical islands, beaches, or pirate themes. Increasing Complexity: As the game progresses, the puzzles often become more complicated, with more pieces and fewer empty spaces, making it harder to slide the pieces into place. Multiple Themes: Some versions of the game offer different themes, such as island landscapes, marine life, or Caribbean cities, adding visual variety. Levels: Multiple Levels: Caribbean Slide typically offers multiple levels, each one featuring a new puzzle with varying degrees of difficulty. In many versions, the difficulty increases as players progress, with puzzles becoming larger and more complex. Some versions may include time-based challenges or "moves allowed" limits, adding extra layers of difficulty.

name: Carnivorous Plant Hungry Escape
description: Carnivorous Plant: Hungry Escape is a quirky and entertaining flash game that combines puzzle-solving with action as you control a ravenous, sentient carnivorous plant trying to escape from a lab. Use the plant's unique abilities to outsmart scientists, bypass traps, and satisfy its hunger along the way. Gameplay: Objective: Guide the carnivorous plant through a series of levels, using its abilities to solve puzzles, avoid dangers, and devour enemies. The ultimate goal is to escape the lab while feeding on anything (or anyone!) in your path. Mechanics: Click and drag to control the plant's vines, allowing it to climb, swing, or grab objects. Use the environment creatively to unlock paths, neutralize threats, or set traps for unsuspecting humans. Features: Unique Plant Abilities: Vine Grab: Extend vines to grab items, climb walls, or pull levers. Predation: Lunge at enemies to eat them and gain energy. Stealth: Hide in shadows or vents to avoid detection by guards or scientists. Challenging Puzzles: Manipulate objects like crates, switches, and platforms to open doors or deactivate lasers. Solve timing-based puzzles to navigate past hazards like spinning saws or fire traps. Use physics to knock over structures or swing to unreachable areas. Enemies and Hazards: Scientists and Guards: Avoid or devour them before they sound alarms or attack. Traps: Dodge electrified floors, motion detectors, and flamethrowers. Level Progression: Levels increase in complexity, introducing new mechanics like acid pools, moving platforms, or enemy patrol patterns. Secret paths or collectibles may unlock bonus levels or alternate endings. Energy System: The plant's actions consume energy, which is replenished by eating prey. Players must balance energy use and strategic feeding to progress.

name: Carrom Pool
description: Disc Pool game against a computer opponent. Pocket all your discs in one of the four corners. If you pocked the red disc, you must pocked one of your discs in the next shot.Carrom Pool HTML is a popular and engaging online version of the classic board game Carrom, adapted for HTML5 browsers. This game combines elements of billiards and shuffleboard, where players use a striker to hit pieces (often called "coins") into the pockets on a square board. It’s a fun and competitive multiplayer game that can be enjoyed in both single-player and multiplayer modes. Gameplay Mechanics: Objective: The objective of Carrom Pool is to knock your colored coins (either black or white) into the pockets using a striker. Players take turns using the striker to hit the coins, aiming to sink them into one of the four pockets on the board. The player who sinks all of their coins first (either all black or all white) and then sinks the queen coin (usually the red coin) in a valid pocket wins the game. There may be different modes like "straight carom" or "pool carom," where rules slightly differ regarding the queen coin or how players can "cover" the queen. Controls: Mouse/Touch Controls: Players click or tap on the screen to aim the striker and then drag it back to set the power and direction of the shot. Striker Movement: The striker is moved around the board using the mouse or touchpad, and the player releases it to hit the coins. In mobile versions, touch controls are used to drag and aim the striker. Gameplay Style: Billiard-style Strategy: Like billiards or pool, the player must plan their shots carefully, considering angles and power to knock the coins into the pockets. Shooting Turns: Players take turns shooting the striker and aiming for the coins. If a player sinks a coin, they get another shot. If they fail, the opponent takes a turn. Queen Coin: In some versions, the red coin (queen) must be sunk after the player sinks all of their regular coins. The player must then "cover" the queen by sinking another coin immediately after. Multiplayer Modes: Many versions of Carrom Pool HTML feature a multiplayer mode where players can compete against friends or random opponents in real-time. Levels: Single-Player Mode: In this mode, the player competes against an AI opponent. The difficulty of the AI can vary, offering a casual or competitive challenge. Multiplayer Mode: In multiplayer mode, players can play online against friends or other players from around the world. This mode adds a competitive element, as players aim for high scores or win streaks. Tournament Mode: Some versions of Carrom Pool HTML feature tournament-style play, where players advance through a series of matches to win the championship.

name: Carser
description: Carser is a racing game that originated back in 1997 but was only fully completed by its developer in 2023. The game is inspired by the Micro Machines series, which features miniature vehicles racing on various dynamic tracks filled with obstacles. This combination of nostalgia and modern refinement makes Carser an exciting and engaging title for fans of both retro and contemporary racing games.Gameplay Mechanics: Objective: The core objective of Carser is to race miniature cars around tracks that are filled with various obstacles. The player must maneuver their car skillfully to avoid hazards, overtake rivals, and finish the race in the fastest time possible. Similar to Micro Machines, the tracks are designed with everyday environments like kitchen tables, garden paths, or other household settings, adding a fun, miniaturized twist to the gameplay. Controls: Arrow Keys / WASD: Players use the keyboard to control the car’s movement, steering left, right, accelerating, and braking. The game's simple controls make it easy for players of all ages to pick up, but the challenge comes in mastering the steering and timing as the tracks get more complex. Gameplay Style: Top-Down Racing: The game utilizes a top-down view of the racing environment, where players can see their miniature car and navigate through twists, turns, and obstacles. Obstacles: Players encounter various dynamic obstacles like ramps, oil spills, barriers, and other hazards that require quick reflexes and timing to avoid. Competitive Racing: In addition to avoiding obstacles, players often race against AI competitors, striving to complete the track as quickly as possible while staying ahead of their rivals. Levels: Multiple Tracks: The game features a variety of unique tracks, each set in different environments. Tracks may range from simple to highly complex, with increasing difficulty as the player progresses. Power-ups: Similar to other kart-style games, players might be able to collect power-ups or speed boosts on the track that help them gain an advantage over opponents. Graphics and Sound: Graphics: Carser boasts nicely done, colorful 2D graphics that capture the fun and chaotic feel of miniature vehicle racing. The environments are detailed with household or outdoor settings, and the cars are well-designed with bright, distinct colors. Sound: Complementing the visuals, the game features upbeat music, sound effects for crashes, engine noises, and even cheering from a virtual crowd in some versions. These soundscapes add to the immersive racing experience.

name: Cash Invaders
description: Cash Invaders is a really cool looking (and playing) Space Invaders variant, which includes 100 levels of shooting action. There are several improvements over the classic space game including raytraced graphics, weapon powerups that can be purchased, and tons of new enemies to battle. When shot, the enemies drop cash, hence the name "Cash Invaders". This game plays great and looks good too, recommended. Cash Invaders is a DOS-based game that blends the classic Space Invaders arcade style with a unique twist focused on money or cash. The game typically features the player defending their virtual money or assets from waves of enemies that try to steal or destroy them. Gameplay Mechanics: Objective: In Cash Invaders, the player must protect their cash, often depicted as dollar bills or treasure chests, from being stolen or destroyed by alien invaders or other types of enemies. The gameplay is inspired by Space Invaders, where waves of enemies descend from the top of the screen, and the player must shoot them down before they reach the bottom. Controls: Arrow Keys: Used to move your character or shooter left and right across the bottom of the screen. Spacebar: Fires projectiles at the incoming enemies. The player must time their shots carefully to eliminate the invaders before they reach the player's cash. Some versions may also include power-ups or upgrades that change the way the player shoots or defends their assets. The enemies usually come in patterns, and as the player progresses, these patterns may become more complex or difficult to avoid. name: Castle Adventure
description: This is a very old "graphic" adventure game which uses textmode / ASCII characters. Despite its simplicity, there is something charming about its gameplay, and it is nostalgically remembered by gamers who played it in the DOS era. Many adventure games back in 1985 were still text based, so having any kind of visual representation would no doubt be welcomed.Castle Adventure is a classic DOS-based action-adventure game released in the 1980s. It is a part of the early wave of PC games and showcases the simplicity and charm of that era's design. The game features exploration, puzzle-solving, and interaction with various enemies and objects in a castle setting. Gameplay Mechanics: Objective: The main objective of Castle Adventure is to explore a mysterious castle, solve puzzles, and collect treasures while avoiding or defeating enemies. The player must navigate through rooms and corridors of the castle, searching for keys and other items to unlock new areas. The ultimate goal is usually to find the exit or defeat a final boss or challenge to complete the game. Controls: Keyboard Controls: The game is controlled via the keyboard, with arrow keys typically used for movement. The player may need to press specific keys to interact with objects, open doors, or use items. Simple Commands: In some versions, players can type simple text commands to interact with the environment, such as "look" to examine objects or "take" to pick up items. Gameplay Style: Exploration: The castle is often designed as a maze or series of interconnected rooms, and players must explore each room to find valuable items or clues. Some areas are locked and require specific items or keys to access. Puzzle-Solving: The game includes puzzles that players must solve to progress. These puzzles might involve using items in creative ways or figuring out how to bypass locked doors. Combat: As the player moves through the castle, they may encounter enemies such as monsters or traps. Players must either avoid or defeat these threats to continue their exploration. Levels: Castle Rooms: The game is set within a multi-room castle, where each room presents different challenges or opportunities. Some rooms may contain treasures, while others could be traps or areas that advance the plot. Collectibles: Throughout the castle, players find items such as keys, potions, and weapons that aid in their quest. Some rooms may only be accessible with the correct key, and others may require solving environmental puzzles. Graphics and Sound: Graphics: Castle Adventure uses simple, pixelated graphics, typical of early DOS games. The game's rooms and corridors are depicted in basic 2D representations, often with minimal animation. Sound: The game features basic sound effects for actions like moving, collecting items, or interacting with enemies. Music, if present, would be minimal but might enhance the mood of certain moments. Difficulty and Replayability: Increasing Challenge: As the player progresses through the castle, the puzzles and enemies become more challenging. Players must carefully explore, manage their resources, and solve puzzles in a limited amount of time or moves. Replayability: The game is replayable because the puzzles and layout of the castle may be different each time, offering new challenges. Players can try different approaches or strategies in each playthrough.

name: Castle Mahjong
description: Build your Castle in this Mahjong Solitaire game. Combine 2 free of the same tiles to remove them and to collect building material.Castle Mahjong in HTML refers to a browser-based version of the traditional Mahjong Solitaire puzzle game, set within a castle theme. This adaptation retains the classic tile-matching mechanics of Mahjong but incorporates visually appealing backgrounds and themes that evoke a medieval castle atmosphere. Gameplay Mechanics: Objective: The goal of Castle Mahjong is to clear the board by matching pairs of tiles. The tiles are usually stacked in layers or arranged in a grid pattern, and the challenge is to remove all tiles by finding and matching identical pairs. Tiles must be free (i.e., not covered or blocked by other tiles) in order to be selected. Controls: Mouse: Players use the mouse to click on tiles. To make a match, click on two tiles with identical symbols. When a pair is matched, both tiles are removed from the board. Touchscreen (for mobile versions): Players can tap tiles on mobile devices to select and match them. Gameplay Style: Classic Mahjong Mechanics: Like traditional Mahjong Solitaire, the game is about finding pairs of matching tiles to remove them. The board consists of various layers or arrangements of tiles, and tiles are arranged with different Mahjong symbols. Castle Theme: The game features a visually rich environment with a castle theme. This includes medieval-style graphics such as castles, knights, dragons, and other related icons as part of the tile design or background. Challenging Layouts: As players progress through levels or stages, the layout of the tiles may become more complex, requiring careful planning and strategy to uncover matches. Tiles: Mahjong Symbols: The tiles in the game feature a variety of symbols, similar to traditional Mahjong sets, such as bamboo, characters, and circles, but may include thematic images tied to the castle theme (e.g., shields, swords, dragons). Special Tiles: Some versions of Castle Mahjong may include special tiles that either serve as wild cards or provide power-ups to assist in clearing the board.

name: Castle Mysteries

Click to find an object or differences.Castle Mysteries is an HTML-based game that typically combines elements of hidden object puzzles, adventure, and mystery-solving. The game is set in a castle environment, where players must explore rooms, find hidden items, and solve puzzles to uncover secrets or mysteries within the castle. Gameplay Mechanics: Objective: The primary goal in Castle Mysteries is to uncover the mystery by solving puzzles and finding hidden objects scattered throughout the castle. These hidden objects could be keys, clues, or other important items that help the player advance through the game. Players might also be tasked with interacting with characters or objects to unlock new areas or gain information that will help in solving the castle's mystery. Controls: Mouse: Players use the mouse to click on items and objects to interact with them. They may click on hidden objects to collect them or click on doors and items in the environment to explore or solve puzzles. As players progress, they uncover more clues, unlock new areas of the castle, and solve intricate puzzles. Players need to explore each room thoroughly to find hidden objects, interact with characters, and gather items to unlock the next part of the story. The player must clear each room to progress to the next area. Storyline: As the player advances, the story may unfold through dialogues, found letters, or journals. Players might need to piece together the story to solve the castle's mysteries and reach the final conclusion. Graphics and Sound: Graphics: Castle Mysteries features detailed and atmospheric artwork to create a mysterious and immersive castle environment. The rooms are often richly decorated with medieval or gothic-style furniture, architecture, and hidden objects. name: Castle Siege
description: Castle Siege is a turn-based strategy game with a fantasy theme. Two players (no CPU opponent available in the shareware version) face off, with one being the defender and the other being the attacker. The gameplay mechanics work similarly for both sides, but one begins with their king (the target to eliminate) inside a small castle and the other with more soldiers but all located outside the castle walls. Each turn you move your pieces and choose how/where they attack. I didn't play much but it seems like it could be fun for two players to compete against each other. There will be a bit of a learning curve, and the instructions are all provided via pages of text at the menu, no in-game or separate instruction file are given.

name: Castle Wars
description: In Castle Wars, the Flash game, cards play a central role in the strategic gameplay. Players use cards to summon units, cast spells, and perform various actions during the game. These cards are crucial for both offense and defense, and managing them efficiently is key to winning.1. Unit Cards: Unit cards represent various types of soldiers or creatures that you can summon to battle. These units often have different stats, such as attack power, health, and special abilities. Some unit cards might also have additional effects, such as causing debuffs to enemy units or defending your castle. Basic Units: These are low-cost cards that summon basic troops to attack or defend. Examples could include archers, swordsmen, or foot soldiers. Powerful Units: Higher-cost cards summon stronger creatures, such as knights, dragons, or other mythical beings. These units usually have high health or powerful attacks. 2. Spell Cards: Spell cards allow players to cast magical effects that can help in both offensive and defensive strategies. They can affect both your castle and the opponent's castle or units. Offensive Spells: These spells damage enemy units or their castle. Examples include fireballs, curses, or lightning bolts that can damage enemy health or weaken their defenses. Defensive Spells: Defensive spells protect your castle or boost your units. Spells like shields or healing potions could prevent damage or restore health to your units or castle. Utility Spells: Some spells affect the game environment in other ways, such as allowing you to draw extra cards or manipulate resources (like gold or mana). 3. Resource Cards: These cards grant you resources, usually gold or mana, which are used to play other cards. Effective resource management is crucial because it ensures that you can deploy powerful units or cast impactful spells during the game. Gold Cards: Increase your gold, enabling you to play more powerful cards. Mana Cards: Increase your mana, which might be required for casting specific spells. 4. Building Cards: Building cards are used to create structures that protect your castle or give you an advantage in the game. Walls: Walls can help protect your castle from enemy attacks, blocking direct damage. Towers: Towers may be used to attack enemy units or add additional defense to your castle. 5. Special Cards: Some cards have unique effects that aren't necessarily part of the other categories. These cards are usually game-changers and can alter the course of a match if played at the right time. Destructive Cards: Cards like "Earthquake" or "Tornado" might destroy a portion of the opponent’s defense or wipe out their units in a single turn. Special Effects: Some cards could trigger random events, such as drawing extra cards, giving extra resources, or even taking control of an enemy unit for a limited time.

name: Castles II: Siege & Conquest
description: Castles II is a real-time strategy game which it set in the middle ages. You choose one of the five feuding lords, all of whom are vying against each other for the crown. You'll need to build your castle and engage in diplomacy and aggression against your enemies in order to earn enough game points to petition the Pope for the throne.Castles II: Siege & Conquest is a classic real-time strategy (RTS) and simulation game released in 1995, developed by InterActive Vision and published by Electronic Arts. It is the sequel to the original Castles game and continues the theme of medieval castle-building and warfare. Players take on the role of a ruler during the Middle Ages, tasked with building a strong kingdom, managing resources, and leading armies to conquer other castles. Gameplay Description: In Castles II: Siege & Conquest, the player is tasked with managing a medieval kingdom and engaging in warfare to expand their territory. The game is divided into two main components: castle construction and management, and siege warfare. Players must strike a balance between building a powerful, defensible castle and managing their army and resources efficiently. Key Gameplay Features: Castle Construction & Management: Players begin by constructing their castle, which serves as the foundation of their kingdom. You can design and fortify the castle with walls, towers, and gates to defend against enemy sieges. The interior of the castle also needs to be managed, with decisions on the allocation of resources such as food, labor, and materials. You can also recruit knights, archers, and other units to defend your castle and bolster your army. Siege Warfare: The siege aspect of the game is critical to success. Players must prepare for attacks on their castle and, when the time is right, launch sieges against enemy castles. The game includes a variety of siege weapons, such as catapults, trebuchets, and battering rams. You can use these weapons to breach enemy defenses and attack key points of their castle. Attacking castles is a strategic affair, as players need to plan their moves carefully to break through the enemy's defenses while minimizing their own losses. A combination of tactics like feigned retreats, siege weapon placement, and even diplomacy plays a crucial role in successful sieging. Diplomacy & Management: Besides military conquest, diplomacy is also an important factor in expanding your kingdom. You can forge alliances with neighboring kingdoms or engage in trade. Managing your kingdom's economy and resources is essential for maintaining a strong defense and offense. Players must deal with the day-to-day management of their lands, including farming, taxes, and trade routes. Loyalty and morale also play significant roles in how your kingdom operates. Keeping your vassals and subjects content is key to ensuring the stability of your rule.

name: Castles in Spain
description: Castles in Spain is a captivating and strategic solitaire card game that challenges players to build foundations from Ace to King while managing the tableau with careful planning and foresight. The game combines elements of traditional solitaire with unique rules that require players to build down in alternating colors on the tableau, adding an extra layer of complexity and engagement. Gameplay Overview: Objective: The primary goal is to move all the cards to the foundation piles, starting with Ace and building up to King in each suit (hearts, diamonds, clubs, and spades). Tableau Setup: The game begins with a tableau of several piles of face-up cards. The exact number of piles can vary, but typically, there are seven or eight piles. The top card of each pile is available for play. Building on the Tableau: On the tableau, players must build down in alternating colors. For example, a red 7 (hearts or diamonds) can be placed on a black 8 (clubs or spades), and vice versa. This requires careful planning and strategy to ensure that cards can be moved to the foundations without blocking potential moves. Foundations: The foundation piles are built starting with Ace and ascending to King, following the order: Ace, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, Jack, Queen, King. Each foundation pile corresponds to one of the four suits. Stock and Waste: If the game includes a stock pile, players can draw cards from the stock and place them in a waste pile. The top card of the waste pile is available for play on either the tableau or the foundations. Empty Tableau Piles: If a tableau pile is emptied, it can usually be filled with a King or a sequence starting with a King, depending on the specific rules of the game. Strategy and Planning: Success in Castles in Spain requires careful planning and foresight. Players must balance moving cards to the foundations with maintaining a flexible tableau that allows for future moves. Blocking cards or creating deadlocks can quickly end the game, so strategic thinking is essential. Winning the Game: The game is won when all cards have been successfully moved to the foundation piles in the correct order from Ace to King for each suit. Key Features: Alternating Colors: Building down on the tableau in alternating colors adds a strategic layer to the game. Foundation Building: Moving cards to the foundation piles from Ace to King is the primary objective. Tableau Management: Careful management of the tableau is crucial to avoid blocking potential moves. Stock and Waste: Utilizing the stock and waste piles effectively can provide additional opportunities to move cards. Strategic Depth: The game requires planning and foresight, making it a mentally stimulating and rewarding experience.

name: Castles of Mew
description: Castles of Mew is an unconventional and quirky game created in QuickBasic by a relatively new programmer. While it may not be considered a "good" game by traditional standards, it has a certain charm and curiosity factor that makes it an interesting piece of gaming history. The game is notable for its unskippable PC speaker music on the title screen, among other quirks and issues. For those interested in early programming efforts and experimental game design, Castles of Mew offers a unique glimpse into the creativity and challenges of a novice developer. Key Features (or Quirks): Unskippable PC Speaker Music: The title screen features music played through the PC speaker, which cannot be skipped, adding to the game's eccentricity. Experimental Design: As the work of a new programmer, the game reflects the learning process and creative experimentation of its creator. Unique Concept: Despite its flaws, the game has a distinctive concept and style that sets it apart from more polished titles. Navigate the Game: Use the controls to explore the game's world, which may involve simple puzzles, exploration, or other mechanics. Experience the Quirks: Encounter the various oddities and design choices that make the game unique. Appreciate the Effort: Recognize the creativity and effort of a new programmer learning the ropes of game development.

name: Cat&Mse
description: Cat&Mse is a quirky and fun DOS game that takes inspiration from the classic puzzle game Rodent's Revenge, which was part of the Microsoft Entertainment Pack 2 for Windows 3.1. In Cat&Mse, you play as a mouse trying to outsmart cats by pushing blocks to trap them and turn them into cheese. With its unique charm, customizable features, and a variety of levels, Cat&Mse is a delightful addition to the puzzle game genre. Here’s a closer look at what makes this game special: Gameplay Overview: The gameplay in Cat&Mse is simple yet challenging, requiring strategic thinking and quick reflexes: Objective: You control a mouse that must trap cats by pushing blocks onto them. Once trapped, the cats turn into cheese, which you can collect for points. Be careful, though—the cats will chase you, and if they catch you, it’s game over! Block Pushing: You can push blocks horizontally or vertically to create barriers or trap cats. Plan your moves carefully, as pushing a block into the wrong position can leave you trapped or make it easier for the cats to catch you. Levels: The game includes a variety of levels, each with a different layout and increasing difficulty. As you progress, the levels become more complex, requiring more strategic thinking and precise movements. Customization: Cat&Mse allows you to edit the colors and sprites used in the game, adding a layer of personalization for players who enjoy tinkering with game assets.

name: Catacomb
description: Catacomb is a classic 2D action-maze game that marks the early beginnings of the Catacomb series, created by the founders of id Software (John Carmack, John Romero, and Tom Hall) during their time at Softdisk. This game laid the groundwork for the series' eventual transition into 3D, much like how Wolfenstein evolved from 2D to 3D. It’s a fascinating piece of gaming history, showcasing the roots of some of the industry’s most influential developers. The gameplay is reminiscent of Gauntlet, with players navigating through maze-like levels, battling enemies, and collecting treasure. You control a wizard who can shoot magical projectiles at enemies, clear obstacles, and explore the sparse, dungeon-like environments. The levels are relatively simple and less cluttered compared to Gauntlet, focusing more on straightforward action and exploration rather than intricate puzzles or dense layouts. Key features of Catacomb include: Top-down perspective: The game uses a 2D top-down view, typical of early action-maze games. Magic-based combat: Instead of traditional weapons, your character uses magical attacks to defeat enemies. Sparse level design: The levels are more open and less detailed compared to similar games of the era, emphasizing exploration and combat. Retro charm: The graphics and sound are simple but effective, capturing the essence of early PC gaming.

name: Catch 'Em
description: Catch 'Em is a fun and straightforward DOS game that serves as a slightly upgraded homage to the classic Atari 2600 title Kaboom!. The gameplay is nearly identical: you control a paddle at the bottom of the screen and must catch falling objects while avoiding misses. However, instead of bombs, you’re catching animals like dogs and cats, adding a quirky and lighthearted twist to the formula. Later levels introduce "stoppers," which add a bit of variety to the challenge. The controls are simple and effective, using the mouse to move the paddle, which works reasonably well for this type of fast-paced action. The visuals are basic but reminiscent of the retro aesthetic of Kaboom!, making it a nostalgic experience for fans of the original. While the game doesn’t introduce many new features or complexities, it captures the essence of what made Kaboom! so addictive. If you’re a fan of Kaboom! or enjoy fast-paced, reflex-testing games, Catch 'Em is worth a try. It’s a faithful and slightly modernized take on a classic, offering a quick and entertaining experience. Even if you’ve never played Kaboom!, this game is a great way to experience its timeless gameplay in a new, animal-filled package.

name: Catch if you Can
description: The game is sort of like a Pong type game mixed in with a baseball type theme. Sounds weird? Well, it is ... but it's fun to play, despite its simple premise. Basically, all you do is catch baseballs. In practice, this works like a slightly enhanced version of the old Kaboom! game on Atari 2600.Catch If You Can is a classic DOS-based arcade game released in the early 1990s. It is a simple yet engaging action game that focuses on quick reflexes and hand-eye coordination. The gameplay revolves around catching falling objects, with the difficulty increasing as the game progresses. The core of Catch If You Can is based on catching falling objects using a moving character (usually represented as a basket or a similar object). The player must move the basket left and right to catch the falling items. If a player misses an item, they lose points or face a penalty. Objective: The primary objective is to catch as many objects as possible within a time limit or until a certain number of missed objects accumulate. The items can vary in nature (e.g., fruits, balls, or other themed objects), and some might be worth more points than others. As the game progresses, the objects fall faster, making it harder to catch them, thus increasing the game's difficulty. Controls: Keyboard: The player uses the arrow keys to move the basket or catcher left and right along the bottom of the screen. Mouse (if applicable): In some versions, the mouse could also be used to move the catcher.

name: Catch Simona in New York City
description: Ever wanted to play a shameless shareware knockoff of Where in the World is Carmen Sandiego? If so, you're a bit of a strange duck. Also, Catch Simona in New York City may be right up your alley! Just like the game it's copying, your goal here is to catch a criminal by traveling around and collecting clues before getting a warrant and arresting the bad guy/girl. As the name suggests, the game takes place entirely in New York. The graphics are decent, obviously derivative of the game it's cloning right down to the typewriter in the lower corner.

name: Catch the Kreis
description: Catch the Kreis is a simple game where the object is to move around your 'X' to catch the 'O' (a "Kreis", or circle). There are a bunch of maps to choose from, and three difficulty levels. The O just tries to flee in the opposite direction, so it'll take some trial and error to figure out how to catch it on each stage. Overall it's not a particularly fun or good-looking game but it's certainly unique. (Press Esc to skip the long intro sequence ...)Catch the Kreis is a simple action-based game released for DOS. It revolves around the player catching or interacting with objects (referred to as "Kreis," which is the German word for "circle" or "ring") that appear on the screen. The game likely focuses on quick reflexes and hand-eye coordination, and similar to other games from the era, it features straightforward mechanics designed for short, engaging play sessions.

name: Catch the Thief
description: Catch all the Thieves by freezing them. Use the on-screen controls or the arrow keys and space bar.Catch the Thief is a simple, fun, and engaging HTML-based game that typically revolves around the player catching or preventing a thief from escaping or completing their task. The game is often designed with basic mechanics, focusing on quick reflexes, timing, and attention to detail. Gameplay Overview: In Catch the Thief, the player’s primary objective is to catch a thief who is either trying to escape or performing some form of sneaky activity. The thief might be represented as a character or an object that moves around the screen, and the player must react quickly to stop them before they get away. Objective: The player must catch the thief or stop their escape by performing specific actions, such as clicking on them, trapping them, or completing a mini-game that involves finding the thief. The game may be time-based, where the player has to catch the thief before time runs out or within a certain number of attempts. Controls: Mouse: Typically, players click on objects, the thief, or locations to catch the thief or stop them from escaping. Keyboard: Some versions might involve using the keyboard to move a character or interact with the game elements.

name: Cats 1010
description: 1010 game with cats. Drag and rotate shapes and reach the indicated goal.Cats 1010 is a puzzle game that can be played in HTML5, offering a fun and relaxing experience, often designed for casual gamers who enjoy block-based puzzles. It's inspired by the popular "1010!" puzzle game, with the twist of featuring cute cat-themed elements. The objective and mechanics are similar to games like Tetris, but with its own unique flavor. Gameplay Overview: In Cats 1010, the player’s objective is to place blocks onto a grid and fill entire lines (either horizontal or vertical) to clear them. The game uses a Tetris-like mechanic, but with a twist: the blocks in Cats 1010 are shaped like cute cats or themed around cats, making it visually unique. Objective: The primary goal is to clear lines on a 10x10 grid by placing various shapes (cat blocks) that are randomly given to the player. The player must fill in rows or columns completely with these blocks to clear them and earn points. The game ends when the grid is full and there are no more room for additional blocks. Controls: Mouse: Players can drag and drop the cat-shaped blocks onto the grid to place them in various positions. Touch (if on mobile): The player taps to drag and place blocks on the grid. Game Features: Simple, Addictive Gameplay: The mechanics are easy to understand: place blocks to fill up rows or columns, and clear them for points. The challenge arises from fitting the given blocks into the grid without leaving gaps, which requires strategic thinking. Cute Cat-Themed Blocks: The most notable feature of Cats 1010 is the cat theme. The blocks are designed with fun, colorful cat faces or cat shapes, making the game feel more lighthearted and fun. This visual theme appeals to cat lovers and adds an extra layer of charm to the game. Increasing Challenge: As the player progresses, the game gets harder by offering more complex cat-shaped blocks and fewer available spaces on the grid. The puzzle aspect lies in efficiently filling the grid without overfilling it, which could cause the game to end prematurely. Scoring System: Players earn points by clearing lines (both horizontally and vertically) as they place the blocks. The more lines cleared at once, the higher the points. There might be a combo system or bonuses for clearing multiple lines in one move, encouraging strategic play.

name: Causality
description: Causality is a flash-based puzzle game that revolves around a time-travel mechanic, where players manipulate events to create specific outcomes. The objective is to interact with characters and objects in a way that causes a chain of events, ultimately leading to a desired result. The game is based on the concept of cause and effect, where each action you take in the game triggers consequences that affect the game's storyline or level progression. Objective: The main objective in Causality is to manipulate events by clicking on characters, objects, or environmental elements at the right time and in the right sequence to trigger specific outcomes. Players need to solve puzzles by causing the right events to happen, which might involve tricking characters into interacting with each other, using objects creatively, or figuring out the best way to make everything fall into place. Controls: Mouse: Click and drag objects or characters to interact with them. Timing and the order in which you interact with them are crucial to solving the puzzles. Some puzzles require you to control the environment or move objects around in a specific sequence to cause the right chain of events.

name: Cave Speed
description: Cave Speed is a text-mode falling-down-a-well type game, similar to Deep II, Pitfall (no, not THAT Pitfall) and Jellyfish. This game has a Star Wars vibe, with a long and pointless introduction story about flying your Y-Wing into an asteroid or something. There are apparently multiple levels, but the gameplay is quite boring. As you speed through the cave (asteroid?) you need to collect fuel (brown smilies) to keep going, collect other things for points, and avoid walls. I think there are supposed to be enemies that attack you, but I guess I didn't make it far enough to encounter any.

name: Cavern of the Evil Wizard
description: If you've ever seen the Tom Hanks movie Big (1988) you'll probably remember a PC graphical adventure game that is shown briefly. It's identified as "Cavern of the Evil Wizard", but to the disappointment of many fans of the movie, it was just made up for the movie; it didn't actually exist. Now a developer has made his own interpretation of the game, based on the screens seen in the movie. It keeps the same CGA graphic aesthetic and text-based input.Cavern of the Evil Wizard is a classic action-adventure game for DOS, known for its dungeon-crawling elements, puzzle-solving mechanics, and combat encounters. In this game, players explore an underground labyrinth filled with traps, enemies, and treasure, with the ultimate goal of confronting and defeating the evil wizard lurking at the heart of the dungeon.

name: Caverns of Xaskazien
description: Caverns of Xaskazien may have been more popular, had its name been easier to remember/spell! (I still haven't got it down even after researching for this game posting!) It's a turn-based Roguelike game with randomized dungeons where the goal is to defeat the evil Xaskazien. Although it shares many traits with other Roguelikes, it also has its own unique feel, in part due to its visual look, and in part due to gameplay mechanics.Caverns of Xaskazien is a classic DOS action-adventure game from the early 1990s. Known for its combination of dungeon crawling, exploration, combat, and puzzle-solving mechanics, it immerses players in a fantasy world filled with dangerous creatures, hidden treasures, and challenging mazes. Objective: The game focuses on exploring the mysterious and dangerous caverns of Xaskazien, where players must complete quests, fight enemies, and collect items. Players must solve puzzles, defeat monsters, and uncover the caverns' mysteries, aiming to reach the final confrontation or objective in the game. Controls: Keyboard: Movement is controlled via the keyboard (typically arrow keys or WASD), with various keys used for actions like attacking, using items, or interacting with objects. Mouse (if supported): In some versions, the mouse could be used for item selection or navigating menus.

name: Caverns of Zoarre
description: Caverns of Zoarre could be called a graphical RPG, but just barely. The game, originally designed for the TRS-80, owes a lot of inspiration to one of the first graphical RPGS, Telengard. After creating a character you begin to explore the randomly-generated dungeon and encounter randomly-generated characters, most of which will kill you.Caverns of Zoarre is a classic roguelike game for DOS, developed in the early 1980s. It is inspired by Rogue and other early dungeon-crawling games, delivering a procedurally generated adventure filled with challenges, monsters, and treasures. Its minimalist design and ASCII graphics make it a quintessential experience for fans of traditional roguelikes.Gameplay Overview: In Caverns of Zoarre, players descend into a series of procedurally generated dungeon levels, battling monsters, collecting loot, and surviving traps. The game emphasizes strategy, resource management, and exploration. Its permadeath mechanic adds tension, as every decision can be the difference between success and failure. Objective: The goal is to explore the dungeon, gather treasure, and ultimately escape alive. Players must navigate increasingly dangerous levels, finding powerful weapons and magical items while avoiding or defeating enemies. Controls: Keyboard-only interface: The game is entirely text-based, using ASCII characters for visual elements. Players control their character with the keyboard, issuing commands for movement, combat, and item interaction.

name: Caves of Thor
description: Caves of Thor is an extremely interesting and oddly playable ASCII game released early in Apogee's existance, shortly after the Kroz series of games. Programmed by Todd Replogle (who later went on to be lead programmer on all of the Duke Nukem games), Caves was Apogee's first game release that was coded by an outside author.
