name: Death Rally
description: Top-down racing games are sort of a sub-genre of the larger racing genre, and Death Rally is a good example of how to do things right. Sort of like Super Sprint with more destruction. The graphics are great, as are the sounds, and the gameplay involves picking up or buying cool weapons to destroy the other cars in the races (hence the name).Death Rally is a DOS-based arcade-style racing game developed by Remedy Entertainment and released in 1996. The game is a top-down, action-packed racing game where players compete in violent races across various tracks, using weapons to sabotage opponents and secure victory. It is widely recognized for its fast-paced gameplay, intense combat, and upgradable vehicles, making it a classic in the arcade racing genre. The game blends elements of racing, vehicular combat, and strategy into a highly enjoyable experience. Top-Down Racing Combat: Perspective: The game uses a top-down view (Bird’s-eye view), where the player sees the action from above. This perspective allows players to navigate tight corners and strategize while engaging in combat. Combat Racing: Unlike traditional racing games, Death Rally integrates combat directly into the racing gameplay. Players can pick up various weapons during the race, such as machine guns, missiles, and mines, which they can use to destroy or disable other racers. 2. Vehicles and Weaponry: Car Selection: Players start with a basic car but can purchase and upgrade vehicles using the money earned from winning races. Weapons: Each car can be outfitted with weapons like machine guns, oil slicks, rockets, and mines. Players can collect power-ups during the race to help them in combat, or purchase these weapons for their vehicles before races. Vehicle Upgrades: The player can upgrade the car’s speed, handling, armor, and weaponry, allowing for better chances in combat and races as they progress. 3. Races and Tracks: Race Types: The game features a series of races in different environments. The races are not just about finishing first; survival is just as important, as opponents will try to shoot you off the track. Track Variety: The game includes various tracks, each with its own challenges. Some tracks feature tight corners, while others have large stretches where you can speed up, but risk encountering more traps and weapons. Environment Hazards: In addition to combat with other players, some tracks include hazards such as oil slicks, potholes, or barriers, making it more challenging for players to navigate. 4. Career Mode and Progression: Winning Races: As players win races, they advance through different levels, unlocking tougher opponents and more dangerous tracks. The career mode involves improving your car and reputation to face tougher enemies. Boss Races: After certain events, players might face boss races, where defeating the boss unlocks new features, weapons, or cars. Money and Rewards: Winning races earns players money which they can use to buy new cars, upgrade weapons, or repair damage done during races. 5. AI and Difficulty: Challenging AI: The opponents are aggressive and intelligent, making it difficult to win races. They will use weapons strategically and try to knock the player off the track at every opportunity. Difficulty Progression: As the player advances through the game, the AI racers become faster, more aggressive, and better equipped with weapons, raising the difficulty of the game.

name: Death Worm
description: Death Worm is a fun and addictive HTML5-based game where you control a giant, underground worm that emerges to devour everything in its path. The game is a retro-styled arcade action game with simple mechanics but increasingly challenging gameplay. Players guide the worm through various levels, consuming animals, humans, and objects, while avoiding obstacles and staying alive. The player controls a giant underground worm that bursts through the surface to wreak havoc. The goal is to consume as many things as possible, including animals, humans, and objects, while avoiding obstacles and staying alive. As the worm grows, it becomes more powerful, but enemies and challenges also become harder. Gameplay Features: 1. Simple Controls: Arrow Keys/Mouse: The worm is controlled by either the arrow keys or mouse, depending on the platform. The worm burrows underground and can surface to grab objects. Movement: The worm moves left, right, and up to pop out of the ground to eat, while also avoiding being hit by obstacles or enemies. Attacking: The player can devour objects (humans, cars, and animals), and, in some levels, fight off other creatures or enemies. 2. Devouring Gameplay: Eat to Grow: The worm can consume a variety of targets, such as humans, cars, trucks, and even military tanks, with each meal making the worm grow in size. Combo Bonuses: Players can earn combo points by quickly devouring multiple objects in succession, leading to higher scores. 3. Obstacles and Enemies: Obstacles: As the worm eats and grows, obstacles such as mines, enemy creatures, and explosives will try to stop the worm. Avoiding these obstacles is critical to staying alive. Enemies: Other enemies, such as military vehicles and helicopters, will actively try to stop the worm with weapons. These enemies add more challenge as the player progresses through levels. 4. Power-ups: Speed Boosts: The game features power-ups such as speed boosts that help the worm move faster or gain a temporary invincibility. Extra Health: Some levels offer health power-ups to keep the worm alive longer. Bombs and Weapons: In later stages, the worm can pick up special weapons to help destroy enemies or larger obstacles. 5. Level Progression: Increasing Difficulty: The game features several levels, each with progressively more challenging environments, faster enemies, and more obstacles. As the worm grows, it faces tougher and more frequent challenges. Varied Environments: The game offers different stages, including urban settings (cities, highways), nature areas (forests), and military bases, each with unique enemies and obstacles. 6. Objectives and Scoring: High Scores: Players earn points by consuming targets. The more things the worm eats, the higher the score. Objectives: In some levels, there are specific objectives (like eating a set number of objects or surviving for a certain period) that add variety to the gameplay.

name: Deathball Incarnate
description: Deathball Incarnate is an interesting action / platforming / puzzle game where the object is to use your "deathball" to steal the souls from the humans that populate the levels. First you need to run them over before they escape, which can prove tricky. There are switches and other obstacles that you'll need to navigate as well. The graphics are decent and the game plays fairly smoothly, although the key choices are a bit strange, see the Instructions section or in-game help. The game is certainly unique and seems to include a variety of levels. It also includes a two-player mode, where the second player takes control of one of the humans!

name: Deck of Cards Mahjong
description: Play Mahjong with Cards. Combine two of the same free tiles and try to remove all tiles.Deck of Cards Mahjong is a HTML5-based variation of the classic Mahjong Solitaire game, combining the traditional tile-matching gameplay of Mahjong with a deck of playing cards. This game typically features 52 playing cards, with a twist on the classic Mahjong rules, where the goal is to match and remove pairs of cards instead of tiles. Key Features: Tile Pair Matching: The game’s goal is to match pairs of cards that are identical in value. For example, two King of Hearts or two 10 of Spades. To make a match, the cards must be uncovered, meaning there should be no cards on top or to the side. Card Layout: The cards are typically arranged in a pyramid, grid, or stacked pattern. Cards that are exposed and on the top layer can be selected for pairing. Moves and Strategy: Players must strategically uncover cards by selecting exposed pairs that match. No random shuffling: Once the cards are placed on the board, players must carefully think ahead to make sure that they can uncover all the pairs without getting stuck. Winning: The game is won when the player has successfully matched and removed all 52 cards from the board. There are no new cards to replace those that are removed. Some versions feature a timer, adding pressure to complete the puzzle within a set amount of time.

name: Dedale
description: The most simplistic maze game you're likely to find. The object is to guide your player to the exit of randomly generated mazes. That's it, no fancy powerups, enemies, etc. Just basic graphics and PC speaker sound effects. Nothing special or exiciting but it does work, the executable file is only 29k in size, and might be appropriate for young children.Dedale is a classic DOS-based maze exploration game released in 1993, developed by Philippe Thibault. It is a puzzle and strategy game where players navigate through 3D mazes, encountering various challenges and trying to solve the maze while collecting objects and avoiding dangers. Key Features: 3D Maze Exploration: Dedale is known for its 3D maze design. The game uses basic pseudo-3D graphics that create a labyrinth with walls, doors, and pathways. The player controls a character and must explore, navigate, and manipulate the environment to solve puzzles and progress. Puzzle Solving: As you explore the maze, you’ll encounter puzzles or challenges that must be solved to proceed. These might include unlocking doors, finding hidden objects, or activating mechanisms. The game features a variety of puzzle types that require logic and spatial reasoning. Collecting Items: Throughout the maze, you will encounter items that can be collected. Some of these items are necessary for solving puzzles or accessing new parts of the maze. Players will need to carefully manage the items they pick up, as they may be needed to progress further or unlock new areas. Obstacles and Hazards: The maze is filled with obstacles such as locked doors, traps, or enemies that must be avoided. Some parts of the maze may feature dangerous elements that the player needs to avoid or disable. Progression: The player must navigate through increasingly complex mazes, gradually opening up more areas and uncovering hidden secrets. As you progress, the mazes become more difficult, introducing new types of puzzles and challenges.

name: Deep Dive
description: Dive as long and deep as possible. Collect coins and air bubbles.Deep Dive is an HTML5-based game that typically involves exploring the depths of the ocean, where players take on the role of a deep-sea diver or submarine. The game often focuses on discovering underwater treasures, surviving against oceanic threats, and completing objectives while managing resources like air supply or fuel. Exploration: The player dives into the ocean, navigating through different layers of the sea. Each level or stage can have distinct environments, such as coral reefs, shipwrecks, caves, or abyssal depths. The game may feature randomly generated underwater maps or fixed-level designs that require players to explore and locate hidden treasures, objects, or artifacts. Resource Management: In many versions of Deep Dive, players must keep track of their air supply or fuel levels. This adds a layer of strategy since players must decide how deep they can go before needing to surface or find air refills. Collecting oxygen tanks or other resources might be required to extend dive time or avoid running out of air. Treasure Hunting: The game often incorporates elements of treasure hunting or scavenging. Players search for valuable items like sunken treasure, jewels, or ancient artifacts. Some versions may feature a storyline where the player seeks to find a legendary treasure or uncover secrets hidden at the bottom of the sea. Challenges and Obstacles: Underwater environments are filled with obstacles, including dangerous marine life, such as sharks or giant squids, and natural hazards like underwater currents or rock formations. Some levels introduce environmental challenges such as low visibility, debris, or enemy submarines. Upgrades and Power-ups: Players may be able to upgrade their diver's equipment, like diving suits, submersibles, or radar systems to assist with exploration and survival. In some versions, players can collect power-ups that enhance abilities like speed, scanning range, or defensive capabilities. Progression and Difficulty: As the game progresses, the ocean depths become more challenging with deeper dives, more aggressive threats, and scarcer resources. New underwater environments, more difficult puzzles, and harder-to-reach treasures may become available as the player advances.

name: Deep II: The Center of the Earth
description: Deep II is a "falling down a pit" (pitfall) type game. The object is to maneuver around the obstacles while collecting bonus items. There is a little strategy involved since you can use the money you collect to buy items occasionally. Simple but colorful ASCII graphics and PC speaker "blips & bleeps" sound round out the game. Might be fun for those who enjoy text-mode games.Deep II: The Center of the Earth is a DOS-based adventure game, released in 1993. The game is a puzzle and adventure title that revolves around exploring the center of the Earth. It follows the player’s journey as they descend into the Earth’s depths, uncovering mysteries, solving puzzles, and surviving various challenges. Exploration of Underground Caverns: The player will journey through a variety of underground environments, such as caves, tunnels, and strange caverns that are located at the Earth's core. The environments are filled with hidden paths, secrets, and obstacles that must be discovered through exploration. Puzzle Solving: As with many adventure games of the time, Deep II is heavily focused on solving puzzles. Players must figure out how to progress through various obstacles, decipher codes, activate mechanisms, and manipulate the environment. Some puzzles may involve mechanical devices, hidden keys, or unlocking doors using clues found throughout the levels. Survival Elements: The journey to the Earth’s center is perilous, and players must manage resources such as oxygen, fuel, and health. Players are forced to make decisions on how to conserve their limited resources while exploring the depths. Storyline: The game has a central narrative focused on reaching the center of the Earth. Along the way, players may encounter various characters, clues, and artifacts that explain the backstory and unravel the mysteries of the journey. The story is told through in-game dialogues, text descriptions, and visuals that immerse players in the adventure. Atmosphere and Exploration: Deep II places a significant emphasis on creating an immersive atmosphere. Players will encounter eerie, dark environments that heighten the sense of mystery and danger. The game uses 2D graphics to depict the underground landscapes, with detailed backdrops and objects to explore, offering a visually captivating experience for the time. Character and Inventory Management: The player controls a character who interacts with the environment and other characters in the game. The player will manage an inventory system to store useful items such as tools, equipment, or other objects required to solve puzzles or survive.

name: Deep Sea Jewels
description: Collapse game: click on groups of 3 or more connected jewels to remove those jewels.Deep Sea Jewels is a casual HTML5-based puzzle game that involves matching jewels or gems in a deep-sea-themed environment. Players match similar jewels in order to clear levels, earning points and progressing through various challenges and increasingly difficult stages. Matching Jewels: The core mechanic involves matching 3 or more jewels of the same type (color or shape) in a horizontal or vertical row. When a match is made, the jewels disappear, and the player earns points. New jewels then fall into place to potentially create new matches. Underwater Theme: The game is set in a deep-sea environment, often featuring colorful and sparkly jewels, fish, sea creatures, and aquatic backdrops. The underwater theme provides a relaxing and visually appealing setting for the match-3 gameplay. Levels and Challenges: As players progress through the game, they are introduced to new levels with increasing difficulty. New obstacles, challenges, or goals may be introduced, such as limited moves, special gems, or needing to clear certain items from the board. Power-ups and Boosters: Special jewels or power-ups may appear in the game, allowing the player to create bigger explosions or clear more jewels in one move. These might include bomb jewels, colorful gems, or wildcards that help complete the objectives faster. Progression: Players can progress through a series of levels or stages, with the difficulty gradually increasing as the game goes on. Some versions feature a level map or stage system, where players unlock new areas as they complete levels. Time Limits or Moves: Some versions of the game include time-limited challenges where the player must clear the board or achieve certain goals within a set amount of time. Alternatively, other versions may have a limited number of moves to clear all objectives, adding a layer of strategy to the game. Visual Effects: When matches are made, colorful explosions or sparkle effects may play, adding to the excitement of clearing jewels and completing levels.

name: Deep Sea Trijong
description: Mahjong Solitaire game with Triangular tiles. Remove tiles in pairs.Deep Sea Trijong is an HTML5-based Mahjong puzzle game that blends the classic game of Mahjong with a deep-sea theme. Players are tasked with clearing the board by matching Mahjong tiles that are visible, while navigating through a underwater-themed environment filled with sea creatures and vibrant colors. Mahjong Tile Matching: The core mechanic of Deep Sea Trijong is matching tiles that are identical in design. Players must match sets of three identical tiles to clear them from the board. As with traditional Mahjong, the tiles are arranged in layers, and only exposed tiles can be selected for matching. Underwater Theme: The game is set in a deep-sea environment, with tiles featuring aquatic designs such as fish, shells, coral, and other underwater symbols. The background and ambient sounds enhance the relaxing and calming atmosphere, immersing players in a tranquil ocean world. Tile Layout: The tiles are arranged in different layouts, often featuring pyramid, stack, or grid-style formations, which vary in difficulty as the game progresses. The goal is to clear all the tiles from the board by finding matches of three and removing them systematically. Levels and Progression: Players progress through levels, with each new level introducing more complex tile layouts, potentially more layers, and requiring more strategic thinking. The game often gets progressively more difficult as the player advances, with fewer exposed tiles available for matching. Special Tiles and Power-ups: Some versions of the game may feature special tiles that can help players clear more tiles or provide bonuses, such as a wildcard tile that matches any tile or a tile-clearing power-up. Occasionally, hint buttons or shuffle options may be provided to help when the player is stuck. Time Limits or Moves: Some versions may introduce a time limit, requiring players to clear the board within a certain number of seconds. Others may have a limited number of moves to clear all the tiles, which adds an extra layer of challenge. Visual and Audio Effects: When matches are made, there may be sparkle effects, tile explosions, or bubbles popping up to indicate a successful match. Underwater sounds, such as bubbling water and gentle waves, complement the soothing aesthetic. Relaxing background music often plays to enhance the immersive, peaceful experience of the game.

name: DEFCON 1
description: DEFCON 1 is a competent Missile Command clone. This one involves the "evil" Switzerland trying to take over the world. (Of course ...) You use your mouse to destroy oncoming ballistic missiles as they rapidly approach cities at the bottom of the screen. Unlike Missile Command, your shots explode instantly, so this makes it much easier to play.DEFCON 1 is a DOS-based real-time strategy game released in 1994. It is set during the Cold War and revolves around the tension between two superpowers on the brink of global annihilation. Players take control of a nation's military forces as they navigate through various geopolitical and military challenges, ultimately trying to survive in a world where nuclear war looms. The game was known for its strategy and diplomatic gameplay, offering a deep and intense experience for players interested in global warfare and Cold War themes. Real-time Strategy: The game is played in real-time, meaning that players must make decisions quickly, considering military deployments, diplomacy, and the threat of nuclear war. The player controls a superpower and is responsible for managing military forces, defensive systems, diplomatic relations, and nuclear weapons. Military Units and Strategic Decisions: Players must control various types of military units, such as aircraft, submarines, land forces, and nuclear missiles. Each unit has specific advantages and weaknesses, and players must use them strategically to either defend their country or eliminate their enemies. Diplomatic Interactions: As the game progresses, players can engage in diplomatic negotiations with other nations, either forming alliances or escalating conflicts. Diplomatic choices have a direct impact on the strategy, as betrayal or negotiation can shift the balance of power in the game. Nuclear Warfare: Central to the game is the ability to launch nuclear strikes, leading to the possibility of global annihilation. The player must balance the threat of nuclear escalation with the need to maintain military dominance. A player can launch nuclear missiles, but doing so risks triggering a full-scale nuclear war that will devastate the planet. Resource Management: Players must manage their military resources, ensuring that enough units and weapons are available to carry out their strategies. Economic and supply chains also play a key role, as military units need to be resupplied to stay effective. Multiple Campaigns and Scenarios: The game includes several pre-designed scenarios that simulate different stages or situations in the Cold War, each with unique objectives and challenges. DEFCON 1 allows for custom campaigns, where players can design their own conflict scenarios or adjust the global situation to suit their strategy. Realistic Cold War Setting: The game offers a realistic Cold War backdrop, with references to actual historical events and the technological limitations of the time period. Political tension, nuclear arms races, and global alliances play out within the scope of the game's setting, adding an element of authenticity.

name: Defender
description: Defender is a clone of ... Defender. If you've never played the classic arcade game, it's a horizontal shooter where you must eliminate all of the aliens before they abduct all the humans. This version controls fairly well and captures the look and feel of the original game quite nicely. There's the minimap which shows the locations of the aliens and humans, and the satisfaction of blowing up your enemies and seeing them explode in a cloud of pixels. I'm not sure how many levels you get in the shareware version but what's here is pretty good.

name: Defender of Boston: The Rock Island Mystery
description: Defender of Boston: The Rock Island Mystery is a first-person perspective graphical adventure game. You play as a 1920's detective who is tasked with solving a mystery and recovering a rare and dangerous artifact. Most of the game is controlled using the mouse, using icons to interact with the scene. Sometimes other options pop up as you explore. Before beginning the game you must assign stats to your character like an RPG, and there are a lot of categories and a lot of stats to assign. Combat occurs in real-time. Definitely a unique and interesting game with its own quirky engine.

name: Deflector
description: Deflector is a difficult two-player battle game where you must hit each-other with lasers. However this is not primarily an action game. Your tank fires its laser across the playing field, and you'll need to strategically turn mirrors to make it bounce around and eventually hit your opponent. You'll still need to move fast, because the laser fires automatically every few seconds, and so you'll need to make your moves quickly, especially if your opponent is trying to turn the same mirrors as you! There are also other hazards on the field.

name: Delicious Duos
description: Delicious Duos is a delightful and strategic puzzle game where the goal is to connect pairs of identical food items on a grid. The challenge lies in creating a connecting path between the items without changing direction more than twice. With its vibrant visuals, engaging gameplay, and food-themed fun, it’s a perfect game for puzzle enthusiasts and food lovers alike. How to Play Delicious Duos: Objective: Connect pairs of identical food items on the grid. The connecting path cannot change direction more than twice. Gameplay: The grid is filled with various food items, such as fruits, vegetables, desserts, and more. Click on one food item and drag to create a path to its matching pair. The path can move horizontally or vertically but cannot change direction more than twice. Rules: Only identical food items can be connected. The path must be continuous and cannot overlap itself. The path cannot change direction more than twice (e.g., right → down → right is allowed, but right → down → right → down is not). Levels: The game features multiple levels, each with increasing difficulty. As you progress, the grid becomes larger, and the number of food items increases. Scoring: Points are awarded for each successful connection. Bonus points may be given for completing levels quickly or with fewer moves. Key Features of Delicious Duos: Food Theme: Vibrant and appetizing visuals featuring a variety of food items. Strategic Gameplay: Requires planning and foresight to create valid paths. Progressive Difficulty: Starts easy but becomes more complex as you advance. Relaxing Yet Engaging: Perfect for casual play while still offering a mental challenge.

name: Deluxe Ski Jump
description: Deluxe Ski Jump is a great ski jump simulation game. The game's sequels are still continuing to this day, ie Deluxe Ski Jump 4 on the author's website. The original DOS version of the game isn't in 3D like the modern versions but it's still fun and well done, albeit simple since you're doing basically the same thing every time.Deluxe Ski Jump is a popular DOS-based ski jumping simulation game that was first released in 1999. It quickly gained a cult following due to its simple but addictive gameplay and realistic physics, offering players the opportunity to experience the thrill of ski jumping in a highly engaging way. Realistic Ski Jumping Mechanics: The game focuses on a realistic physics engine that simulates the physics of ski jumping. Players must time their jump correctly when reaching the takeoff ramp and control their skier's flight and landing by adjusting posture mid-air. The flight distance and jump score are determined by the combination of speed, angle of launch, and the accuracy of landing. Simple Controls: The controls are straightforward: use the up arrow key to speed up and down arrow to slow down as the skier moves down the ramp. Just before takeoff, the player presses the space bar to jump, and during the jump, they can adjust their posture using the arrow keys to influence their flight path. The key to success is mastering the timing of each phase of the jump, from the ramp approach to the landing. Multiple Hill Sizes: The game features different ski jump hills, including small, medium, and large hills with varying levels of difficulty. Larger hills require more precise control and a better understanding of the physics to maximize jump distances. Scoring System: The game uses a scoring system based on how far the player jumps and the quality of their landing. Players earn points for their jump distance, but they can lose points if their landing is poor (e.g., landing too hard, falling, or tipping over). Players compete for the best score in each event and can work towards higher rankings in tournaments. Tournament and Event Mode: The game features tournament modes where players can compete in a series of events, progressing through different ski hills and earning points. Players can also practice individual jumps to improve their skills or compete against AI-controlled opponents in single-player mode. Multiplayer Mode: While the game is primarily a single-player experience, it also includes a local multiplayer mode, allowing friends to take turns competing against each other for the best jumps. Customization and Progression: Players can select different ski jumpers (with varying skill levels) and compete in different tournaments. As players improve, they can unlock more advanced ski jumpers and more difficult events.

name: Demon
description: Demon (or possibly Demon 2, the executable is called DEMON2.EXE) is a variation of a Hunt the Wumpus type game. You explore a grid-based maze, moving from room to room, with hints about what is in the current room and what's nearby. I think it's meant to be somewhat suspenseful since you never know when the demon will appear? It's decent enough I suppose if you're looking for a textmode game in this style.Demon is a DOS-based action-adventure game released in 1991. It was developed by Ocean Software and is known for its dark, atmospheric setting and action-packed gameplay. The game is set in a gothic, demon-infested world, where players must navigate a series of levels filled with challenging enemies, puzzles, and dangerous obstacles.

name: Denarius Avaricius Sextus
description: Denarius Avaricius Sextus is a relatively unknown graphic adventure game along the lines of King's Quest or Secret of Monkey Island. Perhaps it's unknown due to its complicated name? Anyways, this adventure takes place in ancient Rome, in fact the documentation states that it's "the shareware world's first (as far as we know) graphical interactive adventure game about a Roman citizen with red hair".Denarius Avaricius Sextus is a DOS-based strategy game released in 1991. It is a turn-based game that is set in ancient Rome, where players take on the role of a character named Sextus, seeking to amass wealth and power through trade, economy, and political maneuvering in the Roman Empire. Economic Management: A central focus of the game is managing the economy of Sextus' family. Players need to control finances, purchase goods, trade them, and make investments in order to build a strong fortune. Trade routes, marketplaces, and taxation play key roles in increasing your wealth. Social and Political Strategy: The game emphasizes the importance of social status and political influence. Sextus must make decisions regarding alliances, political favors, and maintaining a strong reputation in Roman society. Players must balance gaining wealth and power while avoiding political enemies and threats from rivals. Turn-Based Gameplay: The game is played over multiple turns, with each turn requiring the player to make a series of decisions about their strategy for the day. As the game progresses, players can expand their wealth and influence, engage in public affairs, or sabotage their rivals. Roman Economy and Trade: Players must manage a network of goods, including agricultural products, luxury items, and military supplies. The goal is to use these resources to gain both wealth and power, managing their markets and trade routes effectively. The economy is volatile, meaning that market shifts and political instability can impact a player's assets. Character Development: The protagonist, Sextus, can develop skills in areas like politics, trade, and leadership, which affect the player’s ability to manage situations and make effective decisions in the game. Roman Culture and Events: The game also incorporates various elements of Roman culture, such as festivals, public games, and religious ceremonies, all of which can influence the economy and society. Events like the Senate elections, military conflicts, and other political decisions shape the environment and create challenges for the player.

name: DentureMan
description: DentureMan is a strange clone/reworking of the classic Pacman dot-eating game. The playing field scrolls as you (disembodied teeth) proceed to eat all of the dots (toothpaste?) and avoid the ... uh, things. There are three different levels you can play in the shareware version, and while DentureMan offers decent (yet weird) graphics it doesn't really improve the basic Pacman formula.DentureMan is a DOS-based action-adventure game released in 1991. It is a quirky and somewhat obscure title, blending elements of platforming, action, and comedic storytelling. The game follows the main character, DentureMan, as he embarks on a strange journey. The game is notable for its humorous premise and eccentric design, making it a unique entry in the DOS gaming library. Unique Main Character - DentureMan: The player controls DentureMan, a character with dentures as a central feature of his design. His unusual design and role make the game stand out from other action-adventure titles. The premise is quirky: DentureMan must tackle a series of obstacles, fighting enemies and interacting with the environment. Platforming Challenges: The game features side-scrolling platforming mechanics, where players must guide DentureMan through various levels filled with platforms, hazards, and enemies. The platforming sections include jumping, dodging obstacles, and collecting items to progress. Combat Mechanics: Players will engage in combat against a variety of enemies, with basic attack mechanics that involve hitting enemies or avoiding attacks while navigating the environment. The action is relatively simple, using basic jump and attack commands, but it requires precise timing to avoid hazards and defeat enemies. Puzzle Elements: As players progress through the levels, they encounter puzzles that must be solved to continue. These puzzles could involve interacting with objects, finding keys to unlock doors, or solving simple logic challenges. Humorous and Eccentric Themes: The game is designed with a humorous tone, with odd characters and situations that add to the comedic atmosphere. The story and dialogue often feature quirky humor that adds to the lighthearted nature of the game. The unusual character design and premise make DentureMan stand out as a silly, yet fun title.

name: Depth Dwellers - The Quest
description: Depth Dwellers is a relatively unknown early 3D shooting game that was probably the victim of bad timing: It was released only a few months after DOOM. The game engine developed by TriSoft is somewhere inbetween Wolfenstein 3D and DOOM in terms of features and abilities. The game itself is fairly generic, with not a lot of unique features, and only passable graphics for a 3D game.Depth Dwellers - The Quest is a DOS-based role-playing game (RPG) released in 1991. The game combines elements of adventure, exploration, and combat in a dark, fantasy-themed world. Players venture through underground caverns, battling enemies, solving puzzles, and uncovering the mysteries of the dungeon in a quest for treasure and survival. Dungeon Crawling: The game is centered around exploring a series of underground caverns filled with monsters, traps, and puzzles. The environment is dark and eerie, requiring players to be cautious and strategic in their movements. The layout of the dungeons is grid-based, with each level presenting new challenges as players delve deeper into the complex. Party-Based Gameplay: Players control a party of adventurers, each with their own abilities, equipment, and stats. The player must manage the strengths and weaknesses of the group, making decisions about how to approach enemies, navigate obstacles, and solve puzzles. The party can consist of different classes or character types, each contributing unique skills to the overall success of the quest. Combat: The combat in Depth Dwellers is turn-based, with players choosing commands for each character in their party. Battles are fought against monsters, including a variety of enemies that inhabit the dungeon. Weapons, magic, and special abilities play a key role in defeating enemies. Players need to be strategic in managing their resources, such as health, magic points, and consumable items. Exploration and Puzzle-Solving: Exploration is a central aspect of the game, with hidden rooms, secret passages, and locked doors to discover. Players must solve puzzles to unlock new areas and progress through the dungeon. Environmental obstacles, such as traps and locked gates, require problem-solving skills and the use of items found throughout the dungeon. Character Progression: Throughout the game, characters level up, gaining new abilities and increasing their stats. This progression is important to overcoming increasingly difficult enemies and dungeon challenges. Players can also find and equip better gear such as weapons, armor, and magical items that enhance the party's strength and capabilities. Atmospheric Setting: The game takes place in a dark, mysterious world, with an emphasis on gothic and fantasy themes. The underground setting features caves, dungeons, and labyrinths that are filled with dangerous creatures, treasures, and mystical artifacts. Ambient sounds and low-resolution graphics contribute to the game’s immersive atmosphere, evoking the sense of being in a dangerous and foreboding environment.

name: Descent
description: Descent was quite popular on its release. It expanded on the 3D shooting genre by giving players a real 3D environment unlike Doom or Duke Nukem 3D. In this 7-level DEMO version of Descent you must pilot your spaceship through many 3D levels destroying various bad guys along the way.Descent is a groundbreaking first-person shooter (FPS) released in 1995 for DOS. It was developed by Parallax Software and is notable for its 3D, six-degrees-of-freedom (6DOF) gameplay, which set it apart from other FPS titles at the time. Instead of the traditional ground-based movement, Descent allows players to move in all directions within a fully three-dimensional environment, offering a truly immersive and dynamic experience. Six-Degrees-of-Freedom (6DOF) Movement: Unlike traditional FPS games that are confined to two dimensions (up, down, left, right), Descent allows full 3D movement. Players can move up, down, forward, backward, and rotate in all directions. This added freedom of movement was revolutionary for the genre and set Descent apart from other FPS titles of its time. Maze-Like Levels: The game is set in complex, multi-level underground mines or industrial complexes. Each level is filled with narrow corridors, large open areas, traps, and puzzles that require the player to carefully navigate and explore. Levels are interconnected, and players can access different floors and rooms by moving vertically within the environment. This exploration aspect was one of the defining features of Descent. Combat: Players pilot a spaceship, equipped with various weapons, to fight off hostile robots and other enemies. The combat is fast-paced, and players can use weapons like lasers, missiles, and fireball blasts to destroy enemies. The AI-controlled enemies are scattered throughout the levels, and many are equipped with advanced weaponry, creating a challenging environment for the player. Objectives: The main objective of each level is typically to destroy all enemies and complete specific missions like disabling power generators or rescuing hostages. Many levels feature multi-stage objectives that require players to solve puzzles or find hidden paths to progress. Multiplayer Mode: Descent also features multiplayer modes, where players could compete against each other in split-screen or through modem/Internet play. The multiplayer aspect allowed for deathmatch-style combat, adding another layer of excitement and replayability to the game. Atmospheric Sound and Music: The game uses 3D sound to create a tense, immersive atmosphere. Players can hear enemies approaching or shots echoing through the mines, adding to the overall experience. The background music is composed of atmospheric, electronic tracks that help enhance the mood of the various levels.

name: Descent II
description: The sequel to the awesome original Descent game, this game picks up right where the first left off. You again fly your ship with full range of movement around the many mine shafts destroying enemy robots. There are of course new enemies to fight and new features like the Guide-bot.Descent II is the direct sequel to the groundbreaking Descent game, released in 1996 for DOS. Developed by Parallax Software, Descent II expands upon the innovative features of the original game, offering enhanced gameplay, new weapons, more complex environments, and a deeper storyline. It built on the success of its predecessor, further refining the six-degrees-of-freedom (6DOF) gameplay and establishing itself as a classic in the first-person shooter (FPS) genre. Expanded Six-Degrees-of-Freedom (6DOF) Movement: Like its predecessor, Descent II supports 6DOF gameplay, allowing players to move freely in all directions (up, down, left, right, forward, and backward). The free movement system is enhanced with new abilities, including the ability to roll and strafe more efficiently, providing greater control over your spacecraft in tight, high-speed battles. New Weapons and Power-ups: Descent II introduces new weapons such as the Proximity Bomb, Fusion Cannon, and Gauss Cannon, expanding the player's arsenal. Power-ups are more varied, including shields, weapon upgrades, and speed boosts, adding more tactical options during combat and exploration. Improved Graphics and Environments: The graphics were improved from the original Descent, featuring more detailed textures, enhanced lighting effects, and more complex level design. Levels are designed with varied environments, including industrial complexes, underground bases, and even outer space stations, each with unique hazards, enemies, and objectives. Enhanced atmosphere: The environments are more immersive, with atmospheric sound effects and detailed 3D worlds, contributing to the game's tension and excitement. Multiplayer Mode: Descent II features enhanced multiplayer support, allowing players to compete against each other in deathmatch or cooperative modes, either over a LAN or through a modem. The multiplayer mode is a significant improvement over the original, supporting team-based play, where players can work together to complete objectives or face off in intense combat. Objectives and Missions: Descent II continues with the core idea of completing various missions within complex, multi-level structures. The missions are divided into objective-based levels, requiring players to destroy key targets, rescue hostages, disable power generators, and explore hazardous environments. Each level contains hidden secrets, such as power-ups or hidden doors, rewarding players who thoroughly explore each area. AI and Enemies: The game features a variety of robotic enemies, each with different attack patterns, weaknesses, and strengths. The AI is more sophisticated than in the original game, with enemies capable of working together and responding to the player’s actions in more dynamic ways. New enemy types and mini-bosses appear throughout the game, making combat more intense and challenging.

name: Desert Storm Command
description: Desert Storm Command is actually like two different games in one. Or maybe one game with two different modes. You are tasked with protecting your comrade troops, first by shooting enemy soldiers in windows, then by shooting down enemy missiles and planes "Missile Command"-style.Desert Storm Command is a real-time strategy (RTS) game released in 1992 for MS-DOS. Developed by Calhoun Enterprises, the game was inspired by the events of the Gulf War (Operation Desert Storm), which took place in the early 1990s. Players assume the role of a military commander, tasked with managing and controlling forces during the conflict, and the game is centered around strategic planning, resource management, and tactical warfare. Real-Time Strategy Gameplay: The game is played in real-time, meaning that both the player and the computer-controlled forces make decisions simultaneously. Players must think quickly and decisively, managing military units while simultaneously reacting to enemy actions. Strategic elements include the placement of troops, coordination of attacks, and defending key locations while advancing toward victory. Military Units: The game features a variety of military units, including tanks, helicopters, infantry, and artillery. Each unit has its strengths, weaknesses, and abilities, and players must utilize them effectively to achieve their goals. Units can be controlled individually or in groups, and players can direct them to attack, defend, or patrol various areas of the battlefield. Resource Management: As in many real-time strategy games, resource management plays a crucial role. Players must gather and manage supplies, equipment, and troops, ensuring that their forces remain operational and well-equipped to handle enemy threats. Players also need to be mindful of fuel, ammunition, and other logistical factors that influence the performance of their military units. Combat and Tactics: Players must engage in combat against enemy forces, which require strategic thinking. Flanking enemies, coordinating airstrikes, and timing attacks are all critical for success. The game emphasizes tactical positioning, with terrain such as hills, deserts, and urban environments affecting how battles unfold. Mission Objectives: The game offers various missions inspired by real-life events during the Gulf War. Players may be tasked with capturing key locations, destroying enemy units, or defending strategic points from enemy advances. Missions are typically time-sensitive, adding a sense of urgency to the player's decisions. Multiplayer Mode: In addition to the single-player campaign, Desert Storm Command features a multiplayer mode where two players can compete against each other in tactical warfare. This mode adds another layer of depth, as players need to adapt their strategies based on human opponents.

name: Desktop Tower Defense
description: "Desktop Tower Defense" is a classic flash game where players strategically place towers on a grid to stop waves of incoming enemies. The objective is to prevent the enemies from reaching the end of the path by building and upgrading various types of towers, each with unique abilities and strengths. Players earn money by defeating enemies, which they can use to build more towers or upgrade existing ones. The game features different maps and increasing difficulty levels, making strategy and resource management crucial for success. If you’re looking for tips or strategies for the game, feel free to ask!

name: Destroy Spongebob
description: Destroy Spongebob is a humorous and action-packed Flash game that allows players to engage in over-the-top antics involving the beloved cartoon character, SpongeBob SquarePants. The game is designed for fans looking for a light-hearted, albeit mischievous, experience. Game Overview: Objective: Players aim to "destroy" SpongeBob by utilizing various tools and weapons, all while navigating through different levels filled with obstacles and challenges. Gameplay Mechanics: Variety of Weapons: Players can choose from a range of quirky weapons and tools to target SpongeBob, including explosives, projectiles, and more absurd items that add to the fun. Level Progression: The game features multiple levels, each with unique layouts and challenges that require different strategies to complete. Targeting Mechanics: Players must aim and time their attacks to hit SpongeBob while avoiding obstacles and environmental hazards. Features: Colorful Graphics: The game features vibrant, cartoonish graphics that capture the playful spirit of the original show. Silly Sound Effects: Fun sound effects accompany actions, enhancing the humorous tone of the game. Replayability: Players can try different strategies and weapons to see how quickly they can complete levels, adding a layer of challenge. Visuals and Sound: Destroy Spongebob has a whimsical art style, with bright colors and engaging animations that bring the cartoon world to life. The soundtrack includes catchy, upbeat music that complements the gameplay. Destroy Spongebob is enjoyed for its light-hearted fun and comedic premise, making it a popular choice for casual gamers looking to indulge in some silly antics with a beloved character.

name: Destruction Derby
description: Destruction Derby is an exhilarating DOS-based racing game that focuses on the thrill of demolition derby events. Players compete in destructive races where the goal is not only to finish first but also to cause maximum damage to opponents’ vehicles. Game Overview: Objective: Players aim to win races by either finishing in the top position or by smashing opponents’ cars to earn points. Gameplay Mechanics: Variety of Modes: The game features multiple modes, including traditional races and demolition derbies, where the main focus is on destroying rival cars. Car Customization: Players can choose from a range of vehicles, each with different attributes, and can often customize them for improved performance. Destructive Gameplay: Players earn points by colliding with and damaging other cars, creating an exhilarating and chaotic racing experience. Features: Dynamic Environments: Tracks are set in various locations, each with unique layouts and obstacles that add to the challenge. Realistic Physics: The game incorporates realistic car physics, making collisions and damage feel authentic and impactful. Multiplayer Mode: Players can compete against friends or AI opponents, enhancing the competitive nature of the game. Visuals and Sound: Destruction Derby features early 3D graphics that capture the excitement of demolition racing. The sound design includes engine roars, crashes, and a lively soundtrack that adds to the adrenaline of the gameplay. Destruction Derby is well-regarded for its engaging mechanics and chaotic fun, making it a classic choice for fans of racing and destruction-based games.

name: Destruction Zone
description: Destruction Zone is a game for 1-6 players (3 of those can be humans) where the goal is to eliminate the other tanks. The game looks and plays like a programming game, like Core War or C-Robots, since you can choose from one of several different computer AIs to fight against.Destruction Zone is a DOS-based action game released in 1995. It was developed by Mecc (the same company behind Carmen Sandiego and other educational titles) but with a focus on arcade-style gameplay. The game blends elements of action, puzzle, and strategy as the player navigates an environmental hazard zone filled with obstacles and enemies. Environmental Hazard Zones: The game takes place in destruction zones filled with obstacles such as toxic sludge, explosive devices, moving traps, and hostile enemies. Players must navigate these dangerous areas to reach specific objectives, all while managing limited resources like energy and time. Puzzle Elements: The game contains various puzzle-like challenges that players must solve to progress. These puzzles often involve activating switches, avoiding traps, or finding keys to unlock certain areas. The puzzles become increasingly complex as the game advances. Combat and Enemies: While the primary focus is on navigating hazards, Destruction Zone also includes combat elements. Players will face off against robotic enemies and other hostile forces throughout the levels. These enemies require both strategic thinking and quick reflexes to defeat or evade. Combat involves using laser weapons and other tools that are either found or earned as the game progresses. Limited Resources: Players must manage resources such as energy, ammo, and health. Running out of energy or taking too much damage can result in a mission failure or the need to restart the level. Mission-based Structure: Each level of Destruction Zone presents players with a new mission, typically involving objectives such as disabling a bomb, rescuing trapped characters, or collecting specific items within a set time limit. Some missions require a specific set of skills or tools, making it necessary for the player to adapt their approach in order to succeed. Multiple Levels: The game features a series of increasingly difficult levels set within destruction zones. Each level introduces new obstacles, traps, and enemies, requiring players to use their skills and resource management abilities to progress.

name: Detective Agency
description: Detective Agency is a memorization test / training game where you are presented with a face or a scene and you must memorize as much information as possible in a short period of time. Then you are quizzed to see how much you remember. The time given is short, and the number and intricacy of details you're asked to recall is high, so it can be quite challenging, even on "novice" skill level. There is a practice mode which can help get you used to how the game works.Detective Agency is a point-and-click adventure game that was released in 1992 for MS-DOS. It is a classic mystery-solving game that blends detective work with elements of puzzle-solving and story-driven gameplay. Players take on the role of a private investigator working to solve various cases involving different criminal activities, with each case requiring keen observation, deduction, and analysis. Case-Based Gameplay: The game is divided into different cases that the player needs to solve, each with a unique mystery to uncover. Players begin by receiving a case file and must visit different locations, talk to suspects, and search for clues. Each case involves a combination of investigation, interviews, and forensic analysis. Players must analyze the evidence they gather to draw conclusions about what happened. Point-and-Click Mechanics: The game uses a point-and-click interface, typical of adventure games from the early 90s. Players click on objects, people, and locations to interact with them. The interface is intuitive, allowing players to easily navigate through the game’s environment and manage their inventory of items. Clue Gathering and Analysis: Players will collect clues, such as witness statements, physical evidence, and forensic reports. These clues need to be combined and analyzed in order to make sense of the case. Some cases require the player to analyze suspects' behavior, compare witness statements, and test different theories. Dialogue and Interrogation: A key aspect of the game is the ability to interrogate suspects and witnesses. Players can ask questions to gather more information or uncover inconsistencies in the statements of the characters. Interrogation sessions allow players to ask specific questions based on the clues they’ve found, helping to steer the investigation forward. Inventory and Items: As players explore the world, they will find and collect items that may assist in solving the case. This includes items such as tools, documents, and evidence that may be essential to advancing the story. The inventory system allows players to use and combine items to solve puzzles or unlock new areas to investigate. Multiple Cases and Difficulty: The game includes multiple cases, and each one becomes progressively more challenging. As players solve each case, they will encounter more complex mysteries, requiring greater attention to detail and more careful deduction. Detective Agency presents a variety of cases involving different types of crimes, such as thefts, disappearances, and murders, each with its own set of clues and suspects.

name: Deux Trois Quatre
description: DTQ (or Deux Trois Quatre as it says on the title screen and nowhere else) is a match-two game where you flip over cards, two at a time, and try to remember where the matches are. Except here there are no cards, just empty spaces and a cursor that you move around, which feels a bit weird. Other than that, it's a pretty standard matching game, although each game will use an assortment of random clipart images.Deux Trois Quatre is a DOS-based puzzle game released in 1991. It is a number puzzle game that involves solving mathematical challenges using a grid of numbers. The game combines elements of logic, pattern recognition, and basic math skills, aimed at providing a mental workout for players. Number Grid Puzzles: The main gameplay revolves around working with grids of numbers, where players must manipulate the grid by performing arithmetic operations to reveal the solution or reach a target. Players need to find relationships between numbers, perform calculations, and identify patterns within the grid to progress. Basic Mathematical Operations: Players can use addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division to work through the puzzle and manipulate the grid of numbers. The game is designed to encourage players to think critically about mathematical relationships and use logic to complete the puzzles. Increasing Complexity: As the player progresses through the game, the puzzles become more complex and require more advanced number manipulation. Higher levels introduce more numbers in the grid, making the challenge more difficult. Time Challenges: Some puzzles may be timed, requiring players to solve them within a certain period. This adds an element of pressure and urgency to the gameplay, challenging players to solve problems quickly while maintaining accuracy. Number Patterns and Sequences: A key aspect of the puzzles is recognizing number patterns or sequences. As players advance, the puzzles may involve more sophisticated patterns that require a deeper understanding of numbers and their relationships. Players may need to apply mathematical theories or use trial-and-error to find the correct solution.

name: DiaMaze
description: DiaMaze is a simple but sublimely relaxing game where the goal is to collect as many diamonds in a mine before your lamp runs out. There are no enemies, so you are racing only against the clock.DiaMaze is a DOS-based maze-solving game released in 1993. It is a simple yet engaging puzzle game where players must navigate through a series of increasingly complex mazes. The game challenges players’ spatial reasoning and their ability to find the correct path through the maze. Maze Navigation: The primary gameplay revolves around navigating through 2D mazes. Players must guide a character through a maze, avoiding obstacles and dead ends to reach the exit. The mazes are designed in a way that requires players to carefully plan their route and think critically about direction and movement. Increasing Difficulty: As players advance through the game, the mazes become larger and more complex, requiring more thought and strategy to solve. New obstacles or challenges may be introduced as players progress, such as timed events, moving walls, or additional paths that could lead to the wrong direction. Time Challenges: Some versions of the game feature a time limit for solving each maze. This adds an element of urgency and tests the player’s ability to think quickly and efficiently. Simple Controls: The game is controlled using the keyboard, where the player moves the character through the maze using arrow keys or WASD keys. There may also be options for pausing, restarting, or quitting a level via keyboard commands. Minimalistic Design: DiaMaze focuses on the maze-solving aspect of gameplay, with a minimalist interface and simple visuals. The game uses basic 2D graphics to display the maze and the player's position within it.

name: Diamond Ball III
description: Diamond Ball III is a simple puzzle game where the object is to guide your bouncing ball around the level clearing blocks. Your ball automatically bounces up and down, and you control its left and right movements.Diamond Ball III is a DOS-based puzzle game that was released in 1992. It is the third installment in the Diamond Ball series, offering a mix of arcade-style gameplay and puzzle mechanics. In the game, players are tasked with solving various puzzles while navigating through different levels. Puzzle-Solving: Players must solve puzzles by manipulating different objects or mechanisms in the environment. This often involves pushing blocks, arranging shapes, or activating switches. The puzzles are designed to test the player's spatial awareness, logical thinking, and timing skills. Diamond Collection: Throughout each level, players must collect diamonds scattered across the screen. These diamonds act as the main objectives for the player, and collecting them often requires solving puzzles or avoiding traps. The levels become progressively more difficult, with more complex puzzles and additional obstacles to navigate. Timed Challenges: Some levels feature time limits, where players must complete puzzles within a certain timeframe. This adds an element of urgency and pressure, requiring players to think quickly while solving the puzzles. Arcade Elements: In addition to puzzle-solving, Diamond Ball III includes elements of arcade-style gameplay, such as avoiding enemies or hazards that are present in the levels. Players must also contend with moving platforms, falling blocks, and other dynamic obstacles that make navigating the maze-like levels more challenging. Increasing Difficulty: The difficulty increases as players advance through the game. The puzzles become more intricate, with additional obstacles and more complex arrangements of objects to interact with. Players must learn to think strategically, often needing to plan ahead and carefully manage their movements to solve the puzzles within the constraints of time and space.

name: Diamond Dash
description: Diamond Dash borrows heavily from the classic Lode Runner game. It involves ladders, getting chased by baddies, collecting diamonds and using your "proton accelerator" to blast holes in the floor to trap them.Diamond Dash is a DOS-based puzzle game that was released in the early 1990s. It blends match-3 puzzle mechanics with arcade-style gameplay, where players must match colored diamonds in order to clear levels. The game is centered around creating groups of matching diamonds and scoring points, with each level offering increasingly difficult challenges. Match-3 Mechanics: The core gameplay revolves around swapping adjacent diamonds to create groups of three or more diamonds of the same color. Once the match is made, the diamonds are cleared from the screen. Players must think strategically about which diamonds to swap to maximize their score and clear the board efficiently. Time-Limited Challenges: Some versions of the game have time limits for each level. Players must clear diamonds before the clock runs out. This adds an element of urgency, requiring quick thinking and fast moves. The faster the player clears the diamonds, the higher their score. Increasing Difficulty: As players progress, the difficulty increases. New obstacles may be introduced, such as limited moves or special tiles that affect the gameplay. The diamonds may also fall in more complex patterns, requiring players to think ahead and plan their moves carefully. Scoring and Combos: Players score points by creating matches of three or more diamonds. Clearing larger groups or making chain reactions (where one match leads to another) results in bonus points. Combo systems may reward players for quick matches or for creating multiple matches in succession. Power-ups and Bonuses: Some versions of the game might feature power-ups that help players clear diamonds more easily, such as bombs that clear multiple diamonds or special tools that rearrange the grid. These power-ups can be earned by achieving certain milestones or by creating special combinations of diamonds.

name: DiceDrop
description: DiceDrop is a rare game, re-discovered by the author in his personal archives and now available for the world to play! (Thanks for submitting it!) The game is a well-done implementation of a Columns / Puyo Puyo type game. (The author mentions being inspired by playing Xixit.) Groups of three dice fall, and your goal is to arrange them so that three or more of the same number line up in a row, which will clear those dice from the screen.DiceDrop is a DOS-based puzzle game released in the early 1990s. It combines elements of dice and puzzle-solving mechanics, offering a unique and engaging gameplay experience. The game revolves around dropping dice onto a grid and solving various challenges that require strategy and careful planning. Dice Mechanics: The main mechanic revolves around dice with different face values. The player must place or drop the dice into various grid positions or slots, often aiming to align numbers, match patterns, or complete certain objectives. The dice mechanics are central to the puzzle-solving aspect of the game. The game may involve stacking dice, aligning them in rows or columns, or using dice rolls to meet specific criteria. Grid-based Puzzle Solving: The game takes place on a grid where dice must be placed strategically. The objective typically involves matching dice with specific numbers or achieving a certain arrangement on the grid. The grid may have special rules, such as certain squares requiring specific dice values or dice needing to match in rows, columns, or other formations. Strategy and Planning: Players must plan their moves carefully, as placing dice in the wrong position can make it harder to solve the puzzle or complete a level. The game involves a lot of strategic thinking—deciding where to place the dice, when to drop them, and how to optimize each move. Increasing Difficulty: As players progress through the levels, the difficulty of the puzzles increases. New grid patterns may emerge, additional rules may be introduced, and the player might face new constraints, such as a limited number of dice to use or time limits. Time or Move-Based Challenges: Some versions of the game may impose a time limit or a move limit, requiring players to solve the puzzle quickly or within a specific number of moves. This adds an element of urgency and tests the player’s ability to think and act quickly.

name: DICEWARS
description: "DICEWARS" is a strategy flash game where players control territories on a grid using dice. The objective is to conquer all opposing territories by strategically moving and attacking with dice. Each territory is represented by a number of dice, which indicate the strength of that territory. Key Features: Dice Mechanics: Players roll dice to determine the outcome of attacks. Higher numbers typically mean more successful attacks. Territory Control: Players can expand their territories by attacking neighboring ones, using the number of dice in their territory to fight. Strategic Planning: Players must decide when to reinforce territories, when to attack, and how to best allocate their resources. Strategies: Balance Offense and Defense: Keep some territories strong while expanding. Attack Weak Territories: Focus on attacking areas with fewer dice to maximize your chances of success. Plan for Counterattacks: Be wary of leaving your territories vulnerable after an attack. It's a fun mix of luck and strategy! If you have specific questions or need tips, just let me know!

name: Dig Dig
description: Dig your way into the mine and kill all rodents. Blow up rodents with the space bar.Dig Dig is an HTML-based puzzle game that is typically inspired by classic arcade-style digging games. The gameplay involves controlling a character or object that digs through the ground or a grid to collect items, avoid obstacles, and solve puzzles within a limited amount of time or moves. The concept can vary slightly from version to version, but the core mechanic revolves around digging through a grid, collecting treasure or items, and avoiding or navigating obstacles. In a typical Dig Dig game, the player must control a character or tool that digs through soil or terrain, often represented as a grid of squares or tiles. The goal is usually to collect items or treasures while avoiding enemies, obstacles, or hazards. Key Features: Digging Mechanic: The player digs through the ground or grid by selecting tiles to remove or by controlling a character that digs as it moves. Digs can reveal items, treasures, or even enemies, depending on the game’s design. Collect Items or Treasures: As the player digs, they uncover valuable items like treasure, gems, or keys, which need to be collected to progress to the next level or achieve a high score. The player must strategically decide where to dig to uncover hidden treasures while avoiding dead-ends or hazards. Avoid Obstacles and Enemies: Some versions may include enemies that move around the grid, creating hazards that the player must avoid while digging. Obstacles such as rocks, water, or other environmental hazards may block the path or impede progress. Level Progression: Each level may feature different objectives, such as collecting a certain number of items, avoiding enemies for a set period, or reaching a specific location on the grid. The levels get progressively harder, with more obstacles and fewer safe spots for digging. Time Limit or Moves: The game may include a time limit for each level, requiring the player to dig and collect items quickly before the timer runs out. Alternatively, there might be a limit to the number of moves or digs the player can make before losing the level.

name: Dig It!
description: Dig It! is a platforming game that seems more aimed at children, but still provides a decent amount of gameplay and challenge for adults. I'm not sure what the story of the game is supposed to be, since the "Story" menu option just leads to information about how to register the game. In practice you're running around the levels, shooting at dinosaurs and snails, trying to get to the exit.Dig It! is a DOS-based puzzle game that was released in the early 1990s. The game follows the concept of digging through various levels while solving puzzles and avoiding obstacles. It is a classic example of puzzle-platformers of that era, where players need to navigate through a maze-like environment by digging paths, collecting items, and overcoming challenges. Digging Mechanics: The primary gameplay mechanic revolves around digging. Players can dig through certain types of terrain to create paths, uncover treasures, or collect useful items. The challenge is managing how much of the environment you can alter without running out of time or resources. In some levels, the terrain might collapse or shift, which requires careful planning. Puzzle Solving: Each level features a set of puzzle-like challenges, often requiring the player to use the environment to solve problems. This might include digging certain paths, collecting items, or even triggering mechanisms by digging in specific patterns. The game often asks players to balance exploration with the need to create paths or find hidden objects. Collecting Items: Players are often tasked with collecting specific items scattered around the levels, such as treasure, tools, or keys, which are needed to unlock further levels or complete challenges. Timing is crucial, as some levels may have time limits, requiring you to complete the task before the time runs out. Obstacles and Hazards: As the player digs through the levels, they will encounter various obstacles like rocks, walls, or enemies that need to be avoided or dealt with. These hazards can block progress or lead to failure if not properly handled. Some levels may contain falling rocks or traps that force the player to react quickly or plan their digging strategy carefully. Limited Resources: In some levels, the player may have limited digging power or other resources, forcing them to think strategically about how to approach each puzzle. This adds a layer of difficulty as the player must make the most out of the available resources. Increasing Difficulty: As players progress through the game, the difficulty increases. More complex puzzles, tougher obstacles, and new enemies or hazards are introduced, creating a sense of progression and challenge.

name: Digger
description: Digger is a classic DOS game that was originally released in 1983 by Windmill Software. It is a maze-based arcade game where players control a small digging machine, collecting treasures while avoiding enemies and navigating through underground tunnels. Known for its simple yet addictive gameplay, charming graphics, and catchy music, Digger became a beloved title during the early days of personal computing. It remains a nostalgic favorite for retro gaming enthusiasts. Key Features: Maze-Based Gameplay: Players control a digging machine that moves through a grid-based maze, collecting bags of gold and other treasures. The goal is to collect all the treasures in each level while avoiding or outsmarting enemies. Enemies and Hazards: The game features various enemies, such as Nobbin and Hobbin, which chase the player. Nobbins are slower and follow predictable paths, while Hobbins are faster and more aggressive. Players can temporarily defeat enemies by dropping bags of gold on them or using special power-ups. Digging Mechanics: The player's machine can dig through dirt to create tunnels, which can be used to escape enemies or access treasures. Digging also reveals hidden items, such as emeralds and bonus points. Power-Ups: The game includes power-ups like shovels, which allow the player to dig faster, and potions, which temporarily freeze enemies. These power-ups add an extra layer of strategy to the gameplay. Level Progression: The game features multiple levels, each with increasing difficulty and complexity. Players must complete each level by collecting all treasures and reaching the exit. Retro Graphics and Sound: The game features simple, pixelated graphics that were typical of early DOS games. The soundtrack, composed by Rob Hubbard, is iconic and adds to the game's charm. High Score Challenge: Players can compete for high scores by collecting treasures, defeating enemies, and completing levels quickly. The competitive aspect encourages replayability.

name: Digger Remastered
description: Quite similar to the classic games DigDug and Mr.Do, this game gained some sort of PC gaming cult status. I had a couple of requests for this one since starting the site, so I figured I'd better add it. It plays well, offers lots of command line options, and you can turn off the music! (It's not that bad for PC speaker music, but after playing games and listening to MODs for so long, I've grown rather tired of the "Popcorn" song.)Digger Remastered is a modern remaster of the classic Digger game, originally released in the 1980s. The remastered version was created to bring the nostalgic gameplay of the original into the modern gaming era with updated graphics, sound, and additional features, while keeping the essence of the original game intact. The game remains a favorite for retro gaming enthusiasts and those who enjoy classic arcade-style puzzle and action gameplay. Classic Digging Mechanic: The core of the game revolves around digging tunnels through the ground to collect treasures (usually diamonds) and escape enemies. Digger can dig horizontally or vertically, creating a maze of tunnels within each level. Digger can also destroy rocks and other obstacles that block the path, but certain enemies or obstacles may be able to block or destroy the tunnels too. Enemies and Hazards: The player must avoid various enemies that move around the screen. These enemies are typically animated and follow simple AI patterns. If Digger touches any of the enemies, the player loses a life. In some versions, the game includes hazards like falling rocks, which add to the challenge. Power-ups and Tools: In the remastered version, there may be new power-ups or tools that help the player dig faster, temporarily stun enemies, or even clear obstacles more effectively. These items can make it easier to progress through the game or offer temporary advantages against enemies. Level Progression: The game is organized into levels, and each level presents new layouts and challenges. After completing a level, players move on to a more difficult stage, which typically features more enemies, more complicated terrain, and additional obstacles. The goal in each level is to collect all of the treasures (or a certain number) and escape without being caught by the enemies. Updated Graphics and Sound: Digger Remastered comes with updated graphics that modernize the look while retaining the retro feel. The original 2D pixel graphics are upgraded to look smoother, with more detail and color. The sound design is also enhanced, offering improved music tracks, sound effects, and more immersive audio compared to the original version. New Features: Digger Remastered may add new features such as leaderboards, achievements, or multiplayer modes to modernize the experience and add replayability.

name: Diggers
description: Diggers is a demo of an interesting Lemmings-like game that doesn't seem to have been very popular, despite also being released for Amiga systems in addition to DOS. It was described by PC Gamer magazine as being a "combination of Lemmings and Populous, Diggers doesn't quite offer the appeal of either." That's a bit harsh but does seem to sum up the game.Diggers is a classic DOS-based action and puzzle game that was originally released in the early 1990s. It combines elements of digging, exploration, and strategy, offering a unique experience that was a fun part of many gamers' childhoods. The game is often remembered for its challenging mechanics and engaging puzzle-solving elements. Digging Mechanic: The main feature of the game is the digging mechanic, where players use their diggers to carve out tunnels in the ground. The ground can be made of different types of materials, each requiring different strategies to navigate. Diggers are often tasked with digging through walls or obstacles to create new pathways or access valuable items. Team of Diggers: The player controls a team of diggers, each with specific skills. Each digger has different abilities that can help solve puzzles or overcome challenges. Managing the team is essential, as the diggers can help each other with their tasks. The player must decide which digger to control at any given time to make the most progress. Puzzle Solving: The game is filled with puzzles that players must solve in order to progress through the levels. This might involve creating specific tunnel patterns, collecting resources, or positioning the diggers in strategic locations to complete objectives.
