Some obstacles may be timing-based, requiring players to react quickly. Collectibles and Power-ups: Along the way, you can collect coins, gems, or other items that improve your score or unlock upgrades. Power-ups can help the dragon fly faster, become invincible, or clear obstacles more easily. Simple Controls: Keyboard: Arrow keys or WASD to move the dragon left, right, up (jump), or down (duck). Spacebar: Often used for special actions, like jumping or breathing fire. Mouse/Touchscreen: In some versions, tap or swipe to control the dragon’s movements. Increasing Difficulty: As you progress, the speed of the game increases, and the challenges become more difficult with more complex obstacles and enemies. New environments or levels may be introduced with different themes and challenges. Dynamic Levels: The game may feature procedurally generated levels or distinct stages, each with unique environments, hazards, and obstacles. Expect varied backgrounds, such as snowy mountains, dark caves, or fiery landscapes.

name: Dragon's Mandate
description: Dragon's Mandate is sort of a belated sequel to the classic Atari 2600 game Adventure. Much like that game, you find yourself within a huge maze, and need to figure out how to collect the chalice. You can pick up a variety of objects to help you along the way, such as keys and weapons, the latter of which are used to take out the enemies like skeletons, fire elementals, and of course dragons. The graphics have been upgraded quite a bit from the old Atari 2600 game's barely recognizable objects. The world is quite difficult to navigate, so you may need to resort to paper maps in order to win. Like the 2600 game, there are secrets to find. Basically if you thoroughly enjoyed Adventure on the 2600, give give this a try.

name: Dragon's Shard
description: Dragon's Shard seems to use the same engine as Stone Mist and I suppose was developed after it, since Stone Mist is mentioned in the game's docs. Anyways it's a Ultima-like RPG with a fairly in-depth character generation system and an uncommon 640x200 (!) screen resolution. The story and gameplay is all pretty generic PC fantasy roleplaying stuff, so if that's the sort of thing you're into, this could be a decent adventure for you.Dragon's Shard is a DOS-based adventure game that combines elements of role-playing and strategy. It features a fantasy world where players control characters on a quest involving dragons, magic, and ancient artifacts. This game is designed with retro graphics typical of early DOS games, creating a nostalgic experience for players familiar with classic RPGs from the 1990s. Fantasy Adventure Setting: The game is set in a world filled with dragons, magical realms, castles, dungeons, and other fantasy environments. It features a rich lore and plot centered around the mystical Dragon's Shard, a powerful relic with the ability to shape the destiny of the world. Turn-Based Combat: Combat is typically turn-based, allowing players to choose from a range of attacks, magic spells, and tactical decisions in battles against various enemies like dragons, goblins, and other creatures. Each character may have unique abilities or spells that can be used strategically in combat. Puzzle Solving: As part of the adventure, players will encounter puzzles and challenges that require careful thinking and exploration. Some areas may be locked behind certain conditions, such as finding keys or defeating bosses. Character Progression: Players can develop their characters by gaining experience through battles and quests. New abilities, weapons, and magical powers are unlocked as characters level up. Exploration: The game world is vast and filled with different environments to explore, such as forests, caves, villages, and dragon lairs. Players can discover hidden areas, secrets, and treasures that help them in their quest. Classic DOS Graphics: The game features graphics typical of early DOS titles, using pixelated sprites and 2D landscapes to represent the fantasy world. The visual style is often minimalist but conveys the necessary atmosphere for a retro RPG experience. Music and Sound Effects: Music is often synthesized, typical of games from the DOS era, with atmospheric tracks to enhance the fantasy setting. Sound effects accompany key actions, such as combat or item usage.

name: Dragons Bane: Mah Jongg II
description: Mah Jongg is an "addictive solitaire game played with Chinese tiles" according to the game's manual. This game is the sequel to Arcanum Computing's previous game Maj Jongg Solitaire. It features improved graphics (SVGA 640x480) and features which make it generally a better playing experience than its predecessor. Honestly I never learned how to play Mah Jongg, so I can't tell you if this functions as a good solitaire version of it or not! So you'll need to try it for yourself. It also includes a tile editor called "Tile Factory".

name: Dragons Mahjong
description: Find and combine 2 of the same Mahjong tiles to remove them. Combine the 2 dragons to finish a level.Dragons Mahjong is a variation of the classic Mahjong Solitaire game, but with a specific theme centered around dragons. This game is played on a single-player basis and involves matching tiles to clear the board. The twist in Dragons Mahjong is that it incorporates dragon-themed tiles, such as symbols representing various aspects of Chinese mythology and fantasy. The game is visually appealing, featuring intricate artwork, vibrant colors, and a soothing atmosphere that immerses players in its world. Dragon-Themed Tiles: The tiles are decorated with images of dragons, symbols from Chinese culture, and other mythical creatures or elements. This adds a visually appealing and thematic twist to the traditional Mahjong game. Classic Mahjong Gameplay: The objective is to match pairs of identical tiles to clear the board. The tiles can only be matched if they are free (not covered by other tiles) and have at least one open side. Players must think strategically, as the layout of tiles may vary, and some tiles will be hidden under others until uncovered. Multiple Layouts and Levels: The game may offer different layouts (e.g., traditional, pyramid, or other creative designs) that challenge players to adapt their strategies. As players advance through levels, the difficulty increases, either through more complex layouts or faster time limits. Power-ups and Special Tiles: Some versions of Dragons Mahjong may include power-ups or special tiles that can help clear the board more easily. For example, a tile might allow you to shuffle the board or remove tiles that are particularly difficult to match. Soothing Visuals and Sound: The game typically features relaxing, atmospheric music and sound effects, such as the roar of a dragon or peaceful oriental melodies. The background may include serene landscapes, castles, or dragon imagery, making the experience more immersive. Simple Controls: Mouse/Touchscreen: Simply click or tap on the tiles to select and match pairs. The game might offer drag-and-drop functionality for more intuitive gameplay. Scoring and Time Limits: Players may earn points for each pair of tiles removed. A high score is achieved by clearing the board in the shortest amount of time, with extra points for combo moves or quick matches.

name: Dragonsphere
description: Dragonsphere is a fantasy-themed graphical adventure game which bears resemblance to Lucasarts games, The Legend of Kryandia series, or Microprose's own Rex Nebular and the Cosmic Gender Bender. In Dragonsphere you play as Callash who is out to prevent a powerful wizard from escaping and having his revenge on those that imprisoned him. The graphics and sounds are both top-notch here and judging from reviews of the game at the time it was well received. This demo version gives you a short glimpse into the full game.

name: Drak
description: Drak is a Tetris clone with a fantasy themed story and some extra block features. The game begins with a lengthy illustrated backstory but you likely won't care much about it since it doesn't factor into the gameplay at all. What does affect the gameplay are the various new block types; not block shapes, but how the blocks behave based on what they're made out of. These include: Cristal (eliminate in pairs of the same color), Elemental (opposite elements eliminate each other), and Annulment (similar colors eliminate each other). These also comprise different modes where only these types of blocks will sometimes appear. It's a bit confusing, probably because the author's first language doesn't seem to be English, but for those with patience to learn the intricacies, this may be an interesting Tetris game to try.

name: Drake Snake and the Secret Crypt
description: Drake Snake is a German made platforming game which seems to take inspiration from David Crane's Pitfall game on the Atari and other systems. You play the titular Drake Snake as you explore an underground crypt. The graphics are decent and controls are generally good (except how your rocket pack stops moving whenever you hit a ceiling) but the game itself is quite difficult (one hit death = restart level). Two levels are included in the shareware version.Drake Snake and the Secret Crypt is a DOS-based adventure game that blends elements of exploration, puzzle-solving, and action. The game places players in the role of Drake Snake, a character navigating a mysterious crypt filled with treasures, traps, and ancient secrets. The gameplay is structured around exploring cryptic locations, battling enemies, and deciphering puzzles to progress through the levels. Adventure and Exploration: The game is centered around exploration, with players navigating through different rooms of the crypt, each offering a unique layout and set of challenges. The environment is mysterious and filled with hidden paths, treasures, and enemies, creating a sense of intrigue as you progress. Puzzle-Solving: Many rooms and areas require players to solve puzzles, such as unlocking doors with specific keys, finding hidden switches, or using items in the right combination. The puzzles may become more complex as you delve deeper into the crypt, demanding careful thought and attention to detail. Combat: The game features action sequences where players must fight or avoid enemies within the crypt. Drake Snake can have various weapons or abilities at his disposal, which can be used strategically to take down enemies or defend against attacks. Secret Treasures and Artifacts: The crypt is filled with valuable treasures, artifacts, and secret items that can aid in your quest. These might include health potions, powerful weapons, or magical items that offer abilities like healing or unlocking doors. Classic DOS Graphics: The game uses the pixelated, 2D graphics typical of early DOS games. The visual style may be basic by modern standards but adds to the nostalgic charm and retro feel of the game. The crypt is designed to feel atmospheric, with dark, mysterious backgrounds and simple, but effective, sprite-based character designs. Mystical and Atmospheric Sound: The game’s soundtrack features eerie and atmospheric music that enhances the crypt's dark, secretive mood. Sound effects like door creaks, footsteps, and enemy growls help build suspense as players explore the crypt’s depths.

name: Draughts
description: Classic board game Draughts (international draughts on a 10x10 board), defeat your opponent by capturing his piece and try to promote your piece to a King. Draughts (also known as Checkers in the United States) is a two-player board game where the objective is to capture or block all of the opponent’s pieces. It’s played on an 8x8 grid, and each player starts with 12 pieces placed on the dark squares of the board. The game has simple rules but can become highly strategic as you progress Classic Board Layout: The game uses an 8x8 grid, with alternating light and dark squares. Players only move on the dark squares, and the pieces are placed on the first three rows of the board on each side. The board layout remains faithful to the traditional rules of Draughts. Simple Rules: Each player can move their pieces diagonally forward by one square. To capture an opponent’s piece, a player must jump over it to an empty square. Multiple captures can be made in a single turn, provided the player continues to jump over opponent’s pieces. When a piece reaches the last row on the opponent’s side, it is “kinged” and gains the ability to move backward. Gameplay Mode: Player vs Player: Two human players can compete on the same device or over the internet, depending on the version. Player vs AI: Many online versions offer AI opponents with varying difficulty levels to challenge players of all skill levels. Piece Promotion (Kinging): When a regular piece reaches the last row on the opponent's side of the board, it is promoted to a "king" piece, which is typically denoted by a crown on the piece. Kings can move both forward and backward, giving them more movement flexibility. User-Friendly Interface: Players click or tap to select a piece, then select the destination square, making the game accessible for both desktop and mobile devices. The interface often highlights valid moves to make gameplay smoother, especially for new players. Capture Mechanics: Capturing is mandatory in most versions of the game, meaning that if a capture is available, the player must make it. Capturing is performed by jumping over an opponent's piece, landing on an empty square directly after it. Strategic Depth: While the rules are simple, Draughts has deep strategic elements. Blocking, positioning, and planning ahead for multiple moves are key to success. Endgame: The game ends when one player captures all of the opponent’s pieces or traps them in such a way that they can no longer make a move.

name: Draw Poker
description: Draw Poker lets you play poker against 6 computer opponents in glorious text mode, simulating the experience of poker night with friends, except here, they're just names on the screen. Players ante $2 each, get your five cards, hold or draw, etc. Then you see who's got the best hand. I don't know much about poker but this appears to be Five Card Draw or something similar. There are no options to choose, you just hit the appropriate hotkey (displayed on screen) for the action you want to take, and then likely lose to one of your computer opponents. At least you won't lose real money here!

name: Dream Pet Connect
description: Connect the same animals in this Dream Pet Link game. The connecting path cannot change directions more than 2x.Dream Pet Connect is a casual HTML-based puzzle game that combines elements of match-three and connect-the-dots mechanics. In the game, players are tasked with connecting matching pet icons or tiles in a grid, similar to a Mahjong-style matching game. The objective is to clear the board by linking pairs of identical pets using a path of no more than two or three straight lines. The game mechanics are simple but require strategic thinking as players try to clear the board within a time limit or limited moves. The pets featured in the game can range from cute dogs and cats to more exotic animals, often depicted with bright, colorful designs. Simple Gameplay: Click and drag to connect matching pet tiles. Increasing Difficulty: As players progress, the levels become more challenging with a larger grid or added obstacles. Timer and Scoring: Players race against the clock for the highest possible score. Cute Graphics: The game features adorable pet illustrations and vibrant visuals that make it appealing to all ages. Power-Ups: Special tiles or bonuses can help clear tiles or offer other gameplay advantages.

name: Dream Pet Dimensions
description: Play a Dream Pet Game in 3 Dimensions. Click on 2 of the same blocks that have at least 2 adjacent free sides.Dream Pet Dimensions is a delightful and engaging HTML-based puzzle game that combines pet-themed characters with fun, spatial challenges. The game revolves around matching and connecting pet icons placed on a grid, often within different "dimensions" or levels, each offering a unique twist in gameplay. Charming Pet Characters: The game features a variety of adorable pets, such as puppies, kittens, and exotic animals, each drawn in vibrant, playful styles. These pets serve as the tiles to match, adding a fun and whimsical element to the game. Multiple Dimensions/Levels: Each level or dimension of the game introduces a new layout, sometimes with additional obstacles or fewer moves, making each stage more challenging. Dimensions may also involve different board sizes, adding a layer of difficulty as you progress. Simple Yet Strategic Mechanics: Players connect matching pet tiles using lines, but the challenge lies in finding the optimal path. The game’s rules typically require that lines between tiles cannot cross and may have to follow specific straight-line paths. Timer or Move Limits: The game often comes with either a countdown timer or a move limit, creating an additional layer of pressure as players race to clear the board in time or within the allowed number of moves. Power-ups and Boosters: As players advance, they can unlock power-ups or boosters that help in clearing tiles, such as hints or line-removing tools. These come in handy when the game gets tougher in higher dimensions. Cute and Colorful Visuals: The pet-themed visuals are designed to be bright and cheerful, appealing to players of all ages. The art style is vibrant and cartoonish, adding to the lighthearted and enjoyable experience. Score and Achievements: Players earn points for each successful match, with additional bonuses for completing levels quickly or with fewer moves. The game may include achievements or stars to encourage replayability.

name: Dream Pet Solitaire
description: Play Solitaire Mahjong with the dream Pets. Combine 2 of the same pets to remove the pets.Dream Pet Solitaire is a fun and relaxing HTML-based solitaire game that combines traditional card gameplay with a cute, pet-themed design. In this variation of the classic Solitaire game, players are tasked with organizing a deck of cards in a specific order, while being accompanied by adorable pet characters and vibrant graphics. Classic Solitaire Gameplay: The game follows the classic rules of Solitaire, where players need to organize cards by suit and in alternating colors, working from the tableau to the foundation piles. Pet-Themed Graphics: Instead of traditional card designs, Dream Pet Solitaire features fun, pet-themed artwork. Each card has a unique pet design, making the game visually appealing for pet lovers and adding a sense of fun to the classic Solitaire mechanics. Intuitive Controls: The game is easy to pick up with drag-and-drop mechanics for moving cards between piles. The interface is simple and clean, ensuring that players can focus on solving the puzzle without distractions. Relaxing and Casual Gameplay: With no time limits or stressful conditions, Dream Pet Solitaire is designed to be a casual and relaxing game. It allows players to take their time and enjoy the process of solving the card layout at their own pace. Undo and Hint Options: Players can make mistakes and reverse their moves using an "undo" feature, and if they’re stuck, they can use hints to help guide them toward the next best move. Cute Animations and Sound Effects: The game features light, fun animations and sounds that make the pet-themed atmosphere more engaging. Cards may flip with little animations, and successful moves can trigger cheerful sounds, creating a feel-good experience. Minimalist Design: The user interface is streamlined, allowing players to focus on the game without unnecessary distractions. The background is often calm and simple, complementing the overall relaxed vibe of the game. Scoring and Achievements: Players may be awarded points based on their efficiency in completing the game, including factors such as the number of moves or time spent. Achievements may be earned for completing games without using hints or undoing moves.

name: Dream Prisoner
description: Dream Prisoner is a text adventure game with graphics. Basically it plays like a normal text adventure, but a background image shows you what the room/area you're in looks like. It uses a traditional text parser ("GET KNIFE", "USE KNIFE") so if you enjoy that, give it a try. The story is that you are stranded inside a lucid dream, exploring a high-tech building where some sort of gathering is/was going on. There are paranormal aspects to it as well. I didn't get very far so I don't know how long it is but if the description sounds like something you'd like, no harm in giving it a go.

name: Dreamful Journey to the West
description: Overview: Dreamful Journey to the West is an enchanting flash game inspired by the classic Chinese novel "Journey to the West." Players embark on a whimsical adventure through fantastical landscapes, battling monsters and solving puzzles while exploring themes from the beloved tale. Gameplay: Character Selection: Players can choose from various characters, each with unique abilities and strengths, inspired by figures from the original story, such as the Monkey King, Tripitaka, and others. Adventure Levels: Navigate through beautifully crafted levels, including lush forests, mystical mountains, and ancient temples. Each area presents unique challenges and enemies to defeat. Combat Mechanics: Engage in action-packed battles against a variety of foes, using special moves and combos to defeat monsters and bosses. Graphics & Sound: Visual Style: Features vibrant, colorful graphics that capture the essence of a magical journey, with detailed character animations and enchanting environments. Soundtrack: An immersive soundtrack and whimsical sound effects enhance the adventure, drawing players deeper into the game's world. Key Features: Puzzle-Solving: Encounter puzzles throughout the journey that require logic and strategy to progress, adding depth to the gameplay. Character Upgrades: Collect items and experience points to upgrade abilities and unlock new skills for each character. Rich Storyline: Experience a narrative that blends adventure and folklore, inspired by the original Journey to the West, with charming dialogue and quests. Dreamful Journey to the West offers a delightful mix of action, exploration, and storytelling, perfect for fans of adventure games and classic literature. Join the journey and help your heroes overcome obstacles and fulfill their destinies!

name: Dreamworld Adventure
description: This German platforming game has a simple structure: Collect fruits and other bonuses, avoid enemies, and get to the exit. Nonetheless, it has a certain charm about it. The graphics are colorful, and while the music tends to drone on and on, it does fit the overall aesthetic of the game. Not too complicated but not too intense either, and it could be good to play to relax. Dreamworld Adventure is a classic DOS-based adventure game that combines exploration, puzzle-solving, and fantasy elements, typically with a charming, nostalgic feel. Set in a dreamlike world, the game features vibrant landscapes, quirky characters, and challenging obstacles. It is often structured around progressing through various levels or realms that are part of a fantastical universe, with the player taking on the role of a character (or sometimes an avatar) exploring this whimsical world. Fantasy Setting: The game is set in a dreamy, surreal world where logic doesn’t always apply. Players may encounter fantastical creatures, magical environments, and unexpected events. Exploration and Puzzle-Solving: A significant part of the game involves exploring different areas of the dream world, solving environmental puzzles, and interacting with objects or NPCs (Non-Playable Characters). The puzzles often require clever thinking and using items in unexpected ways. Story-Driven: Dreamworld Adventure typically features a storyline that unfolds as you progress through the game. The narrative often centers around a character (or the player) embarking on a quest, overcoming challenges, or solving mysteries in the dream world. Simple Graphics: Being a DOS-era game, Dreamworld Adventure would feature pixel art or simple 2D graphics, typical of the era. While not graphically advanced, these visuals provide a nostalgic and charming retro feel. Multiple Realms/Levels: The dream world is usually divided into different realms or levels, each with a unique theme, characters, and obstacles. Players need to explore each realm to progress to the next stage, usually solving a series of puzzles or challenges. Conversations with these characters are often key to solving puzzles. Inventory System: Players can collect items along the way that are necessary for solving puzzles or unlocking new areas. The inventory system is typically simple, allowing players to use or combine items as they progress. Atmospheric Sound and Music: Music and sound effects in the game help create an immersive experience. The sound design typically complements the dreamy atmosphere, with calm melodies or whimsical tunes.

name: DressMeUp
description: DressMeUp is a "paper doll game" where you choose two animals (girl animal on the left, boy on the right) and dress them up in clothing. Obviously intended for young children, this game would be a bit difficult for them given that they need to be pretty good using the mouse (or have a patient adult help them) since only some of the given clothing work (due to it being the shareware version?) and you need to click on some pretty tiny spots. The animals and clothing drawings are ... creative? Some children may find them endearing I suppose. No doubt you will remember this if you played with it as a kid, otherwise probably better to skip it ...

name: Drilling Billy
description: Drilling Billy (aka "The Worlds of Billy") is a Lode Runner style single-screen platforming game where the goal is to trap the enemies by digging holes in the ground and trapping them. Here you will face numerous opponents such as the fearsome ... uh, banana. And other similarly scary opponents. This game features a decently high resolution (for a DOS game) and enthusiastic sound effects.Drilling Billy is a classic DOS-based action and puzzle game released in the 1990s. It was developed by Summit Software and features a simple yet engaging gameplay style that revolves around digging and exploring underground environments, typically set in a cartoonish, whimsical world. The player controls Billy, the main character, who is equipped with a drill to dig through layers of earth, solve puzzles, and avoid various obstacles or enemies. Digging Mechanic: The core mechanic of Drilling Billy involves drilling through different layers of earth. The player must manage the limited drill power, navigating through obstacles and avoiding dangerous situations as they dig. Puzzles and Obstacles: As Billy drills through the levels, he encounters various obstacles, such as rocks, enemies, and traps. Players must figure out how to avoid or overcome these challenges to proceed to the next level. Collectibles and Power-ups: Throughout the levels, there are various items to collect, such as power-ups that enhance Billy’s drill, bonus points, and other useful items that help in progressing through the game. These items are often hidden or require solving puzzles to access. Enemies and Hazards: There are different types of enemies in the game that move through the tunnels, or hazards that Billy must avoid, like falling rocks, spikes, or other dangers. Timing and strategy are crucial to avoid these threats while drilling. Level Progression: The game consists of various levels, each with its unique challenges. As the player progresses, the difficulty increases, with more complicated puzzles, tougher enemies, and more intricate underground mazes to navigate. Simple Controls: The controls are typically simple, with a focus on directional movement, drilling, and interacting with the environment. The player controls Billy’s movement using the keyboard, usually arrow keys or specific keys to drill. Cartoonish Graphics: Like many games of the era, Drilling Billy features pixelated, cartoon-style graphics. These visuals give the game a lighthearted, playful feel, despite the sometimes tricky challenges. Challenging Time Limits: Some levels might include time-based objectives, requiring players to finish their drilling tasks before a timer runs out, adding an additional layer of pressure to the gameplay.

name: Drip
description: Drip is a Columns clone with a few unique features. The objective is the same as Columns: Block sets ("drops") will fall into the well, each containing three colors (or special blocks); match three or more to remove them from the playing field. The game works decently and it has Soundblaster music. There are also two special types of blocks: Wilds (which match any color) and bombs (which destroy nearby blocks). You can also play a two-player simultaneous game. Drip is a classic DOS-based arcade-style puzzle game released in the early 1990s. The game features a quirky and engaging concept where players control a small, animated drop of liquid as it moves through various levels. The primary goal in Drip is to guide the drop through challenging environments, overcoming obstacles, solving puzzles, and collecting items. Unique Liquid Mechanics: The central theme of Drip is the movement of liquid. The player controls a drop of liquid that can drip, splash, or flow across the level. This gameplay mechanic is unique for its time, adding a fresh challenge to the typical platformer genre. Puzzle-Solving: As the player progresses, the levels become more intricate, with various environmental puzzles to solve. This might include navigating platforms, avoiding hazards, or triggering mechanisms in the environment that affect the liquid’s movement. Obstacles and Hazards: Throughout the levels, the player will encounter various obstacles, such as spikes, moving platforms, enemies, or traps that can damage or eliminate the drop of liquid. Players need to time their movements carefully to avoid these hazards. Simple, Cartoonish Graphics: Drip features simple, colorful graphics with an emphasis on cartoonish characters and environments. The visuals are in line with many early DOS games, with pixelated designs and bright, cheerful colors. Challenging Levels: The game consists of several levels, each increasing in difficulty. As players progress, the obstacles become more complex, and new environmental elements are introduced that require the player to think strategically about how to move the liquid. Collectibles: In addition to navigating obstacles, players can often collect items scattered throughout the levels, which may include bonuses or power-ups that help the player on their journey. The player may need to manipulate the drop’s behavior based on physics, such as making it drip down walls or flow through narrow pathways. Players must adapt their strategy as they face new types of challenges and hazards.

name: Dropsession
description: Dropsession is a logical puzzle game involving shapes, but they don't drop like they would in Tetris. Instead here the goal is to assemble the shapes into a pattern that is given for each level. Your only means of orienting the shapes is changing the gravity for the room (it's called the "forcefield direction" in the docs) and rotating the pieces before you place them. It seems easy but I found it quite tricky to get the hang of. You will need to hit F1 to see the list of keys, perhaps the most important (that I missed at first) is Home which changes the gravity direction. Definitely a unique puzzle game that's worth a look. (Note that the game refers to itself as "freeware" but it contains explicit registration instructions and an order form, so I'm calling it shareware here.)

name: DropTris
description: Drop down blocks in this Tetris game. Remove full lines and reach the indicated goal.DropTris is a variation of the classic Tetris puzzle game that incorporates elements of falling blocks in a more dynamic way, where the game could focus on dropping blocks into place, much like the traditional Tetris gameplay. In DropTris, players arrange falling shapes (tetrominoes) to create full lines that are then cleared from the screen. As the game progresses, the speed at which the blocks fall increases, making it more challenging. Falling Blocks: In DropTris, various shaped blocks (tetrominoes) fall from the top of the screen. The player must rotate and move the blocks to fit them into the empty spaces below. Clearing Lines: When a horizontal line is completely filled with blocks, it disappears, and the player earns points. The goal is to clear as many lines as possible before the screen fills up. Increasing Difficulty: As players progress, the speed of the falling blocks increases, making the game more challenging. Players must think faster and plan ahead to prevent the blocks from stacking to the top. Controls: The player can rotate the blocks (usually with arrow keys or the space bar), move them left or right, and accelerate their fall (typically with the down arrow key). Key Features: Simple, Intuitive Controls: Easy-to-learn controls for moving and rotating the tetrominoes make the game accessible to both new players and veterans. Endless Play: There is no end to the game except when the player fails to place the blocks. The objective is to clear as many lines as possible and achieve the highest score. Increased Challenge: The speed of the falling blocks gradually increases as the game progresses, providing a continually escalating challenge. Score System: Points are awarded based on the number of lines cleared, with higher points for clearing multiple lines at once (such as a "Tetris," where four lines are cleared in a single move). Classic Tetris Feel: The game stays true to the traditional Tetris mechanics, providing a nostalgic experience with modern web-based accessibility.

name: Drug Wars: A Game Based on the New York Drug Market
description: Written by a high school student and sometimes referred to as the "original GTA", the game has really nothing to do with Grand Theft Auto, and more to do with a stock market type simulation game that happens to have the theme of a drug dealer. In the game, you are given $2,000, and you need to buy and sell drugs to turn that into at least $5,500 to pay off your debt. As you move to different areas, time progresses, random events may occur, and the prices of the drugs changes. The game is presented in a distinct text mode system in monochrome, so you'll have to use your imagination. This game served as the inspiration for several other similar games, and was played by countless kids in high school IT labs back in the day.

name: Drum Blaster
description: Not really a game, more of a musical toy ... Drum Blaster is a virtual drum kit, where you can make simple songs by hitting different keys on your keyboard. Sounds range from different bassdrums and snares, to hihats, squeals, toms, etc. While unlikely to hold your interest for very long (even with included musical accompaniments) it might be a fun program for young children to play with. Drum Blaster is a classic DOS-based rhythm and music game that challenges players to keep up with a beat by pressing corresponding keys or buttons in sync with the music. The game is designed around a drumming theme, where players play as a drummer and must hit the right drum pads or keys at the correct time to keep the rhythm going. Rhythm-based Gameplay: The core mechanic of Drum Blaster revolves around timing. Players must press keys (or buttons) corresponding to drum sounds as they appear on the screen in sync with the music. The better the timing, the higher the score. Drum Pads and Beats: The game displays a set of virtual drum pads or keys, and a sequence of beats is presented. Players need to press the right keys to hit the corresponding drum pads on the screen, following the rhythm of the music. Increasing Difficulty: As players advance, the tempo of the music may increase, and the patterns become more complex. This escalation requires faster reflexes and better rhythm skills to continue progressing. Music Tracks: Drum Blaster features various music tracks that are central to the game. Each track typically has its own unique rhythm and style, which players must learn to follow. Score System: Players are scored based on how accurately they hit the right beats. Perfect timing earns the highest scores, while missing beats or pressing at the wrong time lowers the score. The goal is to achieve a high score and complete the music track. Visual Feedback: The game often includes visual cues that help players understand when they are playing in sync with the rhythm. This can include animated drum pads, flashing lights, or other visual effects that correspond to the beat. Simple Controls: The controls in Drum Blaster are typically simple, with players using keyboard keys (like the number keys or specific letter keys) to simulate pressing drum pads. In some versions, a mouse or game controller could be used. Challenging Gameplay: The game ramps up difficulty over time, with the music becoming faster, and the sequences requiring quicker responses. Players must improve their hand-eye coordination and sense of rhythm to succeed.

name: Dschump!
description: Dschump (according to the docs, it's pronounced "jump" and is sometimes simply referred to as Jump?) is an interesting action / planning game where you direct a bouncing ball as it progresses down the level path. The point of view is overhead, so you need to try to time your ball's bounces to collect bonuses and avoid obstacles. The screen scrolls up constantly so you need to plan ahead (using the map displayed on the right) and time your bounces properly. The graphics are pretty basic but get the job done.Dschump! is a classic DOS-based action puzzle game released in the early 1990s. The game features a unique mix of arcade action and strategic puzzle-solving, and is known for its quirky characters and mechanics. In Dschump!, the player controls a character navigating through levels, solving puzzles, and avoiding or dealing with various obstacles. Platformer Mechanics: Like many DOS-era games, Dschump! uses platforming mechanics where the player must jump between platforms, avoid obstacles, and reach the goal. Puzzle Elements: Along with platforming action, Dschump! introduces puzzle-solving elements where the player must figure out how to move through certain areas, interact with objects, and avoid hazards to advance. Challenging Levels: The game features multiple levels, each with its own set of challenges and enemies. The difficulty typically increases as the player progresses, with more complex puzzles and faster-paced action. Enemies and Hazards: Players encounter a variety of enemies and environmental hazards, such as spikes, moving platforms, or traps that must be avoided or neutralized. Power-ups and Items: Along the way, the player can collect power-ups and items that help them progress. These might include temporary boosts, health recovery items, or new abilities to overcome obstacles. Quirky Art and Sound: The game has a colorful and quirky visual style typical of early 90s DOS games. The characters and environments are often cartoonish and humorous. The sound effects and music contribute to the overall lighthearted atmosphere of the game. Simple Controls: Dschump! uses relatively simple controls for jumping, moving, and interacting with the environment. The player typically uses the keyboard for movement and actions, making the game easy to learn, but challenging to master.

name: Duck Hunt
description: First I have to note that NO, this is not a clone or remake of the classic NES Zapper-based game with the annoying dog that laughs at you. Instead, it is a very simplistic ASCII-mode game, where a single "duck" flies across the screen and you must hit the spacebar to shoot it down. Other than its theme, it's not very much similar to the NES classic, but I'm always intrigued by ASCII mode games, and the presentation of the game is done fairly well. Duck Hunt (DOS) refers to a version of the classic arcade shooting game Duck Hunt, which was originally released in 1984 by Nintendo for the NES (Nintendo Entertainment System). The DOS version, while not officially developed by Nintendo, is a fan-made or third-party port of the original game that was adapted to run on DOS-based systems, particularly during the 1990s when the PC gaming market was expanding. Mouse Control (or Keyboard): Unlike the original Duck Hunt which used a light gun, the DOS version typically uses a mouse to aim and shoot. Some versions might allow keyboard controls, but the mouse allows for a more precise aim, making the game easier to play on a PC. Multiple Ducks: Ducks fly across the screen in different patterns and speeds. In some versions, multiple ducks might fly at once, requiring the player to shoot more than one in a round. Dog Mocking Mechanism: Just like the NES version, Duck Hunt DOS features the familiar dog who appears when you miss a shot. If the hunter fails to shoot a duck, the dog appears and laughs at the player's mistake, adding an element of humor and challenge. Game Rounds: The game is divided into rounds, with each round presenting a new challenge of shooting a set number of ducks. After completing a round, the difficulty may increase, with ducks flying faster or in more complex patterns. Scoring: The game rewards points for each successful shot. Players earn points by shooting ducks, and bonus points are sometimes awarded for hitting multiple ducks in quick succession or for accuracy. Simple Sound and Graphics: The graphics and sound are relatively simple, mirroring the limitations of the era's technology. The pixelated graphics and minimal sound effects help maintain the nostalgic feel of the original arcade game, with quacking ducks and the dog’s mocking laugh as part of the audio. Increasing Difficulty: As the player progresses, the game becomes harder. Ducks might fly faster, appear in more difficult-to-hit patterns, or multiple ducks may appear at once. Quick reflexes and good aim become crucial as the game advances. Level Progression: The game may feature level progression where each new level introduces slightly tougher challenges or variations of the flying ducks. This keeps the game engaging as the player progresses.

name: Duck Hunt
description: Duck Hunt Flash is a web-based adaptation of the classic Duck Hunt game originally released for the Nintendo Entertainment System (NES) in 1984. In the Flash version, players take on the role of a hunter who must shoot ducks that fly across the screen, all while avoiding other challenges and obstacles. Simple, Intuitive Controls: The controls in Duck Hunt Flash are straightforward. Players use the mouse to aim the gun and click to shoot. The gameplay is easy to pick up, making it accessible to casual players. Multiple Rounds: The game is typically divided into rounds, with each round featuring ducks that fly at different speeds and patterns. The difficulty increases as the game progresses, requiring faster reflexes and better aiming. Point Scoring System: Each duck that is shot successfully rewards the player with points. Some versions may offer bonus points for shooting multiple ducks at once or hitting difficult-to-reach targets. Dog Mechanic: A defining feature of Duck Hunt is the inclusion of the mocking dog. In the Flash version, if the player misses a duck, the dog might appear to laugh at the player's failure, adding an extra challenge and humor to the game. Conversely, if the player successfully hits a duck, the dog may appear to retrieve the duck. Variety of Ducks: In some versions of the Flash game, there might be different types of ducks that fly at different speeds or in different patterns. This can add variety and make the game more challenging. Classic Retro Aesthetic: The Flash version often mimics the pixelated graphics and simple sound effects of the original NES game, maintaining a nostalgic feel while being accessible to a modern web audience. Increasing Difficulty: As the player progresses through the rounds, the ducks may fly faster or appear in more complex patterns, making the game progressively harder. Quick reflexes and good aim are essential to reach higher scores.

name: Duck Life
description: Duck Life is an engaging and whimsical Flash game that combines elements of simulation, racing, and training. Players take on the role of a duck trainer, nurturing their duck to become a champion racer. Game Overview: Objective: Players must train their duck in various skills to compete in races and ultimately become the best duck racer in the world. Gameplay Mechanics: Training Minigames: Players can train their duck in several skills, including running, swimming, flying, and climbing. Each skill is developed through fun minigames that test players’ reflexes and timing. Racing Competitions: Once trained, players enter their duck into races against other ducks. The outcome depends on the skills developed during training and the player's strategy. Earning Coins: Players earn coins from races and training, which can be used to purchase upgrades, food, and accessories for their duck. Features: Customization: Players can customize their ducks with various hats and outfits, adding a personal touch to their racing team. Multiple Seasons: The game includes different seasons with varying race difficulties, encouraging players to keep training and improving their ducks. Engaging Graphics: The game features colorful and charming graphics, bringing the duck world to life with a playful aesthetic. Visuals and Sound: Duck Life boasts a bright and cheerful art style, with lively animations and sound effects that enhance the playful atmosphere of the game. Duck Life is loved for its unique blend of training and racing mechanics, making it a favorite among fans of simulation and casual gaming, as well as those looking for a fun and lighthearted experience.

name: Duck Life 2
description: Duck Life 2 is a popular HTML-based simulation game and the second installment in the Duck Life series, originally created by Walt Disney Games and developed by Jesse Venbrux. In this game, players raise and train a duck to compete in various races and challenges. The goal is to improve your duck’s stats, such as speed, endurance, and agility, so it can win races and become the champion. Duck Training: Mini-games: Players can train their duck by playing various mini-games that help improve specific stats such as speed, stamina, strength, and agility. These mini-games include activities like flying, running, swimming, and jumping. Each training mini-game contributes to a specific skill, and the better the player performs in these mini-games, the higher the duck’s stats will become. Competitions and Races: After training, players can enter their ducks into races where the duck will compete against other ducks. These races are the main focus of the game, and the goal is to finish first to advance to the next level. The races are divided into different levels with increasing difficulty. Winning races allows players to earn coins and unlock new areas. Upgrades and Customization: Players can use the coins earned from winning races to buy upgrades and accessories for their duck. These upgrades can enhance the duck’s abilities and help improve race performance. Customization options allow players to make their duck look unique, from changing the appearance to upgrading its training equipment. Stats and Progression: Duck Stats: The duck has several stats that the player must manage and improve over time, such as speed, stamina, and endurance. These stats directly affect the duck’s performance in the races. As the player progresses, they will unlock new races with higher difficulty, requiring better-trained ducks to win. Cute Graphics and Animation: Duck Life 2 features bright and colorful graphics, with an adorable duck that players can train and compete with. The animations are simple yet effective, and the game appeals to players of all ages. Multiple Locations: The game includes various locations for the races, each with different environments and challenges. The player can unlock new race locations as they progress through the game. Simple Controls: The game uses mouse or keyboard controls, making it easy for players of all ages to navigate the training mini-games and races.

name: Duck Life 4
description: Overview: Duck Life 4 is an engaging simulation and adventure game that combines elements of racing, training, and customization. Players take on the role of a duck trainer, raising their duck to compete in various races and challenges, while also exploring a vibrant world. Adventure Exploration: Explore different areas, complete challenges, and interact with other characters to unlock new training opportunities and races. The animations are smooth, and the cheerful sound effects and music enhance the lighthearted and fun atmosphere of the game.
