Its blend of training, racing, and adventure makes it accessible and entertaining for both younger players and adults. Platforms: Originally a Flash game, Duck Life 4 can now be found on various gaming sites that support HTML5 or Flash emulation, making it easily accessible on desktops and laptops. Conclusion: With its mix of training, racing, and customization, Duck Life 4 invites players to embark on a fun journey to raise the ultimate racing duck. Are you ready to train your duck and claim victory in the races?

name: Duck Life: Treasure Hunt
description: Duck Life: Treasure Hunt Flash is a fun and engaging Flash-based adventure game that is part of the Duck Life series, developed by Walt Disney Games and Jesse Venbrux. Unlike the traditional racing games in the series, this particular installment focuses on exploration, puzzle-solving, and treasure hunting. In this game, players guide a duck on an adventure to uncover hidden treasures scattered across various levels, solve puzzles, and overcome obstacles. Treasure Hunting and Exploration: Players guide the duck through several environments such as caves, forests, and ruins to find hidden treasures. The goal is to explore every nook and cranny of each level, uncovering treasures and secrets along the way. Puzzle-Solving: The game features various puzzles that players must solve to progress through the levels. These could involve moving objects, triggering switches, or using the duck’s abilities (such as swimming, flying, or jumping) to reach hidden areas. Some puzzles also involve logic and timing, adding an extra layer of challenge. Mini-Games: There are various mini-games that players can engage in to earn rewards and upgrades. These mini-games are designed to be simple and fun but offer additional challenges to keep the gameplay interesting. Some mini-games involve actions like flying or swimming, while others might focus on timing or memory. Abilities and Upgrades: As the player progresses, the duck can improve its abilities, such as flying higher or swimming faster, which are essential for accessing certain areas and completing puzzles. Players can also unlock special items and upgrades that make exploration easier and more efficient. Charming Graphics and Animation: Duck Life: Treasure Hunt Flash has a bright and colorful art style typical of the Duck Life series. The world is cute and cartoonish, with simple yet appealing graphics. The animations are fluid, and the characters are designed with a lot of personality, giving the game a lighthearted and fun vibe. Collecting Treasures: The player’s goal is to find as many treasures as possible within the levels. Each level features hidden or difficult-to-reach treasures, and exploring the environment carefully is key to uncovering them. Treasures can be gems, coins, or special items that contribute to the player’s score and progress. Increasing Difficulty: As the game progresses, the puzzles become more challenging, and the treasures are placed in harder-to-reach locations. Some puzzles might require the player to unlock special abilities before they can collect all the items. Simple Controls: The game is controlled using the keyboard or mouse, depending on the version. The controls are simple and intuitive, making it easy for players to dive into the gameplay without a steep learning curve.

name: Ducks
description: Remember how addictive Lemmings was when you first played it? Well, Ducks borrows many aspects from Lemmings, but I find it even more enjoyable to play, because unlike Lemmings (where the little green-haired freaks move at their own pace), here YOU decide when/where they move.Ducks (DOS) is a classic, arcade-style DOS game that is based on a simple and fun premise. The game typically revolves around controlling a duck (or multiple ducks) in various scenarios, often involving actions like navigating through obstacles, collecting items, or completing challenges. The gameplay can be compared to other early DOS games in its simplicity and accessibility. Simple Mechanics: The game has straightforward controls, often using the keyboard for movement, allowing players to easily jump into the game. The player may control the duck by moving it left and right or using other commands to navigate the screen. Objective-Based Gameplay: Each level or stage in Ducks (DOS) might have a different goal. Common objectives include collecting items, avoiding enemies or obstacles, or reaching a specific location within a time limit. Levels and Increasing Difficulty: As players advance, the levels may increase in difficulty. Ducks may have to avoid more complex obstacles, face faster-moving enemies, or navigate through more difficult environments. In some versions, the game may have a progression system where players can unlock new levels or challenges as they complete earlier stages. Collectibles and Power-ups: In many levels, the player can collect various items or power-ups, which might help the duck navigate through dangerous areas or provide extra points or health. Power-ups could include items that make the duck faster, give it invincibility for a short time, or grant extra points. Simple Graphics: As with many early DOS games, Ducks features basic, pixelated graphics. The visuals are often colorful and charming in their simplicity, with the main character (the duck) being a central, easily recognizable sprite. The environments are similarly minimalistic, with clear and simple layouts that emphasize gameplay over complex visuals. Charming Sound Effects: The game includes basic sound effects, such as quacking, the sound of the duck flapping its wings, and various effects related to items or obstacles. While the sound design is simple, it adds to the nostalgic atmosphere of classic DOS games. Playability: Due to its simple mechanics and low system requirements, Ducks (DOS) is an accessible game that can be enjoyed by players of all ages. It's also quick to pick up and play, making it ideal for short, casual gaming sessions.

name: Duel
description: Duel is a two-player deathmatch game done in high-res text mode. One of its big features is a built-in editor which allows you to create your own levels. The game includes a wide variety of different objects that can be placed within the levels, and the color / character of each can be customized. However the game only includes one level set (ZONE.MAP) and I'm unaware of any other user-created maps available elsewhere. The editor is also not very intuitive to use (compared with something like ZZT for example. But if you have another person who's willing to play a 25+ year old textmode deathmatch game with you sharing the same keyboard, give it a shot!

name: Dueling Dragons
description: Dueling Dragons is a Snake / Nibbles / Tron variant where the object is to outlast your opponent and make them run into your tail or their own. Calling them "dragons" requires a bit of imagination since they just look like a string of dots. You can play a two-player game or a single player game against the PC. As you can see in the screenshot, the computer AI isn't great, but at least it gives you a chance and isn't super-human. You can speed up the game or slow it down, but other than that there aren't any options. It's a pretty basic Snake-type game.

name: DUFF
description: Duff is a Boulderdash-like game where the object is to collect the required number of skulls and get to the exit before time runs out. You'd figure you were supposed to avoid the skulls, but nope, collect 'em! As in Boulderdash, you can push blocks, which fall and roll in that weird Boulderdash way. There are other items you can collect for points, and seems like there are other useful items and dangerous hazards around too. Decent graphics, but for sound and music it requires a Gravis Ultrasound; if you're willing to set it up to work in DOSBox, it may sound nice? (Sound is disabled here but you can re-run DUFFSET.EXE to turn it on if you set up Ultrasound support.)

name: Duke Nukem
description: One of my all-time favorite action platformers. It just has excellent level design, items, enemies, and interactivity. This is the first appearance of Duke Nukem, who would go on to further fame in his 3D series of games. In the original game he has a little less attitude but the outline of the character he would become is definitely here. Duke Nukem (DOS) is the original DOS-based version of the iconic Duke Nukem franchise, created by 3D Realms (formerly Apogee Software). Released in 1991, Duke Nukem is a side-scrolling platformer that marks the first appearance of the now-famous character, Duke Nukem. This early version of the game differs significantly from the more well-known 3D first-person shooter series that would emerge in later years but still established many of the characteristics that would become a hallmark of the franchise. Side-Scrolling Action: Unlike later Duke Nukem titles, this version is a 2D side-scroller where Duke moves from left to right through various levels. The levels are often full of platforms, enemies, and obstacles, requiring quick reflexes and strategy to navigate. Players use the keyboard to control Duke's movements, jumping, and shooting, as they advance through the levels. Weapon and Combat: Duke Nukem uses a variety of weapons to defeat enemies. Early in the game, players have access to basic guns, but as they progress, they can unlock more powerful weapons to fight off increasingly difficult foes. Weapons include pistols, machine guns, and explosives, with some weapons offering greater firepower but limited ammo. Enemies and Boss Fights: Players face a variety of enemies, including aliens, robots, and other creatures. These enemies appear in different levels, often with unique attack patterns or abilities. Each stage typically concludes with a boss fight, where players must face a powerful enemy that requires skill and timing to defeat. Collectibles and Power-ups: As in many platformers, Duke Nukem features collectibles throughout the levels. These can include health packs, ammunition, and power-ups that grant Duke temporary boosts or enhancements, such as invincibility or rapid-fire weapons. Collecting coins, keys, or other items might also be necessary to unlock doors or progress through levels. Humor and Personality: A defining feature of Duke Nukem is the character’s personality. Even in this early game, Duke is portrayed as a macho, wise-cracking hero. His tough-guy attitude, humorous one-liners, and overall brashness are part of what made the character so memorable. This humor would carry through to the later 3D Duke Nukem games, particularly Duke Nukem 3D. Graphics and Design: The graphics in Duke Nukem (DOS) are typical of early 90s DOS platformers: pixelated and colorful but simple compared to later 3D titles. The environment design includes a variety of settings, including futuristic cities and alien landscapes, all presented with basic, yet distinct, sprites and backgrounds. The pixel art style is somewhat primitive but adds to the nostalgic charm of the game. Levels and Progression: The game is divided into several levels, each with its own theme and set of challenges. These range from city streets to underground bases, with each environment containing its own set of enemies, traps, and obstacles. Players must reach the end of each level while collecting items, defeating enemies, and avoiding hazards. The difficulty gradually increases, with more complex enemies and tougher platforming sequences.

name: Duke Nukem 3D
description: Duke Nukem 3D (DOS) is a landmark first-person shooter released in 1996 by 3D Realms. It is the third installment in the Duke Nukem franchise and one of the most influential games of its time, particularly in the evolution of 3D gaming. Unlike its predecessors, which were side-scrolling platformers, Duke Nukem 3D featured full 3D environments, introducing a new level of immersion and interactivity. Full 3D Environments: Duke Nukem 3D was one of the first FPS games to use true 3D environments. The game used the Build Engine, allowing for multi-floor environments, which was revolutionary at the time. This added verticality to the gameplay, with Duke able to move between different levels of a building, jump down from ledges, or climb ladders. Levels were often designed with intricate details, including destructible objects and interactive elements like mirrors, televisions, and water fountains. Weapon Variety: The game offered a wide range of weapons, many of which became iconic in the series. These included: Pistol: A basic but reliable weapon. Shotgun: A powerful close-range weapon. Machine Gun: For sustained fire. Rocket Launcher: To deal heavy damage to enemies and structures. Pipe Bombs: Throwable explosive devices that could be strategically placed. Freeze Ray: A weapon that could freeze enemies, allowing Duke to shatter them with a single shot. The diversity of weapons allowed players to tackle different combat situations in creative ways. Enemies: Duke faces a variety of enemies, including alien invaders, mutated creatures, robotic enemies, and enemy soldiers. Each enemy has unique behaviors and attack patterns, making combat encounters dynamic and exciting. Notable enemies include Pig Cops (mutated police officers), Octabrains (floating brains with psychic abilities), and Battlelords (powerful alien soldiers). Exploration and Interactivity: One of the standout features of Duke Nukem 3D was the emphasis on environmental interactivity. Duke could open doors, press buttons, flip switches, ride elevators, and even destroy objects in the environment. Some levels featured puzzles that required players to find keys, secret areas, or hidden items. Exploration was rewarded with power-ups and health restoratives, encouraging players to thoroughly search each level. Easter eggs: The game was known for its humorous and hidden references, including arcade machines, posters, and interactive items. Humor and Personality: Duke Nukem’s personality and humor were defining features of the game. His one-liners and catchphrases (such as "Hail to the king, baby!" and "It's time to kick ass and chew bubblegum... and I'm all outta gum!") became iconic in gaming culture. The game’s satirical humor, adult themes, and pop-culture references gave it a unique and irreverent tone, appealing to players who enjoyed a mix of action and comedy. Multiplayer: Duke Nukem 3D featured multiplayer support, including Deathmatch and Cooperative modes. Players could compete against each other in head-to-head matches or team up to fight against enemies. The game supported LAN play (Local Area Network), allowing players to connect via a network and engage in multiplayer battles. Levels and Progression: The game includes a variety of levels, ranging from urban environments and government buildings to alien-infested spaceships and secret military bases. The progression through levels was nonlinear, allowing players to explore different paths and secrets. Boss fights at the end of certain levels required players to use strategy and their arsenal of weapons to defeat giant enemies, often with a unique twist.

name: Duke Nukem II
description: Between the original, classic Duke and the kickass Duke Nukem 3D came the unheralded sequel, Duke II. (Which really would've been Duke 4, if you counted the "registered-only" episodes 2 and 3.) The main advantages of the sequel over the original are in the areas of its graphics (in-game graphics, besides the introduction and some cutscenes, are still EGA, but they look better) and sound (SB instead of the PC speaker).Duke Nukem II (DOS) is a side-scrolling platformer released in 1993 as the second game in the Duke Nukem series. Developed by Apogee Software (later known as 3D Realms), it followed the original Duke Nukem (1991) and was a significant step up, introducing more advanced gameplay and graphics compared to its predecessor. This title laid the foundation for the later, much more famous Duke Nukem 3D, although it retained the classic 2D side-scrolling gameplay.

name: Dune Tank
description: "Dune Tank" is a side-scrolling action game where players command a formidable tank traversing desert landscapes. The primary objective is to navigate through various levels, obliterating obstacles and enemy vehicles, while collecting stars to boost your score. Players must manage their tank's health and ammunition, ensuring they reach the end of each level efficiently. Gameplay Mechanics: Movement: Use the arrow keys to drive the tank forward, backward, and to adjust its aim. Shooting: Press the spacebar to fire the tank's cannon, destroying obstacles and enemy units in your path. Objectives: Complete each level by reaching the endpoint swiftly, destroying obstacles, and collecting stars for bonus points. The game comprises 10 levels, each presenting unique challenges and increasing difficulty. Strategic movement and precise shooting are essential to overcome obstacles and adversaries effectively. Although originally a Flash game, "Dune Tank" remains accessible on platforms that have preserved Flash games through emulation technologies.

name: Dungeon
description: Dungeon won't win any awards for the most original name, in fact it may be confused with several other games. (See elsewhere for Dungeon Crawl, a much more sophisticated Roguelike game.) But despite that, it does offer simplified Roguelike gameplay. Each level is randomly generated and includes treasure to collect and monsters to fight, along with the ASCII text-mode "graphics" popular in the Roguelike genre. One potential problem is that use of the numeric keypad is required, so it won't be easy to play this game on most laptops or other keyboards which lack a keypad. (Note: This game also includes its source code in what looks to be BASICA/GW-BASIC files.)

name: Dungeon Crawl
description: Dungeon Crawl (aka "Lindsey's Dungeon Crawl", after its author) is a Roguelike game in the spirit of Rogue, Nethack, ADOM and many others. The game is continually being refined and improved by "a small group of developers". I didn't play it long enough to really discern what differentiates it from other games like Nethack, so if you're a fan of this genre, you'll have to play it for yourself. If you don't know what a "Roguelike" is, you might want to try Rogue or Nethack first.Dungeon Crawl (DOS), often referred to as Dungeon Crawl Stone Soup (though the modern version is known by the full name), is a roguelike dungeon crawl game that was originally developed for DOS-based systems. This game has roots in the classic roguelike genre, where players navigate procedurally generated dungeons, battling monsters, collecting items, and progressing deeper into increasingly dangerous levels.

name: Dungeon Explorer - Dungeon of the Beast
description: Dungeon Explorer (no relation to the console series most famous on the TG-16) is a simple RPG with no real story, you're just a guy who's out for adventure. Actually the game is intended as more of a framework for RPGs, with the shareware "mini RPG" giving you a taste of what the full-length games would be like.Dungeon Explorer - Dungeon of the Beast (DOS) is a classic dungeon crawler that was released in the 1990s for DOS-based systems. This game fits within the RPG and action-adventure genres, combining exploration, puzzle-solving, and combat in a dungeon setting. Although it didn't achieve the same widespread fame as some other dungeon crawlers of its era, it has maintained a loyal following among fans of retro PC RPGs. Dungeon Exploration: Dungeon Explorer - Dungeon of the Beast features exploration-based gameplay where players move through various dungeon levels. The dungeon itself is grid-based, and players will have to navigate a series of mazes, opening doors, finding secret passages, and unlocking new areas. The game world is largely nonlinear, allowing players to explore multiple paths, search for hidden treasures, and uncover lore. Combat System: Players engage in real-time combat against a variety of monsters. Weapons such as swords, bows, and magical items can be used in battle, with each character class offering a different combat style. The combat system is designed to be straightforward but requires strategic thinking, as enemies often come in swarms and may have unique abilities or resistances. Character Classes: The game offers different character classes, each with its own strengths, weaknesses, and abilities. Players can choose from various heroes, such as warriors, mages, archers, and more. These classes affect how players approach combat, puzzle-solving, and exploration. Some classes may specialize in melee combat, while others focus on casting powerful spells from a distance. The choice of character class influences the game's difficulty and overall playstyle. Spells and Abilities: Dungeon Explorer allows players to cast a variety of spells that can assist in combat or provide utility in exploration. These spells can heal, damage enemies, unlock doors, or provide buffs. Magic items may also be scattered throughout the dungeon, adding an extra layer of complexity and excitement for players who enjoy finding new tools to help in their quest. Monsters and Enemies: The dungeon is filled with a wide range of monsters. These include standard enemies like goblins and skeletons, as well as tougher creatures such as dragons and undead bosses. Some monsters are more intelligent than others, requiring players to use specific strategies to defeat them. Additionally, some enemies may drop valuable loot upon death. Puzzle-Solving: Dungeon Explorer includes puzzles that players must solve to proceed. These puzzles can range from simple key-and-door mechanics to more complex environmental puzzles that require finding items or triggering specific events. Some sections of the dungeon may involve navigating through traps or finding the correct sequence to open secret passages or treasure rooms. Loot and Inventory: Players can collect loot such as weapons, armor, potions, and gold from defeated enemies or hidden chests. Managing your inventory is key, as you may only be able to carry a limited number of items at once. Weapons and armor can be upgraded, allowing players to tailor their equipment to their preferred playstyle. Items can be used to heal, buff, or provide other helpful effects in the dungeon. Story and Atmosphere: The game's story revolves around a quest to defeat a powerful enemy, often referred to as the "Beast" that threatens the world. As the player progresses through the dungeon, they uncover clues about the Beast's origins and its ultimate plan. The atmosphere of the game is dark and ominous, with mood-setting music and sound effects that enhance the sense of danger in the dungeon. The deeper the player goes, the more oppressive and threatening the dungeon becomes. Multiplayer: Some versions of Dungeon Explorer - Dungeon of the Beast (DOS) feature multiplayer options, allowing players to team up with friends to explore the dungeon together. Cooperative play adds an extra layer of enjoyment, as players can work together to defeat tougher enemies and solve more complex puzzles. It also enhances the social experience of the game.

name: Dungeon Hack
description: Dungeon Hack, as the name implies, combines some of the randomized elements that make the various roguelike "Hack" games (like Nethack and Rogue) popular, and putting them into a first-person perspective RPG. The publisher SSI was well known for their line of D&D based games, and this game fits in well with other well-known games in the genre like Eye of the Beholder.Dungeon Hack (DOS) is a first-person dungeon crawler RPG released in 1993 by Strategic Simulations, Inc. (SSI). The game was developed for the DOS platform and is notable for its procedurally generated dungeons, which provided players with a unique experience each time they played. This feature was especially innovative for its time, as it allowed for a high level of replayability. Procedurally Generated Dungeons: One of the standout features of Dungeon Hack is its procedurally generated dungeon system. Every time a new game is started, the layout of the dungeon is different, providing a fresh experience with each playthrough. The dungeon levels are randomized, and this randomness affects not only the layout but also the placement of monsters, items, traps, and other key elements of the game world. This ensures a highly replayable experience, as no two runs are the same. First-Person Perspective: The game uses a first-person perspective, similar to other dungeon crawlers of the era like Eye of the Beholder and Lands of Lore. Players navigate through the dungeon using this perspective, exploring hallways, rooms, and encountering enemies in a more immersive way compared to top-down RPGs. The grid-based movement adds a strategic element to exploration, as players must consider their movement carefully to avoid getting trapped or ambushed. Character Creation and Progression: Dungeon Hack features a character creation system, where players can choose from different classes such as fighter, mage, thief, or cleric. Each class comes with its own set of abilities, strengths, and weaknesses. As players progress through the dungeon, their character levels up, gaining new abilities, improving stats, and acquiring better equipment. This progression system is central to the game, as players grow stronger and more capable of handling the increasingly difficult dungeon levels. Combat System: The game features turn-based combat, where the player and enemies take turns attacking. Combat can be against a wide range of creatures, including goblins, undead, and other fantasy monsters. Some enemies may have special abilities, which require strategic thinking to defeat. The game allows for both melee and ranged combat, and different character classes have access to different types of weapons and spells, depending on their class. Magic plays a significant role, and spellcasters can cast a variety of spells to damage enemies, heal wounds, or protect themselves. Items and Loot: Dungeon Hack features an extensive system for collecting loot. Players can find weapons, armor, potions, and scrolls throughout the dungeon. Items are crucial for surviving the dungeon’s challenges. Players must carefully manage their inventory, making decisions about which items to keep and which to leave behind. Magical items with special properties are also scattered throughout the dungeon. These can greatly enhance the player’s abilities, whether by providing buffs, summoning creatures, or increasing stats. Traps and Puzzles: The dungeon is filled with traps and hazards that can hinder progress. These traps can range from poison gas and spike pits to hidden magical effects. Players must be cautious and use their wits to avoid these dangers. Some areas may also contain puzzles that must be solved to progress further into the dungeon or unlock treasure chests.

name: Dungeon Quest
description: Dungeon Quest is a turn-based first-person perspective dungeon crawl game, developed over a period of six months. This "test drive" version of the game allows you to play the first level, and you don't get any sound effects. Nonetheless, the levels seem to be randomly generated, and the game plays decently, with monsters to fight and items to collect and use. The user interface is a confusing jumble of icons which you can use to navigate the maze, manipulate your inventory and equipped items, and otherwise interact. The mouse is available for use which is a big plus. It also includes an auto-map. Overall the game looks decent, unfortunately it's limited to only a single level, and generally seems pretty challenging.

name: Dungeon Thief
description: Dungeon Thief is essentially a simple ASCII-based maze game. Only a small portion of the maze is revealed at a time, and you must avoid the various baddies and find your way to the exit while collecting treasure. There isn't too much more to the game than that really, but it's a low-stress exercise to be sure. There's also a lot of text contained within the menu, including the designer's philosophy on game design and other boring tidbits. (Run the game in color by typing "DTDEMO COLOR" at the command prompt.)

name: Dungeons of Death
description: Dungeons of Death is a first-person perspective role playing game, similar to classics like Dungeon Hack or Eye of the Beholder. The game's graphics are not great, but the gameplay is simple and intuitive. There is no long story or complicated control scheme. Attacking monsters is done by timing presses of the Spacebar, which is a lot tougher than it sounds! Overall a quick and enjoyable game, with maps randomly generated each time you play!Dungeons of Death (DOS) is a dungeon crawler RPG that was released for the DOS platform, offering players a traditional role-playing experience with exploration, combat, and treasure hunting in a dark and dangerous dungeon environment. Although not as widely known as some other dungeon crawlers of its time, it still holds a place in the hearts of fans of the genre for its engaging gameplay and classic mechanics. Dungeon Exploration: The game is centered around exploring a dark and labyrinthine dungeon. The dungeon is designed to be a maze, and players need to navigate through various levels and rooms, all while dealing with enemies and traps. Players will uncover hidden passages, treasure rooms, and other secrets, encouraging thorough exploration and a methodical approach to progression. First-Person Perspective: Dungeons of Death (DOS) features a first-person perspective, immersing players directly into the dungeon environment as they explore its corridors and face off against enemies. The first-person view allows for a more intense, personal experience as players have to physically "see" their enemies and the dungeon's traps as they navigate through it. Turn-Based Combat: Combat in Dungeons of Death is turn-based, meaning that each action the player takes (whether moving, attacking, or using items) counts as one turn. This system requires strategic thinking, as players must plan out their actions while dealing with enemy turns. Players will encounter a variety of monsters, from simple creatures like goblins to more dangerous and powerful enemies that guard deeper levels of the dungeon. Character Classes and Abilities: Players can choose from different character classes, each with its own strengths and weaknesses. Some classes may excel in melee combat, while others specialize in magic or ranged attacks. As players progress, their character can level up, gaining new abilities, improving stats, and unlocking more powerful spells or combat techniques. Character progression is central to surviving the deeper and more dangerous parts of the dungeon. Weapons and Items: Throughout the dungeon, players will find a variety of weapons, armor, potions, and other useful items. These items can help players survive the dungeon, heal from injuries, or enhance their combat abilities. Managing your inventory becomes an important part of the game, as players must decide which items to carry and which to leave behind. Some items can be used in combat, while others might be necessary for solving puzzles or overcoming specific challenges.

name: Dungeons of Drakklor
description: Dungeons of Drakklor is an action adventure game with some unique elements. Although it may look like it could be an RPG, it's actually closer to a more intentionally designed puzzle-like version of Gauntlet. Also, it may appear at first that the game is using a graphics mode, but it's actually using textmode with a modified character set (similarly to how Megazeux works) and two characters for every "sprite". Dungeons of Drakklor (DOS) is a classic dungeon crawler RPG released for the DOS platform in the 1990s. This game combines elements of exploration, combat, and puzzle-solving within a dungeon setting. Players venture into the depths of a mysterious dungeon known as Drakklor, where they face challenges, battle monsters, and seek treasure while unraveling the mysteries of the dungeon. Dungeon Exploration: Dungeons of Drakklor features grid-based exploration, where players move through different levels of the dungeon in search of treasure, hidden rooms, and key items. The game encourages thorough exploration, with various locked doors, hidden paths, and secret rooms that can only be unlocked through solving puzzles or defeating specific monsters. First-Person Perspective: The game utilizes a first-person perspective, offering an immersive experience as players navigate the dark corridors and interact with the environment from the character's viewpoint. This perspective adds tension and excitement, especially during combat or when exploring dangerous parts of the dungeon. Combat System: Combat in Dungeons of Drakklor is turn-based, allowing players to engage in strategic battles with the many monsters that inhabit the dungeon. Players can use a variety of weapons (swords, axes, etc.), magic spells, and items to fight enemies. Each character class has a different set of combat abilities, and choosing the right approach to battle is key to success. Character Classes and Abilities: Players can choose from several character classes, such as warrior, mage, archer, or rogue. Each class has its own set of strengths, abilities, and weaknesses, which influence how they approach combat, exploration, and puzzle-solving. For example, mages can use powerful spells, while warriors are better suited for close combat. As players progress, they can level up their characters, improving stats and unlocking new abilities. Magic System: The game features a magic system where spellcasters can learn and cast various spells to assist in combat or solve puzzles. Spells can be used for healing, damage, or even altering the environment (e.g., revealing hidden doors or dispelling traps). Magic plays a central role in advancing through the dungeon, as certain areas may require specific spells to unlock or defeat enemies. Puzzles and Traps: Dungeons of Drakklor includes a variety of puzzles that must be solved to progress. Some puzzles are straightforward, such as finding keys to open doors, while others are more complex, involving riddles or manipulating the dungeon’s environment. The dungeon is also filled with traps that can harm or kill the player. These traps range from spike pits to magical traps that curse or debuff the player. Players must remain vigilant and use their wits to avoid these hazards.

name: Dungeons of Grimlor
description: Dungeons of Grimlor is a mild action/adventure hybrid game where the object is to "Find the Evil Dragon Grimlor and retrieve the GEM of Souls!". This actually means fighting through many EGA dungeons and fighting some monsters. :) The game shows potential but in my testing the graphics were quite choppy and slow which made the game a bit tough to play. Still it seems like a reasonably large sized adventure game. (Press the 'S' key to slow down the game, and 'F' to speed it up.) Although it was originally shareware, the full game has now been released for free by the developer.

name: Dungeons of Grimlor II: The Lich
description: Dungeons of Grimlor 2 is the sequel to the original Dungeons of Grimlor game which seemingly uses the same engine (or maybe a modified / improved version) and offers up much of the same sort of gameplay. The dragon from the first game is back (in "lich" form, aka undead) and you must find & defeat it. The game is more of an action / maze / puzzle game than a dungeon crawl per se, and the admittedly pretty graphics are a bit choppy. But still there is a lot of adventuring available in this game. Although originally shareware, the developer released the entire game (all episodes) for free.

name: Dungeons of Kairn
description: Dungeons of Kairn shares much in common with prototypical CRPGs such as the early SSI series. The story is generic fantasy stuff: An evil mage is threatening the land, and your band of five adventurers must stop him. The game is presented in an overhead CGA graphic viewpoint when you explore an overworld and enter towns and other areas whereupon the view switches to a text-mode type interface. Random battles take place on a grid where you move your characters and fight groups of monsters. Looks like a decent game for those who are into the genre, but definitely not an easy one to pick up and play, with its many keyboard keys to memorize and conventions to learn.

name: Dungeons of Noudar
description: No doubt inspired by older turn-based first-person RPG games such as the SSI games, as well as perhaps more modern interpretations such as id Software's Orcs & Elves, Dungeons of Noudar is a simple but enjoyable old-school RPG experience. You play a priest / crusader called into the citadel to purge it from demonic forces. Instead of a life/health stat, you must maintain "faith" in order to survive. Movement takes place one block at a time, and it is turn-based, so you can carefully plan your next moves without having to worry about being attacked. Unlike some older games, you are provided with a deep field of view, rather than just a few blocks ahead.

name: Dunjax
description: Dunjax is not a dungeon-crawling / RPG as you might surmise from its name. Instead it is a side-scrolling run and gun game, where you fight your way through hordes of demons and other monsters Contra-style. Your character can jump quite high (although you're somewhere in outer space I think so maybe it's just reduced planetary gravity) and have unlimited ammo. Dunjax (DOS) is a classic dungeon crawler RPG released for the DOS platform. The game is set in a dungeon environment, where players explore different levels, battle monsters, solve puzzles, and seek treasure. It is designed for fans of old-school roguelikes and turn-based RPGs that enjoy a mix of strategy, exploration, and combat. Here's an overview of the game: Dungeon Exploration: The core of Dunjax is exploring the dungeon. Players move through its maze-like corridors and rooms, looking for keys, hidden items, and monsters to battle. The movement is turn-based, and players need to plan their next moves carefully to avoid getting ambushed by enemies or stepping into traps. Each level of the dungeon is typically a grid layout filled with different challenges, including enemy encounters, locked doors, traps, and hidden treasures. Combat System: Dunjax features turn-based combat, where players and enemies take turns attacking or using abilities. Players can attack enemies with melee weapons, magic spells, or ranged attacks, depending on the character's class and abilities. Monsters in the dungeon vary in difficulty, and each type has its own behavior, requiring different tactics to defeat. Character Progression: Players can choose from different character classes such as warriors, mages, rogues, or others, each with unique abilities and stats. As players defeat monsters and solve puzzles, their character earns experience points, which are used to level up and improve stats like strength, agility, health, and magic power. The character’s progression includes learning new abilities, gaining better equipment, and improving stats to tackle the tougher challenges of the dungeon. Some items can be used to heal, enhance abilities, or unlock paths. Loot is randomly generated and adds an element of excitement as players discover new gear. Spells can have various effects, such as healing, attacking enemies, or solving puzzles. Managing magic resources (like spell points or mana) becomes critical as players delve deeper into the dungeon. Spells might be essential for overcoming certain monsters or obstacles.

name: Dustman
description: Dustman is a strange game that rewards patience and planning but doesn't offer much action or any puzzles to solve. You play as a dustman (aka garbage man) who must run around collecting bin liners (garbage bags) from all around the town. You have a limited time and can only carry 5 at once. (You can carry more but you may drop some as you move, causing a time penalty.) You just need to bring them all back to where you start the game before the timer runs out. It's not particularly fun or challenging but it IS unique and does actually work. Make sure to choose VGA at the beginning, because the ASCII version is borderline unplayable. The game comes with a sprite designer to create your own sprites, if you're REALLY bored.

name: Dutch Shuffleboard

name: Dynamic
description: Dynamic is an impressive space shooter which was coded in QuickBasic. You are a ... space ship, and your job is to blast stuff. The first few stages you're blasting asteroids, but after that you start battling enemy spacecraft. One interesting aspect of the early stages is that you're supplementing your space station's turrets, so they will sometimes destroy asteroids for you. The resolution of the game is high and it offers decent graphics and visual effects. The gameplay is decent, but not particularly great. (The enemy spacecraft don't exactly have good AI.) Overall a very impressive display of what QuickBasic was capable of. (Source code is unfortunately NOT included.)

name: DynaMine
description: DynaMine is a Tetris falling-block game knock-off with some unique features and a simultaneous two-player mode. In addition to clearing horizontal lines to move to the next level, you also must clear a number of gems from the playing field by including them in your horizontal lines. The first level starts with one, but later levels can have many. There are also more piece patterns than the typical Tetris game, some having three or five blocks. There are also special blocks that can appear, and even bombs that you can pick up and drop into the playing field, exploding and destroying everything within a certain radius. The two-player mode is a nice addition as well, so that you can play a head-to-head competition.

name: Dynamo Draughts
description: Draughts (aka "Checkers") is a strategy-based board game for two players. The object is to collect all of your opponents' pieces by jumping over them. This computerized version contains playing options, including adjustable board sizes from tiny 4x4 up to larger-than-usual 10x10. It includes three built-in settings: USA Pool, International, and Spanish, although you can customize it yourself. Strangely there doesn't seem to be a two-player option, so you must play against the computer, and there are no difficulty settings. There are a lot of other things though, like records of all the moves, saving / loading a game, etc. It uses the "WINDOS" system to simulate a Windows-like look in DOS.

name: Dzzee
description: Modern DOS games are still being created, and Dzzee is a great example of a simple but graphically impressive game that is fun to play. It looks sort of like Tempest, and gameplay is simple: Stay on the lines and avoid the gaps. The whole structure rotates around and you need to move up and down on the lines to avoid those gaps. The game looks good and plays fluidly, and there are subtle variations of the gameplay that evolve as you continue playing. There is a Windows 95 (and beyond) version includes, and even a version that uses Glide 3Dfx mode if you want to try that, although it seems like it is not working on real hardware at the moment.

name: Eamon
description: Eamon (aka "The Wonderful World of Eamon") is an example of a very early PC RPG game. Originally created by Donald Brown on the Apple II in 1979, this version was ported by Jon Walker nearly 10 years later. It is text-based, and after creating your character and rolling your stats, you enter commands to perform actions, working sort of like a simple text adventure game, but one with more emphasis on weapons, armor, and combat. The town provides a place to make your purchases. The game itself is pretty bare-bones, but since it was based on a game from 1979 we can probably overlook that! The EAMON.DOC file contains some important information regarding player stats and other things that aren't clearly explained in the game, but at least it gives you a list of commands if you enter some word that the game isn't expecting (ex, "TAKE" instead of "GET")

The sound design includes satisfying engine roars and the crunch of zombies being run over, adding to the game's excitement. Earn to Die is widely enjoyed for its addictive gameplay, customization options, and thrilling zombie encounters, making it a standout title in the Flash gaming community.

name: Earth Invasion
description: Earth Invasion is a simple one-on-one (or one-on-two, three, etc) space shooting / fighting game. There is a stereotypical sci-fi space-opera storyline of some sort (I admit, I didn't read it ...) before being directed into combat to shoot an enemy ship or group of ships and try to avoid being shot. Your ship and opponents' sprites are large so there isn't a large area to maneuver. There does seem to be a boss at the end of each stage, and the graphics are decent enough. But the game itself is pretty basic with not a lot of engaging gameplay going on.

name: Earth Taken
description: Earth Taken is a retro-style Flash game that combines elements of shooting and adventure set in a post-apocalyptic world overrun by aliens. Players take on the role of a survivor navigating through a desolate environment, facing various challenges and enemies. Key Features: Survival Gameplay: Players must gather weapons, resources, and health items to fend off alien threats and stay alive. Diverse Enemies: Encounter different types of alien creatures, each with unique attack patterns that require strategic thinking to defeat. Pixel Art Style: The game features a simple yet atmospheric pixel art design that enhances the grim setting. Exploration and Puzzles: Players explore various levels, solving puzzles to progress and uncover the story behind the invasion. Overall, Earth Taken emphasizes survival and strategy, challenging players to adapt and overcome obstacles in a hostile world. If you have any specific questions about the game or need tips, feel free to ask!

name: Earthworm Jim 1 & 2: The Whole Can O' Worms
description: The Earthworm Jim games are gaming classics, most famous on the 16-bit consoles (SNES and Genesis) but the games were also available for computer platforms such as DOS, WIndows, and Mac. The verbosely titled "Earthworm Jim 1 & 2: The Whole Can O' Worms" is a collection of both of the first two games in a single package. All of the great animation and sounds from the games are here, as well as the levels. Unlike many early PC ports, the Earthworm Jim games translated very well to PCs. Run and gun in this demo version that offers levels from both games.

Some versions might offer a hint button that can be used a limited number of times per puzzle or level. Power-Ups or Bonuses: Some versions of the game may include power-ups, like a shuffle option to rearrange pieces randomly or auto-place features to help speed up the puzzle completion process. Players might receive bonus points for completing puzzles quickly or without hints.

name: Easter Zuma
description: Zuma match 3 game for Easter. Do not let the easter bunnies reach the exit.Easter Zuma (HTML) is an exciting and festive match-3 marble shooter game with an Easter theme. In this game, players control a slingshot or shooter that fires colored marbles into a moving chain of marbles. The goal is to match three or more marbles of the same color to eliminate them and prevent the chain from reaching a certain endpoint. Easter-Themed Marbles: The marbles in Easter Zuma (HTML) are decorated with Easter-related designs such as Easter eggs, bunnies, flowers, and other springtime motifs. The bright, festive visuals add to the cheerful theme of the game, making it ideal for the Easter season. Match-3 Mechanics: Players shoot marbles to match three or more marbles of the same color in the chain. Once matched, the marbles will disappear. Players can aim and shoot the marbles by controlling the slingshot or marble shooter, carefully positioning it to create combinations and clear the chain. Levels and Difficulty: Easter Zuma typically has multiple levels, each increasing in difficulty. As players progress, the speed of the moving marble chain increases, and the layout may become more complex. In later levels, players may encounter obstacles or different marble types, requiring new strategies to clear the chains. Power-Ups and Bonuses: Throughout the game, players can earn or activate power-ups that help them clear marbles more efficiently. Common power-ups include: Bombs: Clears a small area of marbles from the chain. Rainbow Marbles: Can match with any color of marble, providing a strategic advantage. Slowdown: Temporarily slows down the speed of the marble chain, giving players more time to aim.

name: Eat It
description: Eat It is a Pac-Man clone. The author is careful to never make reference to the classic arcade game in the included documentation, but it's obvious which game this is imitating. The basic gameplay is the same as Pac-Man: Gobble up the "candies" (pellets) and avoid the ghosts, and eat the "super candies" to turn the tables on the ghosts and eat THEM. Here though you're a simple yellow ball rather than the classic yellow pizza shape. There is the option to redefine keys which is always welcomed, and you can have up to four players taking turns. (It would've been interesting to have all four at once, but probably more than the keyboard can handle!) Overall it's pretty basic but it does work.

name: EdChess
description: EdChess (later re-published as commercial software under the more generic and enthusiastic name Chess!) is a computer chess program in text-mode. It allows play of two human players, play against the CPU, or watching a CPU vs CPU match. The pieces are represented crudely with 3x3 or 3x2 ASCII boxes. You can change the ability of the CPU by modifying the "difficulty" (maximum thinking time for the computer) and "think ahead" (whether the CPU can be processing while you're making your move). You can also review the moves made by going forward or backward. Overall it's a fairly basic but competent chess program.

name: Effing Worms
description: Overview: Effing Worms is a quirky and entertaining action game where players control a giant worm that wreaks havoc in a vibrant, destructible environment. As the worm, you burrow through the ground, consuming anything in your path, including humans and animals, while trying to grow larger and survive. Gameplay Mechanics: Controls: Use the mouse to control the worm's movement, guiding it through the terrain to hunt for food and avoid threats. Objective: Consume as many creatures as possible to grow your worm while avoiding obstacles and dangers that can harm you. Power-Ups: As you progress, players can collect power-ups that enhance your abilities, such as speed boosts and health regeneration. Visuals and Audio: Effing Worms features colorful, cartoonish graphics with exaggerated animations that add to the game's humor. The sound effects, including squelching and munching sounds, combined with a lively soundtrack, create an engaging atmosphere. Target Audience: This game appeals to players of all ages who enjoy casual, action-packed gameplay with a humorous twist. Its easy-to-learn mechanics make it accessible for newcomers, while the challenge of achieving high scores keeps players returning for more. Platforms: Originally a Flash game, Effing Worms can now be found on various gaming sites that support HTML5 or Flash emulation, allowing players to enjoy it on desktops and laptops. Conclusion: With its unique concept and entertaining gameplay, Effing Worms invites players to dive into a world of chaos and consumption. Are you ready to grow your worm and cause some mayhem?

name: EGA EcoMaster
description: EcoMaster is "an ecology simulation in which you try to predict how animals will survive in a series of different environments or biomes" according to the FILE_ID.DIZ file. Each round you bid on animals (like in an auction) and those you bid on will enter the current environment. I guess you're supposed to decide which animals will thrive the best based on the location? It seems like it could be an interesting game but also a bit shallow and confusing at the same time. You can have up to two human players, and the CPU player (the "EcoMaster") always plays. Decent clipart type pictures of the different animals, but generally not the kind of game I would personally be interested in playing ...

name: EGA Poker
description: This is a fairly basic but well done version of draw poker. You use the mouse to make your bet, then decide whether to draw or stay, etc. The only bad thing is that the different suits can sometimes be hard to distinguish. Other than that it's easy to play, although you won't win any money playing this, even if it turns out that you're unnaturally good at this "gambling" game.EGA Poker (DOS) is a classic poker simulation game released for the DOS platform during the 1980s and early 1990s. The game allows players to engage in various poker games with computer opponents, and it was designed to offer a realistic poker experience within the limitations of early personal computer graphics and interfaces. Classic Poker Variants: Texas Hold'em: The most popular version of poker, where each player is dealt two cards and shares five community cards. Five-Card Draw: Each player is dealt five cards, and the goal is to make the best hand by discarding and drawing new cards. Seven-Card Stud: Players receive seven cards, some face-up and others face-down, and must form the best hand out of the seven cards. AI Opponents: Players face off against computer-controlled opponents who each have their own strategies and betting behaviors. AI opponents are typically programmed to bluff, raise bets, or fold based on the current situation, simulating a more realistic poker environment. Simple EGA Graphics: The game was designed for the EGA graphics standard, which provided 16 colors for visuals. The graphics, while primitive by today’s standards, still offered clear card representations and basic animation for dealing and betting actions. The user interface included a table with a visible pot, player cards, and actions such as bet, raise, fold, and check. Betting and Payout System: Players could place bets, raise, call, or fold based on the strength of their hands and the community cards revealed during the game. The game typically follows a standard poker payout system, with players winning chips or virtual money based on the hand rankings they achieve. Poker Hands and Ranking: EGA Poker follows the standard poker hand rankings: Royal Flush Straight Flush Four of a Kind Full House Flush Straight Three of a Kind Two Pair One Pair High Card Players aim to build the highest-ranking hand possible based on the cards they are dealt. Game Modes: Single-Player Mode: Players compete against the computer, which simulates human-like betting behavior and decision-making. Multiplayer Mode (if available): In some versions, players can compete against other human players, either through local networks or hot-seat play where players take turns.

name: EGA Roids
description: A pretty good conversion of the classic game 'Asteroids'. You won't find any bells & whistles here, but it does present solid gameplay and smooth flowing graphics, in the then-new EGA "high-res" graphics mode. The only real problem is that the keys take a bit of getting used to ... using the arrow keys would've been much easier! If you can get used to the odd key placement, you'll probably like it. (Pay attention to the keyboard key instructions when the game starts.)EGA Roids (DOS) is a classic arcade-style shooter game that was designed for the DOS platform in the 1980s and 1990s. The game is heavily inspired by the famous arcade title Asteroids, but with a unique twist. It was created to take advantage of the EGA graphics standard, offering a simple yet engaging experience for players on early personal computers. Asteroids-Inspired Gameplay: Like Asteroids, players control a spaceship in an open space environment filled with moving asteroids. The goal is to shoot the asteroids to break them into smaller pieces. If an asteroid hits the player's spaceship, they lose a life. EGA Graphics: The game uses EGA graphics, which offer a palette of 16 colors and provide basic visuals such as simple vector-style representations of asteroids, the player's ship, and projectiles. While the graphics were rudimentary by today's standards, they were quite advanced at the time and gave a distinct look to the game. Movement and Controls: Players control their spaceship’s movement with keyboard commands, such as using arrow keys or other specific keys to rotate, thrust, and fire. The spaceship can move freely in all directions within the game’s environment, similar to the classic arcade gameplay style, where inertia and momentum play a key role in navigation. Asteroids and Enemy Ships: Asteroids come in different sizes. The player needs to shoot them to break them into smaller pieces, each of which can be destroyed. As players progress through levels, they may encounter enemy ships or space debris, adding more danger to the already chaotic asteroid field. The game typically gets progressively harder as the asteroid field becomes denser, and enemies become more aggressive. Power-ups and Bonuses: In some versions of EGA Roids, there may be power-ups scattered across the play area. These can give the player temporary advantages, such as: Extra Firepower: Increases the rate of fire or power of the spaceship's shots. Shields: Provides temporary protection from asteroid collisions. Speed Boosts: Increases the movement speed of the ship.

name: EGA Solitaire
description: If you are looking for a clone of the Windows Solitaire card game for DOS, this is it. This game almost exactly mirrors the seminal Windows card game, and is quite well executed. The object of course is to sort the various suits into four separate piles; as such, the only bad thing about the game is that the different suits can sometimes be difficult to distinguish. Other than that it's very well done.EGA Solitaire (DOS) is a classic version of the popular card game Solitaire, designed for the DOS platform with EGA graphics. It was created during the era of early personal computers, offering a simple yet engaging digital card game experience. The game takes advantage of the Enhanced Graphics Adapter (EGA) standard, which provided a limited but vibrant color palette and allowed the game to present a relatively more colorful and visually appealing experience than earlier games using monochrome displays. Traditional Solitaire Gameplay: EGA Solitaire (DOS) follows the rules of Klondike Solitaire, which is the most common and popular version of Solitaire. The objective is to build four foundation piles from Ace to King, using the tableau piles, where cards are arranged in descending order and alternating colors (red and black). Cards can be moved between tableau piles, from one to another, by adhering to the descending order and alternating colors rule. EGA Graphics: The game uses EGA graphics with a 16-color palette, offering a more vibrant and visually appealing design than earlier monochrome versions of Solitaire. The cards are presented with clear symbols and colors for suits (hearts, spades, diamonds, and clubs), making it easier for players to identify cards and suits. While the graphics are simple by modern standards, they were groundbreaking for early personal computer games. Card Movement: Players can drag and drop cards or use keyboard controls (depending on the version) to move cards between piles. The goal is to uncover all cards in the tableau by making legal moves and arranging the cards in the correct order for the foundations. Players must plan their moves to uncover face-down cards and free up spaces for more cards. Deck of Cards: The game begins with a shuffled deck of 52 playing cards. Cards are dealt into seven columns (tableau), and the player must work through these columns and the stockpile to create the four foundation piles, one for each suit. There are face-up cards in the tableau and face-down cards that need to be revealed by moving other cards. Stockpile and Waste Pile: If the player cannot make a move in the tableau, they can draw cards from the stockpile (the remaining shuffled deck of cards). These cards are placed in a waste pile, and only the top card of the waste pile is available for play. Players can flip through the stockpile to find useful cards to continue progressing through the game. Winning the Game: The game is won when all the cards are arranged in the four foundation piles, in ascending order from Ace to King, for each suit. A game can also end in failure if no more legal moves can be made and the stockpile is exhausted. Scoring: Players may earn points for each successful move and the completion of foundation piles. Some versions of EGA Solitaire also feature timed play or bonus points for finishing quickly, while others may offer the option to play without any scoring.

name: EGA Trek
description: EGA Trek is based heavily on very early computer space simulation games. (ie. the first computer game ever, Space War!, aka Computer Space). Since this is a non-licensed game, it never refers to it as "Star Trek", but you know what they were going for. It includes color graphics that although sparse do the job well. The objective is to eliminate other ships and "save the galaxy". This is a simulation/strategy game with not a lot of action, so it won't be for everyone, but it definitely is a classic PC game.EGA Trek (DOS) is a text-based strategy game released in the early days of personal computing, designed to run on the DOS operating system with EGA graphics. It is a derivative of the classic Star Trek game, where players assume the role of a starship captain navigating through the galaxy. The objective is typically to protect the galaxy from enemy forces, particularly the Klingons, and complete various missions, all while managing the resources of the player's starship. EGA Graphics: While EGA Trek is largely a text-based game, it utilizes EGA graphics to represent certain visual aspects of the game, such as the starfield, enemy ships, and the star system map. The game's graphics, while rudimentary by modern standards, still provide basic visuals that enhance the immersive experience compared to earlier text-only games. Mission-Based Gameplay: Players are tasked with completing various missions, which usually involve destroying enemy ships, protecting planets, or exploring the galaxy. The game's narrative is driven by the missions, and success or failure often impacts the overall progress of the game. A common mission objective is to defeat the Klingon ships that threaten the Federation, similar to the original Star Trek games. Ship Management and Resources: Players must manage the starship’s resources, such as shields, energy, and ammo (torpedoes). These resources are limited, and careful management is crucial for survival and success. The ship can be damaged during combat, and players need to make strategic decisions regarding repairing the ship, refueling, or seeking refuge in nearby starbases. Players also have to navigate the galaxy map, which is made up of multiple sectors, each containing planets, stars, and enemy forces. Space Combat: The game features turn-based space combat, where players engage in battles with enemy ships, typically the Klingons. The player uses their starship's phasers, torpedoes, and shields to fight enemies. The combat is usually text-driven, with the player issuing commands to their ship, such as attacking, defending, or maneuvering. Players must choose their actions wisely during combat, considering the energy levels, shield status, and distance from the enemy.

name: EGA-Spider
description: EGA Spiders is a variant of the classic solitaire game ... y'know, the one you played in Windows 3.1 back in the day, whatever that one is called. The goal here is to make piles of the same suit in order, from King down to Ace. You do so by moving the cards around on the piles. The gimmick here is that you can make "illegal" moves by using the right mouse button. Every time you do so, another spider is added to run around the screen and annoy you. The number of times you "cheated" is noted after you complete a game. The mouse cursor seems to flicker a bit (in DOSBox, at least) but it's not too distracting.

name: EGABOMB and VGABOMB
description: EGABOMB / VGABOMB (also apparently called "OnTarget" in a re-release by shareware disk publisher Villa Crespo Software) is a simple artillery/tank combat game. Two players (no CPU opponent is available) set the angle and power of their shots (correcting for the wind) and then try to destroy their opponent. If this sounds quite similar to the QBasic pack-in game Gorillas you're correct, it plays essentially the same. The ground heights are randomly generated but it doesn't impact the game too much. As you might expect, it includes both EGA and VGA versions with separate executable files.

name: Egg Age
description: Connect three or more of the same eggs. Connect as many Eggs as indicated on the left.Egg Age (HTML) is a browser-based puzzle game that combines elements of match-3 mechanics with a whimsical, egg-themed environment. The game is designed to be casual and accessible, making it suitable for players of all ages. Set in a colorful, vibrant world, players engage in various levels of gameplay to match eggs of similar colors, complete objectives, and unlock new challenges as they progress. Match-3 Gameplay: Egg Age follows the classic match-3 gameplay mechanics where players swap adjacent eggs to form groups of three or more eggs of the same color. Once the group is formed, the eggs are cleared, and new eggs drop down from the top to replace them. The game requires strategic planning to maximize the number of matches and clear the grid efficiently. Colorful and Whimsical Theme: The game’s visual design is centered around a colorful, egg-themed world. Eggs come in a variety of bright colors, and the backgrounds are filled with cheerful, playful elements. The overall aesthetic is cartoony and lighthearted, appealing to players looking for a fun and relaxing experience. Levels and Objectives: Egg Age features multiple levels, each with its own unique set of objectives and challenges. Some levels may ask players to clear a certain number of eggs, while others may introduce obstacles like locked eggs or limited moves. As players progress through the levels, the difficulty increases, and the puzzles become more complex, requiring more strategic thinking to complete. Power-ups and Boosters: Players can collect power-ups and boosters that help them clear eggs more efficiently. These may include: Bomb Eggs: Explode and clear a larger area of eggs. Color Eggs: Clear all eggs of the selected color. Row or Column Clear: Clears an entire row or column of eggs. These power-ups can be used strategically to overcome difficult levels or to get higher scores. Timed and Moves-Based Challenges: Some levels may be time-based, where players must match eggs within a specific time limit. Other levels may be move-based, where players are limited to a certain number of moves to achieve the level objectives. Players must think ahead to maximize their moves and complete the level.

name: Eggtastic
description: Eggtastic (Flash) is a classic Flash-based casual game that features an egg-collecting gameplay centered around fun and quirky mechanics. The game combines platforming with puzzle-solving, offering a fun and lighthearted experience where players aim to collect eggs in a variety of challenging environments. Egg Collecting Mechanic: The central mechanic in Eggtastic revolves around collecting eggs scattered throughout each level. Eggs are placed in strategic spots, requiring players to jump, climb, and avoid obstacles to reach them. Some eggs may be hidden or protected by barriers, requiring the player to figure out how to access them or avoid traps. Platforming Challenges: Eggtastic features traditional platforming gameplay where players must navigate different obstacles, such as moving platforms, spikes, and other environmental hazards. The game may include jumping puzzles that require precise timing and control to succeed. Levels and Difficulty: The game is structured in multiple levels, each becoming progressively more difficult with more obstacles, harder jumps, and more tricky egg placements. As players advance, they encounter new challenges, including faster-moving hazards or more complex level designs. Some levels may introduce new puzzle elements where the player has to think strategically about how to collect all the eggs in the shortest amount of time. Cute and Whimsical Art Style: Eggtastic is designed with a fun and colorful aesthetic, featuring cartoonish graphics and cute animations for the main character and eggs. The visual style is lighthearted and playful, making the game appealing to both younger audiences and casual players looking for a relaxing, fun experience. Time-Based Challenges: Some levels in Eggtastic are timed, where players need to collect all eggs before the time runs out. The time pressure adds an element of excitement to the gameplay, encouraging quick thinking and fast reactions. Players can try to beat their own best times or compete for high scores in each level. Power-ups and Boosts: Throughout the game, players may collect power-ups that help them in their egg-collecting quest. These can include things like: Speed boosts to move faster through levels. Shield items to temporarily protect against hazards. Egg magnet to automatically pull eggs toward the player. Power-ups add strategic depth, allowing players to tackle tougher levels more easily.

name: Egypt Collapse
description: Remove all tiles by clicking on groups of tiles. You can remove single tiles with a bomb, but be carefull: you only have a few.Egypt Collapse (HTML) is a match-3 puzzle game set in ancient Egypt, where players are tasked with clearing hieroglyphic tiles from the game board by matching three or more of the same tiles. The game typically features a visually rich Egyptian theme, with iconic imagery such as pyramids, pharaohs, and ancient artifacts. It combines strategy, quick thinking, and puzzle-solving, making it a fun and engaging experience. Match-3 Gameplay: Egypt Collapse follows the traditional match-3 mechanics, where the player swaps tiles to align three or more tiles of the same type. The matching tiles will then collapse, clearing space and allowing new tiles to fall in, creating chain reactions or combos that can lead to more points. The key to success is to make strategic moves, setting up larger matches or combos that maximize the points gained. Egyptian Theme and Visuals: The game’s design is heavily inspired by ancient Egyptian culture, featuring hieroglyphic symbols, Egyptian gods, and pyramids. The backgrounds and tile designs evoke an Egyptian aesthetic, with rich colors, desert landscapes, and iconic imagery such as scarabs, sphinxes, and pharaohs. The theme is visually engaging and adds a layer of fun to the puzzle-solving experience. Levels and Objectives: Egypt Collapse consists of multiple levels, each with its own unique objectives. Objectives might include clearing a certain number of specific tiles, achieving a target score, or completing the level within a set number of moves. As players progress through levels, the difficulty increases with more complex tile arrangements, additional obstacles, or limited moves. Power-ups and Boosters: Players can collect or earn power-ups that can help them complete more difficult levels. Some examples include: Bombs: Clear a small area of tiles. Row or Column Clear: Remove all tiles from a row or column. Color Match: Clear all tiles of a specific color. These boosters can be used strategically to help the player complete more challenging objectives or earn higher scores. Increasing Difficulty: As players progress through the levels, they encounter more difficult challenges. These might include: Limited moves: The player has a specific number of moves to complete the level. Obstacles: Certain tiles may be locked, and the player must match them to unlock and clear them. Timed levels: Players must achieve their objectives before the clock runs out. Casual and Addictive Gameplay: The gameplay in Egypt Collapse is easy to pick up, making it suitable for both casual gamers and those looking for a more strategic challenge. The game encourages replaying levels to improve scores, complete objectives, or discover new combinations. Its simple mechanics combined with a challenging progression system make it highly addictive.

name: Egypt Mahjong - Triple Dimensions
description: Combine 3 Mahjong Cubes in this Triple Mahjong game. Combine 3 of the same free tiles to remove the tiles.Egypt Mahjong - Triple Dimensions (HTML) is an engaging mahjong solitaire game that combines the classic mahjong tile-matching gameplay with a unique 3D perspective. Set in ancient Egypt, the game offers an immersive and visually rich experience where players solve tile-matching puzzles in a multi-dimensional space. The game typically features iconic Egyptian symbols, hieroglyphs, and artifacts, providing a thematic adventure as players progress through the levels. 3D Mahjong Gameplay: Unlike traditional 2D mahjong, this game features a 3D puzzle environment, where tiles are stacked in multiple layers. Players can rotate the puzzle board to view tiles from different angles, which allows them to match tiles that are not immediately visible, adding a new level of strategy and challenge. Classic Mahjong Rules: The primary objective remains the same as traditional mahjong solitaire: match pairs of identical tiles to remove them from the board. Tiles are only available to be matched if they are not covered by other tiles and have at least one side open (either left or right). The game may have a time limit or move restrictions to increase the challenge of completing each puzzle. Egyptian Theme and Visuals: Egypt Mahjong - Triple Dimensions has a strong Egyptian theme, with tiles decorated in hieroglyphs, scarabs, pyramids, pharaohs, and other iconic symbols from ancient Egypt. The 3D visual design adds to the aesthetic, with lush backgrounds depicting Egyptian landscapes like deserts, temples, and pyramids. The game’s sound effects and music enhance the immersive atmosphere, featuring traditional Egyptian-style tunes. Layered Tile Stacks: The 3D layout means tiles are arranged in multi-layered stacks. Players can rotate the game’s perspective to view different layers, making it possible to see tiles that were previously hidden. This multi-dimensional aspect requires players to think ahead and plan their moves carefully to ensure that the tiles are cleared efficiently.

name: Egypt Pyramid Solitaire
description: Pyramid Solitaire game: combine 2 cards to a total value of 13. An A=1, a J=11, a Q=12 and a K=13 (and can be removed as a single card).Egypt Pyramid Solitaire (HTML) is a fun and engaging solitaire card game set against the backdrop of ancient Egypt. In this game, players work to clear a pyramid-shaped structure of cards by pairing cards that total 13, a variation of traditional solitaire. The game features a rich Egyptian theme with beautiful visuals and iconic symbols such as hieroglyphs, pyramids, and Egyptian gods. Pyramid Layout: The cards are arranged in the shape of a pyramid, with each level of the pyramid containing more cards. The first row has one card, the second row has two cards, and so on, forming a classic pyramid structure. The cards in the pyramid must be cleared by pairing them with other cards that add up to 13. Card Values: In Egypt Pyramid Solitaire, the card values are as follows: Ace = 1 2 to 10 = Face value Jack = 11 Queen = 12 King = 13 A King can be removed by itself, as it matches its value of 13. Pairing Cards: To remove a card from the pyramid, it must be uncovered (i.e., not covered by other cards) and paired with another card whose total value equals 13. For example, a Queen (12) and an Ace (1) can be paired together to form a total of 13 and removed from the pyramid.

name: Egypt Runes
description: Click on groups of 3 or more of the same rune items to remove those. Remove all grey backgrounds and/or drop down the coins and reach the indicated goal.Egypt Runes (HTML) is an engaging match-3 puzzle game set in the mysterious and fascinating world of ancient Egypt. In this game, players are tasked with matching runic tiles to clear the board and solve puzzles. The game often incorporates a variety of ancient Egyptian symbols and artifacts, providing an immersive experience. As players progress, they encounter increasingly challenging puzzles and may unlock new levels, power-ups, and boosters. Match-3 Mechanics: Like many match-3 puzzle games, the player’s task is to swap adjacent tiles to create a match of three or more identical runes. The matched tiles disappear, and new tiles fall into the grid, potentially creating more matches or combos. This chain reaction can help clear more tiles with a single move. Egyptian Theming: The game is set against a backdrop of ancient Egypt, and the runes or tiles featured in the game are often inspired by Egyptian symbols such as scarabs, pyramids, hieroglyphs, and other mystical artifacts. The visual design and sound effects create a thematic experience, adding atmosphere and immersion to the game as players explore ancient ruins or temples. Challenging Levels: Egypt Runes typically includes multiple levels, with the difficulty increasing as players progress. The game introduces new challenges in each level, such as different types of tiles or obstacles that block certain moves. Some levels may have specific goals, such as clearing a set number of a specific type of tile, achieving a target score, or completing the level within a set number of moves or time limit. Power-ups and Boosters: As players progress, they can unlock power-ups that help them clear the board more efficiently. Some examples include: Bombs: Clears a small area of tiles. Color Changer: Turns all tiles of a specific color into another tile type. Row or Column Clear: Clears all tiles from a row or column. These power-ups can be strategically used to complete more difficult levels or to score higher. Tile Matching Strategy: Players must use strategy to create large matches and plan ahead, especially as the game board fills up. Some tiles may be harder to clear because they are covered or locked, requiring thoughtful moves and effective use of power-ups. The game may also have special tiles, like locked tiles or tiles that move, which require more complex strategies to clear. Level Objectives: Each level in Egypt Runes typically has a specific objective that players must complete. This might involve matching a certain number of specific tiles, achieving a target score, or clearing all the tiles from the board. As levels progress, new objectives or challenges are introduced, keeping the gameplay fresh and exciting.

name: Egypt Solitaire
description: Egypt Solitaire is a captivating card game set in the mystical world of ancient Egypt. With 100 different levels, this game offers a unique twist on classic solitaire gameplay.
