He is durable and ideal for players who enjoy direct combat. The Cleric: A magic user who can cast powerful spells and use a wide range of ranged weapons, such as a crossbow. The Cleric is more versatile, combining ranged attacks with a variety of magic-based abilities. The Mage: A character who relies heavily on magic and spell-casting. The Mage has an array of elemental spells and a unique ability to teleport short distances, making him more mobile and versatile in combat. First-Person Combat: Combat in Hexen is fast-paced and action-packed, with players using a combination of ranged and melee weapons to defeat enemies. Weapons include crossbows, wands, and magical staffs, each with its unique abilities. The player must navigate through intricate levels, using weapons, spells, and power-ups to overcome obstacles and enemies. Each level features a range of enemies, from humanoid foes to terrifying monsters, each requiring different strategies to defeat.

name: HexGL
description: HexGL is a fast-paced, futuristic racing game built using HTML5 and JavaScript. Inspired by classic arcade racing games, particularly Wipeout, HexGL features sleek, high-speed hovercraft races in a neon-lit, futuristic world. It stands out as a visually appealing game that leverages the power of modern web technologies to deliver a smooth and thrilling experience directly in your web browser. Gameplay Overview: In HexGL, players race hovercrafts through winding, obstacle-filled tracks in a futuristic environment. The game's primary goal is to complete each track as fast as possible while avoiding collisions with the environment and other obstacles. The high-speed nature of the game provides an adrenaline-pumping experience as players strive to set the best times on each course. Key Gameplay Mechanics: Racing Tracks: The game features several tracks, each with its own design, speed bumps, jumps, and sharp turns. The tracks are visually striking, with a futuristic setting that incorporates neon lights, glowing pathways, and intricate designs. As players progress, the tracks become more challenging, with increasingly complex curves and obstacles. Hovercraft Controls: Players control a high-speed hovercraft using standard racing controls: accelerate, brake, and steer. The hovercraft is equipped with boost pads and turbo capabilities, which help players reach higher speeds for short bursts, but timing these boosts correctly is crucial to maintaining control over the craft at high speeds. The game emphasizes tight handling and quick reflexes as players navigate the tracks at breakneck speeds. Boosting and Power-Ups: HexGL features speed boosts that can be picked up during the race. These boosts temporarily increase your craft’s speed, adding an extra layer of strategy as players use them at key moments to gain an edge over their opponents. Players must learn the best timing to use their boost to avoid crashing or losing control. Obstacle Avoidance: The tracks are full of obstacles such as barriers, sharp turns, and tight corners. Players must avoid crashing into these obstacles while maintaining the highest possible speed. Crashing into walls or missing turns results in losing precious time, which can affect your overall race performance and final standings.

name: Hexjong Cats
description: Colorful mahjong game with Hex tiles. Combine two of the same free tiles. Free tiles are highlighted.Hexjong Cats is a relaxing and fun online puzzle game that combines the mechanics of Mahjong with a hexagonal grid layout. The game is themed around adorable cats, and players are tasked with matching tiles featuring cute cat illustrations. It's a great choice for players who enjoy casual puzzle games and want something that combines traditional tile-matching gameplay with a playful theme. Gameplay Overview: In Hexjong Cats, players need to clear a hexagonal board filled with tiles featuring different cat-themed images. The game follows the classic Mahjong principles of matching identical tiles to remove them from the board, but it uses a hexagonal grid instead of the traditional square grid, adding an extra level of complexity and fun to the game. Key Gameplay Mechanics: Hexagonal Tile Grid: The game is played on a hexagonal grid, which means tiles are arranged in a honeycomb-like pattern. This is different from the classic Mahjong game's square grid and adds a new challenge when searching for matching pairs of tiles. The tiles are stacked in layers, and players must select tiles that are exposed on the top layer of the stack. A tile is considered "free" if it’s not blocked by other tiles and has at least one open side. Matching Pairs: Players must find two identical tiles and click on them to remove them from the board. The goal is to match all the tiles and clear the entire board. Unlike traditional Mahjong, where tiles are typically arranged in specific patterns, Hexjong Cats allows for more freeform matching due to the hexagonal grid. Cats-Themed Tiles: The tiles in Hexjong Cats feature various adorable cat designs, making the game visually charming and entertaining. The tiles are decorated with different breeds of cats, cats doing funny poses, and other cat-related symbols, making the game feel light-hearted and fun. Clear the Board: The goal is to match and remove all tiles from the board before time runs out (in some versions). There are usually no moves left once the last pair is matched, and players win once they’ve successfully cleared the board.

name: Hexplode
description: Hexplode is a strategy board game, according to the author based on an original concept by Janet Ansell. The game works similarly to the outbreaks in Pandemic: You add counters to the hexagon tiles on the board, and when the tile reaches its limit (defined as its "number of neighbors") it explodes, placing a counter on each tile around it, potentially causing chain reactions. The object is to eliminate the other player's counters. You can play a two player game or against the CPU, or just watch the CPU play if you want.

name: Hextris
description: Hextris is a fast-paced, addictive puzzle game inspired by the classic Tetris but with a unique twist: it uses a hexagonal grid instead of a square grid. In Hextris, players must rotate and position falling shapes, which are made up of hexagonal blocks, to create complete lines and prevent the game from reaching the top of the screen. The game is simple in concept but becomes increasingly challenging as the speed ramps up. Gameplay Overview: In Hextris, the objective is to prevent the falling hexagonal shapes (or "blocks") from piling up to the top of the screen. Unlike the traditional Tetris game where shapes fall into a vertical grid, Hextris uses a rotating hexagonal grid. This rotation mechanic adds an extra layer of complexity, requiring players to think more strategically about where to place the pieces. Key Gameplay Mechanics: Hexagonal Grid: Hextris is played on a hexagonal grid, which is different from the classic Tetris' square grid. The grid consists of hexagonal spaces, making the game feel unique. The grid is arranged in a circular pattern, and the blocks rotate around the center, requiring players to manage the placement of pieces from various directions. Falling Hexagonal Blocks: Just like in Tetris, blocks made up of smaller hexagonal tiles fall from the top of the screen. Players need to rotate and position these blocks to form complete lines. The blocks come in different shapes, and the goal is to fit them into the available spaces on the grid to clear lines. Rotation Mechanic: Unlike in traditional Tetris, where pieces fall in a straight vertical direction, in Hextris, the entire playing area rotates around a central point. Players rotate the hexagonal grid itself to manipulate the falling blocks and fit them into place. Clearing Lines: The main objective is to clear lines of hexagons by forming complete rows around the central point. When a full ring of hexagons is formed, it disappears, making room for new falling blocks. Clearing lines helps keep the screen clear of falling blocks and prevents the game from ending prematurely. Increasing Difficulty: As the game progresses, the speed at which blocks fall increases, making it harder to react and position pieces correctly. The game continues until the blocks pile up to the top of the screen, signaling the end of the game. Scoring: Players earn points by clearing lines. The faster and more efficiently they clear lines, the higher their score will be. Some versions of Hextris offer additional scoring mechanics, such as combos or bonus points for clearing multiple lines at once. Power-ups (Optional): In some versions of Hextris, power-ups may be available to help players clear lines more effectively. These can include special blocks that clear larger areas or slow down the falling blocks.

name: Hexx: Heresy of the Wizard
description: First of all, if you're looking for the 3D shooting game with a similar name, you'll want to try Hexen instead. Now that THAT is out of the way ... Hexx is a 3D RPG in the same genre as Ultima Underworld (which appeared approx 2 years before Hexx) and other real-time 3D dungeon crawlers. It is apparently an update/sequel to the game Bloodwych. The graphics, sounds, and animations are all done pretty well here. You also get a full party of characters (I imagine in the full version you can generate them yourself) instead of just playing as a single hero. Combat seems to occur automatically when you click the battle graphic.

name: Hexxagon
description: An extremely enjoyable puzzle game. It's quite similar to Reversi/Othello, except with a hexagon grid rather than a square grid. The object is to take over the gameboard (which can be edited by the user and saved) with marbles (gems?) of your own color. It includes a single player vs. computer option (with three skill levels) and also a two player option.Hexxagon is a classic strategy game released for DOS that features a unique hexagonal grid layout. The game was designed to be a blend of the traditional Reversi (Othello) game and a strategy board game with a hexagonal twist. Players aim to dominate the game board by capturing the opponent's pieces and converting them to their own color. Gameplay Overview: In Hexxagon, two players (either human vs. computer or player vs. player) compete to control a hexagonal grid board by placing pieces and converting the opponent's pieces to their own. The objective is to capture as many spaces as possible on the board by strategically placing your pieces to flip the opponent's pieces. Key Gameplay Mechanics: Hexagonal Grid: The game board consists of hexagonal tiles, and each player controls one of two colors (usually blue and red). Players place their pieces on any unoccupied tile, and the goal is to surround and convert the opponent’s pieces. Placing Pieces: Players take turns placing their pieces on empty tiles. Each piece placed can potentially flip one or more of the opponent's pieces, depending on its placement and the surrounding pieces. The piece must be placed in such a way that it can "flip" adjacent opponent pieces, turning them into the player's color. Capturing and Flipping: To capture an opponent’s piece, players must position their own piece so that it is adjacent to the opponent’s piece along a line. The opponent's piece will then be "flipped" and become the player's piece. A piece can flip multiple opponent pieces if they are aligned in the same direction (diagonally or orthogonally) on the hexagonal grid. Board Progression: As the game progresses, the board fills up with pieces, and players aim to strategically plan their moves to capture more territory while preventing the opponent from doing the same. The player with the most pieces on the board at the end of the game wins. End Game and Winning: The game ends when no more valid moves are possible, either when the board is full or when both players can no longer make moves. The player who has the most pieces of their color on the board at the end of the game is declared the winner.

name: Hidden Classroom
description: Find all the hidden objects in the Classroom. Pinch or long tap/click to zoom in and out.Hidden Classroom is an online hidden object puzzle game where players must find specific items hidden within a classroom-themed scene. In this type of game, the objective is to locate various objects that are cleverly concealed within a detailed background. The classroom setting typically includes desks, bookshelves, blackboards, and various educational materials, making it an enjoyable and visually interesting experience. Gameplay Overview: In Hidden Classroom, players are presented with a classroom scene filled with various items. The goal is to find a list of hidden objects that are scattered throughout the environment. The game challenges players' attention to detail and their ability to spot objects in a cluttered space. Key Gameplay Mechanics: Search for Hidden Objects: The main objective is to find all the objects listed at the top or side of the screen within the classroom scene. These objects can be anything from books, pens, rulers, and notebooks to more unconventional items like keys or toys. Time Limit: Some versions of Hidden Classroom feature a time limit, where players must find all the hidden objects within a specific time frame. This adds a sense of urgency and challenge to the game. Other versions may offer a relaxed, no-time-limit mode where players can take as long as they want to complete the task. Interactive Items: Some versions may include interactive items or clues to help you find the hidden objects. These could be hints, magnifying glasses, or the ability to zoom in on certain parts of the image. Zoom Function: Many Hidden Object games, including Hidden Classroom, feature a zoom-in function. This allows players to focus on smaller details in the image, making it easier to spot items that might otherwise be difficult to see. Hints: If players are struggling to find an object, hints are often available. These may highlight an object for a brief moment or provide a visual clue to help players locate it.

name: Hidden Fields
description: Hidden Fields is a takeoff of the classic Qix or Xonix arcade games, where the object is to draw boxes over the playing field to gradually reveal the picture hiding behind it. There are different enemies on each level which try to thwart your chances, and the production values on the game in terms of its graphics and sound effects are pretty high. And are those Frank Frazetta pictures that get revealed?! Use of those images MAY not be legal but hey, they fit the game's over-the-top, rock-and-roll aesthetic. Despite the gratuitous (and long) company logo sequence at the beginning, once you get past that, the game itself plays quite well.

name: Hidden Flowers
description: Match 3 and hidden object game. First find all the hidden flowers and then match 3 or more of the same flowers.Hidden Flowers is an online hidden object game that challenges players to find flowers and other related items hidden in beautifully designed nature scenes. The game offers a relaxing and immersive experience as players explore vibrant environments filled with various objects that are cleverly concealed. Gameplay Overview: In Hidden Flowers, players are given a list of items they must locate within a floral or garden-themed setting. The objects can include various flowers, tools, garden items, and other nature-related objects that blend into the environment. The game is designed to be a relaxing experience, perfect for those who enjoy puzzles and exploring visually rich scenes. Key Gameplay Mechanics: Finding Hidden Flowers and Objects: The primary objective is to find a list of flowers and other objects hidden within the lush and detailed scenes. Players must carefully search the environment, which could be a garden, a forest, or even a floral arrangement, and identify items that blend into the background. Timed Gameplay (Optional): Some versions of Hidden Flowers may feature a time limit, adding an element of challenge. Players must find all the items on the list before time runs out. Other versions may allow players to explore the scene at their own pace, without any time pressure. Hints and Assistance: If players have trouble finding an item, hints are typically available. These hints could highlight an object for a brief moment, point players in the right direction, or provide visual cues to help locate difficult-to-find objects.

name: Hidden Food
description: Find the Hidden Food. Click on the objects you need to find.Hidden Food is a fun and engaging hidden object puzzle game where players need to find various food-related items that are cleverly concealed within detailed and colorful scenes. The game is designed to challenge players' observation skills and attention to detail, with the ultimate goal of locating all the hidden food items in a specified time or with limited moves. Gameplay Overview: In Hidden Food, players are presented with an image that contains a variety of hidden food items. The objective is to find all the food objects listed within the game, which may range from fruits, vegetables, snacks, desserts, or kitchen items, all hidden within the scene. The challenge lies in spotting these items as they are blended into the surrounding environment. Key Gameplay Mechanics: Search for Hidden Food: The primary task in Hidden Food is to locate and identify a list of food-related items within a cluttered or beautifully designed scene. These objects may include common foods such as pizza, fruits, cakes, or drinks, and sometimes even kitchenware or utensils related to food preparation. description: The classic board game hnefatafl in 2 sizes. The white King needs to escape from the black soldiers.Hnefatafl is an ancient Nordic board game, often referred to as Viking chess. The game is a strategic two-player board game that involves asymmetrical gameplay, with one player controlling a king and his defenders, while the other controls attacking forces. The objective of the game is for the king to escape to one of the corner squares on the board, while the attackers aim to capture him before he escapes. In the HTML version of Hnefatafl, the game is typically presented with an interactive interface that allows you to play against either a computer or another player. The rules and mechanics closely follow the traditional gameplay of Hnefatafl, but the online format provides a convenient way to enjoy the game with digital assistance. Gameplay Overview: Hnefatafl is played on a square grid (often 11x11 or 13x13) and involves two different types of pieces: The King: A single piece, initially placed at the center of the board. The king’s goal is to escape to one of the four corner squares. The Defenders: These pieces are positioned around the king in the initial setup. They aim to protect the king from being captured by the attacking forces. The Attackers: A larger group of pieces that aim to surround and capture the king by occupying all the spaces adjacent to it. Objective: The defenders win if the king escapes to one of the corner squares. The attackers win by surrounding the king so that no move is possible for the king to escape. Rules: Movement: Pieces move along the lines of the board, either horizontally or vertically. They can move as far as there is open space, but cannot jump over other pieces. The king moves like a normal piece, but it must be protected by defenders to reach the corner square and escape. Capturing Pieces: A piece is captured when it is surrounded on both sides by opponent pieces (vertically or horizontally). In Hnefatafl, a piece can be captured only if the opponent has two pieces placed adjacent to it in one of the four directions (left, right, up, or down). Corner Escape: The main goal of the defenders is to maneuver the king toward one of the four corners of the board. The corner squares are safe spaces where the king can escape. The attackers aim to capture the king before it can escape, using their larger numbers to create a blockade around the king.

name: Hobo 7

name: Hocus Pocus
description: Simply a great platform game. Similar to Clyde's Adventure and Clyde's Revenge (also developed by Moonlite Software) but Hocus Pocus has better graphics, plus it's more exciting because there are enemies to kill! Here you play a wizard who runs around the levels shooting enemies and triggering switches and walls.Hocus Pocus is a classic DOS-based action-adventure game developed by Moonlite Software and released in 1994. It is a platformer that combines puzzle-solving elements with arcade-style action. Players take control of a young wizard named Hocus, who embarks on a magical adventure to rescue his teacher and save the magical kingdom from evil forces. Gameplay Overview: In Hocus Pocus, players navigate various levels filled with enemies, traps, and puzzles. The core of the gameplay revolves around platforming, magical combat, and using spells to overcome obstacles and enemies. The game is divided into different stages, each with its own theme and set of challenges. Key Features: Platforming Action: Hocus Pocus features a side-scrolling platforming setup where players must guide Hocus through various levels. You need to jump over obstacles, avoid traps, and defeat enemies that stand in your way. The levels are filled with both horizontal and vertical challenges that require quick reflexes and careful planning. Magic Spells: As a young wizard, Hocus has a range of magic spells at his disposal. These spells can be used to defeat enemies, solve puzzles, and navigate the environment. There are several types of spells, including fireballs, ice blasts, and other elemental-based attacks. Spells are also used for various puzzles, such as unlocking doors or creating platforms to cross gaps. Enemies and Bosses: Throughout the game, you’ll encounter a variety of enemies, from simple creatures like skeletons and spiders to more dangerous and magical foes. Levels and Worlds: The game is divided into multiple themed worlds, each with its own set of challenges and unique enemies. name: hole.io
description: Overview: Hole.io is an engaging multiplayer arcade game where players control a black hole, competing to consume various objects in a cityscape. The goal is to grow larger by swallowing everything in sight, from small items to large buildings, while outmaneuvering other players. Fast-paced and strategic, Hole.io offers a unique blend of competitive and casual gameplay. Gameplay Mechanics: Controls: Use the mouse or touch controls to navigate the black hole around the map. Conclusion: With its addictive gameplay and competitive edge, Hole.io invites players to dive into a fun-filled race to become the biggest black hole. Can you outsmart your opponents and dominate the city?

name: Holiday Match
description: Get into the holiday mood with this fun memory game.Holiday Match is an enjoyable and relaxing online matching puzzle game often found in HTML5 format. In this game, the goal is to match pairs of similar items or images within a time limit or until all pairs have been matched. It's typically themed around the holidays, featuring festive images related to various holiday traditions. Gameplay Overview: Objective: The primary goal of the game is to match identical holiday-themed items or images. These could include ornaments, gifts, snowflakes, Christmas trees, or other seasonal symbols. Players must find pairs of matching items on the board to clear them. Board Layout: The game board consists of a grid filled with face-down tiles. Each tile has an image on the other side, and players must click on two tiles at a time to reveal them. If the two tiles match, they are removed from the board. If they don't match, they are flipped back over. Matching Pairs: Players must use their memory and observational skills to remember where certain items are located, aiming to match all pairs before time runs out or within the given moves. Levels and Progression: As players progress, the levels may get more challenging, with larger grids, more tiles, and additional distractions or power-ups that may alter the gameplay. Some versions of the game may include timed levels, where players need to match the pairs within a certain amount of time. Power-ups and Special Features: Depending on the version, Holiday Match may include power-ups like hints, which show the location of a matching pair, or the ability to shuffle the tiles if the player is stuck. Graphics and Sound: Graphics: The game typically features bright, cheerful graphics with holiday-related images. Expect to see traditional holiday symbols such as snowmen, candy canes, stockings, reindeer, presents, and more. The art style is often playful and vibrant, contributing to the festive atmosphere. Sound: Holiday Match is often accompanied by a gentle and relaxing soundtrack with festive music. The sound effects include satisfying "clicks" when tiles are matched and background music that enhances the holiday theme without being overwhelming.

name: Holiday Serpent
description: Quite a nice looking Nibbles-like game, developed by a Finnish team. Here you are a serpent, and must collect flowers while avoiding the skulls, and also avoiding running into your tail. This game looks very nice, and includes some SB effects as well. The only small problem is with the camera: It can be very hard to see what's coming up because of the way it moves, making playing much tougher. (Runs in DOSBox but gets a runtime error when trying to actually play; seems like the accented character in the filename causes a problem.)

name: Hollywood Bash

name: Home Run Derby
description: Home Run Derby attempts to simulate the baseball home run competition, where hitters compete against each other to try to hit the most home runs. In any case, this game offers a full game mode as well as a practice mode, and you'd better practice first before attempting the full derby. Sounds are decent and include some short voice clips.

Whether you’re a fan of cultural games, puzzle challenges, or simply want to explore something new, Albanifest 2004 offers an engaging and lighthearted adventure.

name: Hong Kong Cafe

name: Hong Kong Mahjong
description: Hong Kong Mahjong is a Mahjong game, aimed at being authentic to the particular type played in Hong Kong. (Duh) This is the original shareware game that eventually evolved into a larger more polished game called Hong Kong Mahjong Pro by the same developer but pushed commercially by EA. This shareware game still plays well (from what I can tell) and seems to follow the appropriate rules (however little I understand them). It looks decent enough, includes mouse controls, and even has in-game help so that if you don't know how to play (like me) you can read through it and learn. (I obviously didn't spend the time to do that.)

name: Hook, Line & Sinker
description: Hook, Line & Sinker is an entertaining flash game that revolves around fishing and adventure. In this game, players take on the role of a fisherman, navigating various water bodies to catch a wide variety of fish. The gameplay involves casting your line, reeling in catches, and upgrading your gear to improve your fishing skills. Players must pay attention to different fishing spots, each with unique fish species and challenges. As you progress, you can earn points to unlock new equipment and enhance your fishing experience. With colorful graphics and a relaxing soundtrack, Hook, Line and Sinker creates an enjoyable atmosphere for players who love fishing games. The combination of strategy and skill makes it a fun choice for players of all ages looking for a casual gaming experience.

name: Hooops
description: Hooops [sic] is a hoops-shooting basketball type game where the object is to time your throws to land the basketballs in the baskets. The hoops move back and forth and you'll need to avoid the blocker, which also moves around. You get 15 throws and you need to shoot before the shot clock hits zero. There's a brief "bonus game" that appears halfway through where you get one shot to earn extra points. A single high score is saved. Not a bad game, albeit a very simple one that could've appeared in a slightly different form on the Atari 2600 with some success.

name: Hoosier City
description: Hoosier City is an action-adventure game with puzzle elements, likely inspired by the mechanics and style of The Legend of Zelda games. It combines exploration, combat, and problem-solving, but it has a few issues in terms of gameplay execution. Gameplay Overview: Action and Adventure: The core gameplay involves guiding the player character (likely some form of adventurer or hero) through various environments, solving puzzles, and engaging in combat with enemies. Much like Zelda, the game would likely include dungeon exploration, enemy battles, and item collection, where players need to gather tools or power-ups to advance through areas or overcome obstacles. Puzzle Solving: The game includes puzzle-solving elements, which are key to progressing through levels or dungeons. These puzzles could range from moving blocks, activating switches, finding hidden paths, or even deciphering clues to unlock new areas. Combat: Similar to Zelda, combat might involve swordplay or the use of various items to defeat enemies. Players would need to battle through various opponents as they explore the world, facing both small enemies and possibly larger bosses at key points in the game. Exploration: The game encourages exploration, where players can uncover hidden areas, collect items, and meet NPCs who may provide helpful information or side quests. This open-world exploration is one of the key elements inspired by Zelda, giving players the freedom to wander and discover new locations. Key Features and Problems: Graphics: The game uses EGA graphics, which were a standard for early PC games. While these graphics have a retro charm, they may seem dated and less detailed compared to other action/adventure games, especially if you're used to modern visuals. Controls: The controls are often cited as a major flaw. Poor control mechanics can seriously hinder the gameplay experience, making movement or combat feel sluggish and unresponsive, detracting from the overall enjoyment. This issue can be especially frustrating in action games, where quick reactions and precise controls are critical for both combat and puzzle-solving. Gameplay Execution: Despite having the right idea and being inspired by classic games like Zelda, the game doesn't quite manage to execute its ideas well. This can lead to a less engaging experience, as players may feel that the puzzles or combat aren't as satisfying as in the games that inspired it. The game's difficulty, level design, or progression could also contribute to the feeling that the game isn't as fun as it could be. Fun Factor: While the game has the potential to be fun due to its inspiration from classic adventure games, its execution leaves much to be desired. If you are a fan of Zelda-style games, you may want to like this game, but it doesn't quite deliver on that promise, primarily due to poor controls and underwhelming gameplay mechanics.

name: Hop Mania
description: Hop Mania is a casual, fun, and engaging HTML5 game where players control a character or object that needs to jump over obstacles, avoid enemies, or collect items in various levels. The game typically features a simple, addictive gameplay loop, where players need quick reflexes to progress through increasingly difficult stages. Some versions of the game might include timing or direction-based mechanics, where players can control how far or high they jump. The simplicity of the controls allows for quick learning, making it accessible for players of all ages. Obstacles and Challenges: Players will face various obstacles in the form of pits, spikes, moving platforms, or enemies. They must time their jumps carefully to avoid these dangers and continue progressing. Some levels might introduce different mechanics, such as platforms that disappear or move, requiring players to think ahead and plan their jumps. Levels and Progression: Hop Mania typically features multiple levels, with increasing difficulty as the player progresses. Early levels might be simple, with slow-moving obstacles, but later stages could feature more complex challenges. The game may include a scoring system, where players get points based on how long they survive or how many items they collect. Some versions may also have a time limit or limited number of lives, adding more challenge. Power-ups and Collectibles: Some versions of Hop Mania may include power-ups that give the player extra abilities, such as higher jumps, temporary invincibility, or speed boosts. Collectibles, such as coins or gems, may be scattered across the levels, encouraging players to explore and perform well.

name: Horrorscopes
description: Horrorscopes is a unique, quirky DOS-based game released in 1995, developed by Horrorscope Software. The game is a combination of a horror-themed narrative and astrology-based gameplay, where players interact with various astrological signs and elements in a bizarre and unsettling environment. The game mixes fortune-telling with dark humor and supernatural themes. Gameplay Overview: Plot and Objective: In Horrorscopes, players take on the role of an astrologer or psychic, tasked with predicting the fates of various individuals or characters through a series of eerie and strange scenarios. The primary objective is to provide “readings” and predictions for the people who seek your astrological wisdom. However, this is not your typical astrology game—expect weird, creepy events to unfold as players proceed through the game. Astrology-Based Gameplay: Horrorscopes revolves around the zodiac, astrological signs, and horoscopes. Players interact with these elements to determine the future or fate of characters. Players can use astrology tools, such as reading star charts or deciphering cosmic events, to provide advice or make predictions. name: Horse Racing Game

name: House of Cards

Gameplay Overview: Objective: The main objective in House of Cards is to arrange a deck of cards in a pyramid structure and clear the cards from the board by pairing up cards that add up to a specific value (commonly 13). name: Hoverski
description: Hoverski is an interesting racing-type game which seems to have a lot of promise, however the actual execution is only average at best. The object is to race your hoverski around the track and complete the race as quickly as possible without running out of fuel. You can do tricks off jumps to gain more fuel. From the initial presentation I was expecting perhaps something like Wave Race 64 (which was released in 1996, a year before this game) but I suppose that was a bit unrealistic! The game is presented in 2D with a tiny (albeit well-animated) sprite repesenting your hoverski. The controls are responsive but the hoverski slides around a LOT and will take a lot of trial and error to get used to how it moves.

name: How-Two Build a Robot
description: How-Two Build a Robot is not, as you might assume, a robot-building simulation game. Rather it's an action/arcade game, somewhat similar to Elevator Action and probably many other games like this. The goal is to ... yes, build a robot. You do so by collecting parts, and then trying to assemble them into a working robot. The main enemy here seems to be your rapidly decreasing battery power, and never knowing which parts are in the boxes or where they're supposed to go. It's a difficult game with a lot of rules and things to remember!

name: Huarongdao
description: Huarongdao, also known as the "Huarong Trail" or "Chinese Puzzle," is a sliding block puzzle game. Avoid Unnecessary Moves: Try not to move pieces back and forth without making progress. Would you like tips for specific levels or strategies?

name: Hubie

The goal is to get Hubie to the exit of the level. Hubie has many abilities, such as pushing objects, crushing breakable objects, "coptering", blowing and climbing. name: Huge Spider Solitaire

name: Hugo 2: Whodunit?
description: The second of the trilogy of "Hugo" graphical adventure games, this game keeps the same style as the first but takes a murder mystery theme rather than a horror theme. You still play as the intrepid Hugo who, now along with Penelope whom he rescued in the first game, just want to rest on their vacation. However doings are afoot, and you'll soon be drawn into the action.Hugo 2: Whodunit? is an adventure game released in 1993 for DOS computers, developed by David R. As you interact with the mansion’s various rooms and objects, you’ll need to solve puzzles that might involve logic, memory, or even finding hidden items. name: Hugo III: Jungle of Doom
description: The third and last game in the Hugo series which began with the much more widely-known Hugo's House of Horrors. This game takes place after a plane crash in the jungle, after which Penelope is bitten by a poisonous snake. It's again up to Hugo to save the day! The same game engine is used as the previous games, with a few tweaks, like a hints engine. Hugo III: Jungle of Doom is the third installment in the Hugo series of adventure games, released in 1994 for DOS by Titus Interactive. name: Hugo's House of Horrors
description: This game is the first in the Hugo trilogy of graphical adventure games. Done in the style of those classic Sierra adventures, these feature EGA graphics and annoying PC speaker effects (which, thankfully, can be easily turned off). They're all fun to play, though, especially if you enjoy graphic adventure games.Hugo's House of Horrors is a classic point-and-click adventure game released in 1990 for DOS. Developed by David R. Babcock and published by Titus Interactive, the game is the first entry in the Hugo series. It is notable for its eerie atmosphere, simple graphics, and straightforward gameplay. The game combines elements of horror with puzzles, providing an early example of a horror-themed adventure game. Game Overview: Story and Setting: In Hugo's House of Horrors, you play as Hugo, a courageous adventurer who must rescue his girlfriend Polly from the clutches of the evil Wizard Wilter. The game begins when Hugo receives a mysterious letter from Polly, who has been captured and is held inside a haunted mansion. The mansion, filled with creepy corridors, secret rooms, and strange creatures, serves as the setting for the game. Hugo must explore the house, solve puzzles, and navigate through its dangers to rescue Polly. Gameplay: Point-and-Click Adventure: The game is a traditional point-and-click adventure, where players interact with the environment by moving Hugo around the mansion, clicking on objects, and solving puzzles. The puzzles are integrated into the house's design and require attention to detail and exploration. As players explore, they uncover more about the mansion’s mysteries, meet a variety of strange characters, and eventually come closer to rescuing Polly. For example, talking to NPCs (non-playable characters) may provide vital clues, but some characters may also pose a threat. name: Humbug
description: Humbug is one of the rare text adventure games you'll find on DOSGames.com, and it's here because it is truly a classic of the text adventure genre. The game has a Christmas theme. There are tons of locations to explore in this lengthy and well written adventure game, which contains over 200 objects. Humbug is a DOS game released in 1993 by Impressions Games. The game’s unique charm lies in its setting, which is inspired by the world of Charles Dickens’ "A Christmas Carol", though with a twist of whimsy and fun. Instead of being a traditional adaptation of the story, the game has you navigating through a series of humorous challenges set within a Christmas-themed environment. The main objective is to solve puzzles and interact with various characters in a somewhat whimsical, often humorous version of Victorian England. name: Hunchback
description: Hunchback is based on an old BBC Micro game. It was converted to PC in 1988 in glorious CGA! Originally a commercial product, the game was released by its original author for free. There are several levels, and the goal of each is to get Quasimodo to the other side to ring the bell. You'll need perfect timing to get past the obstacles. Hunchback is a DOS platform game released in 1983, developed by Ocean Software. It is a port of the arcade game of the same name, which was originally released by Sega. In the game, you control Quasimodo, the famous hunchback from Victor Hugo's novel "The Hunchback of Notre-Dame", as he attempts to rescue Esmeralda, a beautiful gypsy girl, while navigating a series of dangerous platforming challenges. The game was praised for its challenging gameplay, tight controls, and the opportunity for players to experience a unique adventure in a medieval setting. Game Overview: Story and Setting: The game is set in the Notre-Dame Cathedral in Paris, where you play as Quasimodo, the bell-ringer with a hunchback, who must rescue Esmeralda. The game is divided into stages, each with different types of obstacles and challenges. For example, in some levels, Quasimodo must jump over pits, avoid falling debris, and navigate moving platforms. Control Mechanics: The gameplay focuses on precise jumping and timing. You control Quasimodo’s movements as he jumps between platforms, climbs ladders, and avoids dangers. The levels become progressively harder, requiring faster reflexes and more careful planning. Rescuing Esmeralda: At the end of each stage, Quasimodo must save Esmeralda by reaching her location before time runs out. Successfully rescuing her moves the player to the next stage, where the difficulty increases.

name: Hunchback 96
description: Hunchback 96 (also known as "Rampart Rampage" for some reason) is a sort-of remaking of Hunchback which itself was a remaking of the original BBC Micro game. This game is more of a homage than a remake although it does include many similarities. The object is the same, get to the end of the level by jumping over obstacles.Hunchback '96 is a DOS platform game released in 1996, and it is an unofficial sequel or reimagining of the original Hunchback arcade game, which was initially released in 1983. Game Overview: Story and Setting: Hunchback '96 takes place in the familiar setting of the Notre-Dame Cathedral in Paris, where you play as Quasimodo, the hunchbacked bell ringer, who must navigate through various levels to rescue Esmeralda and overcome the challenges that await him. name: Hurkle Hunt
description: Hurkle Hunt is a simple game based on earlier games that were simply titled "Hurkle". The object is to find the mythical hurkle, and trap them by destroying all of the grid squares around it, before the hurkle is able to escape the grid of 10x10 squares. You only glimpse the hurkle briefly after it randomly moves. Although it works slightly differently than the previous versions of the game, it's quite similar. Graphics, sounds, and gameplay are all pretty basic. While there is some strategy, there is also a lot of luck involved, and winning can be difficult! Be sure to read the in-game documentation for some humorous instructions!

name: Hyper Blaster
