Weapons: The LHX and other helicopters are equipped with a variety of weapons such as missiles, machine guns, and bombs for attacking ground and air targets. Terrain: 3D Terrain: The game features an advanced 3D engine for its time, displaying varied terrain including mountains, valleys, and cities. Weather: Players may face changing weather conditions, such as rain or fog, which can affect visibility and mission success. Multiplayer: Two-player mode: LHX Attack Chopper allows players to engage in head-to-head combat in the multiplayer mode, adding an extra layer of fun and competitiveness.

name: Lianlian Kan
description: "Lianlian Kan" is a classic puzzle game that often features different themes, including car brands and other popular motifs. The gameplay typically involves matching tiles or items to clear them from the board, and it can be quite addictive. If you're looking for a specific Flash game with a car brand theme or similar puzzle games, it might be harder to find since many Flash games are no longer supported. However, you can look for modern versions or similar puzzle games on various online gaming platforms or app stores. If you need help finding alternatives, just let me know!

name: Liao Zhai Zhi Yi
description: Strange Tales from a Chinese Studio is an interactive fiction or visual novel game based on Pu Songling’s anthology of strange and supernatural stories. Pu Songling’s original collection of stories, written in the Qing dynasty, is a collection of ghost stories, mythical tales, and tales of strange occurrences often blending the supernatural with real life. It’s considered one of the most significant works of Chinese classical literature. The game would have been an attempt to bring these fantastical stories to life through the medium of text-based gameplay and basic graphics, typical of many early DOS-based games. These stories often involve elements like ghosts, spirits, demons, and mythical creatures, as well as themes of love, revenge, and justice.

name: Liero
description: In this game, you play a worm that's loaded up with some hefty ammunition! In this game which has obviously been heavily inspired by the classic Team-17 game Worms (and perhaps moreso gameplay-wise by the game Molez that came out the previous year) your job is to kill your opponent worm (CPU or 2nd player) as quickly as possible. Unlike Worms, your actions here are in real-time instead of being turn-based. This game features excellent control, great graphics, and SB sound effects. It's very polished, and plays well.

name: Life Sudoku
description: Everyday 4 new Sudoku puzzles and an archive of a month. Solve the puzzles using the Sudoku rules. Every number of 1-9 can only occur once in every row, column and 9x9 box.Life Sudoku is a creative twist on the classic Sudoku puzzle game. In this version, the game incorporates life-themed elements, such as color-coded grids, animated hints, or symbolic representations (e.g., animals, plants, or abstract patterns) instead of traditional numbers. This brings a refreshing, visually appealing approach to the logical challenge of Sudoku. Objective: The goal of Life Sudoku is the same as traditional Sudoku: complete a 9x9 grid (or smaller for easier levels) so that every row, column, and 3x3 subgrid contains unique elements without repetition. Instead of numbers, the elements in this variant could be life-related symbols such as flowers, animals, or colors. Gameplay Mechanics: Grid Layout: A standard 9x9 grid divided into nine 3x3 subgrids. Variations include smaller grids, like 4x4 or 6x6, for beginners. Symbols or Numbers: Players can fill the grid with unique symbols or numbers. For example: Symbols: Animals (cat, dog, bird, fish), plants, or other life-inspired visuals. Colors: Instead of digits, use distinct colors in each grid space. Numbers: Stick with traditional numbers (1-9) but add animations or life-themed backgrounds for variety. Hints and Validation: Players can request hints to highlight possible options for a given cell. Instant feedback to validate whether the player's entry is correct or conflicts with the rules. Levels of Difficulty: Easy: More pre-filled cells to make solving simpler. Medium: Moderate number of pre-filled cells, requiring logical deduction. Hard: Minimal pre-filled cells, challenging even experienced players. Timer and Scoring: Players can challenge themselves by completing the puzzle within a set time. Scoring is based on speed and accuracy.

name: Light Cycle
description: Light Cycle is a TRON-based Snake like game. And I really mean it, there is a strong TRON theme throughout the game, from the title screen to the sound effects. You play with four light cycles on the screen at a time, with a combination of human players and CPU opponents in whatever configuration you prefer. There are no options to set other than the players, and no extras available on the board (powerups, different maps, etc) so it's a pretty basic game, but it does work well enough if you can get used to the controls.

name: Light Mixer
description: Light Mixer is a fun and relaxing Flash puzzle game that revolves around creating beautiful light patterns by manipulating various light sources and using your creativity to solve puzzles. In the context of light mixing, these colors combine to form other colors (e.g., red + green = yellow, red + blue = magenta, and so on). Players may need to fill specific regions with certain colors or illuminate particular areas with the correct light combinations. The more advanced levels might introduce obstacles, like walls or barriers, that you need to figure out how to get the light around in order to solve the puzzle. Puzzle Solving: Each level in Light Mixer presents you with a puzzle that requires logical thinking and a basic understanding of color theory. The challenges become more difficult as the game progresses, introducing new mechanics such as moving obstacles, color filters, and increasingly complex targets. Players will need to experiment with different configurations of light sources and color combinations to find the solution. The game is typically non-competitive and designed to be a relaxing puzzle experience, where you can take your time to figure out each level. Visuals and Aesthetics: Light Mixer uses bright, colorful visuals that match the theme of light and color mixing. The game’s design is usually clean and simple, with easy-to-understand graphics that clearly show the color interactions. The game often features smooth animations when light beams interact with objects or fill the targeted areas with color. The aesthetic is usually calming and pleasant, making it ideal for players who enjoy visually engaging puzzle games.

name: Lightning Solitaire
description: Play your cards as fast as lightning. Move your cards to the 4 cards in the centre. Place cards that are 1 more or 1 less in value depending on the arrows below the centre cards.Lightning Solitaire is a fast-paced and thrilling card game that tests your reflexes and quick-thinking skills. Unlike traditional solitaire, the game focuses on speed and accuracy rather than strategic planning, making it an exciting challenge for players of all levels. Objective The goal of the game is to clear all the cards from the tableau by matching them to the discard piles based on their value, either one higher or one lower, as quickly as possible. Gameplay Mechanics Setup: The game begins with four discard piles and a deck of cards arranged in the tableau. Each discard pile starts with one card, while the rest are shuffled into the deck. How to Play: Match cards from the tableau to the discard piles. You can place a card if its value is one higher or one lower than the top card of the discard pile (e.g., place a 6 on a 5 or 7). Suit does not matter in this game. Special Rules: Aces can be placed on Kings or 2s. The game has a timer, encouraging players to make matches quickly. Winning: Clear all cards from the tableau before time runs out. Losing: If no moves are available or the timer expires, the game ends. Power-Ups (Optional): Undo: Revert your last move. Shuffle: Reshuffle remaining tableau cards for new opportunities.

name: Lights Out
description: Lights Out is an electronic game released by Tiger Electronics in 1995.The game consists of a 5 by 5 grid of lights. When the game starts, a random number or a stored pattern of these lights is switched on. Pressing any of the lights will toggle it and the adjacent lights. The goal of the puzzle is to switch all the lights off, preferably with as few button presses as possible. Merlin, a similar electronic game, was released by Parker Brothers in the 1970s with similar rules on a 3 by 3 grid. Another similar game was produced by Vulcan Electronics in 1983 under the name XL-25. Tiger Toys also produced a cartridge version of Lights Out for its Game com handheld game console in 1997, shipped free with the console. A number of new puzzles similar to Lights Out have been released, such as Lights Out 2000 (5×5 with multiple colors), Lights Out Cube (six 3×3 faces with effects across edges), and Lights Out Deluxe (6×6).

name: Line Rider Beta 2
description: Line Rider Beta 2 is one of the most beloved and influential Flash games ever created. Released as a follow-up to the original Line Rider, it allowed players to create and ride custom tracks made entirely out of lines. With a simple premise and an open-ended design, the game inspired millions to create and share their own tracks, leading to a vast and active community. Premise: Line Rider Beta 2 is a physics-based game that lets players create their own tracks by drawing lines on a blank canvas. You control a small sledder (a rider on a sled), and the goal is to design a track that he can safely ride down or even perform stunts on. The key to the game is in the physics: the sledder moves based on gravity and momentum, so your lines must be carefully drawn to create a fun or challenging ride. The sledder can ride on slopes, ramps, and loops, and you can even make him perform flips or tricks by adjusting the trajectory of the lines. Gameplay Mechanics: Drawing the Track: The main mechanic of Line Rider Beta 2 is the ability to draw lines that serve as the track for the sledder. You can draw straight lines, curves, ramps, and even loops. The lines will then interact with the sledder, causing him to ride along the path you’ve created. Physics: The game’s physics engine is based on basic principles of gravity and momentum. The sledder will naturally accelerate down slopes, slow down on inclines, and be affected by the curvature of the lines. Getting the sledder to the end of a track without falling off requires careful planning and understanding of the physics. Test Your Track: Once you’ve drawn a track, you can test it by clicking the "play" button, which will make the sledder ride the track. If your track is too steep, too shallow, or too bumpy, the sledder might fall off, crash, or fail to complete the ride. Editing the Track: If the sledder crashes or you want to try a different route, you can easily edit the track by drawing new lines or erasing parts of the track. This allows for an iterative process of designing and testing tracks. Stunts and Tricks: By adjusting the angles and heights of your lines, you can create ramps and loops that let the sledder perform flips or other stunts. The sledder can even perform backflips and frontflips if the trajectory is right. Physics Objects: In Beta 2, players can also use objects like snowflakes, speed boosts, and other features to enhance their tracks and make the sledder’s journey more interesting.

name: Lines and Blocks
description: Tetris like puzzle game: Create long horizontal or vertical lines with the lines on the falling blocks. Make lines of 3 or more in length to remove them. Remove as many lines as the indicated goal to advance to the next level. Touch a block to rotate it, touch a column to move the block and swipe a block down. You can also use the controls to the right of the playing area.Lines and Blocks is a puzzle game where players arrange falling blocks on a grid to form complete lines. Inspired by classic block-stacking games, it combines strategy and quick reflexes to clear lines and score points. The game ends when the blocks stack up to the top of the grid. Objective: The goal is to manipulate the falling blocks, rotating or moving them horizontally, to create horizontal lines without gaps. Once a line is complete, it disappears, and the player earns points. As the game progresses, the blocks fall faster, increasing the challenge. Gameplay Mechanics: Grid Layout: A vertical grid (e.g., 10x20) where blocks fall from the top. Blocks come in various shapes, including straight lines, squares, L-shapes, T-shapes, and Z-shapes. Block Movement: Players can move blocks left, right, or down. Blocks can also be rotated to fit into gaps. Line Clearing: A full horizontal line is cleared from the grid. Cleared lines earn points and create space for new blocks. Difficulty Progression: The speed of falling blocks increases as the game progresses. Game Over: The game ends when blocks stack up to the top of the grid.

name: Lines and blocks 2
description: Create horizontal or vertical lines with the lines on the falling blocks. Create lines of 3 or more in length to remove them. Remove as many lines as the indicated goal to advance to the next level. Touch a block to rotate it, touch a column to move the block and swipe a block down. You can also use the controls to the right of the playing area.Lines and Blocks 2 is a sequel to the classic block-stacking game, featuring new mechanics, enhanced graphics, and dynamic gameplay. This version introduces new block shapes, power-ups, and a level-based progression system. The core objective remains: stack blocks to create complete horizontal lines and clear them to score points. Objective: Clear horizontal lines by strategically placing falling blocks on the grid. With each level, the game introduces faster block drops and new challenges, such as obstacles or special blocks that enhance gameplay. Gameplay Mechanics: Grid Layout: A vertical grid (e.g., 10x20) where blocks fall from the top. New block shapes and sizes add variety to the gameplay. Power-ups: Bomb Block: Clears a small area of the grid when placed. Line Clearer: Automatically clears a full horizontal line. Freeze Block: Slows down the game temporarily. Level Progression: Completing a set number of lines progresses the player to the next level. Each level increases the drop speed of the blocks and introduces unique challenges, such as immovable blocks or smaller grids. Obstacles: Blocks that cannot be moved or cleared unless a line passes through them. Randomized "junk" blocks that must be worked around. Game Over: The game ends when blocks stack up to the top of the grid.

name: LineWars II
description: Line Wars was a popular "3D" shooting game that was released long before the advent of modern 3D gaming cards. While its gameplay is quite tame compared to today's standards, it can still be fun. Line Wars II updates the original adding new missions and multiplayer modes. (Multiplayer is achived through a modem or DOS-based network.) The game includes three different missions of varying difficulty. This is the full version of the game that has been released for free by its author.LineWars II is a sequel to the original LineWars, a space combat simulation game designed for DOS platforms. Released in 1994 by Patrick Aalto, the game is a blend of action-packed dogfighting, tactical fleet management, and space exploration. It features smooth 3D wireframe graphics and supports both single-player and multiplayer modes. Gameplay In LineWars II, players assume the role of a space pilot navigating a vast, three-dimensional battlefield. The primary objective is to eliminate enemy fleets while protecting your base and resources. Players control a spacecraft armed with lasers, missiles, and shields to engage in high-stakes combat. Key Features: 3D Wireframe Graphics: The game showcases dynamic 3D graphics, which was advanced for its time, allowing for immersive space battles. Multiplayer Mode: Up to two players can engage in head-to-head battles via modem or serial connection, a significant feature for a DOS game. Fleet Management: Players not only pilot their own ship but also oversee a fleet, issuing commands to allied ships for strategic advantages. Resource Management: Refueling, rearming, and repairing ships add layers of strategy, requiring players to manage their base's resources effectively. Varied Enemy AI: The game pits players against increasingly challenging AI opponents, including aggressive fighters, capital ships, and turrets.

name: Link Numbers
description: Add numbers and link all numbers to one path. Add a number in an empty cell, you can connect numbers horizontally, vertically and diagonally.Link Numbers is a fun and challenging puzzle game that tests your logical thinking and pattern recognition skills. Players must connect numbers in a grid to achieve specific goals, such as forming chains or solving mathematical equations. It's an engaging game for people who love math and puzzles! Objective The primary goal of the game is to link numbers by drawing lines between them to meet the target criteria, such as matching totals, creating sequences, or connecting identical numbers. Gameplay Mechanics Setup: A grid of numbers is displayed on the game board. Each level has specific objectives, such as linking numbers to form a target sum or creating a specific pattern. How to Play: Click and drag to connect numbers horizontally, vertically, or diagonally. Chains can only link adjacent numbers. The line must be continuous, and numbers cannot be reused in the same chain. Winning: Complete the level objective (e.g., link numbers to form the sum of 15). Clear the entire grid in some levels. Losing: If there are no valid moves left or the objective is not met within a given time or move limit. Additional Features: Power-ups: Shuffle the grid or highlight a possible move. Challenges: Time limits, limited moves, or locked tiles.

name: Link-Four
description: Link-Four is a PC adaptation of the Connect Four board game where players take turns dropping colored discs into a grid, attempting to get four of their own color in a row horizontally, vertically, or diagonally. It's from 1986 so it's presented in CGA color, and offers the ability to play against a second player or a CPU opponent. That's pretty much it.Link-Four is a DOS-based strategy and puzzle game inspired by the classic Connect Four board game. Developed in the 1990s, it challenges players to strategically place tokens on a grid to form a horizontal, vertical, or diagonal line of four pieces before their opponent does. Gameplay Objective: The goal is to connect four of your pieces in a row (horizontally, vertically, or diagonally) on a 7x6 grid. Game Modes: Single Player: Compete against an AI opponent with varying difficulty levels. Multiplayer: Play against a friend in a turn-based manner on the same computer. How to Play: Players take turns dropping tokens into one of the columns of the grid. The token falls to the lowest available row in the selected column. The first player to connect four tokens wins the game. If the grid fills up without a winner, the game ends in a draw. Key Features Simple Controls: Players use the keyboard (e.g., number keys or arrow keys) to select a column for dropping their token. Color-Coded Tokens: Each player is assigned a color (e.g., red and yellow), making it easy to distinguish between tokens. AI Opponent: The AI opponent provides a challenge with varying levels of difficulty, from beginner to expert. Graphics and Sound: Minimalist graphics and sound effects typical of DOS games, focusing on gameplay rather than aesthetics.

name: Liquid War 5
description: Liquid War is a particle-physics-based "multiplayer wargame". In the game you control an "army of liquid" and your goal is to overpower / consume your opponent(s). It works sort of like a Snake / Nibbles type game, but it actually feels much different to play. You can have up to six human or CPU opponents at once, and there are many options available to set The game received a lot of attention when it was first released, especially since it was available on multiple platforms (including Linux) and was even featured in a segment on CNN. Take a look for a unique competitive multiplayer game.

name: Litil Divil
description: Litil Divil is an interesting game with high production values and a lot of variety in its gameplay. The developer describes it like this: "Joint Mutt in his incredible adventures - a fabulous cartoon-animated adventure literally packed full of action, humour and puzzling conundrums." This demo of the game begins with a short action swordfighting like experience, which transitions into a maze sort of 3D-ish hallway, which continues on from there, also including puzzle aspects.Litil Divil is an action-adventure game released in 1993 by Gremlin Graphics for DOS and other platforms. The game follows the mischievous and curious imp, Mutt, as he navigates a labyrinth filled with traps, puzzles, and enemies to retrieve the mystical “Firestone.” Storyline Mutt, a mischievous demon from the underworld, is tasked with retrieving the legendary Firestone from the labyrinth as part of a rite of passage. The labyrinth is a treacherous maze filled with deadly traps, strange creatures, and mind-bending puzzles. Mutt must rely on his cunning, agility, and occasional brute force to survive and complete his mission. Gameplay Litil Divil combines exploration, puzzle-solving, and combat in a unique and humorous setting. Labyrinth Exploration: Players guide Mutt through a sprawling maze of interconnected rooms and corridors. Each area presents new challenges, from combat sequences to environmental puzzles. Puzzles: Players must solve a variety of puzzles that test logic and observation, such as unlocking doors, activating mechanisms, or figuring out patterns. Combat: Mutt encounters various enemies, which he must defeat using melee weapons or clever tactics. Players need to manage Mutt’s health and inventory to survive tough encounters. Humor and Animation: The game is known for its cartoonish humor, quirky sound effects, and charming animations, bringing Mutt’s personality to life. Key Features Unique Art Style: The game features colorful and detailed 2D graphics with smooth animations. Challenging Gameplay: The labyrinth is filled with devious traps, making the game both challenging and rewarding. Varied Environments: From eerie dungeons to quirky themed rooms, each area offers a unique experience. Memorable Characters: Mutt is an endearing protagonist whose expressive reactions add to the game’s charm. Soundtrack and Effects: The music and sound effects enhance the game’s immersive and comedic atmosphere.

name: Little Willy
description: Little Willy is a platformer game that is inspired by Crystal Caves. The look and feel of the game, the layout of the main map (where you can choose from one of several levels to play) and even the main character looks quite similar. There is a brief story introduction (just start the game, it will automatically force you to watch it) and then you'll be jumping and shooting your way through many levels of one-hit deaths. The game controls well and provides infinite lives to try and try again!Willy, the protagonist, is a small, adventurous boy on a mission to navigate through various challenging levels to complete tasks and solve puzzles. The game's plot is simple yet engaging, as Willy faces multiple environments, ranging from castles to caves, all filled with quirky challenges and adversaries. Throughout his journey, Willy encounters strange creatures and must solve puzzles in order to advance. Gameplay Little Willy is a platformer with a focus on puzzle-solving and exploration. Players control Willy as he navigates through different levels filled with obstacles, traps, and enemies. Platforming Mechanics: The game includes traditional platformer elements such as jumping, climbing, and running. Willy must jump over pits, avoid spikes, and cross moving platforms while collecting items along the way. Puzzle Elements: Each level is designed with a mix of platforming and puzzles that require the player to think critically and figure out how to proceed. Players must solve environmental puzzles, activate switches, and avoid traps in order to reach the end of each level. Enemies: The game features a variety of enemies that Willy must avoid or defeat. Some enemies require quick reflexes to avoid, while others can be outsmarted by solving puzzles. Level Design: The game is divided into multiple levels, each with a unique theme and set of challenges. From castles to caves, each area provides new obstacles and mechanics for the player to tackle. Item Collection: Willy can collect power-ups or items scattered across the levels that help him overcome specific challenges or defeat enemies. Key Features Platforming Action: The game features classic platforming mechanics, with a mix of jumping, running, and avoiding hazards. Challenging Puzzles: The puzzle-solving elements add depth to the game, making it more than just a simple platformer. Varied Environments: Levels are set in different themed environments such as castles, caves, and forests, each with its own unique challenges. Character Interaction: The interactions between Willy and the game environment often have humorous or quirky elements, giving the game a lighthearted tone. Colorful Graphics and Animation: The game features vibrant, cartoonish graphics and smooth animation that were appealing for its time.

name: Lizard
description: If you enjoyed the old-school style platforming games of the NES, you'll likely enjoy Lizard, a new game that was actually developed for the original Nintendo system (it was even released on cartridges) and later ported to DOS. You play as a lizard of course, actually one of six different lizards that can be discovered / changed into throughout the game world. The graphics and sounds of this game really bring to mind the days of the NES. The gameplay reminds me somewhat of Legacy of the Wizard, I mean how the jumping and and platforming feel, and the differing scrolling of the different areas.

name: Llamatron 2112
description: The plot of Llamatron 2112 is rather simple and absurd in typical Jeff Minter fashion. The game is set in a dystopian future where a mysterious alien force is wreaking havoc. The protagonist, a brave, laser-shooting llama, is tasked with saving the world by fighting off waves of enemies. Players must traverse through levels filled with alien enemies, obstacles, and environmental hazards to achieve their goal. Gameplay Llamatron 2112 is a top-down, multi-directional shooter, with an emphasis on fast-paced action and high-intensity combat. The player controls a llama that shoots lasers in all directions, and the objective is to survive waves of enemies, collect power-ups, and defeat bosses. Player Control: The player controls the llama, which can move freely around the screen using the keyboard or joystick. The llama automatically fires lasers in the direction the player moves, and the gameplay involves avoiding enemies while shooting at them. Enemies: The game features a wide array of alien enemies, each with different attack patterns and behavior. Some enemies may shoot back, while others charge toward the player, making it a chaotic and unpredictable environment. Power-ups and Weapons: As players progress through levels, they can collect various power-ups, including additional weapons, health boosts, and special items that enhance the llama's abilities. The llama can gain access to stronger weapons, such as rapid-fire lasers, bombs, and other devastating abilities. Levels: The game consists of multiple levels, each featuring different layouts, enemy types, and challenges. The goal in each level is to destroy all enemies and survive long enough to advance to the next stage. Boss Fights: At the end of certain levels, the player faces off against powerful bosses that require strategic thinking and quick reflexes to defeat. Key Features Fast-Paced Gameplay: Llamatron 2112 is known for its fast and chaotic gameplay. The player is constantly under attack by waves of enemies, requiring quick thinking and fast reflexes to survive. Psychedelic Visuals: The game's vibrant, trippy graphics feature bright neon colors and bizarre enemy designs, contributing to its surreal and humorous atmosphere. Humor and Quirky Elements: The game is filled with Minter's signature humor, including oddball enemies, quirky sound effects, and eccentric gameplay mechanics. The idea of controlling a laser-shooting llama is itself a humorous element that adds to the game's charm. Addictive Action: The game features a simple but addictive gameplay loop: move, shoot, dodge, and survive. The escalating difficulty keeps the player engaged as they progress through increasingly difficult levels. Multiplayer: Llamatron 2112 features a cooperative multiplayer mode, where two players can team up to defeat enemies and work together to advance through the levels.

name: Loader Larry
description: Combining puzzle elements with some light jumping action, Loader Larry is a unique kind of puzzle game. The goal is simply to get Larry to the exit of the room by carrying and pushing boxes around. It's tougher than you'd think! And there are lots of little varients to keep the action going. Pretty good game, passable graphics, PC beeper sounds.The story of Loader Larry is fairly simple and straightforward. Larry is a warehouse loader, who needs to move crates to specific locations within a large warehouse, with the ultimate goal of efficiently organizing the warehouse. However, there are many obstacles, moving platforms, and tight spaces in the warehouse that require careful planning and strategy. The challenge comes from figuring out the right sequence of moves to avoid getting stuck or running out of time while solving each level's puzzle. Gameplay Mechanics Basic Controls: Players control Larry, who can move left and right, jump, and interact with crates. The game has a top-down or side-scrolling view, with multiple levels inside the warehouse, each with unique obstacles. Puzzle Elements: The main gameplay revolves around moving crates onto specific spots on the warehouse floor. There are conveyor belts, elevators, and moving platforms that Larry can use to transport the crates, but these platforms also present obstacles if the player is not careful. Players need to plan their moves carefully to avoid getting stuck, as crates cannot be moved back once they are in a particular position. Time Limits: Some levels may have time limits, forcing players to move quickly while still solving the puzzles effectively. Obstacles: The warehouse is filled with obstacles that Larry needs to avoid, including other workers, machinery, or sometimes hazardous zones that may damage Larry if touched. Levels: The game includes multiple levels, each more complex than the last. As the game progresses, new obstacles and challenges are introduced, such as locked crates, moving elevators, or switches that open doors or activate conveyor belts. Each level has specific objectives (e.g., move crates to specific marked locations) that need to be completed to proceed to the next. Key Features Puzzle-Solving Platformer: The game combines traditional platforming with puzzle elements, requiring players to think critically about each move and solve spatial challenges. Increasing Difficulty: The game starts with relatively simple puzzles, but as players advance, the puzzles become increasingly challenging and require more strategic planning. Time Pressure: Some levels impose time limits, adding an extra layer of difficulty and urgency to the game. Charming Pixel Art: The game’s graphics are typical of early 90s DOS games, featuring pixelated art that captures the industrial warehouse setting. The design is clear, and the environments are varied, with different warehouse areas, moving platforms, and obstacles. Simple Controls: The control scheme is straightforward, allowing players to move, jump, and interact with objects. This simplicity makes it easy to pick up but hard to master. Sound Effects and Music: The game features basic sound effects, including crate-moving sounds, character movement, and background music, fitting the puzzle-solving atmosphere.

name: Lobster
description: Lobster is described by the author as "a tribute to Worms, Scorched Earth, Over The Hill, and whatnot." It does play like a simple version of these more popular games, with limited options. Choose the number of players (up to 5) and which are humans / CPU opponents, then set the power/angle of your shot and try to blow 'em all up. There are no difficulty settings for the CPU players. There are a couple other weapons included; you'll need to play multiple rounds, as the winners get money to buy stuff in-between. Overall it plays well enough but not a lot to differentiate it from other similar games.

name: Lock 'N' Chase
description: As you might expect from the name, this is a clone of the Atari 2600 game Lock 'N' Chase. (I recall playing it on the Intellivision personally.) It's a faithful rendition of the Atari 2600 game, with almost identical graphics and gameplay. It plays similar to Pac-Man, where the goal is to collect all the gold bars in the maze and avoid enemies. Rather than power pills, you can put up temporary barriers to block the enemies. (This is perhaps the smallest game on the site, only 4kb compiled!)The game follows the protagonist, Chase, who is on a mission to collect coins hidden throughout a maze. However, the maze is filled with guards who will chase him down and stop him from collecting all of the coins. To outwit them, Chase must use his ability to unlock gates that block paths, adding a layer of strategy to the gameplay. The objective is to collect all the coins while avoiding the guards and unlocking gates to escape from their pursuit. Gameplay Mechanics Player Control: The player controls Chase, who moves around the maze and collects coins. The movement is directional, using either the arrow keys or joystick for left, right, up, and down navigation. Coins: The maze contains a series of coins scattered throughout. Chase's goal is to collect all of these coins to complete the level. Each coin adds to the score, and the player must clear the maze of all coins before moving on to the next level. Enemies (Guards): The maze is patrolled by guards who move in a pattern and chase Chase when they see him. If they catch him, the player loses a life. The guards follow a set route, but their behavior becomes more aggressive as the game progresses. Locks and Keys: The maze has locked gates that block certain areas. To open these gates, the player must find and use keys scattered in the maze. The addition of locks and keys requires the player to plan their route carefully and strategically unlock paths while avoiding the guards. Speed Boost: The player can pick up speed boosts that allow Chase to temporarily move faster, making it easier to evade the guards and complete the level. Power-Ups: Some versions of the game include power-ups that allow Chase to temporarily turn the tables on the guards, such as items that freeze or eliminate enemies for a brief period.

name: Lode Runner Live
description: Lode Runner Live is a competent implementation of the classic Lode Runner game. It plays quite similarly to the original game, where the object is to collect all the gold bars and avoid the enemies. You can make holes in the ground on either side of you to temporarily trap your opponents. However this game is still quite difficult, or maybe I'm just bad at it! You get a bunch of levels included and you can create your own using the built-in level editor.Lode Runner Live is a version of the classic Lode Runner series, originally developed by Douglas E. Smith and released in 1983. While the original Lode Runner was initially released on various platforms including DOS, Lode Runner Live is a specific version that brings the game's puzzle-platform mechanics into a more modern setting, released in the early 2000s for online play and LAN multiplayer. It retains the core elements of the classic gameplay while introducing a multiplayer mode, making it a unique iteration in the Lode Runner series.

name: Logger
description: Logger is a very simple text-mode game that plays a little bit like the classic arcade game Frogger. You have to zip between the top and bottom of the screen, collecting treasures and avoiding the horizontally-scrolling logs and other hazards. If you collect the minimum number for a level, you'll progress to the next. The game plays fluidly (for text-mode) and it's surprisingly enjoyable given how simple it is at its core.The story behind Logger is straightforward and simple: players control a lumberjack who is tasked with chopping down trees in a forest. The goal is to clear the trees efficiently while avoiding dangers such as falling logs, wild animals, and other obstacles. Each level introduces new challenges that force the player to think quickly and act strategically. Gameplay Mechanics Player Control: The player controls a lumberjack character who must move around the forest, cutting down trees. The lumberjack uses an axe to chop trees, and the primary objective is to chop down all trees in a given level. Chopping Trees: Players chop trees by pressing a button to swing the axe. Trees must be felled in a way that allows the player to clear a path through the level. The trees will fall in different directions based on where the player is standing, requiring strategic thinking. Obstacles and Hazards: As the player progresses through levels, different obstacles and hazards appear, such as falling logs, wild animals, or moving platforms. Players must avoid these dangers while still chopping down trees. Falling logs are a significant threat as they can crush the player if they’re not careful. Levels: The game includes a series of progressively more challenging levels. Each level contains a specific number of trees that need to be chopped down, and the difficulty increases as the levels progress. New challenges, such as more aggressive animals or tricky tree arrangements, are introduced as players advance. Power-ups and Items: Players can collect power-ups and special items that give them advantages, such as extra speed, temporary invincibility, or an extended axe range, making it easier to chop down trees and avoid enemies. Time Limit: Some levels feature a time limit that challenges the player to chop down all the trees before time runs out. This adds an element of urgency and forces players to think fast while dealing with obstacles. Lives and Scoring: Players begin with a set number of lives. If the lumberjack is hit by a falling log or other hazards, they lose a life. The goal is to complete each level without running out of lives. Points are earned by chopping trees, avoiding hazards, and completing levels quickly. High scores are tracked, adding replay value.

name: Logo
description: Also known as "that game where you draw using the Turtle", Logo is described by the Logo Foundation thusly: "The Logo programming environments that have been developed over the past 28 years are rooted in constructivist educational philosophy, and are designed to support constructive learning." Uh, right. So basically you issue text commands to draw on the screen by making the little turtle guy move around. An interesting game-like program that was intended to be used primarily as a child's first "programming" experience; nowadays we might have other methods to do that, but for some of today's programmers this was indeed their first experience.

name: Lomax Coltris
description: Lomax Coltris is a game which includes Columns and Tetris games in a single package. So its name is apt. There are two separate games included, to be clear, not some combination of the two. You get T.Tris which is Tetris and Col.ums which is Columns. The graphics are well done and you get some fancy screen-clearing effects. There are sound effects as well, but no music (at least, no music plays in DOSBox). By default it feels like the games play a little too fast, but you can change the game speed in the options menu.

name: London Cabbie
description: Overview: "London Cabbie" is an engaging flash game that puts players behind the wheel of a classic London taxi. Navigate the bustling streets of London, pick up passengers, and drop them off at their desired destinations while managing time and traffic. Key Features: Realistic Driving Experience: Experience the challenges of driving a taxi in a busy city, including navigating through traffic, following road signs, and adhering to speed limits. Passenger Pickup and Drop-off: Locate passengers on the map and pick them up. Each passenger has a unique destination, and players must plan the best route to get them there quickly. Time Management: Complete rides within a set time limit to earn tips and improve your rating as a taxi driver. Upgrades and Customization: Use earnings to upgrade your taxi with better features, such as improved speed, handling, and passenger comfort. Challenges and Missions: Take on specific challenges, such as reaching a certain number of passengers in a limited time or completing special missions during busy events. Open World Exploration: Explore a detailed map of London, including iconic landmarks and neighborhoods, enhancing the immersive experience. Visual and Audio Elements: Graphics: Stylized 3D graphics depicting the vibrant streets of London, with detailed environments and character animations. Soundtrack: An upbeat soundtrack with realistic sound effects of city life, including honking horns and chatter from passengers. "London Cabbie" offers an exciting mix of driving challenges and time management, providing players with the thrill of navigating one of the world's most famous cities. description: Love Manager (or as it's displayed in the game, L♥ve Manager) is an action / arcade game that is sort of a cross between Elevator Action and a Game & Watch game? Maybe there's some other game that's cloning, but I'm not aware of it. Anyways you're controlling the elevator and trying to get people from the left side to the right side to match up with a SO; also get the hospital workers to the bottom level, and probably some other stuff I'm forgetting. It's fast, and a little confusing, but definitely worth a try if you want a game that would have been popular in the early arcades. (And maybe it was, let me know if you can name an arcade game that this copies ...)

name: Loved
description: Loved is a unique and emotionally charged Flash game created by Alexander "Moppin". It's often regarded as a standout indie game from the era of Flash games due to its innovative storytelling, minimalistic design, and use of simple mechanics to convey a deeper narrative. Released in 2008, Loved explores themes of self-worth, identity, and the human condition, all through an abstract, interactive experience. Premise: Loved is a platformer where the player controls a small, white figure that navigates through a series of abstract, minimalist environments. The game does not have a clear plot or dialogue but instead focuses on creating an emotional journey using visuals, sound, and player choices. The game is notable for how it interacts with the player’s decisions, subtly shifting its mechanics based on how the player behaves, particularly with respect to obeying or defying instructions. The central theme of the game revolves around control and choice, where the player's actions influence the game’s progression and its emotional impact. Gameplay Mechanics: Movement: The player controls a small, white character (often referred to as a "figure") and can move left, right, and jump through a series of levels. The levels are simple, with few obstacles beyond platforms and occasional traps. Choices and Obedience: One of the core mechanics of Loved is how the game interacts with the player's actions. Early in the game, the player is told by a voice (which appears throughout the game) to follow certain rules, such as jumping at specific points or avoiding obstacles. The game frequently prompts the player to obey or disobey these instructions. The voice, which often appears as an omnipresent, commanding figure, will either praise the player for following instructions or punish them for not following the prescribed path. This mechanic reflects themes of control, submission, and rebellion. Player Choice and Consequence: The game tracks your behavior and adjusts accordingly. If you obey the instructions, you might receive praise and progress smoothly, but if you rebel or fail to comply, the game might punish you or shift its tone. This element is integral to Loved's narrative experience. It explores how different approaches (obedience vs. defiance) lead to different outcomes.

name: Lucky Clover
description: Remove all the clover from the field. Click on clover to let it grow. When you grow a 4 leaf clover it shoots leafs that grows other clover. Use as less moves as possible to remove all your clover.Lucky Clover is a fun and engaging match-3 puzzle game that centers around a lucky clover theme, with vibrant graphics and a festive atmosphere. The game features a variety of colorful clovers, coins, and other lucky symbols that players need to match in order to score points and progress through levels. It is designed for players who enjoy solving puzzles, making strategic moves, and uncovering hidden surprises. The goal of Lucky Clover is to match three or more identical symbols in a grid, completing level objectives, and earning rewards as you advance through the game. With a combination of classic match-3 mechanics and thematic elements tied to luck and good fortune, Lucky Clover offers a refreshing and enjoyable gaming experience. Gameplay Mechanics Objective: In Lucky Clover, the primary objective is to swap adjacent symbols (like clovers, coins, or lucky items) to form matches of three or more identical symbols. These matches disappear from the board, and new symbols fall into place. Each level has specific goals that players must achieve, such as reaching a certain score, collecting particular items, or clearing obstacles within a set number of moves or time limit. Match-3 Gameplay: The core gameplay is based on traditional match-3 mechanics, where players need to make matches of three or more symbols in a row, either horizontally or vertically. The symbols on the board then disappear, and new symbols fill the empty spaces. Matching four or more symbols in a single move creates power-ups or special symbols that have enhanced abilities, like clearing entire rows or columns, or destroying obstacles. Power-ups and Boosters: Lucky Clover includes several power-ups and boosters that help players in difficult situations. These power-ups include: Bombs: Clear a specific area or a set of symbols. Lightning Strikes: Clear an entire row or column of symbols. Clovers: Wild symbols that can match with any other symbol to create a match. Shovels: Remove an unwanted symbol from the board to create space for a new match. These boosters can be used strategically to help players overcome tough levels or reach higher scores. Levels and Objectives: The game contains multiple levels, each with a unique layout and set of objectives. Common level objectives include: Score Goals: Achieve a certain score within a set number of moves or time. Item Collection: Collect specific items like lucky clovers or coins scattered on the board. Clearing Obstacles: Clear blocked tiles, frozen tiles, or other obstacles that stand in the way of progress. Some levels may have time limits, requiring quick thinking and fast matching, while others may be move-based, requiring careful planning. Obstacles: Lucky Clover introduces several types of obstacles to make the game more challenging. These obstacles can include: Frozen Tiles: Tiles that are locked in place and can only be cleared with special moves or multiple matches. Stone Blocks: Obstacles that require powerful moves or power-ups to clear. Locked Symbols: Items that cannot be moved or matched until unlocked. Lives and Scoring: Players have a limited number of lives. When they fail a level, they lose a life. If they run out of lives, they must wait for them to regenerate, or they can buy more lives. The game uses a scoring system, where players earn points for each match they make. They are also rewarded for completing levels quickly or with fewer moves. Higher scores are often rewarded with stars or other in-game achievements. Lucky Events: The game might feature lucky events or bonuses that provide additional rewards or boosts to players. For example, a lucky event might give players the chance to earn extra points, unlock new levels, or receive free boosters.

name: Ludo
description: The board game Ludo against 3 AI opponents. Be the first to get all your tokens to the finish.Ludo is a classic board game that has been enjoyed by people of all ages for generations. The game is typically played by 2 to 4 players and is a race-based game where players move their tokens around the board based on dice rolls, with the goal of getting all their tokens from the starting area to the home area first. In the HTML version of Ludo, the game is digitized for easy play in web browsers, with interactive controls and AI or multiplayer options. Whether you're playing with friends or against the computer, the HTML version of Ludo brings this popular game into the digital world, keeping the same fun mechanics while offering smooth, accessible gameplay. Gameplay Mechanics Objective: The main objective of Ludo is for a player to move all of their four tokens around the board from the starting area to the home area before the other players. Each player controls one set of tokens, which are moved based on dice rolls. Basic Setup: The game is played on a square board, divided into four colored sections (one for each player). Each player has four tokens placed in their starting area (home). Players take turns rolling a six-sided dice to determine how many spaces they can move their token(s). The first player to move all four of their tokens to the home area wins the game. Moving Tokens: Players begin by rolling a six to move a token from the starting area onto the track. Once a token is on the track, it can be moved forward according to the roll of the dice. For example, if a player rolls a 4, they move one of their tokens four spaces forward. Players can stack multiple tokens on a single space, blocking the other players from landing on it, unless the other player also has a token there. Special Rules: Rolling a 6: When a player rolls a 6, they are allowed to roll again. If a player rolls a 6 three times in a row, they lose their turn. Safety Zone: Some versions of the game have a safe zone, where tokens are safe from being captured by other players. Capture: If a player's token lands on an opponent's token (and the opponent is not in a safety zone), the opponent's token is sent back to its starting area. Winning the Game: To win, a player must get all four of their tokens to the home area. Tokens enter the home area when they have completed a full loop around the board. The player must roll the exact number needed to land on the home area; for example, if a player is one space away from the home area and they roll a 5, they must wait for another turn.

name: Ludo
description: "Ludo" is a vibrant and engaging flash game based on the classic board game that brings players together in a race to get all their pieces home. The game features a colorful board where 2 to 4 players can compete against each other or against AI. Players take turns rolling a virtual dice to move their pieces around the board, aiming to reach their home base first. Special spaces allow for strategic jumps and blockades, while landing on opponents' pieces sends them back to the starting point, adding a competitive edge. With eye-catching graphics and smooth gameplay, "Ludo" captures the essence of the original game while providing fun sound effects and animations. Whether playing with friends or going solo, this flash game offers a delightful mix of luck and strategy that keeps everyone entertained!

name: Ludo Dash
description: Ludo Dash is a fast-paced and exciting variation of the classic Ludo board game. This HTML version takes the traditional Ludo game and adds a unique twist, focusing on quick turns, strategy, and faster gameplay. Players race to move their tokens around the board while making quick decisions based on dice rolls and available moves, adding an element of speed and competition to the classic Ludo formula. Gameplay Mechanics Objective: The main objective in Ludo Dash is the same as traditional Ludo: to move all your tokens from the starting area to the home area before other players. However, in Ludo Dash, the game is played at a faster pace, and players must make quick moves and react faster to stay ahead of their opponents. Setup: The game can be played by 2 to 4 players, each controlling four tokens that start from their respective starting areas. The board is divided into four color-coded sections, and each player’s tokens are represented by their corresponding color. The tokens move along the board in a clockwise direction from start to finish. Turn-Based System: Players take turns rolling a dice to determine how far they can move their token(s). In Ludo Dash, players must decide quickly which token to move, making the game more intense. Unlike traditional Ludo, where players can take their time between turns, Ludo Dash encourages speedy decisions and quick reactions. Special Rules in Ludo Dash: Time Limit: Each player has a limited amount of time to make their move. This adds an element of pressure to the game, requiring players to think and act quickly. No Rolling Doubles: Some versions of Ludo Dash may exclude the rule of rolling doubles (where players get an extra roll for rolling two matching dice numbers), making the game even faster-paced and competitive. Quick Capture: Players can capture their opponents’ tokens by landing on them, sending the captured token back to its starting area. However, because of the time limit, capturing requires fast and strategic decisions. Dice Rolls: Players roll the dice just like in traditional Ludo, with numbers ranging from 1 to 6. The result of the roll determines how many spaces a player can move. Ludo Dash may have a speed dice mechanic, where the dice are automatically rolled, and players can either choose a token to move or the system will suggest an automatic move based on the game’s logic. Racing to Home: Players race to get all four of their tokens into their home area, just like in traditional Ludo. The first player to move all four tokens to the home area wins. Tokens must complete a full loop around the board before they can enter the home area. The game encourages strategic movement, with players needing to manage their tokens effectively to avoid being blocked or sent back to the start by opponents. Boosters and Power-ups: Ludo Dash often includes boosters or power-ups to make the game more dynamic: Speed Boost: Temporarily increases a player’s token speed, allowing them to cover more ground faster. Extra Dice Roll: Grants an additional dice roll, giving the player more chances to move. Teleport: Teleports a token to a random position on the board, potentially giving players a shortcut.

name: Lumpies of Lotis IV
description: Lumpies of Lotis IV is a first-person RPG game which was provided as BASIC code in Compute! magazine. Authored by John & Jeff Klein, this CGA game could be obtained for free by anyone with enough determination and patience to type in the code provided in the magazine. (This version has been compiled by someone into an .EXE fileLumpies of Lotis IV is a DOS-based video game released in 1994. It is a platformer/action game with an emphasis on exploration and puzzle-solving, developed by Free Spirit Interactive. Set on the distant planet of Lotis IV, players are tasked with navigating various challenging environments, dealing with enemies, and overcoming obstacles. Here's an overview of the game:

name: Lunatix
description: Lunatix: The Insantiy Cycle is a classic IF (Interactive Fiction) game that also includes some graphics of some scenes. What that means is that it's a text adventure game with pictures. It was created for an online IF competition. If you enjoy text adventure games you'll probably want to give this game a try, otherwise you probably won't like it. I don't often enjoy text adventures so I didn't make it very far in this game. There is also a BBS door game from the same author, also called Lunatix.Lunatix: The Devil's Dare is a DOS-based adventure game released in 1991 by MicroProse. It combines action, puzzle-solving, and adventure elements. The game features a surreal, quirky atmosphere and is set in a psychedelic world full of strange characters and bizarre situations.

name: Lure of the Temptress
description: The first game ever published by Revolution Games, it was recently made available for free download for the first time! In this graphical adventure game you play the role of Diermot, who starts the game in a prison cell. The game has decent graphics and sound effects, and is generally quite fun to play. The only complaint about it is that is is rather short, but it is still quite enjoyable to play.Lure of the Temptress is a graphic adventure game released in 1992 for DOS by Revolution Software. It was one of the first games to use the Virtual Theatre engine, which allowed for a more dynamic and interactive world compared to many other adventure games of the time. The game is set in a medieval fantasy world, combining puzzle-solving, exploration, and a strong narrative with unique gameplay mechanics.

name: Luxor Tri Peaks
description: 100 different Tri Peaks levels. Remove all cards, you can select cards that are one higher or one lower in value than the open card.Luxor Tri Peaks is an online card game that combines elements of traditional solitaire with a triangular pyramid layout. It is a part of the Luxor series, which is known for its puzzle-based card games. The objective in Luxor Tri Peaks is to clear all the cards from the pyramid by matching them to cards from the deck, following a set of rules. Objective: The goal is to clear all the cards from the pyramid by making valid moves. A valid move is one where the top card of the pyramid can be matched with a card in the deck or by using the free cards available from the deck. Triangular Pyramid Layout: The layout of the cards is a triangular pyramid, with the cards arranged in rows. The first row has 1 card, the second row has 2 cards, and so on until the bottom row, which has 7 cards. Some cards are placed face-down and must be revealed before being played. Card Matching: Cards can be removed from the pyramid if they are either one rank higher or lower than the card in the deck. For example, if the card in the deck is a 7, you can select a 6 or 8 from the pyramid to remove. The top-most card of the pyramid is available to play. If a card is covered by another card, it cannot be played until the covering card is removed. The Deck: The deck is placed next to the pyramid and contains a set of face-up cards that the player can use to match with the cards in the pyramid. If you are unable to make a valid move from the pyramid, you can flip over the next card in the deck. Power-ups and Boosters: Some versions of the game feature power-ups like wild cards or card removals, which can help clear particularly tricky situations. These power-ups can be obtained through special moves or achievements. Boosters can clear groups of cards or shuffle the pyramid to allow the player to have more opportunities to make valid matches. Scoring: Points are awarded based on the number of cards removed from the pyramid and how quickly they are cleared. The game may also have a scoring multiplier for streaks or combos, where several cards are cleared in quick succession. Completing a level or clearing all cards gives additional points, and the player’s performance may be measured in terms of stars or other metrics. Key Features Classic Solitaire Gameplay: Luxor Tri Peaks offers a variation of solitaire, making it familiar to players who enjoy other solitaire-style card games. It has a blend of strategy and luck, as players must think ahead about which cards to play and when. Triangular Card Layout: The triangular pyramid card layout offers a unique twist on the typical solitaire game. It provides an interesting visual style and forces players to strategize in new ways as they try to uncover and match cards. Power-ups and Special Cards: Power-ups make the game more dynamic and provide players with tools to help them complete difficult levels or situations. These special abilities can help in clearing cards or shuffling the pyramid when the player is stuck. Engaging Visuals and Sound: Luxor Tri Peaks often features bright, engaging visuals with thematic backgrounds and animations. The relaxing music and sound effects contribute to the overall atmosphere of the game, making it fun and immersive to play. Multiple Levels: The game has multiple levels with increasing difficulty. As you progress, the pyramid layouts become more complex, and new obstacles may be introduced, requiring more strategic thinking to complete.

name: Lynq
description: Lynq bears striking similarities to another of Anarchy Entertainment's games, Too Many Geckos! The object here, like that more intriguingly-named game, is to match up the colored shapes on the different pieces so they all match. The pieces (pyramids) are displayed in three dimensions, so you'll need to rotate them around, and carefully change your viewpoint, to be able to match them properly.Lynq is a DOS-based puzzle game released in 1991 by Ocean Software. It is a unique and challenging game that combines logic puzzles with a bit of strategy. Players need to connect different points or nodes in a series of puzzles, where the goal is to form a network or a continuous path that links up correctly.

name: Mack's Domino Parlor
description: Mack's Domino Parlor is a simple dominoes game which is played against a computer opponent. The registered version offers many features (outlined in the included documentation) but the shareware lacks most of them. Including, apparently, color? The docs mention different color modes and color scheme choices but the game displays in gray and black only, at least in DOSBox. This may be the first instance of a shareware game requiring registration to view the game in color?! In any case, it's a working dominoes game where each player takes turns putting dominoes down.

name: Mad Painter
description: Mad Painter is a Pac-Man type game that differentiates itself through its theme and the scrolling city in which you play. The goal is to paint lines on the streets, and the level ends when you cover all the streets. However there are of course "crazy cars" that will attempt to crash into you. There are no Pac-Man style power pellets, but you can press Spacebar to honk your horn and try to get the other cars to turn around! It's a near little game that seems to use text mode with an edited character set for the actual game portion, but uses graphics mode for the title screen, menu, and endgame screens! Unfortunately you only get one life, so a single mistake ends your game and you have to start over.

name: Madball
description: Madball is a simple but challenging game of reflexes. Your objective is to guide the white box from the left side of the screen to the exit on the right. Each level has a number of balls (equal to the level number) that are bouncing around the screen in predictable patterns that you must avoid. Presentation is basic, with monochrome textmode characters and minimal PC speaker sounds. It gets tough quickly, even at the easiest difficulty setting. According to the documentation the highest level / number of balls reached is 23 (!) but that seems impossible.

name: Madman
description: Dr. Dungeon seems to have been (or still is?) a prolific creator of classic-style RPG games. In his own words, his games are intended to "retain the classic flavor of games like Ultima 7, Fallout and Baldur's Gate." So if you like those games, you may like this. Madman is an isometric perspective RPG with decidedly retro graphics and PC beeper sound effects.Madman is a DOS-based action game released in 1991 by Creative Software. It is a platformer with action-adventure elements that places players in the role of a character who must navigate through different levels, defeating enemies and solving puzzles to progress. The game is known for its dark humor, quirky story, and challenging gameplay.

name: MadMaze
description: Mad Maze is quite similar to the similarly named Blind Maze, also released by Soleau Software. William Soleau was certainly prolific, even if several of his games seem rather the same. This sort of maze game probably culminated in the release of Maze Mission Adventure Game which seems superior to this one. In any case, you wander around a randomly generated maze, blowing up walls, hoping not to cause a cave-in or run out of oxygen before finding an artifact. Not too thrilling gameplay and basic text-mode display.

name: MadMix Game
description: Maxmix is a freeware Pac-Man like game which features a zoomed-in perspective. The game plays basically the same as Pac-Man: Collect dots, avoid ghosts, and turn the tables when you collect a power pellet. The game is presented in CGA mode and the zoomed-in view allows you to see more detail on Pac-Man and other characters but it does make it tougher to avoid the ghosts. The second level adds one-way arrows that move you in the direction the arrow points. Later levels may have other innovations, but you'll need to play farther to discover them yourself! Quickbasic source code is included, and it also includes an editor, which the author notes has a bug (mouse cursor may not be visible) but it's still usable anyways.

name: Madness Accelerant
description: If it runs slow, Q toggles the quality. This game is a shot-by-shot playable remake of Krinkel's Madness Consternation! We took a few liberties but overall tried to match the progression pretty closely. Enjoy!!!Madness Accelerant is an action-packed HTML5 game based on the Madness Combat series created by Krinkels. Originally a Flash game, it has been ported to HTML5 to ensure it remains playable in modern browsers, following the discontinuation of Flash support. This game is known for its over-the-top violence, intense combat, and chaotic gameplay, offering a non-stop action experience.In Madness Accelerant, players take on the role of Hank J. Wimbleton, the protagonist of the Madness Combat series, a ruthless and skilled warrior caught in an endless battle against enemies. The game doesn’t have a deep storyline but instead focuses on action and combat. The environment is chaotic, and the levels are filled with waves of enemies that Hank must defeat to survive. The world is a dark, gritty, and surreal place, filled with violence and absurd humor. Gameplay Mechanics Combat: Madness Accelerant is a fast-paced shooter and fighting game where Hank faces off against waves of enemies. The gameplay focuses heavily on intense combat where players engage in melee attacks, use guns, and perform execution moves. The combat mechanics are straightforward, with players having to shoot or fight enemies using various weapons, including guns, axes, knives, and other hand-to-hand combat tools. Weapon Variety: Throughout the game, Hank can grab weapons dropped by enemies or found scattered across the levels. Weapons include guns, bladed weapons, crowbars, and more, giving players various ways to fight off enemies. Players can also perform special execution moves where Hank finishes off enemies in cinematic, brutal animations. Levels and Environments: The game features a series of levels, each set in a different environment filled with enemies to defeat. These settings include dark, industrial areas, abandoned rooms, and other chaotic spaces that reflect the world of Madness Combat. Each level is designed to increase in difficulty, with more enemies, obstacles, and challenging platforming segments. Controls: The game uses keyboard and mouse controls. The keyboard is used for movement and actions like jumping, while the mouse controls aim and shooting. Players must be quick and responsive to move through the levels, avoid enemy attacks, and strategically use weapons and combat skills.

name: Madness Interactive
description: Madness Interactive is a Flash-based action game that was created by Krinkels, the same developer behind the Madness Combat animated series. The game was released as part of the Madness Combat franchise, and it was popular for its fast-paced combat, chaotic gameplay, and exaggerated violence, typical of the Madness series.Madness Interactive is a top-down shooter and fighting game where players control a character (usually Hank, the protagonist of the Madness series) and engage in fast-paced combat against waves of enemies. Here are the key elements of the gameplay: Combat System: The game features intense combat, with the player using both melee weapons (like knives, crowbars, and axes) and ranged weapons (guns, including pistols, rifles, and shotguns). Players must fight their way through enemies that are relentless and come in different forms. The game emphasizes fast reflexes and quick decision-making as you deal with large numbers of enemies. Weapons and Ammo: The game has a variety of weapons scattered throughout the levels. Some are dropped by enemies, while others are available in specific locations. Ammo for guns is limited, and players must manage their resources efficiently to avoid running out of weapons or ammunition in tough situations. Movement and Controls: The game uses keyboard controls for movement and attacking. Players can move their character around the environment, dodge incoming attacks, and engage in combat with enemies. Mouse control is typically used for aiming and shooting in the game, providing precision in attacking enemies. Levels and Enemies: Madness Interactive features various levels filled with enemy hordes. Each level introduces new enemies and more challenging combat scenarios. The enemies often appear in large numbers, and the game doesn’t shy away from difficult challenges, requiring quick reflexes to survive. Animation and Visual Style: Madness Interactive retains the minimalistic, cartoonish style that is a hallmark of the Madness Combat series. The animations are highly exaggerated, especially for the violence, with enemies often exploding into blood or falling apart in dramatic ways. The environment is gritty and industrial, fitting the chaotic and violent world of Madness Combat.

name: Madness Project Nexus (Classic)
description: Madness project nexus is a game based off of the flash series made by Krinkels on newgrounds. The animations featured unfinished characters with floating hands and feet who fought till the ends of time meet. The series gained traction and eventually got some games made leading to this game. The game features 2 playable modes, Arena and Story. Story: The story of the game features the main character of the animations and his friends working through a facility killing agents and many other creatures with an assortment of weapons. Arena: The arena mode is a rougelike where you battle through waves of enemys getting money and XP to level up your characters attributes allowing you to get things like more strength or allies to fight with you. The game is old but still holds up today and I hope you enjoy!

name: Madness: Project Nexus (Classic)
description: "Madness: Project Nexus" is an action-packed flash game set in the chaotic universe of the "Madness" series. Players navigate through intense battles filled with frenetic combat and a variety of weapons. The game features a compelling storyline, where players take on the role of a character fighting against hordes of enemies in a dystopian setting. Gameplay includes a mix of melee and ranged combat, allowing players to use different weapons and abilities to defeat foes. The controls are responsive, and the action is fast-paced, with smooth animations that enhance the experience. With its distinct art style, engaging gameplay, and a rich variety of levels and challenges, "Madness: Project Nexus" offers a thrilling experience for fans of action games and the "Madness" series. The game also features multiplayer modes, adding to its replayability and fun.

name: Madness: Retaliation
description: This game is an early build of madness project nexus! The game captures the essence of the Madness series, making it a favorite among players looking for intense, over-the-top action.

name: Magic Carpet
description: Magic Carpet is a unique 3D experience. You play a mage who rides a magic carpet, and your goal in each level (50 in the full game, two in this demo) is to collect enough mana to fill your castle. You collect it via golden balls, and you'll also need to watch out for enemies such as giant worms and rival mages flying on their own carpets.Magic Carpet is a classic DOS-based action-adventure game developed by Bullfrog Productions and released in 1994. It combines elements of first-person flight, real-time strategy, and spell-based combat in a fantasy setting. The game was groundbreaking at the time for its immersive graphics, open-world exploration, and dynamic combat mechanics.

name: Magic Castle Solitaire
description: Build a Magic castle in this colorfull tripeaks game. Remove all cards from the game by playing cards that are 1 higher or 1 lower in value then the open card at the bottom. Use the speciale bonuscards to help you.Magic Castle Solitaire is an online card game, typically a variation of the classic Klondike Solitaire but with a fantasy-themed twist. This version of Solitaire adds unique graphics, themes, and sometimes additional gameplay mechanics to provide a more engaging and visually appealing experience compared to the standard Solitaire games.Objective: Like traditional Solitaire, the goal of Magic Castle Solitaire is to move all the cards onto four foundation piles (one for each suit) in ascending order from Ace to King. Cards Layout: Cards are dealt into seven tableau columns, where you can move the cards between columns and on top of the foundation piles. The tableau is arranged in such a way that only the top card of each pile is visible. The remaining cards are placed in a deck, which you can draw from to help uncover new cards. description: Magic Hoops is a simple text-mode game based on an idea the author found in an old textbook. The object is to rotate the "hoops" A and B in the right column to match the pattern of the hoops in the left column. You can only rotate hoop A and B, that's it. The author's chosen colors and symbols doesn't help much; it would be better if they were more distinct from each other. It's a pretty simple game but if you have the patience to beat a level, you can play increasingly difficult versions. The game features 50 unique layouts, each filled with beautifully designed tiles. The goal is to clear the board by matching pairs of identical tiles that are "free" (not covered by other tiles and accessible from the sides). With its mystical atmosphere and challenging gameplay, it’s a captivating experience for Mahjong enthusiasts.
