name: Magic Maycabs
description: Magic Maycabs is based on a BBC Micro game called "Magic Mushrooms", except here you drive a car. Sure, why not? The object is to collect all of the mushrooms and avoid the enemies. And also not to fall too far, because your car can't handle a drop of hardly anything. One hit and you're dead, and need to restart the level! It's a good thing that you can choose a level on the menu screen because the levels seem quite difficult! The graphics are decent enough and the game plays well, even though it's a tough game!

name: Magic Maze
description: Magic Maze is a charming puzzle/action game where the object is to rescue the princess. You'll need to collect various items and avoid the monster(s) to do so, and also be aware of your goal to plan ahead and not get trapped. I initially thought the levels were being randomly generated but they seem static. However the levels actually change every five seconds, so some of the blocks will move to different positions. It's a neat game with simple but lovely graphics. It doesn't seem overly difficult, and includes both puzzle/planning and a little action. Make sure you review the in-game help menu to learn what all of the objects are.

name: Magic Mushroom
description: Magic Mushroom is a simple but frustratingly difficult game. The object is to hop your mushroom around the screen, collecting gems and avoiding things that try to kill you. It looks decent with 256 color sprites. However the main problem is that it's VERY difficult. You need to collect 5 gems to progress to the next level, but collecting even 2 before dying (in one hit, whenever you touch an enemy or fall off the bottom of the screen) will be tough. There are three different stage layouts / themes you can choose before starting a game.

name: Magic Olymp
description: Magic Olymp is a Boulderdash-style game in that there are pushable blocks that fall using rules similar to that type of game, however this is more of an action game with enemies to avoid. The goal seems to be to get as many points as possible; you get points by collecting nectarines and for finishing levels (getting to the door) quickly. Each level has a variety of obstacles including baddies that try to kill you (Google Translate calls them "red hunchbacks" based on the game's included German docs), pushable blocks, running water, etc. It also includes a level editor. Much of the actual game is in English but the docs are in German.

name: Magic Pockets
description: The Bitmap Brothers were well known for their distinctive artistic style, and it's on full display here in the platforming game Magic Pockets. This one level demo version of the game has you playing as a kid running through a cave throwing tornadoes at blobs and other monsters. The tornadoes are interesting weapons which take a bit of getting used to; I'm still not sure I've mastered how to throw them properly. The pace of the game seems quite slow and plodding, so despite the detailed graphics, it may be difficult to stay interested in this one.

name: Magic Tower
description: "Magic Tower" is a classic flash game where players take on the role of a hero venturing into a mysterious tower filled with monsters and treasures. The objective is to ascend the tower by defeating various enemies, collecting loot, and upgrading abilities. Each floor presents unique challenges, with stronger foes and hidden secrets. Players can choose from different character classes, each with special skills, and must strategize their approach to survive increasingly difficult encounters. With charming pixel art and engaging gameplay, "Magic Tower" offers a nostalgic experience for fans of retro RPGs.

name: Magics I
description: Magics I is actually a small collection of three action/puzzle games. The first two (Magics-Ball and Magics-Cobra) are snake variants. The first of the three games (Magics-Ball) is rather confusing, the goal seems to be to fit as many snakes a possible into the lower part of the screen without the snake running into an obstacle or itself; also matching three or more colored balls clears them from the playing field. Seems like an attempted combination of a "Snake" game with a "Columns" game? (Thanks goes to Mr Fibble for attempting to understand this one, partially via translation since the docs are in German.) Anyways, the second snake game is more straightforward, collect all of the things (robot moths?) without running into your own tail.

name: MagiDuck
description: MagiDuck is an interesting platforming game starring, yes, a magical duck. It uses a special tweaked CGA mode (40x25 text mode) so it's actually using text characters for its graphics. Despite the limitations and inherent blockiness, the game is colorful and has a unique, fun look. The story is not too important, but the gameplay is the focus and it's smooth as you jump and shoot your way through the levels. The game also features a detailed in-game help system which explains the controls and provides information about the various enemies and objects that you will encounter.

name: Magus
description: Magus is a roleplaying game created by Ronny Wester, better known for his Cyberdogs and C-Dogs action games. This, however, is a somewhat small-scale and comical turn-based RPG. You begin by creating your party, which includes the usual character types (such as barbarian and wizard) and not-so common types (duck and duck wizard). Then you proceed to move each member of your party in turn around the map, collecting treasure and fighting enemies. It can be somewhat tedious to move each character, and there's really no plot. However, the graphics have an endearing quality to them, and there is some random humor in the game that helps keep things interesting.

name: Mama Soybean's Delicious Oyster Sauce
description: Mama Soybean's Delicious Oyster Sauce is a Sokoban-like CGA puzzle game. (You couldn't figure that out from the title?) There are a total of 16 levels of block-pushing action to work your way through. Later levels add keys, doors, and other stuff. Controls are simple, and the gameplay is intuitive. The story is presented in a single paragraph before the game begins (not like you need any, really) and then you're right into the action. Or lack of action cuz it's a puzzler. Decent game that was released in 2018 but uses CGA mode for extra authenticity! (The executable file is only 60KB!)

name: Manhole
description: Manhole is a simple game that uses some unique controls and nicely drawn graphics, borrowing its concept from the 1981 Game-n-Watch game of the same name. The object is to keep the people walking safely over manholes, all of which lack manhole covers. You have a single cover, and can only cover a single manhole at any given time. So you'll have to be quick to swap the manhole around as more and more people keep walking. It's an arcade-style experience that feels a little like whack-a-mole but with more forethought needed. It uses a VGA mode and has decent sprites for the backgrounds and people. It also saves your high score. Instructions are included in-game!

name: Manic Miner
description: Manic Miner is a remake of the ZX Spectrum game Manic Miner originally by Bug-Byte Software. This remake features the same level design and gameplay as the original, but with upgraded graphics and music, while keeping the same general aesthetic. The game seems to be a very competent remake which plays similarly to the original, with upgrades. However if you don't fondly remember the ZX Spectrum game, you may not enjoy this too much, since the controls are a bit hard to get used to, and the game is quite difficult; you may never see all 20 rooms since you only get three lives and no continues!

name: Marble Guess
description: Marble Guess is a variation on the popular Mastermind-type game where you must guess a pre-determined pattern of colored marbles. When you guess, you're told how many you got correct but in the wrong space (red star) and how many you got correct in the right space (blue star). The main different between this version and competitors is that it's more difficult. A standard Mastermind game has you guessing a pattern of four marbles with six possible colors. This game makes you try to guess a pattern of six marbles with eight possible colors, making it MUCH tougher. Try this if you want a more difficult Mastermind game.

name: Marble Man
description: Marble Man is one of numerous single-player pushing type games made by Soleau Software, kings of churning out puzzle games in the early/mid 90's. The object is to push as many of your blue marbles as far up on your opponent's side as possible. You and your computer AI opponent take turns pushing balls, and when they game is over you'll tally up your points and see who wins. Not much else to say about it; it works well enough, although some of the later Soleau games work similarly but with a bit more personality and/or depth.

name: Marble Mayhem
description: Marble Mayhem is not nearly as crazy as its name might suggest. It's a Sokoban clone, and this is freely admitted by the author in the included documentation, where he notes that the levels are copied directly from Sokoban. At least the game itself is fairly well made, with easy to use controls and a no-frills interface which allows you to use the mouse for menus while keeping the keyboard arrow keys for moving aroundMarble Mayhem is a fast-paced, arcade-style puzzle game released for DOS by Soleau Software, known for its collection of simple but fun strategy and puzzle games in the early 1990s. In Marble Mayhem, players are tasked with navigating a marble through various obstacle-filled levels, solving puzzles, and avoiding traps in a colorful and engaging environment. Gameplay: Main Objective: The core objective of the game is to guide the marble from the starting point to the goal, overcoming obstacles and solving puzzles along the way. Navigating the Marble: Players control the marble's movement through each level by rolling it over platforms, ramps, and other structures. The marble can be affected by gravity and other environmental factors, which adds a layer of strategy and planning. Puzzle Elements: The game features a variety of puzzles and obstacles that need to be solved to progress through the levels. These include switches, timed platforms, and other environmental elements that require precision and careful planning. Levels: The game is divided into a series of increasingly difficult levels, each with its own set of challenges. As players progress, the obstacles become more complex, and the marble's path becomes more difficult to navigate. Time and Score: Players are often given a set amount of time to complete each level, adding an element of urgency. Completing levels quickly and efficiently results in a higher score, encouraging replayability. Features: Gravity and Physics: The game features realistic physics, where gravity plays a key role in the marble's movement. Players must carefully consider the environment and use the physics to their advantage to reach the goal. Obstacles and Challenges: Each level features various obstacles such as moving platforms, walls, and switches. The player must solve puzzles to manipulate the environment and clear the path. Increasing Difficulty: The levels increase in difficulty as the game progresses, introducing more complex puzzles, faster-moving obstacles, and more challenging terrain. Simple Controls: Marble Mayhem features intuitive controls, allowing players to move the marble with ease. The game primarily uses the keyboard, with arrow keys to control movement. Graphics and Design: The game utilizes colorful, simplistic 2D graphics, typical of many early 90s DOS titles. While not advanced by modern standards, the visuals are clear and functional, allowing players to focus on puzzle-solving. Replayability: The combination of puzzles, increasing complexity, and the pursuit of high scores provides significant replay value. Players can try different strategies to beat the clock or solve the puzzles in the most efficient way possible.

name: MARDEK Chapter 1: A Fallen Star
description: "MARDEK Chapter 1: A Fallen Star" is a captivating RPG flash game that introduces players to the whimsical world of Mardek, a young hero on a quest to save his homeland. The game features classic turn-based combat, allowing players to engage in strategic battles against a variety of enemies. Players explore a richly detailed world filled with quirky characters, engaging quests, and intricate puzzles. The narrative is enhanced by humor and charm, drawing players into Mardek's journey as he interacts with allies and uncovers the mysteries surrounding a fallen star. With its charming pixel art graphics, engaging storyline, and in-depth character development, "MARDEK Chapter 1" offers a delightful RPG experience that appeals to both casual and seasoned gamers. The game encourages exploration and creativity, making each playthrough unique and rewarding.

name: Mario & Luigi
description: Mario & Luigi is a clone of the popular Super Mario Bros game for the NES. The game has an interesting backstory, where the developer Mike Wiering made the game as a programming exercise, and a beta version somehow leaked out and even was taken and sold by another guy! (You can download this alternate version in the "extra files" area above.) The actual game, titled Mario & Luigi later released by Wiering (obviously with no official license from the "Big N") offers decent gameplay and six levels to complete.

name: Mario Cart
description: Mario kart but with a shopping cart that's all the info you'll needMario Kart Flash is an unofficial, browser-based racing game inspired by the famous Mario Kart series. Developed using Flash technology, the game offers a fun and fast-paced racing experience with iconic characters from the Mario universe. Players race through colorful tracks filled with obstacles, power-ups, and challenging AI opponents, with the goal of finishing in first place. Gameplay: Character Selection: Players can choose from a variety of beloved characters from the Mario universe, such as Mario, Luigi, Princess Peach, Yoshi, Bowser, and more. Each character has unique stats, including speed, handling, and acceleration, which affect their performance on the track. Race Tracks: The game features several Mario-inspired tracks, ranging from standard courses to those filled with exciting hazards. Players race through various environments, such as green hills, desert landscapes, and icy roads, similar to the iconic tracks in the Mario Kart series. Power-Ups and Items: As in the original Mario Kart games, players can collect power-ups scattered around the track. These may include items like Bananas, Shells, Mushrooms, and Stars, which can help players speed up, attack opponents, or defend themselves from attacks. Obstacles and Hazards: The tracks feature obstacles like jumps, tight turns, and enemy racers. Players must carefully navigate these challenges to avoid slowing down or crashing. Multiplayer Options: Some versions of Mario Kart Flash offer local multiplayer features, allowing friends to race against each other on the same computer. Others may include AI opponents that challenge the player as they try to finish first. Simple Controls: The controls are typically simple, with arrow keys or WASD to control movement, and additional keys to use power-ups or boost abilities. Features: Classic Mario Kart Feel: The game strives to capture the fun and excitement of the official Mario Kart games, offering a similar racing experience with power-ups, strategic racing, and colorful environments. Multiple Tracks and Characters: Mario Kart Flash typically features a wide range of characters and tracks, offering players variety and replayability. Fast-Paced Racing: The game offers quick and thrilling races, with tight turns, jumps, and obstacles that keep players on their toes. Simple Graphics: The Flash version often uses basic but vibrant graphics that capture the essence of the Mario Kart world without the need for advanced 3D rendering. The focus is on fun gameplay rather than highly detailed visuals. Engaging Soundtrack: The game features energetic music and sound effects that add to the excitement of the race. Fans of Mario Kart will recognize familiar tunes that accompany the gameplay.

name: Mario Combat
description: "Mario Combat" is an action-packed flash game that reimagines the classic Mario universe in a fighting format. Players control Mario as he battles through a series of levels filled with enemies, utilizing a mix of martial arts moves, jumps, and power-ups. The gameplay features smooth controls that allow players to execute punches, kicks, and special attacks while dodging and blocking enemy attacks. Each level is designed with various challenges and enemy types, requiring players to strategize and adapt their combat style. With its vibrant graphics, nostalgic sound effects, and engaging combat mechanics, "Mario Combat" offers a unique twist on the beloved franchise, allowing players to experience the thrill of fast-paced fighting in a familiar world. Whether facing off against classic foes or navigating tricky environments, players will enjoy a fun and action-oriented adventure.

name: Mario Teaches Typing
description: If you were a kid with a PC but no Super Nintendo Entertainment System back in 1992 (or even the original NES) it may have been exciting to hear that there were some official Mario games coming to PC! Unfortunately they were "edutainment" games created by Interplay, not by Nintendo themselves. Mario Teaches Typing is at least upfront about what it is. The game does LOOK like a Mario game with colorful graphics and well known characters like Mario, Luigi, Peach, and Toad making appearances. And it does attempt to teach you typing through a series of four typing mini games. This demo version seems to only include the first of these mini games, "Mario's Smash & Dash", whereas the full version also includes "Mario's Wet World Challenge", "Mario's Tunnel Of Doom", and "Mario's Expert Express", all of which are likely less fun than they sound. The program does seem to keep track of the player's statistics and allows for multiple profiles.

name: Marios Bombs Away
description: Mario's Bombs Away is a fun, action-packed Flash game inspired by the Mario universe. In this game, Mario takes on the role of a bomb-throwing hero, tasked with defeating enemies and navigating various challenging levels. The objective is to strategically throw bombs at enemy targets while avoiding obstacles and clearing levels within a set time. Gameplay: Bomb Throwing Mechanics: In Mario's Bombs Away, players control Mario as he throws bombs to defeat enemies. The bomb trajectory and timing are crucial, requiring careful aim and strategy to successfully hit enemies without wasting bombs or hitting obstacles. Levels and Obstacles: Each level presents Mario with a set of platforms, enemies, and obstacles. Players must aim and throw bombs at enemies while avoiding getting hit by projectiles or falling into traps. The bombs have a countdown timer before they explode, adding an element of tension and requiring precision timing. Enemy Types: Various enemies appear throughout the game, each with different behaviors and vulnerabilities. Players must figure out how best to use the bombs to defeat these enemies, whether by hitting them directly or using the environment to their advantage. Power-ups and Bonuses: As Mario progresses through levels, he can collect power-ups or bonus items that help him in his mission, such as extra bombs, faster bomb throwing, or shields to protect him from enemy attacks. Time Limit: Players often need to complete each level within a certain time limit. This adds an extra layer of pressure to the gameplay, as players must act quickly and efficiently to clear the level and move on to the next. Features: Classic Mario Characters: The game features Mario and his familiar enemies from the Mario franchise. The inclusion of iconic characters and a Mario-themed environment adds charm and nostalgia for fans of the series. Simple Controls: The game uses straightforward keyboard controls to aim and throw bombs, making it easy to pick up and play. The controls are intuitive, requiring a combination of aiming, timing, and strategy. Multiple Levels: Mario's Bombs Away offers multiple levels, each with unique layouts, enemies, and challenges. As players progress, the levels become more difficult, with additional obstacles and more complex enemy patterns. Cartoonish Graphics: The graphics are simple yet colorful, typical of Flash games, with cartoon-like character designs and environments that resemble Mario’s world. The vibrant colors and fun animations enhance the game's overall charm. Sound Effects and Music: The game features upbeat music and fun sound effects, adding to the energetic atmosphere. Players will hear the familiar sounds of Mario's world, such as jumping, bomb explosions, and enemy defeat sounds.

name: Marshmallow Duel
description: Two-player combat action! However, it isn't combat in the usual 3D shooter sense. Here, your task is to push your opponent off the game platforms into the water below, or otherwise kill them by using various bombs and other weapons. The graphics of the game aren't very good (neither is the sound) but it can be enjoyable when you've got someone to battle against. (The full version of this game has now been released as freeware, and is downloadable Marshmallow Duel is a humorous and engaging two-player combat game that was developed for the DOS platform. Released by Soleau Software, it features a lighthearted battle between two players, each controlling a character armed with marshmallow-based weapons. The goal of the game is to outsmart and outshoot your opponent by launching marshmallows and strategically dodging attacks. The game’s combination of quirky gameplay and simple mechanics makes it a fun experience for fans of competitive, action-oriented games. Gameplay: Objective: The main objective in Marshmallow Duel is for each player to try and hit the opponent with marshmallows to reduce their health while avoiding being hit. The first player to deplete their opponent’s health bar wins the round. Control and Combat: Players take turns shooting marshmallows at each other, adjusting the angle and power of the shot. The marshmallows can travel at different speeds and distances depending on how the player adjusts the aim and power. The goal is to predict and outwit the opponent’s movements and shots. Dodge and Defend: While attacking, players also need to dodge incoming marshmallow shots by moving their characters around the screen. Players can move left or right, but there are limited options for defense, so timing and positioning are critical. Power-ups: Throughout the game, power-ups can appear on the screen. These can grant advantages, such as increased marshmallow speed, the ability to shoot multiple marshmallows at once, or enhanced movement speed. Using power-ups effectively is a key strategy in gaining the upper hand during a duel. Single Player Mode: In Marshmallow Duel, players can also face off against the computer in a single-player mode. The AI is relatively simple, but it provides a fun challenge for beginners or those practicing their aim and strategy. Two-Player Mode: The most fun aspect of the game is its competitive two-player mode. Players can face off on the same computer, trying to out-maneuver and outshoot each other in a series of rounds. This adds a lot of excitement and replayability to the game. Features: Simple Controls: The game features simple keyboard controls. Players control their characters using arrow keys or a combination of keys, while aiming and shooting marshmallows is done by adjusting power and angle. Colorful Graphics: Marshmallow Duel uses colorful, cartoonish graphics typical of early DOS games. The characters, backgrounds, and marshmallow projectiles are rendered in a playful, exaggerated style, adding to the game’s whimsical atmosphere. Sound Effects and Music: The game features fun, upbeat sound effects that accompany the action, such as the sound of marshmallows being shot and the “splat” when an opponent is hit. Background music enhances the light-hearted, competitive tone of the game. Multiple Arenas: Players can battle it out across different arenas. The environments add variety and challenge, with each level introducing new obstacles or layout changes that can affect the marshmallow trajectory or movement. Replayability: Marshmallow Duel offers a high replay value due to its fast-paced nature and the competitive aspect of multiplayer duels. Players will want to try different strategies and master the mechanics to outplay their friends or AI opponents. here.)

name: Martian Memorandum
description: Martian Memorandum is the award-winning second game in the Tex Murphy series. (It won the Software Publishers Association (SPA) Adventure Game of the Year award.) This is a demo of the full game. I personally only played Under a Killing Moon (the third in the series) back when it was originally released, but I enjoyed it immensely. This game is another detective adventure for protagonist Tex Murphy, involving investigating the disappearance of a client's daughter. It's a point-and-click adventure game (assuming you have a mouse!) with great graphics, sounds, and storytelling. Unlike the original game in the series (Mean Streets) this game adheres pretty much to the typical graphical adventure game formula, so if you enjoy that type of game, give it a try!

name: Master Mind
description: Master Mind is a Mastermind clone with many configurable options. It also somehow gives off a slot-machine vibe due to its use of fruit instead of mere colors. You can choose the number of fruits to guess, as well as how many varieties of fruit to include as possibilities, and also whether duplicates are allowed. You can also choose what level you want to play: 1 is easiest (it shows you exactly which are correct in which position) and 3 is toughest. Overall it's a good Mastermind clone to play if you like fruit. If you hate fruit, probably find another one.

name: Master Qwans Mahjong
description: Classic Mahjong game now as html5 game. Combine two of the same free tiles to remove the tiles.Master Qwan's Mahjong follows the classic rules of Mahjong Solitaire, where the goal is to match pairs of identical tiles to clear them from the board. The game may incorporate additional features or themes based on the "Master Qwan" character, making it more interesting and immersive than standard Mahjong games. Tile Matching: In the game, tiles are arranged on a grid and players must identify matching pairs to remove them. The key to progressing through levels is finding matching pairs that are not blocked by other tiles (they must be free on at least one side). Themes and Layouts: Like many Mahjong games, Master Qwan's Mahjong may feature different tile sets or themes, such as Chinese characters, animals, or seasonal symbols, making the gameplay visually engaging. The layout and difficulty increase as players advance through levels. Hints and Shuffle: Most Mahjong games, including this one, offer a hint system for players who are stuck, along with a shuffle button to rearrange the tiles if there are no more available moves. Master Qwan's Influence: The game may incorporate a storyline or mentorship-style gameplay where "Master Qwan" offers guidance, providing hints or a backstory to make the game more immersive. Features: Relaxing Music and Sound: Like other Mahjong games, Master Qwan's Mahjong likely features calming background music, adding to the game's soothing experience as you play. Visuals: The game uses colorful and vibrant tile designs that make the game more enjoyable. The design might reflect traditional Chinese elements, including dragons, flowers, and other cultural symbols. Multiple Difficulty Levels: The game might offer different difficulty levels, allowing players to enjoy a casual experience or a more challenging puzzle with increasingly complex tile arrangements. Time Limits (Optional): Some versions of Master Qwan's Mahjong may feature timed challenges or high-score objectives, motivating players to clear the tiles as quickly as possible.

name: Match 'Em
description: Match 'Em is a tile matching game. Flip over two tiles; if they match, you get a point. If not, try to remember their location before they flip back over. You've probably seen and played it many times. This version gives you a few options, like the speed and number of pieces. You can play against the computer, or against a second human player, but there is no solitaire option. There also seem to be no other tile sets other than the default, and while the default tiles are passable, they're basic EGA clipart-style graphics so they're not exactly impressive to look at. Also some of the tiles look similar, which I suppose was a design choice but I found it annoying.

name: Match 3 Master
description: Match 3 Master is an addictive and visually dazzling match-3 puzzle game where the goal is to swap jewels to create rows of 3 or more identical gems. With 1,000 levels of increasing difficulty, this game offers endless hours of fun, challenges, and strategic gameplay. It’s perfect for fans of classic match-3 games who enjoy a mix of simplicity and depth. How to Play Match 3 Master: Objective: Swap adjacent jewels to create matches of 3 or more identical gems in a row or column. Clear the board by completing level-specific goals, such as reaching a target score, collecting special items, or breaking obstacles. Gameplay: The game board is filled with colorful jewels of different shapes and colors. Swap two adjacent jewels to create matches of 3 or more. When a match is made, the jewels disappear, and new ones fall from the top to fill the gaps. Special jewels and power-ups are created when you match 4 or more jewels in a row or column. Controls: Swap: Click or tap on two adjacent jewels to swap their positions. Match: Create rows or columns of 3 or more identical jewels to clear them from the board. Levels: The game features 1,000 levels, each with unique challenges and objectives. Early levels are simple, but later levels introduce obstacles like locked tiles, ice blocks, and bombs. Special Jewels and Power-Ups: Line Clearer: Match 4 jewels in a row or column to create a special jewel that clears an entire row or column. Bomb: Match 5 jewels in an L or T shape to create a bomb that explodes and clears surrounding jewels. Rainbow Jewel: Match 5 jewels in a row to create a rainbow jewel that can clear all jewels of one color. Key Features of Match 3 Master: 1,000 Levels: A massive variety of levels with increasing difficulty and unique challenges. Colorful Graphics: Bright, vibrant jewels and visually appealing designs. Special Jewels and Power-Ups: Exciting combos and boosts to help you clear the board. Strategic Gameplay: Requires planning and foresight to complete harder levels. Relaxing Yet Addictive: Perfect for quick play sessions or longer gaming marathons. Tips for Mastering Match 3 Master: Plan Ahead: Look for potential matches and combos before making a move. Focus on Objectives: Pay attention to the level goals (e.g., score, collecting items, breaking obstacles). Create Special Jewels: Aim to match 4 or more jewels to create powerful power-ups. Use Power-Ups Wisely: Save special jewels and power-ups for tricky situations or large obstacles. Stay Patient: Take your time to analyze the board and avoid rushing.

name: Match 3 Rabbits
description: Grab rabbits and drop them again to create 3 or more in a row (horizontally or vertically). Remove as many Rabbits as indicated.Match 3 Rabbits is an online puzzle game based on the popular "match-3" gameplay mechanic. In this game, players need to match groups of three or more rabbits of the same type, which are arranged in a grid, to score points and clear the board. The game often features colorful, whimsical visuals and fun, family-friendly mechanics.Match-3 Mechanic: The main objective in Match 3 Rabbits is to swap adjacent rabbits on a grid to create matches of three or more identical rabbits. When a match is made, the rabbits disappear, and new ones fall into place, creating new opportunities for additional matches. Levels and Objectives: The game may be divided into different levels, each with specific goals such as clearing a certain number of rabbits, reaching a target score, or completing the level within a certain number of moves or time limit. Special Rabbits or Items: Many match-3 games feature special items or characters that can be used to clear larger areas or create more significant combos. Match 3 Rabbits might include special rabbit types that can help clear rows or columns of rabbits, explode tiles, or trigger bonus effects. Power-ups: As players progress through levels, they might earn or unlock power-ups such as bombs or extra moves, which help clear difficult sections of the board. These can be used strategically to make the game easier or to achieve higher scores. Hints and Boosters: Some versions of the game may include a hint system or boosters that can be used when the player is stuck, offering a helpful suggestion or the ability to clear a portion of the grid.

name: Match 3D
description: Match two of the same 3D objects and remove all objects as fast as possible.Match 3D is an engaging and fun puzzle game that uses the popular "match-3" mechanics in a 3D environment. Unlike traditional 2D match-3 games, Match 3D allows players to match three or more identical objects in a three-dimensional space, offering a fresh twist on the classic puzzle format.Match-3 in 3D: In Match 3D, players need to match three or more identical objects that are scattered across a 3D grid. The game uses a rotating, 3D-style layout where players can look around the grid to spot possible matches from different angles. Objects to Match: The game features a variety of objects that players need to match. These objects can range from colorful shapes, fruits, toys, animals, or other thematic icons. Players need to group three or more identical items together to clear them from the grid. Rotating View: Since the game takes place in a 3D space, players are able to rotate the board by dragging their mouse or using touch gestures (if on a touchscreen device). This rotation helps players identify new matches from different perspectives, adding a layer of strategy and depth to the gameplay. Levels and Challenges: The game may offer multiple levels with varying challenges. As players advance, the puzzles become more difficult with more objects to match, more complex grid layouts, or obstacles that make matching harder. Power-ups and Bonuses: In Match 3D, players can earn power-ups or bonuses by creating large matches or completing special objectives. These power-ups can clear sections of the grid, shuffle items, or add other helpful effects. Time Limits and Moves: Some levels may come with time constraints or a limited number of moves, increasing the challenge. Players must think quickly and efficiently to complete the objectives within the given limits. Features: 3D Gameplay: The most notable feature of Match 3D is the 3D board, which adds a new level of excitement and strategy compared to traditional 2D match-3 games. The ability to rotate the board allows players to look for matches in ways that 2D games cannot offer. Colorful and Engaging Visuals: The game features vibrant and attractive visuals, often with bright, colorful objects that make the gameplay visually stimulating and fun. The 3D aspect enhances the experience, making it more immersive. Multiple Levels: Match 3D offers a variety of levels, each with increasing difficulty. The levels introduce new types of objects, layouts, and challenges, keeping the gameplay fresh and engaging. Relaxing Soundtrack: The game typically includes a relaxing soundtrack and sound effects that complement the puzzle-solving atmosphere, helping players focus and enjoy their time. Simple Controls: The controls in Match 3D are straightforward. Players click and drag to rotate the grid, and select objects to match. The interface is intuitive, making it easy for new players to get started quickly. Leaderboard and Achievements: Some versions of the game may include leaderboards or achievement systems, where players can compete to achieve the highest scores or complete special challenges.

name: Match all Zoobies
description: Chan all Zoobies into the same color. You start with one Zoobie (top left). Change your current Zoobies to another (pick a Zoobie on the right) and grow your group of the same Zoobies.Match All Zoobies is a fun and engaging puzzle game where players need to match different Zoobies—adorable animal-like creatures—on the game grid. The core mechanic is similar to traditional match-3 games, but with a focus on collecting and pairing up Zoobies.Match Zoobies: The objective of the game is to match identical Zoobies on the grid. Zoobies are often colorful creatures with unique appearances. When players successfully match a set of three or more Zoobies of the same type, those Zoobies disappear, and new ones fill their place. Matching Mechanic: To make a match, players swap adjacent Zoobies to align three or more of the same type either horizontally or vertically. The matched Zoobies are then cleared from the grid, and players score points for each match they make. Levels and Challenges: The game might be structured with different levels, each with its unique layout and goals. Some levels may have specific targets, like clearing a certain number of Zoobies or reaching a score threshold. Power-ups: Like many match-3 games, Match All Zoobies may feature special power-ups or bonus Zoobies. These can help clear large sections of the grid, such as bombs that eliminate nearby Zoobies or Zoobies that can clear entire rows or columns when matched. Time or Move Limits: Certain levels may have time limits, requiring players to match Zoobies quickly to reach the goal. Alternatively, players may be given a set number of moves to complete a level, increasing the strategic aspect of the game. Features: Colorful Visuals: The game features vibrant and visually appealing graphics with various types of Zoobies, each designed in a cute, cartoonish style. The colorful designs make the game both fun and eye-catching. Simple Controls: Match All Zoobies is easy to play, with simple drag-and-drop or click-to-swap mechanics. The intuitive controls make it accessible for players of all ages, from beginners to more experienced puzzle enthusiasts. Multiple Levels: As players progress, they encounter different levels with increasing difficulty. New obstacles, challenges, or additional Zoobies might be introduced, keeping the gameplay fresh and exciting. Achievements and High Scores: Many versions of the game include an achievement system or high score leaderboard, allowing players to compete for the highest score and replay levels to improve their performance. Casual Play: The game is designed to be casual and relaxing, making it a great choice for players looking to unwind or pass the time with a lighthearted puzzle game.

name: Math Assault I: Word Problems
description: Math Assault I: Word Problems is ostensibly a kid's edutainment game which aims to teach children math via word problems. The target age is grade 2-7 (so kids age 7 to 12). There are different modes, first a platforming mode with decent enough graphics but poor controls, and then a boring math word puzzle quiz mode. You are asked simple math problems in word form, using the game's theme of an ancient Greece-like setting. There is a long text-heavy introduction that must be endured before getting to the actual game, which I imagine most kids would be unlikely to wait through. The game does offer voice samples, but that setting doesn't seem to work in DOSBox.

name: Math Castle
description: Math Castle is simply a math drill game with some prettied-up graphics accompanying it, but it's done well. The object is to protect your medieval castle from invading aliens (?!) by typing in answers to math questions. The questions can be addition, subtraction, multiplication or division (or all four) at twelve different difficultly levels.Math Castle is an educational puzzle game that combines math challenges with engaging gameplay. It was designed to help players improve their math skills while also providing entertainment in the form of puzzle-solving and strategy. The game may involve various levels and tasks, with the objective of solving math-based puzzles in a fun and interactive way.In Math Castle, players likely take on the role of a character navigating through a castle or dungeon, solving math problems to progress through different rooms, floors, or stages. The game uses simple math challenges as the primary mechanic. Key Features of Gameplay: Math Challenges: The game revolves around solving math problems, which could involve addition, subtraction, multiplication, or division. Players are required to answer math questions correctly to unlock doors, gates, or other obstacles within the castle. Castle Exploration: The game might feature a castle-like environment where each level is represented by a new room, floor, or set of challenges. Solving math problems might grant access to new rooms or areas within the castle. Puzzle Solving: Beyond basic math problems, players could encounter logic puzzles or brainteasers that require a combination of math skills and critical thinking to progress. Progressive Difficulty: As players move through the levels, the math problems may increase in difficulty, requiring faster thinking and more advanced math skills. Timed or Turn-Based Gameplay: Some levels may have a time limit, requiring players to answer questions quickly. Alternatively, there may be a turn-based structure, where players can take their time to solve each problem. Objective: Solve Math Problems: The main goal is to answer math problems correctly. These could be simple arithmetic equations or more complex puzzles, depending on the level of difficulty. Advance Through the Castle: By solving math challenges, players can unlock new areas of the castle and progress through the game. name: Math Fun

These problems can vary in complexity, ranging from simple addition and subtraction to more challenging multiplication and division tasks. name: Math Rescue
description: This game is very similar to another Apogee game, Word Rescue, but with a math theme. Supposedly an educational game, this game doesn't seem to provide as much educational merit as some other titles, but it sure is fun for an "educational" game. It's from Apogee (publisher of many shareware classics like Commander Keen), so you know it'll have good control, graphics, etc. Its attempts to be educational can be annoying at times ... Basically you're trying to answer simple math questions while avoiding enemies.

name: Math Search

Drag to mark the answer.Math Search is an educational puzzle game where players need to search for numbers or math-related terms hidden within a grid of letters and numbers. name: Mather
description: Mather is a text-mode math game. If that description doesn't stir excitement within your soul, I don't know what will! Anyways, the aim of this game is ostensibly to help children improve their math skills. And what better way to do so than to bribe them via rampant consumerism? As you answer questions you earn money which can be used to buy in-game virtual prizes, like "A 386 33mhz computer", "The latest in VCRs", and "The Presidency". (All things any child would covet!) This is a strange game which likely won't hold the attention of a child for more than a couple of minutes but it does work decently enough and it's a much different game than any of Moraffware's other titles so it stands out for that fact alone!

name: Maths Paper Escape
description: Overview: Maths Paper Escape is an exciting flash game where players find themselves trapped in a classroom filled with math problems and puzzles. To escape, they must solve a variety of mathematical challenges while uncovering clues hidden throughout the environment. Key Features: Engaging Puzzles: Players solve arithmetic problems, geometry puzzles, and logic challenges to unlock doors and discover hidden objects that aid in their escape. Interactive Environment: Explore a detailed classroom setting with interactive objects, such as desks, lockers, and chalkboards, that provide hints and clues. Progressive Difficulty: The game features levels that gradually increase in difficulty, catering to a range of skill levels from beginners to advanced math enthusiasts. Hints and Tips: Players can access a hint system if they get stuck, providing nudges without revealing complete solutions. Timer Challenge: An optional timer adds an extra layer of challenge, encouraging players to think quickly and efficiently. Conclusion: Maths Paper Escape offers a fun and educational experience, blending math practice with escape room-style gameplay. It's perfect for students and puzzle lovers alike, providing an entertaining way to enhance math skills while enjoying an immersive adventure. If you have specific questions or want tips on solving puzzles in the game, let me know!

name: Matrix
description: Matrix is a great Tetris variant which in most respects plays the same as the original game, but adds several options and variations, as well as presenting the game in a visually appealing yet still simple way. The basic gameplay is the same: Make lines by fitting falling pieces into the well. There are multiple speeds and handicaps to set, as well as "Scenarios" (which start with the well partially filled). You can record your playing session to watch again later, and you can also save your game and load it to continue at a later time. The controls work fluidly and since it offers many options it's a solid choice to play a game of Tetris!

name: Matrix Rampage
description: "Matrix Rampage" is an action-packed flash game inspired by the iconic "Matrix" film series. Players control a character with exceptional martial arts skills and supernatural abilities, navigating through a stylized, urban environment reminiscent of the movie's aesthetic. The gameplay features intense combat mechanics, allowing players to perform acrobatic moves, slow down time, and unleash powerful attacks against waves of enemies. Players can use various weapons and take advantage of the environment to defeat foes in dynamic, cinematic battles. With its smooth animations, engaging combat, and nods to the film's iconic moments, "Matrix Rampage" offers an exhilarating experience for fans of action games and the Matrix universe, making players feel like they're part of a thrilling action sequence.

name: Mau Mau
description: Mau Mau: the German version of Crazy Eights. Be the first player to play away all your cards.Mau Mau is a popular card game that is often compared to games like Uno. It is a fast-paced and simple game, typically played with a standard deck of cards, where players aim to get rid of all their cards by matching them with the top card on the discard pile. It has different regional variations, but the basic gameplay remains the same.Objective: The main objective of Mau Mau is to be the first player to get rid of all their cards. Players take turns matching a card from their hand to the card on the discard pile, either by number or suit. Special cards can change the direction of play or force other players to draw cards. Card Matching: Players can play a card that either matches the number or the suit of the card on the top of the discard pile. For example, if the discard pile shows a 5 of hearts, the player can play another 5 or any card from the hearts suit. Special Cards: 8: When a player plays an 8, they can choose any suit to continue the play, making it a versatile card. Jack: The Jack typically has a special rule, such as forcing the next player to draw a card or skip their turn. 2: In some variations, playing a 2 forces the next player to draw two cards or skip their turn. Game Flow: Players take turns, and the game continues until one player gets rid of all their cards. The player who manages to discard all their cards first wins the round. Penalties: If a player forgets to say "Mau Mau" when they have only one card left in their hand, they may face a penalty, such as drawing additional cards. Winning a Round: The round ends when a player successfully discards their last card. Points are usually calculated based on the remaining cards in the other players' hands. Players then play multiple rounds until one player reaches a target score (often 50 or 100 points). Features: Multiplayer Gameplay: Mau Mau can be played in multiplayer mode, either against AI or real players online. It provides a social and interactive experience, especially when played with friends or other online players. Simple Controls: The game’s controls are easy to use. Players can drag and drop cards from their hand onto the discard pile, and special actions like choosing a new suit are clearly presented with on-screen buttons or options. Visual and Sound Effects: Mau Mau typically features vibrant graphics and animations that show cards being played or discarded. The sound effects, such as card shuffling or the declaration of "Mau Mau," add to the excitement and engagement of the game. AI Opponents: If playing solo, players can compete against AI-controlled opponents. The difficulty level of these AI opponents can vary, providing a challenge for both beginners and more experienced players. Leaderboards and Scoring: The game tracks players' scores and ranks, allowing players to compete for the best performance. Leaderboards may be available for multiplayer games, showing top players. Multiple Game Modes: Some versions of Mau Mau might include different game modes, such as a timed mode, or challenges with specific card rules or restrictions.

name: Max Dirt Bike
description: Max Dirt Bike is a classic Flash game developed by Max Games Studios, and it is one of the more popular dirt bike racing games from the Flash era. It stands out for its fun and challenging physics-based gameplay, where players control a dirt bike rider through various obstacle-filled courses. The game was widely played across many Flash game sites and is a favorite for fans of simple yet challenging physics-based racing games. Premise: In Max Dirt Bike, you control a dirt bike rider who must navigate through increasingly difficult terrain filled with obstacles, jumps, and traps. The goal is to reach the finish line of each level without crashing or getting stuck, while managing your speed and balance. The game is structured in a series of levels, each one featuring a unique course with a variety of hills, ramps, boulders, pits, and other obstacles. The challenge comes from maintaining balance and momentum while negotiating these obstacles, as the bike's physics can be tricky to master. Gameplay Mechanics: Controls: The game uses basic controls, typically the arrow keys (or WASD keys on some versions) to control the bike’s movement: Up Arrow: Accelerate (move forward) Down Arrow: Brake (move backward) Left/Right Arrow: Lean left or right (to control balance) Balance and Momentum: A key element of the game is maintaining the correct balance and momentum. If you go too fast, you may flip over and crash; if you go too slow, you might not make it over obstacles. The challenge is to find the right speed for each situation while keeping the bike steady. Obstacle Navigation: The levels are designed with various obstacles, including steep ramps, jumps, and gaps. Players need to time their jumps and adjust their leaning mid-air to land safely and avoid crashing. Crash Recovery: If you crash, you have to restart from the last checkpoint (or from the beginning of the level, depending on the version you're playing). A crash could happen if you flip the bike too far forward or backward, or if you land too harshly after a jump. Speed and Timing: Some levels require more careful timing and precision, as you may need to hit certain ramps at just the right angle or speed to clear a gap. Other times, you might need to slow down to carefully make it through tight or narrow spaces.

name: MaxMan
description: MaxMan is "slightly similar to PAC-MAN" says the included documentation, which is pretty accurate, since it's not really a clone of the popular maze game. It does have mazes and "gremlins" (ghosts) and "coins" (dots) and "energy apples" (power pellets) to collect, similar to Pac-Man. However the coins are not laid out in a consistent way, and each you collect gives you a bit of energy back. Collecting the energy apples allows you a brief period of turning the tables on the gremlins. When you die, your ghost lives on as a "grim reaper" which becomes another enemy that you must avoid. Some interesting variations on what has become a standard formula, presented with text-mode ASCII characters.

name: Maxtris
description: Maxtris is, at its core, a pretty basic Tetris clone, but it attempts to jazz up the experience through high-res SVGA raytraced graphics and SoundBlaster .MOD music. It plays the same as Tetris: Pieces drop, fit them into horizontal lines to clear them from the well. You do this while listening to some tunes (ex a remix of Korobeiniki, aka the Tetris theme song) and staring at the lovely shapes falling down. Other than the graphics and sounds, it's a perfectly decent clone of the original gameplay, but it doesn't add any extra features or options other than disabling the "Next piece" box.

name: Maya Bubbles

Try to remove all bubbles by matching 3 or more of the same.Maya Bubbles is a fun and colorful bubble-shooting puzzle game that is typically set in a vibrant, ancient Maya-inspired environment. The objective is to match three or more bubbles of the same color to make them pop and clear from the board. Match Three: The game follows the classic "match three" mechanic. The courses are designed with various obstacles such as trees, rocks, water hazards, and sand traps that make it more challenging to reach the hole. The fewer the shots, the better the score. Players may be awarded points for completing levels quickly or efficiently. Alternatively, players might need to achieve a specific score to advance to the next level. The game’s aesthetic typically includes lush jungles, grand temples, and mysterious ruins, adding an immersive and adventurous feel to the golfing experience. Players adjust the angle and power of their shots by clicking and dragging or using keyboard controls, making it accessible to players of all ages. The environment feels dynamic and engaging. Leaderboard and Achievements: Players can compete for high scores, and the game may feature leaderboards to track the best performances. Achievements or rewards may be earned for completing certain milestones or completing levels in a set number of strokes.

Try to putt the ball in as less shots as possible.Maya Golf 2 is a sequel to the original Maya Golf, featuring more challenging and exciting golf courses set in the same vibrant, ancient Maya-inspired world. With updated mechanics, more obstacles, and additional levels, Maya Golf 2 builds on the success of the first game, offering players a deeper golfing experience with enhanced visuals and more intricate courses.Objective: Similar to the original game, the goal of Maya Golf 2 is to complete each golf course by getting the ball into the hole using as few strokes as possible. Players must navigate through challenging terrains and unique obstacles, making strategic decisions about their shots. The game features a variety of unique holes that challenge players to think creatively and plan their shots carefully. The golf ball can be hit toward the hole while avoiding obstacles like rocks, trees, water hazards, and sand traps. Obstacles and Hazards: New obstacles and challenges appear in Maya Golf 2. These include: Moving Obstacles: Some levels introduce moving objects or platforms that block or redirect the path of the golf ball. name: Maya Pyramid Solitaire
description: Combine cards (or coins) to a total value of 11 to remove the cards (or coins) and built a Maya Pyramid.Maya Pyramid Solitaire is a captivating solitaire card game that combines the classic rules of the traditional pyramid solitaire with an engaging Maya theme. The objective is to clear the pyramid by pairing up cards that add up to a total value of 13, using strategy and skill to complete the game.Objective: The main goal of Maya Pyramid Solitaire is to clear the pyramid-shaped card layout by removing pairs of cards that add up to 13. The game ends when all cards are removed or when no more moves are possible. Card Values: King is worth 13 points. Queen is worth 12 points. Jack is worth 11 points. Ace is worth 1 point. All other cards (2-10) are worth their face value. Pyramid Layout: The game starts with a pyramid layout of cards. The pyramid consists of several rows of cards arranged in a triangular shape, with the top row having one card and each subsequent row adding one more card. Some cards will be face-up, while others will be face-down. The goal is to match pairs of face-up cards that add up to 13. Removing Cards: To remove a card, it must be uncovered (i.e., no cards are covering it), and the player must select two cards that add up to 13. For example: A King (13) and any other card can be removed, as the King itself is worth 13 points. A Queen (12) can be paired with an Ace (1) to make 13 points. A Jack (11) can be paired with a 2. A 10 can be paired with a 3, and so on. Using the Deck: If there are no possible pairs left in the pyramid, players can draw cards from the deck, which is typically displayed in a stack at the bottom or side of the screen. A new card is drawn and can be used to form pairs with the exposed cards in the pyramid. Game End: The game ends when the pyramid is cleared (all cards are removed), or when no more valid pairs can be made, and the deck is exhausted. Features: Maya Theme: The game is set against a backdrop inspired by ancient Maya culture. The cards may feature Maya artwork, including colorful designs, symbols, or characters that reflect the rich history and aesthetic of the Maya civilization. The background might include images of temples, jungles, and ruins, enhancing the immersive atmosphere of the game. Easy-to-Understand Rules: The gameplay is simple and accessible to all players. The core mechanics of matching pairs of cards that total 13 are easy to grasp, making the game suitable for both beginners and experienced players. Simple Controls: Players click on two cards to form a pair. If they add up to 13, the cards are removed. The game also allows drawing cards from the deck when necessary. Unlimited Undo: Many versions of Maya Pyramid Solitaire allow players to undo a move if they make a mistake, giving them a chance to correct their strategy and avoid errors. Time and Moves Tracking: Some versions of the game may track how long it takes to clear the pyramid and how many moves the player made. This can add an element of challenge for those aiming to complete the game in the shortest time or with the fewest moves. High Scores: Players can aim for high scores by completing the game quickly or efficiently. The game may offer a leaderboard where players can compete against others for the best scores.

name: Maya Zuma
description: Zuma match 3 game. Shoot bubbles in the chain and get three or more of the same connected bubbles.Maya Zuma is a thrilling and fast-paced marble shooter game that combines the classic gameplay mechanics of Zuma with a captivating Maya-inspired theme. In the game, players are tasked with shooting colored marbles into a chain of moving marbles, aiming to match and eliminate groups of three or more marbles of the same color to prevent the chain from reaching the end of the path.Objective: The primary goal in Maya Zuma is to prevent the marble chain from reaching the end of the path. To do so, players must shoot marbles into the chain and create matches of three or more marbles of the same color. When a match is made, the matched marbles are removed from the chain. The game ends if the marble chain reaches the destination. Controls: Players control a marble shooter located at the center of the screen. The marble shooter can be rotated to aim in different directions. By clicking or pressing a button, players fire marbles into the moving chain. The marble shot will travel along the path until it lands or hits another marble. Players can usually swap the current marble in the shooter by clicking on a button or pressing a key, allowing them to aim more strategically. Matching Marbles: When three or more marbles of the same color are aligned in the chain, they are removed from the game. As players progress, the marble chain may move faster, increasing the difficulty and urgency. Levels and Challenges: Maya Zuma typically has multiple levels, each with different layouts and challenges. As players advance, the marble chains move faster, and the course layout may include twists, turns, and other obstacles. Some levels may feature additional obstacles like stones or barriers that block the marbles, requiring players to find ways around them. Power-ups and Bonuses: Bomb Marbles: These special marbles, when shot into the chain, can destroy all marbles in a certain radius. Color Bombs: These marbles eliminate all marbles of the same color from the chain. Speed-up or Slow-down: Some power-ups can alter the speed of the marble chain, either speeding it up to increase the challenge or slowing it down for a more strategic advantage.

name: Mayan Marbles
description: Special Bubble shooter game: shoot at the rotating bubbles. Get a group of 3 or more connected bubbles to remove them. Click/tap on the shooter to change the color.Mayan Marbles is a captivating marble-puzzle game that blends the classic marble-shooter mechanics with an immersive Maya-themed backdrop. The objective of the game is to shoot marbles from a shooter to create groups of three or more of the same color, which then disappear from the chain, preventing it from reaching the end.Objective: The goal of Mayan Marbles is to prevent the marble chain from reaching the end of its path by shooting marbles at the chain and matching groups of three or more marbles of the same color. Once matched, the marbles will be removed from the chain. The game ends when the marbles reach the end or the player fails to clear the entire chain. Controls: Players control a marble shooter located at the center or bottom of the screen. The shooter can be rotated to aim at the marble chain. Players click or tap to shoot marbles into the moving chain, where the marble will travel along the path. The player can swap the current marble in the shooter to choose the most effective color for a match by clicking a button or tapping a key. Matching Marbles: To clear marbles from the chain, the player needs to match three or more marbles of the same color in a row. When a match is made, the marbles are removed from the chain, and the remaining marbles shift along the path.
