Players use this information to deduce the location of mines and avoid dangerous cells. Flagging Mines: Players can flag squares where they believe a mine is located. This helps avoid accidental clicks on those squares. Flagging is important for keeping track of potential hazards as players solve the puzzle. Difficulty Levels: The game typically offers multiple difficulty levels, ranging from easy (with fewer mines) to hard (with more mines and larger grids). As the difficulty increases, the grid size grows, and more mines are added, making it more challenging to find and avoid the mines. Winning and Losing: The player wins by successfully uncovering all the safe squares without triggering any mines. The game ends when the player uncovers a square containing a mine, causing an explosion and a loss.

name: Minelayer
description: Minelayer is a strange game that at first appears to be a prototype to Carr Software's more well-known Islands of Danger (aka Rescue) game. However, the game mentions Islands of Danger and provides media quotes about that game, so it must have been made/released afterwards. In any case, Minelayer seems to actually be an experiment with the Islands of Danger engine, where instead of shooting the enemy bases, you simply ram into them with your ship. To stop the enemy missiles you drop mines. The screen also switches into 40x25 text ode when playing the actual game for some reason which means you can see less of the map. Generally seems less fun than the Islands of Danger games which may explain why it's not even mentioned on the Carr Software website.

name: MinerVGA
description: MinerVGA is part strategy, part maze exploration, and part simulation. The object is to mine as many precious metals out of the ground as you can. You can then sell them to get as much money as possible. The graphics and sounds are mostly "just there" but there is a surprising amount of strategy involved in this quite old game. There is a certain laid-back charm here that makes it enjoyable and memorable despite its simplicity.MinerVGA is a DOS-based arcade-style game that was released in the early 1990s. It is a variation of the classic mining or digging genre, where players control a miner navigating through underground levels, avoiding dangers, collecting treasures, and completing objectives. The game features simple but engaging mechanics with VGA (Video Graphics Array) graphics, which were considered a significant improvement in visuals during that era.

name: MineSweeper
description: Determine where the mines are before your opponent does. Click 1x to show surrounding mines and click 2x on a spot to confirm a mine location.The Minesweeper HTML game is an online, browser-based version of the classic Minesweeper puzzle game, which has been a popular part of computing since the early days of Windows. It is designed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, making it easy to play directly in any modern web browser without the need for additional plugins or software. Players must clear a grid of hidden mines by clicking on cells to reveal either a number (indicating how many mines are adjacent) or a mine (which ends the game). The goal is to uncover all the cells without triggering a mine. Grid Setup: The game consists of a grid of cells, typically 10x10 in size. This can be customized to different grid sizes and difficulty levels, such as Beginner, Intermediate, and Expert. Some versions may include options for even larger grids or custom difficulty settings. Cell Interaction: Left-click on a cell to reveal what’s underneath. If the player uncovers a mine, the game ends with a loss. If the player uncovers a number, it shows how many mines are adjacent to that cell. A number indicates the count of mines in the surrounding eight cells (vertically, horizontally, and diagonally). Flagging Mines: Players can right-click (or use an equivalent action) to flag cells they suspect contain mines. This helps track potential dangers. Flags are an essential part of the strategy, allowing players to mark and remember dangerous spots. Winning Condition: The player wins by revealing all cells that do not contain mines. Once all safe cells are uncovered, the game ends with a win. Losing Condition: If the player reveals a mine, the game ends immediately and the player loses.

name: Minesweeper
description: Minesweeper HTML is a web-based version of the classic Minesweeper game, playable directly in a web browser. The game is a logic-based puzzle where the player needs to uncover a grid of cells, avoiding mines and using clues to reveal safe areas. The objective is to clear the grid without detonating any mines.Grid Layout: The game is played on a rectangular grid of cells, typically 8x8, 16x16, or 30x16 (depending on the difficulty level). Some versions allow players to choose custom grid sizes. Uncovering Cells: Players click on a cell to reveal what is underneath. If the player clicks on a mine, the game ends, and they lose. If the player clicks on an empty cell, a number is revealed, indicating how many mines are adjacent to that cell. The numbers are crucial for deducing the locations of hidden mines. Numbers and Logic: Each revealed cell may contain a number between 1 and 8, showing how many mines are adjacent to that cell (horizontally, vertically, or diagonally). The player uses these numbers to deduce the locations of mines. For example, a cell with the number "1" means there is exactly one mine in the adjacent cells. Flagging Mines: Players can right-click (or long-press on mobile devices) on a cell to flag it, marking it as potentially containing a mine. Flags help players keep track of where they suspect mines are located. However, excessive flagging or incorrect flags can lead to mistakes. Winning and Losing: Winning: To win, the player must uncover all the cells that do not contain mines. Losing: If the player uncovers a mine, the game ends immediately, and all the mines are revealed. Difficulty Levels: Beginner (8x8 grid, 10 mines): This is the easiest level. Intermediate (16x16 grid, 40 mines): A more challenging version. Expert (30x16 grid, 99 mines): The hardest difficulty, with a larger grid and more mines. Timer: Some versions of Minesweeper HTML include a timer, which tracks how long it takes the player to complete the game. A timer adds a competitive edge, where players aim to finish the grid in the least time possible. Resetting the Game: After winning or losing, the game can be reset for a new round. Typically, a "restart" button is available.

name: Minesweeper Classic
description: The classic Minesweeper game. Can you find all the mines?Minesweeper Classic is a web-based version of the iconic Minesweeper game, built using HTML5, CSS, and JavaScript. This version recreates the classic gameplay that has been a staple of casual gaming for decades. It allows players to clear a grid of cells, uncovering either numbers (which indicate how many mines are adjacent) or mines (which end the game). The challenge is to avoid the mines while using logic to uncover all the safe cells. Grid Setup: The game consists of a grid, typically 10x10, but can be customized for different difficulty levels. The number of mines on the board increases with difficulty. Cell Interaction: Left-click on a cell to reveal its contents. If it's a number, it indicates how many mines are in the adjacent cells. If the player uncovers a mine, the game ends immediately. If the player uncovers a blank space (a cell with no surrounding mines), all connected blank spaces are automatically revealed. Flagging Mines: Right-click (or long press on mobile devices) to flag cells where you suspect mines are located. Flags are important for keeping track of suspected mine locations and preventing accidental clicks. Winning the Game: The player wins when all non-mine cells are revealed. When all the safe cells are uncovered, the game automatically ends with a victory. Losing the Game: If a player reveals a mine, the game ends immediately and the player loses.

name: Minesweeper1996
description: A good looking version of the classic MineSweeper game. (Big surprise, eh?) Nice VGA graphics, however, you can't customize the game at all, and the sound effects are played through the PC Speaker. (They can be turned off.) Overall, a good alternative to the Windows version. Also, the author lives/lived in my old home town, Mississauga, in Ontario, Canada!Minesweeper 1996 is the classic DOS version of the popular puzzle game Minesweeper, which became a staple of casual gaming on Windows and DOS systems in the 1990s. It follows the same basic concept as the other versions of Minesweeper, but with a retro look and feel that was typical of the era. In Minesweeper 1996, players are tasked with uncovering a grid of squares while avoiding hidden mines. Each revealed square gives clues as to how many mines are adjacent to it, and players must use logic to deduce where the mines are located without triggering any of them.Grid Setup: The grid is usually square-shaped, typically consisting of 9x9, 16x16, or larger grids depending on the selected difficulty. The number of mines is proportionate to the grid size, with a higher number of mines in larger grids. Cell Interaction: Left-click on a cell to uncover it. If the cell is empty, it may trigger an automatic revealing of adjacent cells with no mines. Numbers indicate how many mines are in adjacent cells (horizontally, vertically, or diagonally). If you reveal a mine, the game ends and you lose. Flagging Mines: Right-click (or the equivalent DOS key combination) to place flags on cells you suspect contain mines. Flagging is a strategic feature, as it helps keep track of possible mine locations. Winning the Game: To win, you must reveal all cells that do not contain mines without triggering any mines. The game will automatically end with a victory once all non-mine cells are uncovered. Losing the Game: If you reveal a mine, the game ends, and you lose. The mine locations are then shown on the grid, and the game will display a "game over" message.

name: Mini Golf
description: Mini Golf is a fun and challenging game where players aim to complete a course of 18 holes using as few strokes (or strikes) as possible. The game combines precision, strategy, and a bit of luck, making it enjoyable for players of all ages. Each hole presents unique obstacles and layouts, requiring players to adapt their approach to succeed. How to Play Mini Golf: Objective: Complete all 18 holes by getting the ball into the hole with the fewest strokes possible. The player with the lowest total score at the end of the course wins. Setup: Each hole has a starting point (tee) and a hole (cup) with various obstacles in between (e.g., walls, tunnels, ramps, water hazards). Players take turns hitting the ball from the tee toward the hole. Gameplay: Use a putter to strike the ball, aiming to navigate it around obstacles and into the hole. Each stroke counts toward your score, so plan your shots carefully. If the ball goes out of bounds or into a hazard, you may incur penalty strokes. Continue playing until the ball is in the hole, then move on to the next hole. Scoring: Your score for each hole is the number of strokes it takes to get the ball into the hole. The total score is the sum of all 18 holes. The player with the lowest total score wins. Winning: Complete all 18 holes with the fewest strokes to achieve the best score. Key Features of Mini Golf: Variety of Holes: Each hole has a unique layout with different obstacles and challenges. Skill and Strategy: Requires careful planning and precision to navigate the ball effectively. Fun Obstacles: Includes ramps, loops, tunnels, and other creative elements to keep the game exciting. Multiplayer Fun: Play with friends or family to compete for the lowest score.

name: Mini Golf Mania
description: Mini Golf Mania is a text-mode miniature golf game. It includes a bunch of pre-made courses, and as you might expect controls for a text-mode golf game are a bit iffy. It was made in 1987 and uses monochrome so there's no color either. Nevertheless, the courses are reasonably designed and there were plans to allow creation of new courses via an editor (available from the author for $10) but there likely were no other courses created. (At least, we don't currently have any.) In any case an interesting historical artifact of how anything can be remade in text-mode if you try ...

name: Mini Prince
description: Mini Prince is a charming and creative "demake" of the iconic Prince of Persia (originally created by Jordan Mechner), reimagined in ASCII art and text-mode graphics. Developed by Anne Bras, a well-known collector of boxed PC games, this minimalist version captures the essence of the original game while adapting it to the constraints of a 13x5 character window. Here’s a closer look at what makes Mini Prince a delightful and nostalgic experience: Gameplay Overview: Mini Prince stays true to the core mechanics of the original Prince of Persia, offering a simplified yet recognizable version of the classic platformer: Objective: Navigate through a series of levels, avoiding traps, solving puzzles, and defeating enemies to rescue the princess. Controls: The controls are adapted for text-mode, with basic inputs for movement, jumping, and attacking. While the controls are functional, they may feel a bit clunky compared to the original game. Level Design: The levels are designed to approximate the layout and challenges of the original Prince of Persia, albeit in a much smaller and simpler format. Traps, enemies, and puzzles are all present, though they are scaled down to fit the text-mode environment. ASCII Graphics: The game uses ASCII characters to represent the prince, enemies, traps, and environments. While primitive, the visuals are surprisingly effective at conveying the game’s action and atmosphere. Graphics and Presentation: Graphics: The ASCII art is simple but charming, with characters and environments represented by text symbols. The 13x5 character window gives the game a unique and minimalist aesthetic. Sound: As a text-mode game, Mini Prince doesn’t include sound effects or music, but the focus is on the gameplay and nostalgia. Interface: The interface is straightforward, with clear indicators for your progress and objectives.

name: Mini-Putt
description: "Mini-Putt: Exciting Golf Simulator." This game was another mini-golf game within the Flash game genre, but with a bit more dynamic and engaging design than many of the simpler versions that just focused on putting. It stood out for its interactive elements, creative course designs, and overall fun factor. Premise: Like other mini-golf games, the goal in Mini-Putt: Exciting Golf Simulator was to get the ball into the hole in as few strokes as possible. However, the game offered a more exciting experience by featuring more interactive courses, moving obstacles, and more challenging layouts than typical mini-golf games. The game was designed to simulate the fun and challenge of mini-golf with a focus on exciting courses, each with its own theme, such as desert, cave, or jungle, often featuring ramps, jumps, and tricky curves. Gameplay Mechanics: Controls: Similar to other mini-golf games, you control the power and direction of the shot by using the mouse (or arrow keys, depending on the version). The mouse is typically used to drag and aim, while the power is controlled by how far you drag the mouse back and release. The ball moves based on the power and direction you set, and there are usually visual guides or indicators to help with precision. Realistic Ball Physics: The game simulated realistic ball physics to a certain extent, so you had to factor in the angle and the momentum of the ball, especially when navigating around obstacles like ramps, sand traps, and bumpers. Obstacles: Each hole had unique features that added to the challenge, such as: Ramps: Some holes required you to launch the ball up ramps to reach the hole. Moving Platforms: Certain obstacles would move back and forth or rotate, requiring good timing to navigate. Barriers and Walls: Some holes had barriers or walls that made the shot more challenging, and you might need to bounce the ball off them to get the perfect angle. Water Hazards or Sand Traps: Certain holes had areas where the ball could get stuck, requiring extra strokes to escape. Levels and Difficulty: The game consisted of multiple courses or levels, each with a progressively harder difficulty, and the holes became more complex, featuring more unique hazards and layouts.

name: Miniwar
description: Miniwar is a fun and competitive two-player battle game where you and a friend can duke it out using a variety of weapons on platform-style levels. While the gameplay is solid and enjoyable, the graphics are quite basic, and the Sound Blaster (SB) effects are nothing to write home about. The lack of single-player options or online multiplayer means you’ll need a second player to enjoy the game, but if you have a buddy to play with, Miniwar offers a simple and entertaining way to engage in some friendly competition. Key Features: Two-Player Battle: The game is designed for two players to compete against each other, using a variety of weapons to outmaneuver and defeat their opponent. Platform-Style Levels: The battle arenas are designed like platforming levels, with platforms, ladders, and obstacles that add strategic depth to the fights. Variety of Weapons: Players can pick up and use different weapons scattered throughout the levels, adding variety and excitement to the battles. Simple Controls: The controls are easy to learn, making the game accessible to players of all skill levels. This allows for quick and fun matches. Basic Graphics and Sound: The visuals are quite basic, even for the time, and the Sound Blaster (SB) effects are minimal. The focus is on gameplay rather than presentation. Local Multiplayer Only: The game requires a second player to play, as there is no option to battle against the computer or play online.

name: Mirkwood Forest
description: Mirkwood Forest is a Roguelike-like game. What I mean is that it is a text-mode, randomly generated RPG game, but it lacks many of the other familiar tropes of the genre. In this game you generate your character, then proceed through a truly randomly placed map (there are no recognizable rooms/structures) and attempt to escape Mirkwood Forest. The included MS Word documentation is basically required reading since there is no in-game help. It explains what all of the characters represent, and how to play the game. It seems interesting but has a high barrier of entry, and seems like it was never fully finished, although it's fully playable in its current state.

name: Mirror Maze
description: Mirror Maze is an interesting action / puzzle game that looks a little like Pac-Man crossed with Snake, but plays quite differently. The object is to collect all of the power pellets spread across the maze as your beam of light races through it. You can control your speed using the +/- keys but not your direction. Your direction changes when you hit a mirror. These mirrors placed around the maze and can be rotated using Spacebar. It's challenging to try to keep track of which pellets remain to be collected as well as how to navigate around the maze with all of the mirrors changing their orientation!

name: Mirror's Edge
description: Mirror's Edge Flash, which is a flash-based, browser game. Mirror's Edge is a popular parkour-based action game developed by DICE and published by Electronic Arts, but its Flash version was a simpler, browser-based adaptation of the main game. In Mirror's Edge Flash, players control the protagonist, Faith, as she runs and jumps across rooftops in a futuristic city. The gameplay focuses on speed, fluidity, and parkour mechanics, similar to the full version, but with a simpler interface and mechanics due to the constraints of Flash technology. This Flash version was a small, free-to-play experience that allowed players to get a feel for the Mirror's Edge concept without requiring a full gaming setup. It has since been discontinued, as Adobe Flash Player was phased out at the end of 2020.

name: Missile Attack
description: This is a pretty poor Missile Command clone by Soleau Software, which is much better known for its puzzle games. Although this game has decent production values and looks good at first, there are numerous problems, one being that the missiles fall far too fast to handle properly. They also fall all at once, rather than gradually, and your own missile explosions are tiny, making hitting multiple shot very difficult. The only real strategy seems to try to quickly judge which city the shots are aiming for, and them aim directly above it to try to stop all missiles headed there. There are much better Missile Command clones out there.

name: Missile Strike
description: Missile Strike is an exciting and fast-paced flash game where players take on the role of a defender tasked with protecting their space base from incoming enemy missiles and attacks. Using a missile defense system, players must strategically launch counter-missiles to intercept and destroy threats before they reach the base. Here's a detailed description of the game: Game Overview: In Missile Strike, players control a missile defense system to protect their space base from waves of enemy missiles, aircraft, and other threats. The game combines elements of strategy, precision, and quick reflexes as players aim and fire missiles to intercept incoming attacks. The goal is to survive as long as possible and achieve the highest score. How to Play: Setup: The game screen displays a space base at the bottom and an open sky above. Enemy missiles and aircraft appear at the top of the screen and move downward toward the base. Controls: Use the mouse to aim the missile launcher. Click to fire a counter-missile at incoming threats. Some versions of the game may include additional controls for special abilities or upgrades. Gameplay: Enemy missiles and aircraft move at varying speeds and trajectories. Players must aim and fire counter-missiles to intercept and destroy threats before they reach the base. Each successful interception earns points, while missed threats damage the base. The game becomes progressively harder as waves of enemies increase in number and speed. Power-Ups and Upgrades: Some versions of the game may include power-ups, such as: Rapid Fire: Temporarily increases the firing speed of the missile launcher. Cluster Missiles: Fires multiple missiles at once to take out several targets. Shield: Temporarily protects the base from damage. Game Over: The game ends when the base's health is depleted by enemy attacks. Players can compete for high scores based on the number of threats intercepted and waves survived.

name: Mission: Mainframe
description: Mission: Mainframe is an interesting strategy / RPG game with a sci-fi / cyberpunk aesthetic. Your goal is to rise through the office tower, find the mainframe, defeat its operator, and return to safety. The presentation uses text mode and is thus mostly text-based, although you do view a map of sorts of the current floor you're on. Move around and navigate various encounters, battling NPCs and finding / hacking information. It seems like quite a deep game and there is a lot of help included within the program. Apparently it's inspired by The Wizard's Castle from 1981.

name: Mixed World
description: Mixed World is a unique and versatile game that blends elements of action, adventure, and maze exploration into one engaging experience. Featuring nice graphics and sound effects, the game offers an interesting variety of puzzles and challenges that keep players on their toes. Additionally, it includes a level editor, allowing players to create and share their own custom levels. While it may not appeal to everyone, Mixed World is a well-crafted and innovative game that offers something for fans of multiple genres. Key Features: Hybrid Gameplay: Combines action, adventure, and maze exploration into a single experience. Variety of Puzzles: The game features a wide range of puzzles and challenges, ensuring that gameplay remains fresh and engaging. Level Editor: Create and customize your own levels, adding replayability and creativity to the game. Nice Graphics and Sound: The visuals and audio enhance the immersive experience, making the game more enjoyable. Exploration: Navigate through diverse environments, uncovering secrets and solving puzzles along the way. How to Play: Explore the World: Navigate through maze-like levels, discovering new areas and uncovering secrets. Solve Puzzles: Encounter a variety of puzzles that require logic, timing, and strategy to solve. Engage in Action: Face enemies and obstacles that require quick reflexes and combat skills. Use the Level Editor: Create your own levels, designing puzzles, mazes, and challenges to share with others. Progress Through the Game: Complete levels and overcome challenges to advance through the game's story or custom content.

name: Modern City Design
description: A modern city design flash game typically allows players to build and manage their own urban environments with various features. In such a game, players might: City Planning: Design the layout of the city, including residential, commercial, and industrial zones. Players can decide where to place roads, parks, and public spaces. Resource Management: Manage resources like water, electricity, and waste. Players must ensure their city runs efficiently while keeping citizens happy. Customization: Customize buildings and landscapes with different architectural styles, landscaping options, and public amenities. Challenges: Face various challenges, such as natural disasters, economic downturns, or population booms, requiring strategic planning to overcome. Upgrades and Expansion: Unlock new technologies and upgrades as the city grows, allowing for more complex structures and better services. Social Dynamics: Address the needs and happiness of citizens by providing services like schools, hospitals, and recreational areas. Visual Appeal: Enjoy a vibrant and colorful art style that makes the gameplay experience engaging and fun. Overall, a modern city design flash game offers a creative outlet for players to explore urban planning concepts while balancing fun and strategy!

name: Modern Problems
description: Modern Problems is a great game for fans of puzzle games who want to test their abilities in a variety of different puzzles. Okay granted, most of them are variations of only a few basic types, but still, at least they're not all the same. Your goal is to figure out how to pass each level. You can select which level you want to try (or at least each group of levels) so you don't need to pass them all to try the others. Usually the goal will be fairly obvious, or after failing once, you can get the general idea. Graphics are basic but get the job done, and control is fluid using the mouse. The game exhibits a lot of personality as well, which you may love or dislike depending on your own preferences!

name: Molefest
description: Molefest is a variant of Pipe Dream / Pipe Mania, where the object is to lay down pieces of a pathway so that your mole can find his way home. You'll need to think fast and be strategic as you place the pieces. This variant doesn't add much to the typical formula (other than the non-water theme) but it does look decent with its high resolution (640x480) and it plays well enough. There is some flickering of the graphics, and the sound doesn't work, so that somewhat hurts the playability of the game generally.

name: MoleZ
description: MoleZ is a two to four player fighting game, where your "molez" battle it out using a variety of over-the-top weapons. The predecessor to Liero and games that followed, MoleZ offers frantic fighting action as you burrow through the dirt to inflict damage on your opponents, and try not to blow yourself up in the process. There are no AI opponents so you'll need to have at least one human friend at the keyboard to fight against. You choose your weapons and go at it! The game looks pretty good in 640x400 resolution even though your moles are rather small. (Originally this game was "donationware" but this is the freeware release from 1999.)

name: Molécula
description: Overview: Molecula is an interactive flash game designed to teach players about molecular structures and chemistry concepts in a fun and engaging way. Players get to explore the world of atoms, molecules, and chemical reactions while solving various challenges. Key Features: Molecular Building: Players can create and manipulate different molecules by combining various atoms, learning about bonding and molecular geometry in the process. Interactive Challenges: The game features quizzes and puzzles that test players’ knowledge of chemical formulas, reactions, and properties of substances. Visual Learning: Colorful graphics and animations illustrate molecular structures, making complex chemistry concepts more accessible and easier to understand. Educational Content: In-depth explanations of chemical principles, such as the periodic table, chemical reactions, and stoichiometry, are integrated throughout the gameplay. Progress Tracking: Players can monitor their progress and scores, allowing them to revisit challenging topics and improve their understanding over time. Conclusion: Molecula offers a dynamic way to learn chemistry while having fun. With its blend of educational content and interactive gameplay, it’s perfect for students and anyone interested in exploring the fascinating world of molecules and chemistry. If you have any specific questions or want tips related to the game, feel free to ask!

name: Momentum Missile Mayhem: Ultimate Edition
description: Momentum Missile Mayhem: Ultimate Edition is an action-packed, physics-based Flash game developed by Demon Entertainment, known for its unique blend of strategic missile launching and intense, fast-paced gameplay. It was the Ultimate Edition of the original Momentum Missile Mayhem series, offering enhanced features, more levels, and refined mechanics. It quickly became a fan favorite among Flash game enthusiasts for its chaotic missile action and its emphasis on strategy and timing. Premise: The goal of Momentum Missile Mayhem: Ultimate Edition is to launch missiles to destroy enemy bases or targets while navigating a set of physics-based challenges. Players control a launch pad and are tasked with firing missiles at various enemies, which could include enemy bases, tanks, helicopters, or other structures. The twist in the game is that the missiles' momentum (their speed and trajectory) is critical to their success. Rather than just firing straight ahead, players must account for the angle and force of the launch to make sure the missile reaches its target. Gameplay Mechanics: Missile Launching: The core gameplay revolves around launching missiles by adjusting the angle and strength of the shot. Players aim at enemy targets using a trajectory arc that shows where the missile will land if launched at a given power and angle. You can adjust the strength by holding down or tapping the fire button and modify the angle by moving your mouse or cursor. Physics-based Mechanics: The game is built around a physics engine, which means that the missile will follow realistic trajectories. The missile can bounce off walls, change direction based on momentum, or even be affected by gravity, making the game feel dynamic and requiring careful thought for each shot. Some missiles have special properties (e.g., splitting into smaller missiles, bouncing, or having explosive effects). Special Weapons: Momentum Missile Mayhem includes a range of different missiles and special weapons that players can use to destroy their enemies more effectively. These include bombs, seeking missiles, and splitter missiles that divide upon impact for additional damage. Enemy Units and Bases: Your enemies vary by level and often have a mix of stationary targets (like bases) and moving targets (like tanks or helicopters). This adds a layer of difficulty since you must predict where moving targets will be at the time of impact. Level Design: Each level presents a different scenario with obstacles like walls, obstructions, and hazards that require the player to find creative solutions to launch their missiles successfully. As you progress, the levels get more challenging with tougher enemies, more complex environments, and additional obstacles. Power-ups: Throughout the game, players can find power-ups like extra missiles, special types of ammunition, or speed boosts that enhance the player's capabilities. Objective: The primary objective in each level is to destroy all of the enemies (bases, tanks, helicopters, etc.) within a certain number of missile shots or time limit. Bonus points and achievements can be earned by completing levels with fewer shots or destroying all targets in creative ways. There's often a limit to the number of missiles you can launch, which means precision is key. The game features multiple levels with varying degrees of difficulty, and success in one level unlocks the next. Higher levels often require more precise aiming, faster reaction times, and the strategic use of special missile types.

name: Monika's Tic Tac Toe
description: Monika's Tic Tac Toe is unsurprisingly a Tic Tac Toe game played against a CPU opponent. The author created it for his wife for their first anniversary together. The game plays exactly like you'd expect, and you use the mouse to place your X's against the computer opponent. The docs note that the computer doesn't always play perfectly so you should have a chance to win sometimes. There are no options to set or other modes or anything, it's just Tic Tac Toe, with a picture of the author's wife on the side.

name: Monkey Bubbles
description: Monkey Bubbles is a fun and colorful bubble-shooting puzzle game that combines strategy, precision, and a playful monkey protagonist. In this game, players control a cheerful monkey who shoots bubbles upward to create groups of three or more matching bubbles, causing them to pop and clear from the screen. The goal is to clear all the bubbles before they reach the bottom of the playfield, with each level presenting new challenges and increasing difficulty. Gameplay Overview: Bubble Shooting: Players control a monkey at the bottom of the screen who can aim and shoot bubbles upward. The bubbles come in a variety of vibrant colors and patterns. Matching Bubbles: The objective is to create groups of three or more bubbles of the same color. When a group is formed, the bubbles pop and are removed from the playfield. Clearing the Playfield: The ultimate goal is to clear all the bubbles from the screen before they reach the bottom. If the bubbles stack up and touch the bottom, the game ends. Strategic Aiming: Players must carefully aim their shots to create matches and strategically position bubbles to set up future combos. Bubbles that are not matched will stick to the playfield, so precision is key. Special Bubbles: Some levels may include special bubbles with unique abilities, such as rainbow bubbles that can match any color or bomb bubbles that clear surrounding bubbles when popped. Level Progression: Each level introduces new challenges, such as more bubbles, tighter spaces, or obstacles that make it harder to clear the playfield. As players advance, the difficulty increases, requiring faster thinking and better aim. Combo and Chain Reactions: Creating large matches or triggering chain reactions (where one pop causes others to fall and pop) awards bonus points and helps clear the playfield more efficiently. Cute Monkey Theme: The game features a playful monkey character who adds charm and personality to the gameplay. The vibrant visuals, cheerful sound effects, and lively animations make the experience enjoyable for players of all ages. Key Features: Bubble Matching: Create groups of three or more matching bubbles to pop them. Precision Aiming: Carefully aim and shoot bubbles to set up matches and combos. Special Bubbles: Use rainbow bubbles, bomb bubbles, and other power-ups to clear the playfield. Increasing Difficulty: Progress through levels with more bubbles, obstacles, and challenges. Chain Reactions: Trigger cascading pops for bonus points and faster clearing. Playful Theme: A cheerful monkey protagonist and colorful, vibrant visuals.

name: Monkey Connect
description: Monkey Connect is a delightful and engaging Mahjong Connect game with a fun monkey theme. Here's a detailed description of the game: Gameplay Mechanics: Objective: The primary goal is to connect pairs of identical fruit tiles by drawing a path between them. The game is won when all fruit tiles are successfully connected and removed from the board. Tile Matching: Fruit Tiles: The game features a variety of fruit tiles, such as bananas, apples, oranges, and more. Each tile type has unique designs, adding to the game's visual appeal. Connecting Tiles: To remove tiles, you must connect two identical fruit tiles by drawing a continuous path between them. The path can change direction up to two times. Path Rules: Path Direction: The connecting path can be horizontal, vertical, or diagonal but must not change direction more than two times. No Obstructions: The path cannot be blocked by other tiles or obstacles. It must be a clear, unobstructed line between the two tiles. Game Flow: Initial Setup: The game starts with a grid of fruit tiles arranged in a specific pattern. Some tiles may be blocked or require special conditions to be connected. Connecting Tiles: Click or drag to draw a path between two identical fruit tiles. When connected, the tiles are removed from the board, and new tiles may fall into place, potentially creating new connections. Clearing the Board: Continue connecting and removing tiles until the entire board is cleared. Level Progression: The game is divided into levels, each with increasing difficulty. As you progress, the tile arrangements become more complex, and the number of tiles increases, requiring more strategic thinking and planning. Hints and Assistance: Hints: If you get stuck, the game may offer hints to show possible connections or highlight tiles that can be connected. Undo: Some versions of the game might include an undo feature, allowing you to reverse your last move and try a different path.

name: Monkey Go Happy
description: Monkey Go Happy is a popular series of point-and-click puzzle games that gained a large following due to its simple but engaging mechanics, cute characters, and fun challenges. The original game was created by Robamimi and became one of the standout Flash games thanks to its mix of humor, creativity, and the satisfaction of solving puzzles. Objective: In each level of Monkey Go Happy, your goal is to cheer up the sad monkey by completing various tasks or solving puzzles. Typically, this involves finding objects, interacting with the environment, and solving mini-puzzles to progress. At the end of each level, the monkey becomes happy, and you can move on to the next puzzle or level. Point-and-Click Puzzle Mechanics: Point-and-click: The game is based on classic point-and-click mechanics, where players interact with the environment by clicking on objects, characters, or locations. Some objects are hidden, and players need to investigate thoroughly. Object Finding: The player may need to find and collect hidden objects to use them in other parts of the level. For example, a hidden key might unlock a chest or door, or a piece of fruit might be used to lure an animal to help the monkey. Mini-Puzzles: Many of the levels feature small puzzles, such as matching games, memory challenges, or simple riddles that must be solved before the monkey can be made happy. Interactions: Some puzzles require you to interact with other characters (like other animals or objects) to get clues or items necessary to progress. Levels and Progression: The game consists of sequential levels, each with a new puzzle or challenge. While each level generally follows the same pattern (find items, solve puzzles, make the monkey happy), the puzzles become more elaborate and imaginative as you progress through the game. The difficulty of the puzzles increases in each new level, keeping the gameplay engaging and encouraging players to think creatively to solve problems.

name: Monkey in Trouble
description: Monkey in Trouble is a fun and action-packed arcade game where you help a mischievous monkey collect all the fruit while avoiding dangerous enemies. Using simple controls, you’ll navigate through levels, dodge threats, and shoot bananas to defend yourself. With its charming visuals and addictive gameplay, Monkey in Trouble is perfect for players who enjoy quick reflexes and lighthearted challenges. How to Play: Move the Monkey: Use the arrow keys (on a computer) or swipe (on a touch device) to move the monkey around the screen. Collect Fruit: Gather all the fruit scattered across the level to progress. Avoid Enemies: Steer clear of enemies that roam the level. If they touch you, you’ll lose a life. Shoot Bananas: Press the space bar (on a computer) or tap the screen (on a touch device) to shoot bananas at enemies and temporarily stun them. Complete the Level: Collect all the fruit and reach the exit to advance to the next level. Features: Simple Controls: Easy-to-learn mechanics make the game accessible for players of all ages. Challenging Levels: Each level introduces new obstacles, enemies, and layouts to keep the gameplay fresh and exciting. Power-Ups: Look out for special power-ups that can help you clear levels faster or defeat enemies more easily. Colorful Graphics: The vibrant and cartoonish visuals add to the game’s playful and fun atmosphere. Addictive Gameplay: The combination of collecting fruit, avoiding enemies, and shooting bananas creates a satisfying and engaging experience.

name: Monkey in Trouble 2
description: Monkey in Trouble 2 is the exciting sequel to the original Monkey in Trouble game, featuring new levels, fresh challenges, and even more fun! In this action-packed arcade game, players help a mischievous monkey collect all the fruit while avoiding dangerous enemies. Using simple controls, you’ll navigate through levels, dodge threats, and shoot bananas to defend yourself. With its charming visuals, addictive gameplay, and new content, Monkey in Trouble 2 is perfect for fans of quick reflexes and lighthearted challenges. How to Play: Move the Monkey: Use the arrow keys (on a computer) or swipe (on a touch device) to move the monkey around the screen. Collect Fruit: Gather all the fruit scattered across the level to progress. Avoid Enemies: Steer clear of enemies that roam the level. If they touch you, you’ll lose a life. Shoot Bananas: Press the space bar (on a computer) or tap the screen (on a touch device) to shoot bananas at enemies and temporarily stun them. Complete the Level: Collect all the fruit and reach the exit to advance to the next level. New Features in Monkey in Trouble 2: New Levels: The sequel introduces a variety of new levels with unique layouts, obstacles, and challenges. Enhanced Graphics: Improved visuals and animations make the game even more vibrant and engaging. Additional Power-Ups: New power-ups and bonuses add extra excitement and help you clear levels faster. More Enemies and Obstacles: Encounter new types of enemies and obstacles that require quick thinking and precise movements.

name: Monkey Island
description: Monkey Island is a fun and lively bubble-shooting puzzle game where players help adorable monkeys collect bananas by popping bubbles. The goal is to shoot bubbles into a chain to create groups of three or more bubbles of the same color, causing them to pop and clear the board. Along the way, you’ll need to collect bananas scattered throughout the levels, adding an extra layer of challenge and excitement. With its colorful graphics, charming monkey characters, and addictive gameplay, Monkey Island is perfect for fans of bubble-shooting and match-3 games. How to Play: Shoot Bubbles: Aim and shoot bubbles from the bottom of the screen into the chain of bubbles above. Match 3 or More: Create groups of three or more bubbles of the same color to make them pop and clear them from the board. Collect Bananas: Strategically pop bubbles to collect bananas, which are often hidden behind or within the bubble chains. Clear the Board: Remove all bubbles and collect all bananas to complete the level. Plan Your Shots: Think carefully about where to shoot bubbles, as each move affects the chain and your ability to collect bananas. Features: Monkey Theme: The game features cute and playful monkey characters, adding a whimsical and fun atmosphere. Bubble-Shooting Mechanics: The classic bubble-shooting gameplay is easy to learn but offers plenty of strategic depth. Banana Collection: Collecting bananas adds an extra objective, making the levels more challenging and rewarding. Colorful Graphics: Vibrant and cheerful visuals make the game visually appealing and enjoyable to play. Multiple Levels: The game offers a variety of levels with increasing difficulty, ensuring hours of engaging gameplay.

name: Monkey King Air Fight
description: Overview: Monkey King Air Fight is an exciting action-packed flash game that follows the legendary Monkey King on a thrilling airborne adventure. Players take control of the Monkey King as he battles enemies and navigates through various challenges in the sky. Gameplay: Aerial Combat: Engage in fast-paced aerial battles against a variety of foes, utilizing the Monkey King’s unique abilities and weapons. Controls: Simple and intuitive controls allow players to maneuver, attack, and unleash special moves with ease, making it accessible for all skill levels. Levels: Navigate through beautifully designed levels filled with obstacles, enemies, and power-ups, all while trying to achieve the highest score. Graphics & Sound: Visual Style: Features vibrant, colorful graphics that capture the whimsical essence of the Monkey King’s story, complete with dynamic animations and detailed backgrounds. Soundtrack: An energetic soundtrack and engaging sound effects enhance the gaming experience, immersing players in the action. Key Features: Boss Battles: Face off against challenging bosses at the end of each level, each requiring different strategies to defeat. Power-ups: Collect power-ups to enhance abilities, restore health, and gain special powers during battles. Upgrades: Earn points to unlock upgrades and new skills, making the Monkey King even more formidable in combat. Monkey King Air Fight delivers a thrilling mix of action and adventure, making it a perfect choice for fans of fast-paced games and the legendary tale of the Monkey King. Get ready to soar through the skies and take down your enemies!

name: Monkey King Match
description: Monkey King Match Game is a delightful and engaging flash puzzle game that invites players to match colorful tiles featuring characters and symbols from the legendary tale of the Monkey King. This game combines strategy and quick thinking, perfect for puzzle enthusiasts of all ages. Gameplay: Matching Mechanics: Players must swap adjacent tiles to create matches of three or more identical tiles, clearing them from the board and earning points. Levels and Challenges: Progress through various levels, each with different layouts and objectives. Complete specific goals to advance and unlock new challenges. Power-ups: Utilize special power-ups that can clear rows, columns, or specific tiles, adding strategic depth to gameplay. Graphics & Sound: Visual Style: Features bright, colorful graphics with charming artwork that reflects the whimsical nature of the Monkey King story, making the game visually appealing. Soundtrack: An upbeat soundtrack and playful sound effects enhance the experience, keeping players engaged as they solve puzzles. Key Features: Diverse Levels: A variety of levels with increasing difficulty, ensuring that players stay challenged and entertained. Bonus Rewards: Earn bonuses for making quick matches or achieving high scores, encouraging skillful play. User-Friendly Interface: Intuitive controls and a straightforward layout make it easy for players to dive right in. Monkey King Match Game offers a fun and addictive puzzle experience, making it perfect for fans of matching games and the enchanting world of the Monkey King. Challenge yourself to clear the board and score high!

name: Monkey King: The Untold Journeys
description: Overview: Monkey King: The Untold Journeys is an action-packed flash game that draws inspiration from the legendary tale of the Monkey King, a beloved figure in Chinese folklore. Players embark on an adventurous journey filled with combat, puzzles, and monster-slaying action as they help the Monkey King restore peace. Gameplay: Controls: Simple and intuitive controls allow players to move, jump, and attack. Special moves and combos can be executed for added flair and damage. Levels: Navigate through various beautifully designed environments, including lush forests, mystical mountains, and ancient temples, each populated by different types of monsters and challenges. Enemies: Face a variety of monsters, each with unique abilities and attack patterns, requiring players to adapt their strategies. Graphics & Sound: Visual Style: Features vibrant, colorful graphics with a cartoonish art style that brings the characters and environments to life. Soundtrack: A lively soundtrack and engaging sound effects enhance the gameplay experience, immersing players in the adventure. Key Features: Character Upgrades: Collect power-ups and experience points to upgrade the Monkey King’s abilities, enhancing combat and survivability. Boss Fights: Encounter challenging bosses at the end of levels, each requiring unique tactics to defeat. Story Mode: Unfolds a captivating storyline inspired by traditional tales, adding depth to the gameplay. Monkey King: The Untold Journeys offers a delightful blend of action and adventure, making it an entertaining experience for fans of platformers and classic tales alike. Get ready to unleash the Monkey King's legendary powers and subdue the monsters that threaten the land!

name: Monochrome Mahjongg
description: Monochrome Mahjongg is a unique and visually striking twist on the classic Mahjong Solitaire game. Instead of matching identical tiles, players must pair black tiles with their corresponding white counterparts to clear them from the board. This monochromatic theme adds a fresh and challenging dynamic to the traditional gameplay, making it a captivating experience for puzzle enthusiasts. The goal is to clear all the tiles to advance to the next level, testing your observation and strategic skills. How to Play: Match Tiles: Find and select a black tile and its corresponding white tile to remove them from the board. For example, pair a black flower tile with a white flower tile. Clear the Board: Strategically remove all the tiles to complete the level and progress to the next stage. Plan Ahead: Think carefully about your moves, as some tiles may become blocked if you don’t clear them in the right order. Free Tiles: Only tiles that are not blocked by other tiles on the left or right side can be selected. Features: Monochrome Theme: The black-and-white tile design creates a sleek and minimalist aesthetic, offering a fresh take on traditional Mahjong. Unique Matching Mechanic: Pairing black and white tiles instead of identical ones adds a new layer of challenge and strategy. Multiple Levels: The game offers a variety of levels with increasing difficulty, keeping the gameplay fresh and engaging. Relaxing Yet Challenging: The game is easy to pick up but offers enough depth to keep players engaged and entertained.

name: Monopoly
description: Monopoly (text-based version) is a faithful adaptation of the classic board game, bringing the timeless gameplay of buying, trading, and building to the DOS era. While it may lack the visual polish and flexibility of the physical board game, it captures the essence of Monopoly and provides a fun and nostalgic way to play on older systems. Here’s a closer look at what this version offers: Gameplay Overview: This text-based version of Monopoly replicates the core mechanics of the original board game, allowing players to compete against each other or AI opponents: Objective: The goal is to bankrupt your opponents by buying properties, charging rent, and strategically managing your money. Text-Mode Interface: The game uses text-based graphics to represent the Monopoly board, properties, and player actions. While the visuals are minimal, the interface is functional and easy to navigate. Game Mechanics: Roll virtual dice to move around the board. Buy properties, pay rent, and build houses and hotels. Draw Chance and Community Chest cards, which can bring good fortune or unexpected expenses. Trade properties with other players to complete sets and increase your earning potential. Multiplayer: The game supports multiple human and computer-controlled players, allowing for competitive gameplay. The AI opponents provide a decent challenge, though their strategies may feel predictable over time. Rigid Rules: Unlike the physical board game, this digital version enforces the rules strictly, with no room for house rules or loans from the bank. Graphics and Presentation: Graphics: The game uses ASCII characters to represent the Monopoly board and properties. While primitive, the visuals are clear and functional. Sound: There is no sound, keeping the focus on the gameplay and text-based interface. Interface: The interface is straightforward, with menus and prompts guiding you through each turn and action.

name: Monopoly (Hoops)
description: Monopoly (Hoops) is a text-mode adaptation of the classic board game Monopoly, bringing the timeless (and sometimes contentious) gameplay to the DOS era. While it may not have the visual polish or advanced features of modern digital versions of Monopoly, its simplicity and nostalgic charm make it a fun and accessible way to enjoy the game on older systems. Here’s a closer look at what this version offers: Gameplay Overview: Monopoly (Hoops) faithfully replicates the core mechanics of the original board game, allowing players to buy, trade, and build their way to real estate dominance: Objective: The goal is to bankrupt your opponents by buying properties, charging rent, and strategically managing your money. Text-Mode Interface: The game uses text-based graphics to represent the Monopoly board, properties, and player actions. While the visuals are minimal, the interface is functional and easy to navigate. Game Mechanics: Roll virtual dice to move around the board. Buy properties, pay rent, and build houses and hotels. Draw Chance and Community Chest cards, which can bring good fortune or unexpected expenses. Trade properties with other players to complete sets and increase your earning potential. Multiplayer: The game supports multiplayer, allowing you to compete against friends or AI opponents. The AI opponents provide a decent challenge, though their strategies may feel predictable over time. Graphics and Presentation: Graphics: The game uses ASCII characters to represent the Monopoly board and properties. While primitive, the visuals are clear and functional. Sound: There is no sound, keeping the focus on the gameplay and text-based interface. Interface: The interface is straightforward, with menus and prompts guiding you through each turn and action.

name: Monopoly1985
description: Monopoly (1985) is a digital adaptation of the classic board game, bringing the timeless property-trading experience to early PCs. While it primarily operates in text mode, it switches to CGA graphics for dice rolls and board visualization, offering a nostalgic and functional take on the beloved game. Here’s a detailed look at what makes this version of Monopoly a noteworthy retro gaming experience: Key Features: Faithful Adaptation: The game stays true to the rules and mechanics of the original Monopoly board game, allowing players to buy properties, build houses and hotels, collect rent, and engage in trades. Text-Based Interface: Most of the gameplay is handled through a text-based interface, where players input commands to perform actions like rolling dice, buying properties, or managing their assets. CGA Graphics for Dice Rolls: When rolling the dice, the game switches to CGA (Color Graphics Adapter) mode, displaying a graphical representation of the board and an animated dice roll. This adds a visual element to the otherwise text-heavy experience. Smooth Gameplay: The game progresses efficiently, with players able to perform actions like viewing the board, buying houses, selling properties, and trading with opponents after rolling the dice. Multiplayer Support: The game supports multiple players, either human or AI-controlled, allowing for a full Monopoly experience on the computer. Nostalgic Appeal: For fans of retro gaming, this version of Monopoly is a nostalgic trip back to the mid-80s, when text-based interfaces and simple graphics were the norm. Wide Distribution: The author notes that this version of Monopoly was widely distributed in the mid-80s, making it a familiar title for many early PC users. Gameplay: Objective: Become the wealthiest player by buying, trading, and developing properties while bankrupting your opponents. Controls: Use text commands to perform actions like rolling dice, buying properties, building houses, and trading. Switch to CGA graphics mode during dice rolls to see the board and watch the dice animation. Turn-Based Play: Players take turns rolling the dice, moving around the board, and making decisions about buying, selling, or trading properties. AI Opponents: Play against computer-controlled opponents with varying levels of strategy.

name: Monster Bash
description: This is another of Apogee's EGA sidescrollers. This one is lesser known because it was a bit outdated when it was released ... VGA graphics were quickly becoming the norm by that time. However, while it IS a bit more linear than their previous games, it's still worth a look if you enjoyed Apogee's other EGA platformers. In this game you play a kid ("Johnny Dash") who is trying to rescue captured animals, and to do it, he must use his trusty slingshot to kill various undead and ... uh, alive enemies.

name: Monster Brawl
description: Monster Brawl is an action-packed flash game where players control monsters in a battle arena, fighting against other monsters or players to emerge victorious. The game typically features a variety of monsters with unique abilities, customizable stats, and fast-paced combat mechanics. Here's a detailed description of the game: Game Overview: In Monster Brawl, players take on the role of a monster and engage in intense battles against AI-controlled opponents or other players. The goal is to defeat all enemies using a combination of attacks, special abilities, and strategic gameplay. The game often includes RPG elements, allowing players to level up their monsters and unlock new skills. How to Play: Setup: Choose your monster from a selection of unique creatures, each with its own strengths, weaknesses, and abilities. Enter the battle arena, where you’ll face off against one or more opponents. Controls: Use the keyboard or mouse to move your monster and perform attacks. Basic controls typically include: Arrow keys or WASD for movement. Spacebar or mouse clicks for basic attacks. Number keys or special buttons for unique abilities. Gameplay: Engage in real-time combat, using a mix of melee attacks, ranged attacks, and special abilities to defeat your opponents. Manage your monster’s health and energy (if applicable) to survive the battle. Some versions of the game may include environmental hazards or power-ups in the arena. Abilities and Upgrades: Each monster has unique abilities, such as fire breath, lightning strikes, or healing powers. As you progress, you can unlock new abilities or upgrade existing ones to make your monster stronger. Winning the Battle: Defeat all opponents in the arena to win the match. Some versions of the game may include a campaign mode with multiple levels or a multiplayer mode for battling friends.

name: Monsters Ate My Neighbors
description: Monsters Ate My Neighbors is an exciting tower defense flash game where players must strategically place defenses and fight off waves of monstrous invaders to save their neighborhood. With a mix of quirky humor, creative towers, and challenging enemy waves, the game offers hours of engaging gameplay. Gameplay: Objective: Defend your neighborhood by building and upgrading defensive towers to stop waves of monsters from reaching and devouring your neighbors. Protect as many houses as possible while strategically managing resources. Mechanics: Use in-game currency (earned by defeating monsters) to build towers, set traps, and upgrade your defenses. Each level has unique paths and terrain, requiring players to carefully plan tower placement. Features: Variety of Towers: Basic Defenders: Simple towers like water guns or BB launchers for standard enemies. Advanced Towers: Flamethrowers, laser turrets, and electrified fences for high-damage attacks. Support Towers: Slowing towers like sticky goo or scarecrow towers that frighten monsters away temporarily. Monster Variety: Zombies: Slow-moving but tough creatures. Ghosts: Fast and can bypass certain towers unless countered by specific defenses. Giant Mutants: Huge monsters with massive health pools that require coordinated defenses to take down. Upgradeable Defenses: Upgrade towers to increase their damage, range, or special effects. Unlock new defensive options as you progress through the game. Multiple Levels: Each level introduces new paths, terrain challenges, and increasingly difficult waves of monsters. Bonus objectives, like saving specific houses or neighbors, add extra difficulty and rewards. Resource Management: Earn resources by defeating monsters or rescuing neighbors. Balance spending between building new towers and upgrading existing ones.

name: Montana Solitaire
description: Montana Solitaire is a unique and challenging card game that requires strategic thinking and careful planning. Here's a detailed description of the game: Gameplay Mechanics: Objective: The primary goal is to arrange all cards from 2 to King in each suit by moving cards to empty spots based on specific rules. The game is won when all cards are successfully arranged in the correct order. Card Movement: Empty Spots: You can move a card to an empty spot only if the card on the left is of the same suit and is one rank lower in value. For example, you can move a 5 of Hearts to an empty spot if the card to the left of the empty spot is a 4 of Hearts. Sequential Order: The cards must be arranged in ascending order from 2 to King within each suit. Game Flow: Initial Setup: The game starts with a tableau of cards arranged in a specific layout. Some spots may be empty, providing opportunities for moving cards. Moving Cards: Click on a card to select it, then click on an empty spot to move it, provided the move follows the rules. The goal is to create sequences of cards in ascending order within each suit. Completing Sequences: Continue moving cards to empty spots and arranging them in the correct order until all cards from 2 to King are in place for each suit. Level Progression: The game is divided into levels, each with increasing difficulty. As you progress, the initial card arrangements become more complex, requiring more strategic thinking and planning. Hints and Assistance: Hints: If you get stuck, the game may offer hints to show possible moves or highlight cards that can be moved to empty spots. Undo: Some versions of the game might include an undo feature, allowing you to reverse your last move and try a different strategy.

name: Monuments of Mars
description: Monuments of Mars is a classic action-puzzle platformer and one of the spiritual successors to the popular Pharaoh’s Tomb. Developed independently by Todd Replogle, the game shares a similar style and gameplay but stands on its own as a unique experience. The game features a side-scrolling format where each level is confined to a single screen, and the objective is simply to navigate to the exit to progress to the next screen. With its straightforward mechanics and challenging puzzles, Monuments of Mars is a fun and engaging title for fans of retro gaming. Key Features: Single-Screen Levels: Each level takes place on a single screen, requiring players to solve puzzles and overcome obstacles to reach the exit. This design makes the game easy to pick up and play in short sessions. Action-Puzzle Gameplay: The game combines platforming with puzzle-solving. Players must navigate hazards, avoid enemies, and figure out how to reach the exit using the tools and mechanics available on each screen. Side-Scrolling Format: While each level is confined to a single screen, the side-scrolling perspective allows for creative level design and varied challenges. Simple Yet Challenging: The gameplay is easy to understand but becomes increasingly difficult as players progress, requiring quick reflexes and strategic thinking. Retro Aesthetic: The game features simple but effective graphics and sound, typical of early DOS games. The visuals are functional and add to the game’s nostalgic charm. Independent Development: Although it shares similarities with Pharaoh’s Tomb, Monuments of Mars was developed independently by Todd Replogle, showcasing his creativity and programming skills.

name: Moon Lander
description: Moon Lander is a Lunar Lander type game in CGA. Although this game was released in 1986, Lunar Lander type games go back as far as 1969 (!) and were popular through the 70's and 80's on whatever machine was available at the time. This is a pretty basic implementation, where each game takes only a few seconds. You need to steer left and right, and use the down arrow key to toggle your downward boosters on and off. It's tricky but possible with a little practice. That's the whole game so don't expect a lot of replayability.

name: Moon Mahjong
description: Moon Mahjong is a serene and enchanting variation of the classic Mahjong puzzle game, set against the backdrop of a tranquil moonlit landscape. In this game, players are tasked with matching and removing pairs of identical Mahjong tiles to clear the board and progress through various levels. The game offers a relaxing and visually stunning experience, perfect for unwinding while engaging in a bit of strategic thinking. Gameplay Overview: Mahjong Tiles: The game features traditional Mahjong tiles, each adorned with intricate designs and symbols, such as characters, bamboo, circles, winds, dragons, and seasons. These tiles are arranged in elaborate, multi-layered patterns on the board. Matching Tiles: The primary objective is to find and match two identical tiles. Unlike traditional Mahjong, where three tiles are typically matched, Moon Mahjong simplifies the matching requirement to pairs. When two matching tiles are selected, they are removed from the board. Only tiles that are not covered by others and have at least one side free (left or right) can be clicked. Clearing the Board: The goal is to remove all the tiles from the board. As tiles are removed, new layers and patterns are revealed, requiring players to continuously adapt their strategy. Stack Interaction: If no visible matches are available, players can click on the stack to get new open tiles. This adds an element of strategy, as players must decide when to refresh the available tiles to find new matches. Level Progression: Each level presents a new tile arrangement, often inspired by celestial and lunar themes. As players advance, the layouts become more complex and challenging, with more tiles and intricate patterns. Hints and Shuffles: To assist players, the game may offer hints that highlight possible matches or a shuffle feature that rearranges the remaining tiles to provide new opportunities for matches. Time and Moves: Some versions of the game may include time limits or move restrictions, adding an extra layer of challenge. Players must think quickly and plan their moves carefully to complete the level within the given constraints. Celestial Themes and Backgrounds: The game is rich in celestial visuals, with stunning backgrounds depicting moonlit landscapes, starry skies, and serene night scenes. The soothing sounds of nature and gentle music enhance the immersive experience. Key Features: Traditional Mahjong Tiles: Authentic and beautifully designed tiles that stay true to the classic Mahjong aesthetic. Pair Matching: Simplified matching requirement of two identical tiles, making the game accessible to a wider audience. Multiple Levels: A variety of levels with increasing difficulty, each offering a unique tile arrangement and visual theme. Hint System: Optional hints to help players when they are stuck. Stack Interaction: Ability to refresh the available tiles by clicking on the stack. Celestial Immersion: Stunning visuals and soundscapes that celebrate the beauty of the moon and night sky.

name: Morabis
description: Morabis is a game that functions like a Roguelike, but although it uses textmode, a bizarre mix of hotkeys, and other Roguelike tropes, it's not randomly generated. Your quest, as with Nethack and others, is to collect an amulet. In order to do so, you must explore through many floors of the dungeon, avoiding many dangerous enemies and collecting items to help you. I have to admit I didn't make it far in this game. The first room you enter is filled with ghosts, which will quickly kill you. If you manage to get through there, the thing in the next room will likely off you. You can come back to life as many times as you want apparently so maybe it's possible to make it through the game? See included .DOC file for instructions!

name: Moraff's Dungeons of the Unforgiven
description: Moraff's Dungeons of the Unforgiven is a classic dungeon-crawling RPG that harkens back to the golden age of computer role-playing games, particularly those from SSI (Strategic Simulations, Inc.) like Eye of the Beholder, Dark Sun, and AD&D series. While it may not have the polish or depth of some of its more famous counterparts, it delivers a solid hack-and-slash experience that will appeal to fans of old-school dungeon crawlers. With its focus on exploration, combat, and loot, it’s a game that caters to computer RPG purists who enjoy straightforward, action-oriented gameplay. Key Features: Classic Dungeon-Crawling Gameplay: The game follows the traditional dungeon-crawling formula, with players navigating through multi-level dungeons, battling monsters, and collecting treasure. The focus is on exploration and combat rather than complex storytelling. Hack-and-Slash Action: Combat is a central element of the game, with players engaging in real-time battles against a variety of enemies. The emphasis is on fast-paced, action-oriented gameplay rather than turn-based strategy. Average Graphics: The visuals are functional but not groundbreaking, with simple sprites and environments that get the job done. While the graphics may not impress by modern standards, they are adequate for the time and genre. Minimal Story: The game doesn’t have a deep or intricate narrative, but it does offer more story than some other titles in the Moraffware catalog. The focus remains on gameplay rather than plot. Loot and Progression: Players can collect weapons, armor, and other items to improve their character’s abilities. The game encourages exploration and rewards players with valuable loot for their efforts. Replayability: The procedurally generated dungeons ensure that no two playthroughs are exactly the same, adding to the game’s replay value.

name: Moraff's Entrap
description: Moraff's Entrap is a simple game with a distinctive graphical style. All of Moraff's games have this colorful slightly odd style, but it fits better in this type of strategic game than it does in the company's RPGs. The object here is simply to make it to the end of the suspended pathway. You move with the arrow keys (numeric keypad is pretty much required to succeed here) and you can lay traps (empty tiles) to prevent the robots from catching you. Touching a robot means instant death and the end of the game. The levels seem like they could be randomly generated, but the level layout is always the same, and only the position of the robots is random for each game.

name: Moraff's Escapade
description: Moraff's Escapade is a DOS-era puzzle-platformer that draws clear inspiration from classic games like Lode Runner and Jumpman. Developed by Steve Moraff, known for his minimalist yet challenging games, Moraff's Escapade tasks players with collecting diamonds while navigating levels filled with ladders, blocks, and enemies. The game starts off simple but quickly becomes challenging, requiring strategic thinking and precise execution to succeed. Key Features: Gameplay: The core gameplay revolves around collecting all the diamonds in each level while avoiding or outsmarting enemies. Players can climb ladders, pick up blocks, and drop them to create barriers or traps. This mechanic is reminiscent of Lode Runner, but Moraff's Escapade adds its own twists and challenges. Level Design: The game begins with relatively easy levels to help players get accustomed to the mechanics. However, the difficulty ramps up quickly, introducing more complex layouts, faster enemies, and tricky puzzles that require careful planning and quick reflexes. Enemies and Strategy: Enemies roam the levels, and players must use blocks strategically to trap or evade them. Running away is also an option, but timing and positioning are crucial to survival. Graphics: True to Steve Moraff's style, the graphics are sparse and functional, with simple sprites and minimal visual flair. While this might not appeal to players looking for eye-catching visuals, it keeps the focus squarely on the gameplay. Controls: The controls are reasonably responsive, which is essential for a game that requires precision and quick decision-making. Players use the keyboard to move, climb, and interact with blocks. Strengths: Challenging Gameplay: The game offers a satisfying mix of puzzle-solving and platforming, with levels that gradually increase in difficulty to keep players engaged. Strategic Depth: The ability to pick up and drop blocks adds a layer of strategy, allowing players to create their own paths or traps to outwit enemies. Nostalgic Appeal: Fans of classic DOS games like Lode Runner or Jumpman will appreciate the familiar mechanics and retro charm.

name: Moraff's Monster Bridge
description: Moraff's Monster Bridge is a trump-based card game ("a distant relative of Bridge") set in the same world as Moraff's RPGs like Dungeons of the Unforgiven. Like all Moraff games there are many video modes available (thirteen actually) and probably due to this plethora of options, the game's graphics can look a little strange at times. The gameplay here is a simple trump-type card game, except with an RPG theme and a custom card deck with six fantasy-inspired suits numbered from 1 to 16. You can only play against the computer, there is no local multiplayer. The game works well and is easy to understand, but probably won't have a lot of longevity of play. (This version of the game also comes with Moraff's Stones included.)

name: Moraff's Morejongg
description: Moraff's Morejongg is a single-player Mahjongg game developed by Moraffware, known for its distinctive graphical style and extensive customization options. Released during the heyday of shareware games, it offers a classic Mahjongg experience with a variety of features that set it apart from other titles in the genre. Here’s a detailed look at what makes Moraff's Morejongg unique: Key Features: Classic Mahjongg Gameplay: The game follows the traditional rules of Mahjongg Solitaire, where players match pairs of identical tiles to clear the board. The goal is to remove all tiles by finding and matching open pairs. Unique Graphical Style: Like other Moraffware titles, Morejongg features a distinctive visual style with colorful, detailed tiles and backgrounds. The graphics are retro but charming, reflecting the era in which the game was created. Customizable Video Modes: The game supports a wide range of video modes and resolutions, allowing players to choose the display settings that work best for their system and preferences. Tile and Background Customization: Players can change the color schemes of the tiles and backgrounds, adding a personal touch to the game and making it easier to distinguish between tiles. Mouse and Keyboard Controls: The game offers flexibility in controls, allowing players to use either the mouse or keyboard to select and match tiles. This makes it accessible to a wide range of players. Multiple Layouts: Morejongg includes a variety of tile layouts, each with its own level of difficulty. This adds replayability and ensures that players of all skill levels can find a challenge. Relaxing Experience: The game is designed to be a calming and meditative experience, with no time limits or pressure. It’s perfect for unwinding after a long day. Shareware Roots: As a shareware title, Morejongg was distributed widely in the 90s, making it a nostalgic favorite for many retro gaming enthusiasts. Gameplay: Objective: Clear the board by matching pairs of identical tiles. Tiles are only considered "open" if they are not blocked by other tiles on either side. Controls: Use the mouse or keyboard to select and match tiles. Winning: Successfully remove all tiles from the board to complete the level.

name: Moraff's Pinball
description: Moraff's Pinball is a unique entry in the Moraffware catalog, a collection of games primarily known for their RPGs and puzzle titles. Unlike its siblings, Moraff's Pinball ventures into the realm of arcade-style gaming, offering a digital pinball experience. While it may not stand out as a pinnacle of pinball simulation, it has its own quirky charm and serves as an interesting piece of retro gaming history. Here’s a closer look at this game: Gameplay Overview: Moraff's Pinball attempts to replicate the pinball experience on a computer, with mixed results: Single Table: The game features only one pinball table, limiting its variety compared to other pinball games of the era. Physics: The ball physics are somewhat wonky, making the gameplay feel less realistic than traditional pinball machines or more polished digital pinball games. Controls: The controls are more complicated than necessary, requiring players to use multiple keys to operate the flippers and other table mechanics. This can make the game feel unintuitive, especially for newcomers. Objective: Like real pinball, the goal is to score as many points as possible by hitting targets, ramps, and other elements on the table while keeping the ball in play.

name: Moraff's Revenge
description: Moraff's Revenge is the first entry in a series of dungeon-crawling RPGs developed by Moraffware, paving the way for later titles like Moraff's World and Moraff's Dungeons of the Unforgiven.
