Beginner players can enjoy slower speeds, while more experienced players can challenge themselves with faster falling blocks and higher speeds. Combo Scoring: The game may include special scoring bonuses for clearing multiple lines at once (e.g., clearing two or more lines simultaneously). Players can aim for high scores by strategically stacking blocks and clearing several lines in a single move. Smooth Controls: The controls are intuitive and easy to use. Players can use arrow keys or WASD to move, rotate, and drop the blocks. The simplicity of the controls ensures that players can focus on the strategy and fast-paced action of the game. Soothing Soundtrack and Effects: The game includes an upbeat electronic soundtrack and satisfying sound effects when completing lines or placing blocks. The music complements the neon aesthetic and adds energy to the gameplay. Leaderboards and Achievements: Many versions of NeonTris feature leaderboards where players can compare their high scores with others. Achievements may be unlocked for completing certain challenges, such as clearing a set number of lines or achieving a specific score. Endless Gameplay: NeonTris typically has an endless mode where players keep playing until the screen fills up completely with blocks. The game continues to increase in difficulty as the blocks fall faster, providing endless replayability.

name: Nephew's Puzzle Pack
description: Nephew's Puzzle Pack is a collection of six puzzle games bundled together, offering a variety of challenges for players of all skill levels. While the graphics may not be impressive, the diversity of games and adjustable difficulty levels make it a worthwhile package for puzzle enthusiasts. Here’s a detailed look at what’s included in this pack and why it’s worth checking out: Key Features: Six Puzzle Games: The pack includes a variety of puzzle games, each with its own unique mechanics and challenges. The confirmed games are: Tic-Tac-Toe: The classic two-player game of strategy and foresight. Marbles: A game similar to Mastermind, where players guess a sequence of colors. Other Games: While the full list isn’t specified, the pack likely includes additional puzzle games to provide variety. Adjustable Difficulty: Each game offers multiple difficulty levels, making the pack accessible to both casual players and those seeking a greater challenge. Basic Graphics: The graphics are simple and functional, reflecting the era in which the pack was created. While not visually stunning, they get the job done. Replayability: With six different games and multiple difficulty levels, the pack offers plenty of replay value for puzzle fans. Updated Version: A newer version of the pack has been released, adding features like a level editor for Marbles and variable level selection, enhancing the overall experience. Included Games: Tic-Tac-Toe: The classic game of Xs and Os, where players take turns marking spaces on a 3x3 grid. The goal is to get three of your marks in a row. Marbles: Similar to Mastermind, players must guess a hidden sequence of colors. After each guess, the game provides feedback on how many colors are correct and in the right position. Other Puzzle Games: While the full list isn’t specified, the pack likely includes additional puzzle games such as: Memory Match: A card-matching game where players flip cards to find pairs. Sudoku: A number-placement puzzle where players fill a grid based on specific rules. Sliding Puzzles: Rearrange tiles to form a complete picture or pattern.

name: Neptune Solitaire
description: Neptune Solitaire is a captivating and strategic card game that challenges players to remove all cards from the board by combining cards of consecutive ranks. Here's a detailed description of the game: Gameplay Mechanics: Objective: The primary goal is to remove all cards from the board by pairing cards of consecutive ranks. The game is won when the entire board is cleared. Card Ranks: Consecutive Ranks: Cards can be paired if they are of consecutive ranks. For example, a 2 can be paired with a 3 or an Ace (A), a Jack (J) can be paired with a Queen (Q) or a King (K), and an Ace (A) can be paired with a King (K) or a 2. Special Cases: The game treats Ace (A) as both high and low, allowing it to be paired with King (K) or 2. Game Flow: Initial Setup: The game starts with a layout of cards arranged in a specific pattern. Some cards may be face-up and available for pairing, while others may be face-down and need to be uncovered. Pairing Cards: Click on two cards of consecutive ranks to remove them from the board. When paired, the cards are removed, and new cards may be revealed or fall into place. Clearing the Board: Continue pairing and removing cards until the entire board is cleared. Level Progression: The game is divided into levels, each with increasing difficulty. As you progress, the card arrangements become more complex, and the number of cards increases, requiring more strategic thinking and planning. Hints and Assistance: Hints: If you get stuck, the game may offer hints to show possible pairs or highlight cards that can be paired. Undo: Some versions of the game might include an undo feature, allowing you to reverse your last move and try a different pair.

name: Nerakian Adventure
description: Nerakian Adventure is a traditional CRPG created using the DCGames RPG creation system. As such it presents the same basic look and feel as other games created using the system such as Rescue of Lorri in Lorrinitron. You wander around various towns and other locations on a world map using hotkeys to interact with the world: Talking to people, opening chests, using items. You can fight things to gain EXP and money. It has an endearing title screen.Nerakian Adventure is a pixel-art fantasy game that blends exploration, puzzle-solving, and storytelling. Players are transported to Nerakia, a mystical realm teeming with ancient ruins, quirky villagers, and malevolent forces threatening its harmony. The game features a charming blend of retro visuals, whimsical music, and intricate gameplay that has made it a cult classic among DOS-era enthusiasts. Story: The once-prosperous land of Nerakia has fallen into shadow after the rise of the sinister Sorcerer Karath. You play as Korin, a reluctant hero drawn into the conflict after discovering an ancient artifact—the "Shard of Illumina"—hidden in the woods. Guided by cryptic messages from the artifact, Korin must travel across diverse regions of Nerakia, from lush forests and icy mountains to treacherous caves and abandoned temples, unraveling the secrets of the Shard and confronting Karath to restore balance to the realm. Gameplay: Nerakian Adventure is a top-down adventure game with a focus on exploration and puzzle-solving. The gameplay is divided into several key elements: Exploration: Players navigate Korin through interconnected areas, encountering NPCs, hidden paths, and secrets. Puzzles: Challenges include deciphering riddles, manipulating switches, solving sliding block puzzles, and combining inventory items to progress. Combat: While not the central focus, players can defend themselves with limited weapons (like slingshots or enchanted orbs) and must rely on clever thinking and resource management to outwit enemies. Dialogue System: Interact with quirky villagers and wise sages, choosing dialogue options that affect the story or unlock special hints.

name: Nethack
description: Despite it's name, this game does NOT involve any type of computer "hacking". It's actually my favorite "Roguelike" game, orignally based on the "Hack" roguelike. While it may take awhile to learn all of the different commands, the game itself is very deep and involving. Plus, it's different each time you play. Unlike most Roguelikes, Nethack also features optional VGA graphics.NetHack is a legendary roguelike dungeon-crawler that offers endless replayability, depth, and challenge. Designed for ASCII graphics but fully playable in DOS, NetHack immerses players in a perilous dungeon where death is frequent, strategy is key, and discovery is its own reward. Known for its humor, complexity, and richly detailed world, NetHack remains one of the most celebrated and influential games in the roguelike genre. Story: You are a hero chosen to descend into the depths of the Mazes of Menace in search of the fabled Amulet of Yendor. Along the way, you’ll encounter cunning monsters, powerful artifacts, deadly traps, and a host of other surprises. Your journey will test not just your combat prowess, but your cleverness, resourcefulness, and sheer perseverance. Will you ascend as a demigod, or will you perish like countless adventurers before you? Gameplay: At its core, NetHack is a turn-based dungeon crawler with a procedurally generated world, ensuring no two playthroughs are ever the same. Here are the game’s key elements: Classes and Races: Choose from a wide variety of roles (like Wizard, Knight, or Rogue) and races (like Human, Dwarf, or Elf), each with unique abilities and starting equipment. Exploration: Delve through multiple dungeon levels, uncovering secret doors, hidden traps, and mysterious treasures. Combat and Strategy: Face monsters ranging from goblins and dragons to the infamous floating eye, using melee, magic, or ranged attacks. Complex Systems: Interact with your environment in unexpected ways—eat monsters, read cursed scrolls, dip weapons into potions, or pray to your deity for aid. Permadeath: Death is permanent, making every decision matter. Each playthrough is an entirely new adventure. ASCII Graphics or Tile Sets: The DOS version supports classic ASCII art for a minimalist, highly imaginative experience, or optional graphical tiles for players preferring visuals. Notable Features: Rich Interactivity: Almost every object in the game can be interacted with in unique ways, leading to emergent gameplay. For example, dropping a ring into a fountain might summon a water demon—or give you a wish. Pet System: Players begin with a loyal pet (like a dog, cat, or pony) that helps in combat and scavenging. Alignment and Deities: Your character’s alignment affects interactions with the gods. Anger them, and you may be struck by lightning. Sense of Humor: From inside jokes to bizarre item descriptions (e.g., “A +2 Hawaiian Shirt”), NetHack never takes itself too seriously. Reception: NetHack has been praised for its incredible depth and emergent gameplay, earning it a place in gaming history as one of the greatest roguelikes ever made. However, its steep learning curve and ASCII graphics can intimidate new players. Nonetheless, those who persevere are rewarded with a deeply satisfying and endlessly replayable experience.

name: Neut Tower
description: Neut Tower is a new MS-DOS game developed on actual 286 hardware and released for the DOS Games Jam. As such, although it is a new game, it very much has the feel of a puzzle game created back in the early 90's. The object is to escape the tower, with the aid of your AI entity; you can switch back and forth between the human protagonist and the AI at any time, and you'll need the abilities of both to get through all of the rooms.Neut Tower is a unique blend of sci-fi platforming and brain-teasing puzzles, set in a mysterious tower filled with shifting mechanics, gravity-defying traps, and hostile machines. The game’s innovative mechanics and challenging levels made it a cult classic for DOS gamers who loved testing their wits and reflexes in equal measure. Story: The Neut Tower stands as the last relic of an ancient civilization that once controlled the energy flows of the galaxy. You play as Vek, a skilled engineer sent to activate the tower’s core and prevent an imminent collapse of the galaxy’s power grid. As you ascend the tower, its AI, Tethra, begins to interfere, reprogramming rooms and unleashing robotic guardians to stop you. Is Tethra protecting the core—or hiding a more dangerous secret? Gameplay: Neut Tower combines puzzle-solving and platforming mechanics in a labyrinth of increasingly complex levels. The player must navigate rooms by manipulating energy nodes, avoiding traps, and finding keys to unlock new areas. Core Mechanics: Manipulate neutral energy orbs (the “neuts”) to power platforms, deactivate traps, or reprogram hostile robots. Adjust the tower’s gravity fields to walk on walls, ceilings, or across deadly gaps. Use the multi-tool to interact with switches, hack terminals, or repair broken mechanisms. Challenges: Each floor of the tower introduces new mechanics, like laser grids, time-limited puzzles, or teleportation pads. Avoid or outsmart hostile drones, which become more sophisticated as you ascend.

name: New Dash Dimension
description: There are many Boulderdash clones out there, probably way more than is warranted based on how good the original game is. I mean it's cool and all (with its weird physics) but there are seriously a LOT of clones out there. New Dash Dimension is a pretty good clone in most ways. It accurately represents the original's physics and style, with decent graphics and a variety of levels.New Dash Dimension is a high-speed, sci-fi platformer where reflexes and strategy collide in a neon-lit, interdimensional adventure. Players must dash, dodge, and outsmart enemies across a series of shifting dimensions, each with unique physics and hazards. Featuring tight controls, vibrant VGA graphics, and a pulse-pounding soundtrack, New Dash Dimension became a must-play for DOS gamers seeking fast-paced action. Story: In the far future, the Multiverse Nexus is crumbling, and chaos threatens to consume all dimensions. You play as Ryn Altair, a renegade pilot who stumbles upon the Dimensional Dash Drive, a prototype device that allows interdimensional travel. Tasked by a rogue AI, Vectoris, Ryn must repair the Nexus by collecting shards of the shattered Dimension Core while evading an intergalactic syndicate bent on exploiting the chaos for profit. Gameplay: New Dash Dimension combines high-speed platforming with gravity-defying mechanics, challenging players to adapt to constantly changing environments. Core Mechanics: Dash Drive: Teleport short distances to evade enemies, cross gaps, or bypass traps. Dimensional Shifts: Each level shifts between dimensions, altering gravity, colors, or hazards in real-time. Combat: Use a mix of energy blasts, melee strikes, and clever dashing to outmaneuver enemies. Level Design: Navigate sprawling, multi-path levels filled with moving platforms, gravity wells, laser grids, and environmental puzzles. Discover secret rooms containing upgrades, lore, and hidden Dimension Core shards. Progression: Collect shards to unlock new abilities, like longer dashes, temporary invincibility, or dimension-freezing powers.

name: New year's Mystery
description: New Year's Mystery is a graphical adventure game about a murder that takes place at a New Year's Eve party. It's described thusly: "Invited to a party, that ends in disaster. Can you find the murderer amongst the ever expiring guests." It uses the Sierra SCI engine so you move around with the keyboard or mouse, and type simple commands to make things happen. It has pretty good graphics, nearly on par with early Sierra titles (at least IMHO) and impressively the author noted it was created in a single month. (Maybe there was some reuse of assets going on there.) It seems like a short game (only 35 points) so it's probably worth trying out. (Source code is included in the src directory.)

name: New York City Gangs
description: Overview: New York City Gangs is an exciting flash fighting game that immerses players in the gritty streets of New York City. With a blend of classic beat 'em up gameplay and street brawler mechanics, players can engage in fast-paced combat against various opponents in a vibrant urban setting. Gameplay: Controls: Easy-to-learn controls allow players to punch, kick, and execute special moves. Players can also perform combos for increased damage and style. Characters: Choose from a diverse roster of street fighters, each with unique abilities and fighting styles, reflecting the city's cultural diversity. Levels: Fight through multiple stages set in iconic New York locations, such as alleyways, subway stations, and street corners, each with its own challenges and enemies. Power-ups: Collect items and power-ups during fights to enhance abilities and restore health. Graphics & Sound: Visual Style: Features colorful, dynamic graphics with a cartoonish aesthetic that captures the lively spirit of street culture. Soundtrack: An energetic and engaging soundtrack, along with punchy sound effects, enhances the immersive combat experience. Key Features: Single and Multiplayer Modes: Play solo against AI opponents or team up with friends for local multiplayer battles. Combo System: Master intricate combos and special moves to dominate opponents and score high. Unlockables: Progress through the game to unlock new characters and stages, adding depth and replayability. New York City Gangs offers an action-packed experience filled with thrilling battles and colorful visuals, making it a great choice for fans of fighting games looking for a nostalgic flash experience!

name: New York Hidden Objects
description: Find all the hidden objects in New York. Click on the objects. You can zoom in. Use the light bulb for a hint.Embark on an exciting journey through the bustling streets of New York City in this captivating hidden objects game! Explore iconic locations such as Times Square, Central Park, and the Brooklyn Bridge while hunting for cleverly concealed items. With stunning visuals, challenging puzzles, and engaging mini-games, each scene brings the spirit of the city to life. Test your observation skills across multiple levels, earn rewards for completing tasks, and unlock secrets about the Big Apple. Whether you’re solving riddles, finding rare artifacts, or racing against the clock, Hidden Objects: New York Adventure promises endless fun and discovery! Features: Over 50 beautifully designed scenes set in New York City. Multiple gameplay modes: timed challenges, relaxed exploration, and story-driven quests. Fun mini-games and bonus puzzles to keep you entertained. Suitable for players of all ages and skill levels. Step into the adventure—New York is waiting for you to uncover its hidden treasures!

name: Newgrounds Rumble
description: Step into the ultimate battle arena in Newgrounds Rumble! This action-packed flash game brings together iconic characters from the Newgrounds universe in an epic brawler. Choose your favorite fighter and duke it out across diverse stages inspired by the Newgrounds community. Whether you’re smashing through opponents in single-player story mode, perfecting your skills in training, or proving your dominance in multiplayer battles, Newgrounds Rumble delivers non-stop excitement. With unique moves, special abilities, and fan-favorite characters, this game is a must-play for any Newgrounds enthusiast! Features: Playable characters from popular Newgrounds creations. Multiple game modes: Story, Versus, Survival, and Training. Dynamic combat mechanics with special moves and combos. Unlockable content, including new characters and stages. Retro-style graphics and soundtracks that bring back the classic flash game vibes. Ready to rumble? Jump into the fight and claim your spot as the ultimate Newgrounds champion!

name: NHL 96
description: Described upon release as being "the best PC hockey game released yet" (CGW, Jan 1996) NHL 96 debuted EA's Virtual Stadium, with a 3D feel even without a 3D accelerator card. (Unlike the SNES version which retained the sprite-based gameplay of the previous games.) This demo version allows you to experience a taste of what the full game offers (sans music) by playing a short game between the Detroit Red Wings and the New Jersey Devils.NHL 96 brings fast-paced hockey action to life on DOS with thrilling gameplay, authentic teams, and realistic features that set a new standard for sports games of its time. Developed by EA Sports, this classic hockey sim puts you in the skates of your favorite NHL stars as you chase the Stanley Cup in a variety of modes. Take control of all 26 NHL teams (including the newly added Colorado Avalanche) and their rosters, complete with real player stats. Featuring smooth animations, updated player models, and improved AI, NHL 96 delivers an immersive hockey experience that keeps the action intense and unpredictable. Features: Full NHL license with real teams, logos, and players from the 1995-1996 season. Multiple modes, including Exhibition, Playoffs, and Full Season. New gameplay features like fake shots, drop passes, and improved puck physics. Dynamic camera angles for a cinematic hockey experience. Create-your-own player feature to build your ultimate hockey star. Classic MIDI soundtracks and commentary that enhance the retro gaming vibe. With its blend of strategy, skill, and fast-paced action, NHL 96 is a nostalgic gem for hockey fans and retro gaming enthusiasts alike!

name: NHL Hockey94
description: his demo of the first PC version of EA's still continuing hockey series removes all options and lets you play a brief 2-minute game with a random selection of two of the 26 teams. (Back then there were "only" 26!) It features well drawn but slightly choppy graphics, and was the template upon which all future 2D EA Sports hockey games were built upon. Its simple 2-button controls and gameplay can actually be quite refreshing compared to modern hockey games.Relive the golden age of hockey gaming with NHL Hockey 94! This iconic DOS classic, developed by EA Sports, is hailed as one of the greatest sports games of all time. Featuring fast-paced gameplay, fluid controls, and the perfect mix of arcade fun and hockey simulation, NHL 94 captures the excitement of the NHL like never before. Choose from all 26 NHL teams, complete with real rosters from the 1993-1994 season. Skate, pass, shoot, and check your way to glory in modes like Exhibition, Playoffs, or Full Season. With innovative mechanics like one-timers and improved goalie AI, NHL Hockey 94 set the standard for future hockey games. Features: Authentic NHL teams and players from the 1993-1994 season. Revolutionary one-timer mechanic for quick, dynamic scoring plays. Multiple modes: Exhibition, Playoffs, and Best-of-Seven series. Realistic player animations and fluid gameplay. Customizable lineups and strategies to suit your playstyle. Classic crowd cheers, organ music, and sound effects for an authentic arena atmosphere. Perfect for casual fans and hardcore hockey enthusiasts, NHL Hockey 94 is a timeless masterpiece that continues to deliver fun and competitive action!

name: Nibbler
description: Nibbler is a variation of the popular Nibbles/Snake game where the object is to eat items to make your snake grow while avoiding your tail. This version has decent graphics, sounds and a variety of different enemies and levels for you to play.Dive into the fast-paced, addictive world of Nibbler, a classic DOS arcade game that combines the strategic movement of Snake with the maze-chomping fun of Pac-Man! Guide your snake through a series of intricate mazes, consuming all the pellets to clear each level. But beware—the more you eat, the longer your snake grows, making navigation increasingly challenging! Race against the clock, avoid colliding with your own tail, and strategically plan your moves to conquer progressively difficult levels. With its simple yet engaging gameplay, Nibbler offers endless hours of retro gaming fun. Features: Dozens of challenging mazes with increasing difficulty. Smooth, fast-paced gameplay that tests reflexes and planning. Classic 1980s-style graphics and sound effects for a nostalgic arcade feel. Easy-to-learn controls that make it accessible to players of all ages. High-score tracking to compete against yourself or friends. Can you master the mazes and keep your snake from getting tangled? Put your skills to the test in Nibbler!

name: Nibbles
description: Nibbles is a vibrant remake of the classic QBasic game, reimagined with all-new levels and colorful 256-color animated graphics! This retro-inspired game brings a fresh twist to the familiar Snake/Nibbles formula, challenging players to navigate unique mazes, collect fruit, and avoid walls and their ever-growing tail. Each level is carefully designed with its own name and distinct layout, adding variety and creativity to the gameplay. While the game lacks sound effects, the colorful visuals and smooth controls make it a solid and enjoyable version of the timeless Snake genre. Features: 256-color animated graphics for a bright and engaging visual experience. Unique, named levels with creative layouts to test your skills. Simple and intuitive controls that capture the spirit of the original game. No sound, keeping the focus on the strategic and reflex-based gameplay. A modernized take on the classic Snake formula, perfect for fans of retro games. Guide your snake to victory and see how far you can go in this fresh take on a nostalgic classic!

name: Nicholas' Weird Adventure
description: Nicholas' Weird Adventure is a classic point-and-click adventure Flash game that is well-known for its quirky humor, absurd storylines, and surreal gameplay. It was developed by Scott R. Jones and was released as part of the Flash game genre that gained popularity in the 2000s. The game has a fun, whimsical tone with bizarre puzzles and out-of-the-box thinking required to progress. Storyline: The game begins with Nicholas getting caught up in an eccentric series of events that lead him to different strange locations. The story is filled with quirky, random events and characters. The dialogue and writing have a sarcastic, self-aware humor, and the narrative is full of absurd twists that keep the player on their toes. Gameplay Mechanics: Point-and-click interaction: The game follows a traditional point-and-click adventure model, where you click on objects, characters, and locations to interact with them. This is key for solving puzzles and advancing in the game. Inventory system: Throughout the game, Nicholas can collect items that he needs to solve puzzles or use in different scenarios. You'll have to figure out how to combine and use items in creative ways to move forward. Humor and absurdity: The game is known for its weirdness, often pushing the boundaries of logic. Some puzzles can be intentionally nonsensical, and solutions might not always be what you'd expect. The humor often plays on this unpredictability. Key Features: Bizarre Puzzles: Expect odd, quirky puzzles that may require thinking outside the box. You might need to use a rubber chicken to solve a puzzle or perform actions in a strange sequence. Comedic Writing: The game is filled with witty dialogue, humorous interactions, and sarcastic characters. It's all part of the game's charm and is one of the reasons it's loved by players. Surreal Art Style: The visuals are simple but effective in creating the weird world that Nicholas inhabits. The environments are cartoonish and exaggerated, helping reinforce the absurd nature of the adventure.

name: Nicolausi
description: Santa is in trouble! He's lost his presents, and his list telling him which presents go to which house! So he must navigate the maze-like streets of the city, finding presents, and attempting to deliver them to the correct house. And of course, the Easter Bunny is chasing him with his boom box, and if he catches Santa, the Easter Bunny will kick his ass! Well, this all sounds normal and reasonable. It's sort of a maze game, but with action, since you have to avoid the Easter Bunny. You pick up presents and deliver them to houses, but there's apparently no way to know which present goes to which house, so you just have to hope you get lucky.

name: Night Fire
description: Night Fire is a classic, early artillery-style game that laid the foundation for the beloved tank battle genre, similar to Tank Wars or Scorched Earth. Up to 8 players can compete in this turn-based strategy game, battling it out on randomly-generated terrains. Carefully calculate the direction and velocity of your shots, or use your turn to reposition your tank strategically for the next round. The game’s simplicity is its charm, as players balance offense and defense while contending with dynamic landscapes and their opponents’ cunning moves. With its competitive gameplay and endless replayability, Night Fire is a perfect pick for fans of retro strategy games. Features: Supports 2-8 players for intense multiplayer battles on the same device. Randomly-generated terrain for fresh challenges in every match. Turn-based mechanics that let you shoot or move your tank each turn. Simple yet engaging strategy gameplay with no-frills design. A great introduction to the artillery genre that inspired future classics. Can you outmaneuver and outshoot your opponents to claim victory? Jump into the battlefield with Night Fire!

name: Night Raid
description: Similar to Ack-Ack Attack, but with a bit more polish. From the publishers of the excellent Hexxagon game comes this one ... I don't like this game as much, it feels a bit like Missile Command but it's just not the same. The idea is that you control a cannon and have to shoot down the various paratroopers, bombs, etc. before they hit the ground. Nice presentation but not the greatest gameplay in my opinion.Night Raid is an intense, fast-paced DOS action game that puts you in the hot seat as the defender of a city under relentless aerial assault. As waves of enemy planes and paratroopers descend from the sky, it’s your mission to aim, fire, and protect your territory from destruction. Armed with anti-aircraft cannons, you’ll need quick reflexes and sharp aim to destroy enemy forces before they overwhelm your defenses. With increasing difficulty, Night Raid challenges players to survive as long as possible in this addictive arcade-style shooter. Features: Endless waves of enemy planes, bombs, and paratroopers to test your skills. Fast-paced, reflex-driven gameplay that keeps you on edge. Simple, classic DOS graphics that capture the spirit of 1980s arcade games. Progressive difficulty for an ever-growing challenge. High-score tracking for bragging rights and competitive replayability. Prepare for a barrage of action—how long can you last in the chaos of Night Raid?

name: Nine Men's Morris
description: The board game Nine Men Morris or Mill. Nine Men's Morris is a classic strategy board game that has been enjoyed for centuries, and now you can play it in your browser! Also known as Mill, this ancient game challenges players to strategically place and move their pieces (or "men") on a grid, aiming to create a "mill"—three pieces in a row—while blocking their opponent from doing the same. With two players taking turns, the game begins with each player placing their nine pieces on the board, followed by the movement phase. The goal is to capture the opponent’s pieces by forming mills and gaining control of the board. The first player to reduce their opponent to just two pieces, or to leave them with no legal moves, wins the game. Features: Simple and elegant gameplay with easy-to-understand rules. Classic Nine Men’s Morris grid for an authentic experience. Play against a computer AI or challenge friends in a multiplayer mode. Option for different difficulty levels when playing against the computer. A game of strategy and foresight, with no luck involved—every move counts! Whether you’re a casual player or a strategic mastermind, Nine Men's Morris offers hours of engaging gameplay for fans of classic strategy games. Ready to create your mill and outsmart your opponent? Let the game begin!

name: Nine Rooms
description: Nine Rooms is a puzzle-based Flash game that was part of the growing genre of escape-the-room games popularized in the mid-2000s. The game is often cited for its atmospheric design, clever puzzles, and the challenge of figuring out how to escape each room using the items and clues provided. Gameplay Mechanics: Point-and-click interaction: As with many escape games, you control your character's actions by clicking on various objects, furniture, and elements within the room. You’ll need to find hidden items, solve riddles, and sometimes combine objects to unlock the next puzzle. Inventory system: Throughout the game, you’ll collect items that will be essential for solving puzzles. These could range from keys and tools to cryptic documents that hold part of the solution. Your inventory can be accessed and used to interact with other items or objects in the environment. Room-based puzzles: Each of the nine rooms presents unique challenges, often with a mix of logic puzzles, hidden object searches, and combination tasks. You'll have to examine the room thoroughly and think outside the box to solve each puzzle. Atmosphere: One of the distinctive features of Nine Rooms is its eerie, sometimes unsettling atmosphere. The rooms are often dimly lit, with the occasional creepy sound or detail that keeps players on edge. This adds to the feeling of being trapped, and the puzzles reflect that tension as you try to escape. Game Structure: Nine Rooms: As the name implies, the game consists of nine distinct rooms. Each one has a different theme and set of challenges. You may encounter things like locked boxes, coded messages, or intricate mechanisms that need solving before you can move on to the next room. Progression: To advance through the rooms, you'll need to solve puzzles in each one. Typically, you’ll need to find key items, use logic to decipher codes, and sometimes piece together parts of a larger puzzle. The puzzles grow progressively more complex as you move through the rooms. Atmosphere and Story: While the main focus is on solving the puzzles, Nine Rooms is set in a creepy, atmospheric environment. The minimalist art style, dark tones, and eerie music contribute to the sense of isolation and urgency that enhances the puzzle-solving experience. Challenge: Some puzzles may require patience or trial-and-error, especially if you don’t immediately understand how the items in your inventory interact with the room. Part of the challenge of the game is figuring out how to combine and use objects creatively. Key Features: Clever puzzles: The game features a variety of puzzles, including logic puzzles, math puzzles, hidden object searches, and code-breaking. Each room is unique, so you’ll need to adapt your thinking to different types of challenges. Atmospheric design: The game’s eerie environment, along with its minimalistic yet detailed art and sound, creates an immersive experience that keeps players engaged while solving puzzles. Item management: You must carefully keep track of the items you’ve collected and figure out how they relate to the rooms. Sometimes, you’ll need to use an item in a way you didn’t expect, so paying attention to details is key.

name: Ninja
description: Ninja is a very early CGA platforming game. You are a ninja, and must defeat all of the "black-belt karate fighters" who for whatever reason want to kill you. The instructions say that you can use the function keys (F1-F10) to attack, but all of the keys seem to do the same basic attack. You can crouch, jump, and your fighter gets tired if you attack too quickly. I couldn't get past the first level, even defeating a single enemy is a bit of a chore.Ninja is a classic action platformer game from the early days of DOS gaming that puts you in the shoes of a skilled ninja warrior. Tasked with infiltrating enemy strongholds and defeating rival ninjas, you must navigate dangerous environments, avoid traps, and defeat enemies with your martial arts skills and precision. The gameplay features fast-paced action, where you can jump, attack with shuriken, and use your sword to slice through enemies. With its challenging platforming, hidden traps, and multiple levels of increasing difficulty, Ninja offers an engaging experience for fans of retro action games. Features: Side-scrolling action platformer gameplay with fluid movement and combat. Multiple levels with varied environments, each filled with enemies and obstacles. Intuitive controls for sword fighting, shuriken throwing, and jumping. Increasingly difficult levels that require quick reflexes and strategic thinking. Classic DOS graphics and sound effects that capture the 80s/90s gaming atmosphere. Can you become the ultimate ninja and defeat your foes across challenging levels? Test your skills and stealth in Ninja—where every move counts!

name: Ninja Blitz
description: Ninja Blitz is a simple action game, which is a variation on the VIC-20 game Blitz from 1981. In this text-mode game the object is to successfully dive-bomb dollar signs ($) from a cityscape, while avoiding hitting the buildings as much as possible. Once you collect enough money ($1000) you hit a detonator and move on. It's simple in concept and the controls are pretty responsive, but not easy accomplish, fun to play in short bursts. It sorta feels like the claw-catcher prize games. Made in 2020, and the executable is only 12kb!

name: Ninja Breakout
description: Ninja Breakout is an exciting twist on the classic Breakout game, combining the fast-paced action of brick-breaking with a ninja theme. Players control a ninja character who uses shurikens (throwing stars) or other ninja weapons to destroy bricks and clear levels. The game adds a layer of strategy and skill with its unique ninja-inspired mechanics. How to Play Ninja Breakout: Objective: Use your ninja skills to destroy all the bricks on the screen by throwing shurikens or other weapons. Clear each level by breaking all the bricks before running out of attempts. Setup: Each level features a grid of bricks at the top of the screen. The player controls a ninja at the bottom who can move left and right to aim and throw shurikens. Gameplay: Aim your shurikens by moving the ninja horizontally. Throw shurikens to hit and break the bricks. Some bricks may require multiple hits to break, while others may contain power-ups or special items. If a shuriken misses the bricks and falls off the screen, you lose a life or attempt. Power-Ups and Bonuses: Collect power-ups that fall from broken bricks to gain advantages, such as: Multi-shurikens: Throw multiple shurikens at once. Explosive shurikens: Destroy multiple bricks in one shot. Speed boosts: Increase the speed of your shurikens. Extra lives: Gain additional attempts. Winning: Clear the level by breaking all the bricks. Progress through increasingly challenging levels with different brick patterns and obstacles.

name: Ninja Darts
description: Try to score 501 points in as less tries as possible. Click-hold-release for aiming.Ninja Darts is a fast-paced, action-packed HTML game that combines the precision of darts with the stealth of a ninja! In this unique and fun take on the classic dartboard game, you play as a ninja armed with throwing darts, aiming to hit targets while overcoming various obstacles. The game features multiple levels, each with its own set of challenges, such as moving targets, timed challenges, or even enemies that must be avoided. As a ninja, your goal is to throw darts with perfect accuracy to defeat your opponents, break objects, or hit high-score targets within each level. The game’s simple yet addictive mechanics make it easy to learn, but challenging enough to keep you coming back for more! Features: Fun and challenging dart-throwing mechanics with a ninja twist. Multiple levels with unique targets, moving obstacles, and timed challenges. Smooth controls and fast-paced gameplay for quick action. High-score tracking to compete with friends or beat your own best scores. Colorful, engaging graphics that bring the ninja theme to life. A relaxing yet competitive experience for players of all ages. Step into the shoes of a skilled ninja and test your dart-throwing precision in Ninja Darts! Ready, aim, and throw!

name: Niosa
description: According to the official website: "NIOSA (pronounced 'knee-oh-sa') is a four-night event that celebrates San Antonio's diverse cultural heritiage with 15 ethnic areas that serve fabulous foods in over 250 food booths and provides entertainment to over 85,000 revelers." This game (circa 1987, with CGA graphics to match) attempts to simulate the experience of attending this event. It's an odd mix, sort of a timed adventure game where the object is to locate your friend, experience the festival, and leave by midnight.

name: Nippon Safes, Inc
description: Nippon Safes, Inc. is a graphical adventure game, similar to Sierra or Lucasarts adventures released in the early 90's. It is the predecessor to the more well-known game The Big Red Adventure by the same developers and featuring the same characters. Originally a commercially released game, this game was released for free by its original developers. You take control of three different characters throughout the game, and it's a nicely crafted adventure with great graphics and a MIDI music soundtrack. Definitely worth checking out if you're a fan of the genre.

name: Nitemare 3D
description: Nitemare 3D is a first-person shooter with horror and adventure elements, released in 1994 for MS-DOS by David P. Gray. Known for its eerie atmosphere and puzzle-solving mechanics, the game was a departure from typical shooters of its era, incorporating a spooky storyline and creepy visuals. Story You play as Hugo, the protagonist of the Hugo’s House of Horrors adventure series, on a mission to rescue his girlfriend Penelope, who has been kidnapped by the evil Dr. Hamerstein. Hugo must fight through a series of haunted levels filled with monsters, traps, and dark magic to reach the villain and save Penelope. Gameplay First-Person Shooter: The game features a 3D perspective similar to early FPS games like Wolfenstein 3D. Combat: Use a variety of weapons, including magic wands and energy-based guns, to defeat ghosts, zombies, vampires, and other supernatural enemies. Exploration: Navigate through 3 main episodes, each consisting of multiple levels. Explore eerie castles, haunted mansions, and dungeons filled with puzzles and secrets. Puzzle Elements: Collect keys to unlock doors, find hidden switches, and manage resources to progress. Health and Mana: Monitor Hugo's health and energy (used for magical weapons) while avoiding enemy attacks and traps. Features Spooky Atmosphere: Creepy environments, enemies, and sound effects create a light horror experience. Retro Graphics: Simple, colorful sprite-based visuals that add charm to the 3D environments. Sound Effects and Music: Atmospheric MIDI music and spooky sounds contribute to the game's eerie vibe. Episodes: Episode 1: The Labyrinth of Doom Episode 2: The Dungeon of Darkness Episode 3: Death or Glory

name: No Time to Explain
description: No Time to Explain is a fast-paced, action-packed Flash game that gained popularity for its chaotic gameplay, over-the-top humor, and distinctive art style. Developed by Tom Fulp and released by Newgrounds, the game combines platforming, action, and quirky storytelling to create a fun and often hilarious experience. Platforming and Action: The game is a side-scrolling platformer with action elements. You’ll jump, shoot, and interact with various enemies and obstacles as you move through each level. The levels are often short but filled with hazards and traps. You control your character using basic platforming mechanics, jumping from platform to platform, avoiding or defeating enemies, and solving simple puzzles to progress. Time Travel and Weapons: The game’s time travel element plays a crucial role in both the story and gameplay. You encounter future versions of yourself, each with their own unique weapons or abilities. This includes gadgets like jetpacks, laser guns, and even an absurd “time gun” that allows you to warp between areas or manipulate the environment in strange ways. The gameplay is fast-paced, with constant movement, shooting, and dodging. Your primary tool is the jetpack, which lets you fly and navigate through the levels, adding a layer of verticality to the otherwise standard platforming mechanics. Humor and Storytelling: One of the key elements of No Time to Explain is its humor. The game is full of quirky dialogue, weird scenarios, and references to time travel tropes. The story progresses through bizarre encounters, where you’ll meet various future versions of yourself, each offering strange and often hilarious commentary. The game's tagline, "No Time to Explain," is a running joke that plays into the absurdity of the narrative and its breakneck pace.

name: No-Pity Island
description: No-Pity Island is what I'll call a "strategic platforming game". It's done in textmode, and as such your player (drawn with ASCII lines to be multiple characters big) steps in character-sized blocks. It's like a turn-based platformer, since you can carefully consider your next moves before doing them. The goal is to collect all of the $ and reach the end of the level @. The gameplay is pretty basic but it's always fun to see what kind of gameplay skilled coders (in this case members of the demoscene) can fit into a 14k executable file.

name: Nogginnockers
description: Nogginnockers (or "Noggin Nockers" as it's mistakenly shown on the title screen) is the original game upon which the improved Nogginnockers 2 is based. You should probably play the sequel if you're looking for a fun time, since it features many improvements from the original. The authors themselves clearly point out that this game was made in a couple days and you shouldn't expect an exemplary experience. Anyways, it's basically Pong, but much more bloody. This game is not for children!Nogginnockers is a quirky and obscure DOS-based puzzle/action game released in the early 1990s. Developed by Acord Games, the game features a unique mix of arcade-style mechanics and reflex-based challenges, providing players with a fun and unusual experience. Gameplay Core Objective: The player must defeat enemies (called Noggins) by strategically smashing their heads together in increasingly challenging levels. Mechanics: Control your character as you move around the screen to manipulate enemies. Push and pull the Noggins into each other to "knock" them out. Avoid being trapped or touched by the enemies, as this can lead to losing a life. Levels: Each level introduces more enemies, obstacles, and hazards, requiring both quick thinking and fast reflexes. Power-ups: Collect occasional power-ups to gain advantages like temporary invincibility or speed boosts. Features Retro Graphics: Simple pixel art visuals with colorful characters and environments. Humorous Tone: The game embraces its lighthearted and comical premise, with goofy animations and sound effects when Noggins are knocked out. Arcade Gameplay: Fast-paced, challenging gameplay that becomes progressively harder as you advance through levels. Sound Effects: MIDI-based audio and amusing sound cues that add charm to the game.

name: Nogginnockers 2
description: Nogginnockers 2 is the sequel to the quirky DOS-based puzzle/action game Nogginnockers, developed by Acord Games in the 1990s. The game builds on the original's humorous and frantic head-smashing gameplay while introducing new mechanics, levels, and challenges for players. Gameplay Core Objective: Similar to the first game, the goal is to defeat enemies (known as Noggins) by smashing their heads together. This time, the game introduces new enemy types, more complex levels, and fresh mechanics to ramp up the difficulty. Key Features: Strategic Movement: Navigate the arena to manipulate Noggins into colliding with each other. Timing and positioning are crucial to succeed. Hazards and Obstacles: Levels now include moving platforms, traps, pits, and environmental hazards that require careful planning. Power-ups: New power-ups offer a range of temporary abilities, such as speed boosts, shields, or stunning enemies. Level Progression: Levels become increasingly intricate, with more enemies, tighter spaces, and environmental puzzles to solve. Features Improved Graphics: Nogginnockers 2 features refined sprite art and smoother animations, with more colorful and varied environments. Enhanced AI: Enemy Noggins now behave more unpredictably, adding an extra layer of challenge. New Enemy Types: Different Noggins have unique behaviors or resistances, requiring varied strategies to defeat. Arcade Action: Retains the original's fast-paced, reflex-based gameplay but adds depth with environmental interactions. Soundtrack and Effects: Improved MIDI music and wacky sound effects enhance the game's playful atmosphere.

name: noitcelfeR
description: Noitcelfer is a lesser-known but intriguing Flash puzzle game that has become popular among fans of mind-bending, reflective, and surreal games. The title itself is a clever play on the word "Reflection" (spelled backwards), which is a core theme in the gameplay and puzzles. The game is a point-and-click adventure that focuses on the concept of mirror images, perspective, and reflection—both literally and metaphorically. Gameplay Mechanics: Point-and-click puzzle-solving: Like many Flash puzzle games, Noitcelfer is a point-and-click adventure where you interact with the environment to find clues and solve puzzles. You’ll click on objects, characters, and various elements in the world to uncover secrets and solve the various tasks at hand. Reflection Mechanic: The central mechanic of Noitcelfer is its use of reflections. The game world often has mirrored surfaces or reflects a version of the environment that may be different from what you see at first glance. Players must use these reflections in their puzzles—what looks like an obstacle in one world might be the solution in the reflected version. Environmental puzzles: Many of the puzzles are based on manipulating or using reflections in the environment. For example, a locked door might require you to solve a puzzle in its reflection, or objects in the real world might need to be aligned perfectly with their mirrored counterparts in order to unlock the next section of the game. Visual and Sound Design: The game has a minimalistic art style, often using simple lines, shapes, and shadows to convey a sense of space and symmetry. The sound design is subtle but atmospheric, adding to the surreal, reflective quality of the world. Core Concepts: Reflection and Symmetry: The gameplay revolves heavily around symmetry and reflection. You’ll often need to analyze the reflected world and how it differs from the one you can directly interact with. What’s important to you in the main world may be mirrored or inverted in the reflected world, requiring creative thinking. Manipulating the Environment: Many puzzles involve manipulating the environment in such a way that the reflection matches up with a desired outcome. For example, you might need to move objects in the real world to affect their mirrored counterparts and unlock the next puzzle element. Reversal of Perspective: The title Noitcelfer (a mirror image of "Reflection") hints at the idea of looking at things from a different angle. The game challenges you to constantly change your perspective, think backwards, and look at your surroundings through a different lens—literally and figuratively. Key Features: Reflective Puzzles: The unique reflection-based mechanics make this game stand out among other puzzle games. Your task is to solve puzzles by either manipulating physical objects in the world or by adjusting your perspective so that reflections align in the correct way. Minimalist Art Style: The art style is simple yet effective, relying on the interplay of light, shadows, and reflections to create a surreal atmosphere. The game's visual design reinforces the theme of perception and illusion. Clever Puzzle Design: The puzzles can be quite challenging, requiring you to think carefully about the relationship between the real and mirrored worlds. Sometimes, the solution involves thinking not just logically, but also creatively or symbolically.

name: Nonogram
description: Play nonogram puzzles in different sizes. Use the hints in the rows and columns to solve the puzzle.Nonogram HTML is a browser-based puzzle game that brings the classic Nonogram (also known as Picross or Griddlers) to modern web platforms. The game challenges players to use logic and deduction to reveal hidden pixel art images by filling in or marking grid cells based on numeric clues. Gameplay Core Objective: Solve the puzzle by filling in the correct cells on a grid to reveal a hidden picture. How to Play: Each row and column has a series of numbers that indicate how many consecutive cells should be filled. Players must deduce the placement of filled cells using logic, avoiding mistakes. Mark cells as either filled or blank (often using a cross or dot). Grid Sizes: The game often includes puzzles of varying difficulty, ranging from small grids (5x5 or 10x10) to larger grids (20x20 or more). Features Intuitive Controls: Play using simple mouse clicks or touchscreen gestures to fill or mark cells. Difficulty Levels: Puzzles range from beginner-friendly to highly challenging for experienced players. Undo and Hints: Many versions include undo options or hints to help when stuck. Customizable Themes: Some HTML versions offer customizable grid colors or dark mode for better visual comfort. Auto-Check Option: Certain games highlight mistakes in real-time or at the end of the puzzle.

name: Noose
description: Noose is a text-based adventure game released for DOS in the early 1990s. Developed as a small indie project, it offers a simplistic but engaging narrative-driven experience, often compared to classic text adventures like Zork. The game revolves around exploration, problem-solving, and interacting with the environment through typed commands. Gameplay Core Objective: Navigate through a series of narrative-driven scenarios, solving puzzles and avoiding traps to progress. Story: While the story varies slightly between versions, the general premise involves escaping danger—often represented by a mysterious, foreboding "noose"—and uncovering hidden truths about the protagonist's predicament. Mechanics: Use text commands like LOOK, MOVE, TAKE, USE, and TALK to interact with the environment. Read descriptions carefully to identify clues and solve puzzles. Manage resources and make choices that impact the story's direction or outcome. Puzzles: Solve logic-based challenges, find hidden objects, and make sense of cryptic descriptions to proceed. Features Text-Based Interface: Entirely reliant on descriptive text and player imagination, creating an immersive storytelling experience. Minimal Graphics: Some versions included simple ASCII art or static images to represent key locations or items. Atmospheric Writing: Descriptions are vivid and eerie, building a sense of suspense and mystery throughout the game. Multiple Endings: Depending on choices and puzzle solutions, players may achieve different outcomes.

name: Notebook Wars
description: Notebook Wars is a classic Flash-based shooting game that was popular during the Flash game era. It stands out for its creative theme, where players control an aircraft and fight through a series of notebook-drawn environments and enemies. The game’s art style is based on the idea of a school notebook or doodles, giving it a fun, unique aesthetic. Gameplay Mechanics: Vertical Shooter Gameplay: Notebook Wars follows the traditional vertical scrolling shooter formula. Your plane constantly moves forward, and you must control it by dodging enemy fire, avoiding obstacles, and shooting down incoming enemies. Enemies approach from the top of the screen and often attack in swarms, meaning quick reflexes and good shooting accuracy are essential to surviving each wave. Power-ups: Throughout the game, you collect power-ups that upgrade your plane's weapons, giving you an edge in battle. Power-ups may include: Machine Gun upgrades: Increasing your firing rate or adding extra projectiles. Bombs: Special attacks that deal massive damage to enemies. Shielding: Temporary invincibility to help you survive intense moments. Missiles: Stronger and more powerful projectiles that deal heavy damage to enemy planes. Boss Fights: At the end of each level, you'll face off against a large enemy boss that is more challenging than the regular enemies. These bosses have unique attack patterns and require more strategy to defeat. Upgrades and Currency: As you progress, you collect points or in-game currency by defeating enemies. These points can be used to purchase upgrades for your plane between levels. Upgrades can enhance the plane’s weapons, health, and speed, allowing you to take on more difficult enemies as you advance. Levels and Environments: The game features multiple levels, each set in a different "notebook" environment. The enemies and challenges vary from stage to stage, with new types of enemies and more complex bullet patterns. The stages get progressively more difficult, with the appearance of different enemy types and more intense waves. Enemies and Obstacles: The enemies in Notebook Wars are varied and include different types of aircraft, some of which may be drawn in different styles (e.g., sketchy, doodle-like planes). There are also environmental hazards in some stages, such as obstacles or hazards that you must avoid while fighting.

name: Notes
description: Notes is a simple puzzle game where the object is to place musical notes on staves. The staves have different times signatures so you'll need to make sure the different types of notes (whole, half, quarter, etc) fit evenly, and strategically save space for different notes so you'll have a place to put them as they randomly appear. It's a neat idea for a puzzle game and it works pretty well, although I didn't personally find it too fun to play. It looks & plays decently so check it out if you like puzzles. Source code in Quickbasic/Qbasic is included.

name: NOW: A Computer Chess Program
description: NOW is a chess program where you play against the CPU. According to the docs, it was a powerful chess program at the time, able to beat most other non-commercial chess algorithms. There does not seem to be a two-player option, so you must play against the CPU. There are also a lot of variables to set but no difficulty selection. The CPU sometimes takes some time to choose its moves, but you can crank up the CPU cycles in DOSBox if you want it to go faster. (By default it's set to a reasonable speed that it would have run back when it was released.)

name: NRMaze
description: NRMaze is a variant of the classic Windows puzzle game Minesweeper. The twist is that you cannot start the puzzle just anywhere. You start at the top left corner of the board, and must systematically work your way to the other side of the board. This makes the game more challenging. I personally perfer the original, but some may like this variant better.NRMaze is an obscure DOS-based maze and puzzle game from the 1990s. Designed as a simple, yet engaging single-player experience, it challenges players to navigate complex mazes while overcoming obstacles and solving light puzzles. Its clean mechanics and retro style made it a straightforward game for fans of maze challenges during the DOS gaming era. Gameplay Core Objective: Navigate through increasingly difficult mazes, finding the exit while avoiding obstacles and traps. Key Mechanics: Players move a character or cursor through a 2D overhead-view maze. Solve light puzzles, like activating switches or collecting keys to unlock paths. Avoid hazards such as dead-ends, moving traps, or enemies that might restart the maze. Progression: Mazes start small and manageable but gradually grow larger and more complex, introducing new challenges and mechanics. Features Simple Controls: Players typically use the arrow keys for navigation, with optional interactions like pressing switches or collecting items. Minimalist Graphics: Classic retro 2D visuals featuring simple lines and blocky environments common in DOS-era games. Increasing Difficulty: Later levels introduce timed challenges, hidden paths, and other obstacles to keep players on their toes. Sound Effects: Basic PC speaker sounds to signal actions like completing a maze or triggering a trap.

name: Number Fill
description: Drag the numbers to the correct spots.Number Fill is a type of logic-based puzzle game that involves filling a grid with numbers based on specific rules, similar to puzzles like KenKen or Fill-a-Pix. It's a web-based game often implemented in HTML, making it easy to play directly in a browser without the need for downloads. Gameplay Core Objective: The goal of Number Fill is to fill in the grid with numbers so that each row and column meets certain numerical constraints or patterns. Rules: The numbers in each row and column must follow a specific sequence or sum to a certain total. For example, in some variations, each number from 1 to N (where N is the size of the grid) must appear exactly once in each row and column. In other cases, the grid may have sum constraints for each row or column, where the numbers added together must match a given total. Players may need to deduce the correct numbers using logic or trial and error. Features Grid Size: The size of the grid can vary, often ranging from 5x5 to 10x10 or larger grids depending on difficulty. Clues: In more advanced versions, there may be pre-filled numbers or clues that assist the player in solving the puzzle. Difficulty Levels: Many online Number Fill games offer various difficulty levels, from easy grids with fewer constraints to complex ones requiring careful calculation. Interactive Interface: Users can click on cells to fill in numbers and interact with the puzzle directly using a mouse or keyboard.

name: Number Mahjong
description: 100 different layouts in a Number Mahjong Solitaire game. Can you complete all levels?Number Mahjong is a variation of the traditional Mahjong game, but with a numerical twist. In this browser-based game, HTML is used to deliver a fun and relaxing puzzle experience where players match numbered tiles instead of the usual Mahjong symbols. Gameplay Core Objective: The goal of Number Mahjong is to match pairs of tiles that feature the same number. The tiles are arranged on a board in a layered structure, and players must remove tiles in pairs to clear the board. How to Play: Players start with a board filled with tiles that have numbers on them. To remove a tile, you must find another tile with the same number. Tiles can only be selected if they are unblocked. A tile is considered unblocked if it has at least one side (left or right) free and isn't covered by another tile. Continue matching pairs of tiles until the entire board is cleared or until no more valid moves are available. Tile Layout: The tiles are often stacked in a layered arrangement, requiring players to strategically uncover tiles beneath others. Tile Numbers: In some versions of Number Mahjong, the tiles are labeled with numbers that correspond to specific sets or groups, while others may use a randomized set of numbers, with matching pairs scattered across the board. Features Simple Controls: Select and match tiles using the mouse (or touchscreen on mobile devices). Hints: Some versions provide a hint feature that suggests a valid move if players are stuck. Scoring System: The game may include a score based on the time taken or the number of moves made to clear the board. Time Pressure: Some versions feature a timer, adding a challenge to complete the puzzle within a set time limit. Level Progression: As the player progresses, the difficulty may increase, with more complex tile arrangements or added rules. Visual Style The design of Number Mahjong often features a minimalist and clean grid layout with a background that resembles traditional Mahjong boards. The tiles are typically designed with clear numbers, and the overall aesthetic is relaxed and calming. Colorful Tiles: Number Mahjong often includes bright, distinguishable colors for the tiles, making it easy to identify pairs at a glance.

name: Number Maze
description: Connect all numbers in the Maze. Start at 0 go up and use all dots.Number Maze is a logic-based puzzle game often implemented in HTML for browsers. The game presents a grid or maze filled with numbers, where players must navigate through the maze by following a sequence of numbers in a specific order. Gameplay Core Objective: The goal of Number Maze is to move through the maze in a particular sequence, typically starting from 1 and progressing through the grid, following a path dictated by the increasing numbers (e.g., 1 → 2 → 3 → 4 → …). The maze usually has a starting point and an exit, and players must figure out how to travel through the maze in the correct number order. How to Play: Players move through the grid by clicking or dragging to adjacent numbered tiles. The numbers must be followed in the exact sequence—1, 2, 3, etc. If players select the wrong number or move incorrectly, they may have to restart from a checkpoint or the beginning. The maze can contain obstacles, dead-ends, or special features like teleporters, which add complexity. Maze Design: The maze may be a 2D grid or a more intricate design with multiple paths to the exit. Numbered Tiles are scattered throughout the maze, and players must traverse them in order without skipping any numbers. Some versions of Number Maze may include multiple levels, each with increasing complexity and larger grids. Features Simple Controls: Navigate through the maze using either mouse clicks (to select tiles) or keyboard arrow keys (to move between numbers). Timer: Some versions of Number Maze include a timer, challenging players to complete the maze as quickly as possible. Hint System: Some games offer hints to help players find the correct number path if they get stuck. Levels and Progression: As the player progresses, new mazes with different layouts and more complex rules may be unlocked.

name: Number Munchers
description: Number Munchers is an educational DOS game released in 1990 by The Learning Company. It is one of the most well-known titles in the Munchers series, designed to help students practice and reinforce basic mathematical concepts in a fun, interactive way. Gameplay Core Objective: The primary goal of Number Munchers is to help the player (the "Muncher") eat the correct numbers based on mathematical problems. The game features a grid of numbers, and the player must "munch" the correct ones that satisfy a given mathematical rule, such as multiples of a number or numbers within a certain range. How to Play: Muncher: The player controls a little green character known as the Muncher, which moves around the grid. Math Problems: A math problem is displayed at the top of the screen, such as "Eat multiples of 6" or "Eat numbers greater than 20". The player must then guide the Muncher to eat the numbers that meet the criteria. Avoid Enemies: The game features enemies called Grunts, which try to catch the Muncher. If the Muncher touches a Grunt, the player loses a life. Levels and Progression: As the player progresses, the levels increase in difficulty with more complex math problems and faster-moving Grunts. Features Educational Focus: The game helps children practice basic math skills such as addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, and number recognition. Various difficulty levels allow the game to scale for different age groups or skill levels. Multiple Game Modes: Math Facts: Players solve problems based on addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division. Range Game: The Muncher must eat numbers within a specified range. Number Identification: Players identify specific numbers, such as prime numbers, odd/even numbers, or multiples of a given number. Gameplay Style: The game is set in a grid-like environment, with numbers scattered around and the Muncher trying to avoid or outmaneuver Grunts. Power-ups may appear, giving the Muncher temporary advantages (e.g., invincibility or the ability to freeze the Grunts).

name: Number Search
description: Find the numbers as fast as possible. Drag on the grid to locate a number.Number Search is an online puzzle game based on the traditional word search format, but with numbers instead of words. The objective of the game is to find a set of numbers hidden in a grid of random digits. It's a fun and simple game that helps with number recognition, pattern recognition, and mental focus. Gameplay Core Objective: The goal of Number Search is to locate specific numbers or sequences of numbers in a grid filled with randomly placed digits. Players must search the grid and find the numbers or sequences listed as the target. How to Play: Search for Numbers: The game provides a list of target numbers or number sequences (e.g., "17", "253", "19", etc.), which players need to find in the grid. Number Locations: The target numbers may appear horizontally, vertically, or diagonally within the grid. Mark Found Numbers: Players can typically click or tap on the grid to highlight or mark the numbers they've found, or use a drawing tool to circle the numbers. Time or Move Limits: Some versions of the game may include a timer or move limit to add a layer of challenge. Features Difficulty Levels: Many Number Search games offer multiple difficulty levels. Easy levels might feature smaller grids with fewer numbers, while harder levels may include larger grids and longer number sequences to find. Grid Size: The size of the number grid can vary depending on the difficulty level, ranging from 5x5 grids to 15x15 or larger grids. Timed Mode: In some versions, players are given a limited amount of time to find all the numbers in the grid. Others may let players play at their own pace. Hints: Some Number Search games offer a hint system that highlights a number or sequence if the player is stuck, but it may be limited to a few uses.

name: Numbers & Logic I
description: Numbers & Logic is actually a collection of three different number-based logic games. The first is Maze 8, where you need to find the path through the maze which gives you the lowest sum total of the spaces you move through. The second is Find 9, where you have to find squares of 9 numbers which are all unique (contain numbers 1-9). And the third is Dial 10, where you must rotate concentric circles of numbers to have unique numbers (again 1-9) in each quadrant of the circle. Each game plays well enough and contains in-game instructions. It will also show you the solution if you give up which is a nice feature.

name: Numbers in the City
description: Find all the numbers hidden in the City in this HTML5 hidden number game. Try to find all the numbers within the time limit and use the hint button carefullyNumbers in the City is an educational HTML-based puzzle game where players are tasked with solving number-based puzzles in an urban environment, often involving mathematical challenges that can be solved by locating or interacting with numbers scattered throughout the "city." The game typically involves using number sequences, simple arithmetic, or patterns to advance through various levels or areas in a city-like setting. Gameplay Core Objective: The goal of Numbers in the City is to navigate through different city zones, solving number-related puzzles and challenges to progress. Each puzzle might require locating numbers on buildings, solving arithmetic problems, or using numbers in a particular order to unlock areas. How to Play: Players are presented with a city grid or map where numbers are scattered across various buildings, streets, or landmarks. The player must interact with the numbers by solving math problems, identifying sequences, or finding patterns that relate to a specific puzzle in each city zone. Each level might include mathematical operations such as addition, subtraction, multiplication, or division. Some puzzles require simple problem-solving, while others involve more advanced number-based logic. Unlocking Areas: Solving number puzzles or finding the correct sequence of numbers may allow players to access new areas of the city. Features Mathematical Challenges: The game incorporates basic math operations like addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division, with varying difficulty levels based on the player's progress. Puzzles may require identifying number patterns, finding prime numbers, matching numbers to their multiples, or solving simple algebraic problems. City Exploration: The game's urban setting often includes different districts or areas, each with a set of unique number-based puzzles to solve. Players may be able to zoom in and out, explore different zones, or choose their path depending on the puzzles they wish to tackle first. Increasing Difficulty: As players advance, the puzzles become more complex, involving multiple-step math problems or larger number grids. Players may encounter time limits or challenges that require quick thinking and faster responses. Visual Style: The game typically features a colorful and cartoony urban environment with interactive elements like streets, buildings, and landmarks. Numbers are displayed on buildings, in the streets, or in special boxes where players can click or tap to reveal math challenges or complete puzzles.

name: Numjump
description: Numjump is a text-mode ASCII platformer with puzzle elements, where careful planning is key to success. Unlike most platformers that rely on quick reflexes and agility, Numjump challenges players to think strategically about their movements, especially how to navigate tricky jumps and fall safely. It's a short but engaging game that is simple to understand yet requires thoughtful execution. Gameplay Core Objective: In Numjump, the goal is to complete each level by collecting all of the gold scattered around the screen and then reaching the exit. Players must navigate through a series of platforms and obstacles using only ASCII characters in a text-based environment. How to Play: The player controls a character represented by an ASCII symbol (often a single character like an "@" or a similar representation). The character must carefully jump and fall between platforms to collect all the gold. The levels are designed in such a way that jumping and falling aren’t straightforward; players need to plan ahead and take into account the physics of their movements. This means that timing and positioning matter significantly. After collecting all the gold, players must make their way to the exit to complete the level and move on to the next one. Platforming and Puzzle Elements: The jumping and falling mechanics are somewhat abstract and harder to describe, but they involve a careful balance between moving in the right direction and choosing when to jump or fall. The level design requires players to plan their jumps and avoid pitfalls or dangerous obstacles (such as falling too far or missing platforms). Levels get progressively more difficult as players encounter new challenges, such as tighter jumps or more complex platform arrangements. Features Simple ASCII Graphics: The game uses basic ASCII characters to represent both the player and the environment, with platforms and obstacles created using simple text symbols. This gives the game a retro charm and a minimalist, text-based aesthetic. Puzzle Solving: Unlike most platformers that focus on quick reflexes, Numjump emphasizes puzzle-solving. Players must think ahead about the best way to move and jump through the level to avoid falling into traps or missing crucial jumps. Multiple Levels: The game consists of five levels, each with increasing complexity and more challenging platform arrangements. As players progress, the puzzles become more intricate, requiring a deeper understanding of the game's mechanics. Strategy Over Reflexes: Since the game’s mechanics are not based on reflexes but on careful planning, Numjump encourages a slower, more thoughtful approach to each level. Players need to think carefully about how they move around the level and execute each jump.

name: Numlo
description: Numlo is similar to other Soleau games like Tribolo. Very similar in look and feel, and quite close in gameplay. It's a Reversi / Othello type game where the object is to gradually take over the board by turning all the squares into your own color. Here you play against two computer opponents at the same time (no option for human multiplayer) random point values are spread over the board, adding an extra element of strategy. Not bad if you enjoy this type of game and are looking for something with a bit of a twist to the traditional game.

name: Nyet
description: Nyet is a DOS-based game released in the early 1990s. It is a strategy puzzle game that challenges the player's decision-making and logic. The game was created by James Han and released as a shareware title. It gained attention for its simple mechanics, unique gameplay, and its catchy title. Gameplay Core Objective: The primary goal in Nyet is to align symbols or complete certain tasks using a series of moves within a limited number of steps. The game focuses on logical thinking and requires players to plan ahead and consider their moves carefully. How to Play: Players are presented with a grid or board filled with symbols or tiles, and their task is to manipulate or move these pieces to achieve specific objectives. The game features a turn-based system where the player must carefully choose moves to achieve a specific configuration of symbols or numbers. The game often includes multiple puzzles or levels with different goals and configurations that increase in difficulty. Puzzle Mechanics: The puzzles typically involve manipulating a set of tiles or symbols on a grid to achieve a desired arrangement. The player has to think about the rules of how pieces move or interact with each other, often requiring the player to plan several moves in advance to solve the puzzle. There may also be obstacles that prevent the player from making certain moves, adding layers of complexity to each puzzle. Features Puzzle Design: Nyet offers a wide variety of puzzles that involve arranging or manipulating symbols, tiles, or objects according to certain logical rules. The puzzles start simple but become more challenging as the game progresses, with more complicated grid layouts and additional rules to consider. Limited Moves: One of the key challenges in Nyet is that players often have a limited number of moves to solve each puzzle. This forces players to think strategically and carefully plan their actions. Simple Interface: The game uses a text-based interface with ASCII-style graphics. The player interacts with the game by using the keyboard to move tiles, select options, or trigger actions. Puzzle Variety: The game features a variety of puzzles that test different aspects of logic and strategy. Some levels might involve matching numbers, rotating tiles, or other similar mechanics.

name: Nyet 3: The Revenge of the Mutant Stones
description: NYet 3 (which may or may not be related to NYet) is a Tetris clone that goes way beyond the standard Tetris formula by adding a huge variety of different level variations. You earn money for clearing the levels, which you can use to buy powerups or the ability to save your game. This is a game for hardcore Tetris players and/or people who want a very challenging game, as the Ross' Game Dungeon NYet 3 video shows quite nicely.
