Definitely and innovative and challenging game, but also not one that many people would have the patience to get through!

name: Obama vs. Santa
description: This is the epic showdown between Obama and Santa!

name: Obliterator
description: Obliterator is a technically impressive game which serves more as a tech demo than it does an entertaining gaming experience. The goal is to fly your ship around and destroy other ships, while avoiding crashing into them or other obstacles like planets. Since the other ships fly around quickly and there is no radar or way to track them once they're off-screen, destroying them can be difficult, especially with the propulsion-based movement (similar to Asteroids) of your own vessel. The game ends when you run out of energy, and the goal is simply to collect as many points as possible. There is .MOD based music which is of the early 90's techno style, and likely copied from other sources. Overall it's decent looking but a little difficult to play.

name: Ocean Bubbles
description: Classic Bubble Shooter game in HTML5. Shoot bubbles up and create groups of 3 or more of the same bubbles to remove them.Ocean Bubbles is a fun and relaxing HTML-based puzzle game that combines simple gameplay mechanics with a calming underwater theme. The game typically involves clearing bubbles or matching colors in a way that resembles other popular bubble-popping games like Bubble Shooter. In Ocean Bubbles, players need to pop bubbles in specific patterns to complete levels or achieve objectives, all while enjoying a tranquil, ocean-themed setting. Gameplay Core Objective: The primary goal of Ocean Bubbles is to pop groups of bubbles by matching three or more of the same color. Players shoot or launch bubbles into a grid of floating bubbles, and when the launched bubble connects with other bubbles of the same color, they pop. How to Play: Players control a bubble launcher, which is typically positioned at the bottom or side of the screen. A bubble will appear at the launcher, and the player aims it using their mouse or by tapping on the screen (on mobile versions). When a bubble is shot, it will travel towards the group of floating bubbles, trying to match colors with other bubbles. When three or more bubbles of the same color come into contact, they pop and disappear from the screen, earning points for the player. Levels and Objectives: The game is often divided into different levels, with each level requiring the player to clear all bubbles from the screen or meet specific goals, such as reaching a target score or clearing a certain number of bubbles in a set time limit. Features Simple and Addictive Mechanics: The core mechanics of Ocean Bubbles are easy to understand but can become increasingly challenging as the levels progress. The player is tasked with clearing bubbles, but over time, the number of bubbles or the speed at which they appear can increase, making it harder to match and pop bubbles efficiently. Colorful and Relaxing Theme: The game features a soothing ocean environment, with the bubbles and background often designed in bright, pastel colors to create a pleasant atmosphere. The soundtrack is typically calm and relaxing, complementing the peaceful underwater setting and making it a great game to unwind. Multiple Levels: Ocean Bubbles often includes multiple levels, each with varying difficulty. In the early levels, players might have fewer bubbles to manage and slower-moving targets, while later levels introduce more bubbles, faster speeds, and additional obstacles. Power-ups and Boosters: Some versions of the game may offer power-ups or boosters that help clear bubbles faster, such as bombs that destroy large groups of bubbles or color changers that turn a bubble into a different color. Time-based or Goal-oriented Challenges: Depending on the version of Ocean Bubbles, there may be time-limited challenges or goals to reach, such as clearing all bubbles within a certain amount of time or achieving a set number of points.

name: Ocean Puzzle
description: Push ocean blocks inside and match 3 or more of the same to the delete the blocks and try to delete all ocean blocks.Ocean Puzzle is a relaxing HTML-based puzzle game that features an oceanic theme, where players solve various types of puzzles related to ocean elements like marine life, underwater scenery, and aquatic creatures. The game is designed to be both fun and educational, offering players a chance to explore the beauty of the ocean while solving engaging puzzles. Gameplay Core Objective: The primary goal of Ocean Puzzle is to complete different puzzle types that revolve around the ocean theme. This could involve solving jigsaw puzzles, matching game mechanics, or arranging pieces to form pictures of marine life, such as fish, coral reefs, or underwater landscapes. How to Play: Jigsaw Puzzle: The game may feature a classic jigsaw puzzle format, where the player is given a picture (often an underwater scene or a marine creature), and the puzzle pieces need to be dragged and dropped into place to complete the image. Matching or Pattern Puzzles: Some versions may involve matching similar objects or colors, like matching pairs of fish or underwater items, where the goal is to find and match the correct items to complete the puzzle. Objective-based Challenges: In some levels, players may have specific objectives to reach, such as solving the puzzle within a set time or with a limited number of moves. Level Progression: Ocean Puzzle could consist of multiple levels, each featuring different puzzles with varying difficulty. As players complete puzzles, they may unlock new, more challenging puzzles or new ocean-themed images and scenes. Features Oceanic Theme: The game has a relaxing underwater theme, with puzzles featuring beautiful ocean scenes, including coral reefs, marine life, whales, sea turtles, and fish. The calm setting makes the game ideal for players seeking a stress-free experience. Multiple Puzzle Types: Depending on the version of Ocean Puzzle, there may be different types of puzzles, such as: Jigsaw Puzzles: Players put together pieces to form an image. Memory Match: Players flip cards and match identical ocean-themed images. Sliding Puzzles: The player arranges tiles to create a full image, often by sliding tiles around a grid. Simple Controls: The gameplay mechanics are straightforward, often relying on dragging and dropping pieces or clicking and tapping to select tiles or match items. This makes it easy to pick up and play. Relaxing Soundtrack: The game often features a calming soundtrack, with soothing ocean sounds or ambient music, enhancing the immersive underwater atmosphere. The sounds of waves, seagulls, or whale calls can provide a relaxing backdrop to the puzzle-solving experience. Colorful Visuals: The puzzles themselves are designed with vibrant, beautiful ocean-themed images. The bright and colorful graphics help create an enjoyable and visually appealing experience for players of all ages. Difficulty Levels: The game might offer multiple difficulty settings, with easier puzzles featuring larger pieces or fewer items to match, while harder puzzles could include smaller pieces, intricate images, or more complex patterns to complete.

name: Office Hidden Objects
description: Find all the objects hidden in the Office. Click on an object when you find it.Office Hidden Objects is a fun and engaging HTML-based puzzle game that challenges players to find hidden objects within a cluttered office setting. The game combines hidden object gameplay with a workplace theme, offering a delightful experience for players who enjoy searching for items in detailed scenes. Gameplay Core Objective: The main goal of Office Hidden Objects is to find and click on a list of hidden objects that are cleverly concealed within a detailed office scene. Players are given a list of items to find, and they must search the screen to locate each item as quickly as possible. How to Play: Players are presented with a cluttered office environment, such as a desk, shelves, cabinets, or meeting rooms. A list of hidden objects appears on the side or top of the screen, which players need to find within the office scene. The items are hidden in plain sight, but they may be disguised among other objects or tucked away in corners, drawers, or behind objects. Players click on the objects once they’ve found them. If they click on the correct item, it disappears from the scene and is marked as found. Time Limit or No Time Limit: In some versions, players may be given a time limit to find all the objects, while in others, they can take their time. The difficulty may increase as the level progresses, with more objects to find or more complex scenes. Features Hidden Object Gameplay: The core mechanic revolves around the hidden object puzzle format, which is both challenging and enjoyable. Players must carefully observe the scene to find items that are not immediately obvious. Office Theme: The game takes place in a detailed office setting, which could include desks filled with papers, office supplies, computers, and various other work-related objects. This theme adds a fun, everyday twist to the hidden objects genre. Multiple Levels: The game may feature multiple levels, each with more complex office scenes to search through. As players progress, they may encounter new environments like meeting rooms, conference tables, or break rooms, each offering fresh challenges. Hints: If players are struggling to find an object, there may be a hint button they can use to reveal the location of one object temporarily. However, hints might be limited or come with a cooldown period, adding to the challenge. High Score or Rating: Some versions of Office Hidden Objects may include a scoring system based on how quickly players can find the objects, how many hints they used, and whether they completed the level within a set time.

name: Offroad
description: Offroad is a Moon Patrol take-off which features smooth-scrolling CGA graphics, decent for a game made in 1988. The object is to drive forward while shooting or avoiding the obstacles. You do this by pressing right and then hammering on the shoot button. This game was the precursor to the much more widely known Jumpjet which was made by the same company a few years after Offroad.Offroad is a DOS-based racing game from the early 1990s that offers players the chance to experience off-road racing in various rugged terrains. Unlike typical racing games that take place on smooth tracks, Offroad features challenging landscapes with obstacles like rocks, mud, and other natural elements that affect driving. Gameplay Core Objective: The goal in Offroad is to race through challenging tracks in an off-road vehicle, typically a 4x4 truck or similar off-road vehicle, to reach the finish line before other competitors. The game emphasizes driving over rough terrain, where players must navigate obstacles like hills, rocks, mud, and even water, testing their driving skills and control. How to Play: Players control a vehicle through off-road tracks filled with obstacles and uneven terrain. The game is typically a time-based racing experience where players must complete each track as quickly as possible while avoiding crashing or getting stuck in difficult sections of the terrain. Along the way, players can collect power-ups, such as speed boosts or other enhancements, to help them navigate more effectively. The game may feature multiple levels with increasing difficulty, where the tracks become more challenging with steeper hills, tighter turns, and more obstacles. Players can often race against AI opponents or play in a two-player mode where they compete against each other to reach the finish line first. Features Off-Road Terrain: The game is designed to focus on the challenges of driving on rugged, uneven terrain. Tracks may include muddy trails, dirt roads, rocky paths, hills, valleys, and even rivers, making it different from traditional racing games with smooth, paved tracks. Vehicle Handling: The vehicles in Offroad are designed to simulate off-road handling. Players need to manage acceleration, braking, and turning to maintain control of their vehicle while navigating the tough terrain. This adds a layer of skill and realism to the gameplay. Multiple Tracks: The game often features several tracks or environments, each with different terrain features. As players progress through the game, the tracks typically become more difficult, requiring better control and faster reflexes. Multiplayer Mode: Some versions of Offroad feature a multiplayer mode that allows two players to race against each other. This adds a competitive edge to the game, as players try to outmaneuver each other while facing the challenges of the off-road environment.

name: Oh No! More Lemmings
description: Oh No! More Lemmings gives you exactly what you'd expect from a sequel to the original classic Lemmings game: More! More of the same basically, the same engine and lemming abilities with 100 new levels. The quality of the levels is, according to a review I read, a bit dubious compared to the original game. However if you have already played the original and are looking for some additional levels, this is a decent source. The demo only provides a few of the many levels available in the full game.Oh No! More Lemmings is a DOS-based puzzle game and the sequel to the highly popular game Lemmings. Released in 1991 by Psygnosis, it continues the franchise's unique formula of guiding the titular lemmings, small, hapless creatures, through increasingly difficult obstacle-filled levels. As with the original game, the goal is to help the lemmings safely navigate each stage to reach an exit without them falling to their doom. Gameplay Core Objective: The primary goal of Oh No! More Lemmings is to lead a group of lemmings through each level, using their various skills to avoid traps, hazards, and obstacles. Players must use the right combination of skills to ensure the lemmings reach the exit before time runs out or too many lemmings are lost. How to Play: Skills and Abilities: The game features a range of skills that can be assigned to individual lemmings to help them overcome obstacles. These skills include: Climbing: Lemmings can climb walls to reach higher ground. Digging: Lemmings can dig through soft ground to create paths or avoid obstacles. Blocking: Some lemmings can block others from walking into dangerous areas. Bridging: Lemmings can create bridges over gaps or rivers. Bashing: Lemmings can bash through walls or barriers. Parachuting: Lemmings can safely descend from great heights by deploying parachutes. Exploding: Some lemmings can blow themselves up to clear paths or remove obstacles. Assigning Skills: Players have control over the skills that each lemming can use. The challenge is to assign the appropriate skills to the right lemmings in the right order to safely guide the group to the exit. Limited Time and Lemmings: Each level has a time limit and a limited number of lemmings. If too many lemmings are lost (falling into traps, walking into walls, or falling off ledges), the level is failed. Levels and Progression: The game features over 100 levels across various difficulty stages. The levels become progressively more challenging, with more obstacles and requiring more strategic use of the available skills. Features New and Improved Features: While retaining the original game's core mechanics, Oh No! More Lemmings introduced several new features: More lemming skills, allowing for a greater range of creative solutions to each level. The ability to assign multiple skills to a single lemming, allowing for more complex strategies. Tougher puzzles that require careful planning and management of the lemmings. Puzzle Solving: As with the original, Oh No! More Lemmings is primarily a puzzle game that requires players to think ahead and use their limited resources effectively. Each level is essentially a logic puzzle that demands thoughtful decision-making. Animated and Fun Design: The lemmings are cute and humorous, with their quirky movements and amusing reactions when they succeed or fail. This adds a layer of charm and fun to the challenging puzzles. Level Editor: The game also includes a level editor, allowing players to create their own levels and share them with others. This feature greatly expanded the game's replayability and community involvement.

name: Oilcap
description: Oilcap is perhaps the least innovative of Soleau Software's many Pipedream / Oilswell clones, but perhaps because of its simplicity (and closeness to its source material) it turned out to be perhaps the most popular. Oilcap plays like the aforementioned games: Place tiles to create a path for the oil to flow. Keep it going longer for more points; if you score enough points (and don't waste too many pieces) you'll progress to the next level. It's not easy but it flows well. It would be nice to drag an outline of the piece you're placing, since it disappears after you click it.

name: Oleg Sobolev's ASCII DOOM
description: Oleg Sobolev's ASCII DOOM was apparently made by someone named Oleg Sobolev, although his name does not appear anywhere in the game or in any included files. This is, as you might expect, a 3D shooter-ish game made using text-mode ASCII characters.Oleg Sobolev's ASCII DOOM (often referred to as ASCII DOOMdos) is a fan-made ASCII art-based reimagining of the iconic first-person shooter DOOM. This version, created by Oleg Sobolev, takes the fast-paced action and level design of the original DOOM and translates it into a text-based, ASCII art format suitable for playing on DOS systems. While the original DOOM was groundbreaking in its graphical fidelity and gameplay, ASCII DOOM offers a minimalist approach, utilizing only characters and symbols to represent the game's environments, enemies, and actions. Gameplay Core Objective: In ASCII DOOM, players still take on the role of the Doom Slayer, fighting through various levels filled with monsters and traps to ultimately defeat the forces of hell. The goal is to navigate through mazes of corridors, rooms, and enemies to reach the exit of each level while surviving the onslaught of enemies. ASCII Representation: Instead of 3D models and detailed textures, ASCII DOOM uses ASCII characters (letters, numbers, symbols) to represent every element of the game: Enemies: Various monsters, demons, and bosses from the original game are represented by letters or characters. For example, imps could be represented by the letter "I", zombiemen as "Z", and cacodemons as "@", etc. Weapons and Items: The player's arsenal, health packs, and other items are represented by symbols or short letters (e.g., "P" for a pistol, "S" for shotgun). Environment: The game’s environment, including walls, doors, and obstacles, are depicted using a combination of symbols such as "#", ".", or "*". Combat: Combat in ASCII DOOM remains relatively similar to the original. Players engage in turn-based combat, where each move can either result in a successful shot, dodging an enemy attack, or taking damage. The game focuses on strategic positioning as players must avoid enemies while shooting, utilizing their weapons and health items strategically. Movement and Exploration: Players move through the game's 2D ASCII maps, which are representations of the original DOOM levels but entirely in text form. The player moves through corridors, explores rooms, and interacts with objects like switches, doors, and terminals. Each move is depicted as a change in the layout of the ASCII grid, and players can move and interact using the keyboard. Levels and Difficulty: The game follows the structure of the original DOOM, with different levels of increasing difficulty. As players advance through the levels, the maps grow larger and more complex, and the enemies become tougher and more numerous.

name: Olko
description: Remove all tiles from the game. You can only reach the tiles via the sides.Objective: The goal of Olko is to remove all tiles from the game board. You can only remove tiles that are reachable via the edges of the grid. Tiles that are surrounded on all sides by other tiles cannot be removed, which adds a strategic challenge. Gameplay: The game grid consists of tiles arranged in rows and columns. Tiles can be removed if they are not surrounded by other tiles on all four sides. The player can only interact with tiles that are connected to the edge of the grid. The challenge comes from carefully planning which tiles to remove and when to ensure that all tiles can eventually be removed. Rules: You can only remove tiles that are connected to the edges of the grid (left, right, top, bottom). As you remove tiles, the board gradually empties. The goal is to remove all the tiles, leaving an empty board. Game Over: If no more tiles can be removed, or if all tiles are removed successfully, the game ends.

name: Olko 2
description: Remove all tiles from the game. You can only reach the tiles via the sides.Objective: Remove all tiles from the grid. Gameplay Rule: You can only remove tiles that are connected to the sides (top, bottom, left, or right) of the grid. Goal: Clear all the tiles, respecting the rule that you can only remove tiles connected to the edges.The objective is to remove all tiles from the board. You can click on any tile, but only tiles connected to the edges or already removed tiles can be removed. Once all tiles are removed, a "You Win!" message will appear.

name: Olympic Volleyball
description: "Olympic Volleyball" is an exciting flash game that brings the fast-paced action of beach volleyball right to your screen. Players can take part in thrilling matches, either solo against AI opponents or in multiplayer mode with friends. The game features vibrant graphics and dynamic animations, capturing the atmosphere of a sunny beach setting. Players control their characters to serve, spike, and set, aiming to score points by outmaneuvering their opponents and landing the ball in the designated court area. With intuitive controls, players can easily execute various techniques, from powerful serves to tricky shots. The game includes multiple difficulty levels, allowing beginners to learn the basics while providing a challenge for more experienced players. With energetic sound effects and an engaging soundtrack, "Olympic Volleyball" delivers a fun and competitive experience, perfect for fans of sports games looking for some fast-paced action!

name: Omega
description: Omega is a text-mode roguelike game that was unique and innovative in several ways, however its most-remembered trait is generally not considered to be a positive. The game's positive elements include huge towns (which span larger than a single screen), wildernesses, multiple quests, and several different "win" conditions. The biggest negative is the inventory system, which is somewhat more realistic but also generally considered overcomplicated and unnecessary, having to perform several commands just to pick up and store an item. Nevertheless this is a complex and unique roguelike game that those who are willing to put up with the inventory system will want to check out.

name: One Arm Bandit
description: One Arm Bandit is a very simple slot machine simulation game, with an inordinate amount of documentation included. The game runs in text-mode (VGA mode, for the actual slot machine) and all you do is press A, B, C, or D to bet $1, $2, $3, or $4 respectively. (Why not just press 1, 2, 3, or 4?) Clearly a lot of work went into making this, but the game itself with its single-line slot mechanic is not engaging to play for more than a moment or two.One Arm Bandit is a classic arcade-style game released for DOS. It's a type of slot machine game where the player pulls a lever (or clicks a button) to spin the reels and tries to line up matching symbols to win virtual currency or points.

name: One Cell
description: Freecell game with only one Free cell. Try to move all cards to the foundations. On the tableau build down on alternating color.One Cell is likely referring to a puzzle game where the goal is to manipulate or fill a single cell within a grid, often with a set of rules or challenges to solve. Since there is no widely known or established game with this exact title, I will interpret One Cell as a simple logic puzzle where you must manipulate or fill a grid's single cell to satisfy certain conditions.In this version of the One Cell game, you need to fill a single cell in a grid (let’s assume a 3x3 grid for simplicity) that satisfies a rule, such as the sum of the numbers in the row or column.

name: One Chance
description: One Chance is an emotional, narrative-driven Flash game developed by Simon Meek, and it gained popularity for its unique premise and storytelling approach. The game revolves around choice and consequence, and it challenges players with tough decisions that impact the fate of the world, offering no second chances. Gameplay Mechanics: Narrative and Choices: The primary focus of One Chance is on the narrative and the choices the player makes. The game is story-driven, with various dialogues and scenarios that present the player with hard decisions. Players must make choices that affect both their personal relationships and the fate of the world. The game is divided into a series of days, each representing the passage of time as the world descends into chaos. Each day presents new events, and players must make decisions that can lead to different outcomes. The narrative explores themes of guilt, regret, and redemption as the protagonist is confronted with the consequences of his actions. The game doesn't allow the player to change their decisions or go back, so each choice is impactful and irreversible. Limited Time: The game takes place over six in-game days, and each day represents a limited period during which you must make decisions. As the days progress, the consequences of the player's choices become more evident, and the world moves closer to its inevitable downfall. Players are essentially playing out the last days of humanity, and there is a constant sense of urgency as you navigate the emotional and ethical choices the character faces. Character Relationships: One of the major components of the game is the personal relationships the scientist has with other characters, including his family, colleagues, and friends. Your interactions with these characters affect how the story progresses and influence the emotional impact of the game. For example, you might be asked to decide whether to spend time with your wife and child, work in the lab, or try to find a solution to the problem. Each of these decisions changes the course of the game. Moral Dilemmas: The game is full of tough, emotional dilemmas. For example, you’ll need to decide whether to try and save the world, or accept that there’s no way out and focus on your loved ones. There are no "right" answers—only personal choices that impact the story and the ending. The game gives you a sense of weight with each decision, as it forces you to think about the consequences of your actions, without the ability to undo them. Endings: One Chance has multiple endings based on the player’s decisions throughout the game. Since you only get one chance to play, your first run is your definitive experience. The choices you make during the game determine which of these endings you’ll experience. The endings are poignant and deeply emotional, leaving players to reflect on the moral complexity of their decisions. The game can end in multiple ways, including: Saving humanity at the cost of personal loss. Sacrificing the protagonist’s family to save the world. Or, in some cases, the world may simply descend into irreversible chaos without any solution, emphasizing the theme of "no second chances."

name: One Line
description: Fill all cells with just one line. Move the snake to fill all cells.One Line is typically a logic puzzle game where you need to draw a continuous line connecting all the dots on a grid without lifting your pen or revisiting any dot. It is usually a puzzle that challenges your ability to plan a path and think spatially. Grid Layout: The game consists of a 300x300 container with 4 dots placed in a 2x2 pattern. Connecting the Dots: The player clicks on the dots in sequence, and the goal is to connect all the dots using a continuous line. As the player clicks on a dot, it is added to the path, and a line is drawn connecting all the dots in the order they are clicked. Winning Condition: The game checks if all 4 dots have been connected. If so, a message appears stating that the player has completed the puzzle. Canvas for Drawing: A canvas element is used to draw the line connecting the dots. Each time the player clicks on a dot, the line is updated to include that dot in the path. The line is drawn using the moveTo and lineTo methods in the canvas' 2D context. Event Handling: The game listens for click events on the canvas. When the player clicks on a dot, the game checks if that dot is part of the puzzle and if it’s not already included in the path. Then, it updates the line drawn on the canvas.

name: One Must Fall 2097
description: One Must Fall 2097 is a futuristic one-on-one fighting game in the style of other popular fighting games of the time such as Street Fighter II, Mortal Kombat, and numerous others. Upon release, the game was praised for its graphics, smooth gameplay mechanics, and innovative features. Based on the game developer's initial demo, this game takes place far in the future, with mech-like robots fighting each other. There are several game modes: One player vs computer, two player competitive combat, or tournament mode. The last mode is the most innovative: You start by creating your own character to pilot your robot, then gain experience and new powers as you defeat other robots. Sort of like some minor RPG mechanics.

name: Ono
description: Ono is a competent version of the popular Uno card game which is itself derived from Crazy Eights. The rule-set is similar: Match the color and/or number of the top card in the pile, use a wild card, or draw one more. The first to empty their hand wins. The game uses mouse control which is appreciated, and features simple but bright graphics. You can play against 1-3 CPU controlled opponents who seem to behave reasonably. For a Uno-like game in DOS, it's pretty good.Ono is a classic DOS game that is part of the "falling blocks" puzzle genre, much like Tetris. The goal in Ono is to arrange falling blocks in such a way that they form complete lines, which are then cleared from the screen. It uses a similar concept to Tetris but with its own unique set of rules and features.

name: Oo-Topos
description: The oddly named Oo-Topos is a sci-fi themed graphical adventure game where you type in simple commands, collect items, and try to figure out what the game expects you to do. It uses the same engine as other Polarware games like Transylvania and The Crimson Crown and likewise features CGA graphics. In the game your space cargo ship has crash-landed on Oo-Topos and you've been taken prisoner. You must escape! LOOK carefully and GET ready to play this fairly typical but professionally done adventure game.

name: Operation Body Count
description: Operation Body Count is a 3D shooting game built using a modified version of the Wolfenstein 3D engine. Unfortunately, the game does not offer much in the way of improvements over the basic Wolf3D formula, while at the same time lacking that certain ineffable quality that made Wolf3D so engaging. It features average graphics and sounds, and may be worth playing if you are a fan of 3D games from this era, otherwise you may want to take another spin through Wolf3D instead.Operation Body Count is a first-person shooter game released in 1994 for MS-DOS. The game was developed by The Software Refinery and published by IntraCorp. It is set in a fictional urban environment, and players take on the role of a soldier tasked with clearing out enemy forces in various environments.In Operation Body Count, players are placed in a first-person perspective and must fight their way through enemies using various weapons. The game focuses on shooting and combat in urban environments, and it features several different missions and levels. Combat: Players are equipped with a variety of weapons, including guns, grenades, and knives. The gameplay emphasizes shooting and strategy, as players must navigate different levels while dealing with enemy forces. Levels and Missions: The game features multiple levels, each set in different environments such as city streets, buildings, or military compounds. The player’s mission is to clear these areas of enemy combatants, which can be humanoid enemies or enemy soldiers. Health and Ammo: Players need to manage their health and ammunition throughout the game. Health can be replenished by finding medical supplies, while ammunition is limited, so players need to make careful decisions about when and how to use their weapons. Enemies: Various types of enemies appear throughout the game, from foot soldiers to more heavily armed enemies. Players need to defeat these enemies to progress through the levels. Graphics: Operation Body Count features 2D graphics with 3D effects, similar to other shooters from the early '90s. The environments are relatively simple, but the game was notable for its use of perspective and the way it presented the first-person view. Controls: The game uses the standard keyboard controls typical for DOS-based FPS games at the time. Players move using the keyboard, aim and shoot with the mouse, and use various keys for weapons or actions. Sound: The game includes basic sound effects for shooting, enemy interactions, and environmental sounds. The music and sound effects help set the tone of the game, adding to the overall atmosphere.

name: Operation Carnage
description: Operation Carnage (originally a shareware title but now released by its developer for free) is a Smash TV inspired arena shooting game, where you progress through different single-screen sized areas and blast everything that you see. You can collect powerups to provide special abilities or enhance your weaponry. You can hold multiple guns and switch between them. The visuals and sounds are quite good and the game plays well; the fact that this is the full, complete version of the game is a fantastic bonus.

name: Operation Just Because
description: Operation Just Because is a strangely named Battleship clone. Just like the board game, you place your ships and then take turns firing at your opponent's grid. The game is presented well here, with nicely drawn graphics. The shareware edition is one player vs CPU only, you would've needed to register to play 2-player mode.Operation Just Because is a DOS-based action-adventure game released in 1995. It was developed by Leaping Lizard Interactive and distributed by GT Interactive. The game is known for its mix of action, humor, and strategy, and is considered a cult classic from the mid-90s. The title also features a lighthearted, humorous approach to military and tactical gameplay.

name: Operation Spacehog
description: Operation Spacehog is an enjoyable, well-designed and playable SHMUP. The game scrolls horizontally from left to right, and the gameplay is similar to Gradius in how you collect powerups to earn different abilities, and you can choose to use your powerup right away, or wait to collect more to fill your bar and choose a different ability. Unlike most space shooting games there is actually a story here, told both before the game and during cutscenes in-between the levels. You can even choose different ships to fly with slightly different attributes. It also features two player simultaneous play! The main problem with the game is that there seems to be a lot of the same stuff in the levels, but maybe I just didn't make it far enough.

name: Operation Vulture 3: Cyber Chopper
description: Cyber Chopper (full name "Operation Vulture 3: Cyber Chopper, The Return of Vulture") is a horizontally scrolling shooting game where you control a helicopter and must destroy various targets on each level. The game's graphics and sounds are impressive, with parallax scrolling and digitized music. The actual gameplay is decent enough, and the way that everything EXPLODES when you shoot it is fun for a while. It also includes a two-player mode, with your choice of cooperative or competitive play! (Although either way your bullets still damage each-other so ... yeah, both will probably end up being VS-mode ...)

name: Operation Vulture IV: Escape from Station 7
description: Escape from Station 7 (full name "Operation Vulture IV: Escape from Station 7") is a horizontally scrolling shooting game where you control a helicopter and must destroy various targets on each level. The game's graphics and sounds are impressive, with parallax scrolling and digitized music. The actual gameplay is decent enough, and the way that everything EXPLODES when you shoot it is fun for a while. It also includes a two-player mode, with your choice of cooperative or competitive play! (Although either way your bullets still damage each-other so ... yeah, both will probably end up being VS-mode ...) This is the sequel to part 3 of the series. (Apparently games 1 & 2 weren't great so the developers never released them.) The full registered version of this game was released for free by its authors.

name: Opposites Attract
description: In this game you do not need to combine two of the same tiles, but two tiles with an opposite meaning. You can only use the free highlighted tiles.Opposites Attract is a HTML-based puzzle game where players need to match opposites in a fun and engaging way. This game challenges the player to match items that are opposites of each other, helping to improve quick thinking and knowledge about various opposites.Matching Opposites: Players are presented with a set of words or concepts, and the objective is to pair up the opposites. For example, a word like "day" might need to be paired with "night," or "light" with "dark." Timed Gameplay: In some versions of the game, players are given a limited amount of time to match as many opposites as possible, adding a sense of urgency and challenge to the game. Other versions may allow players to play at their own pace. Drag and Drop Mechanic: In the HTML version, the gameplay may involve dragging words from one side of the screen and dropping them on their opposite counterparts on the other side. The game may include various levels, where more challenging pairs are introduced as the player progresses. Levels of Difficulty: The game may start with easy pairs and gradually introduce harder ones. Players might also face different types of puzzles (such as matching words with pictures) as the game progresses. Educational Value: This game is educational, helping players, especially younger ones, to learn and remember common opposites, which are essential concepts in vocabulary building. Visuals and Sound: The game typically features simple, colorful visuals to represent the words and concepts. It is often designed with a playful and engaging style to keep players entertained. The game might also include sounds or background music, adding to the overall experience. Features: Educational Focus: Aimed at helping players learn common opposites. Interactive Gameplay: Often uses drag-and-drop mechanics or simple clicks to match opposites. Progressive Difficulty: Levels or stages of increasing difficulty to challenge players as they improve their knowledge. Fun and Engaging: The game is designed to be light-hearted and fun, encouraging players to improve their vocabulary skills through gameplay.

name: Orb Wars
description: Orb Wars is a two-player deathmatch game where you fly around your "orbs" and blast each-other until one of you dies. Apparently this genre of game is referred to as a "caveflyer", a term I learned just now. Anyways this game doesn't present as many options as other games in the genre. You have two attacks, and there are several level layouts to choose from. Some levels have the object of reaching the end first, so they're more of a race. But most are purely deathmatch between two players. There is a CPU opponent option hidden at the bottom right corner of the options screen, but the computer is not exactly a fair opponent, destroying you almost immediately, so you'll need two players to enjoy this game!

name: Orbots
description: Orbots is an obscure horizontally scrolling shoot-em-up. It boasts decent graphics and sound effects. The story is summarized in the FILE_ID.DIZ as follows: "Pilot the astro-chopper to defeat an invasion of half machine, half organo mutants from another dimension." Sounds good! The gameplay feels a bit unrefined, and the bullets from the enemy ships are difficult to avoid due to the touchy controls and the constant stream of shots that they fire. It does support mouse or joystick so maybe those work better; I didn't try them. There are multiple kinds of enemies to fight, as well as powerups to collect. Not sure how many levels are included but it seems like there is a decent amount of game here to play.

name: Orca Slap
description: Orca Slap is a Flash-based arcade-style game that became popular for its fun, quirky mechanics and simple, addictive gameplay. In the game, players control an orca whale and must launch it out of the water to smack objects or enemies, gaining points as they go.Controlling the Orca: Players control the orca by clicking or pressing a key at the right moment to launch it out of the water. The orca then flies into the air and attempts to slap or hit various targets. Power-ups and Points: Players can earn points by successfully slapping targets, which could range from objects to enemies. The game often includes power-ups, such as speed boosts or larger slaps, which help the player score more points. Levels and Obstacles: As the player progresses, the game may introduce obstacles or increasingly difficult targets. Some enemies may try to dodge or counter the player's slaps, increasing the challenge. Improving Performance: Players can improve their performance by getting better at timing the orca's slaps and figuring out which targets give the most points. This can require quick reflexes and strategy. Humor and Cartoony Style: The game’s humor, whimsical characters, and exaggerated actions are one of its key features. The visual style is typically cartoonish, with exaggerated movements and effects when the orca hits or slaps objects. Visuals and Sound: Graphics: The game uses simple but fun 2D graphics with vibrant colors and exaggerated animations. The orca and targets are usually drawn in a cartoony, playful style that adds to the light-hearted nature of the game. Sound: The sound effects are playful and humorous, often including splashing sounds when the orca enters the water or slaps objects. Background music typically matches the game's fun tone. Reception: Orca Slap was a casual, fun game that appealed to players who were looking for something lighthearted and easy to play. It’s not a game that requires much strategy but instead focuses on fun, fast-paced action. The game's silly concept and addictive gameplay made it popular among players looking for a quick, entertaining diversion.

name: Original Mahjongg
description: The original Mahjong Solitaire game. Combine two of the same free tiles and try to remove all tiles.Original Mahjongg is an HTML-based version of the classic Mahjong game, a popular tile-matching puzzle game. It’s based on the traditional Chinese game of Mahjong, where players match pairs of tiles to remove them from the board, ultimately trying to clear all the tiles.Tile Matching: The game consists of a board filled with various tiles, typically in a stacked layout. Each tile has a symbol or character on it, and the player’s goal is to find pairs of tiles with the same symbol. Tiles must be "free," meaning they are not covered by other tiles and have at least one side exposed. Gameplay Rules: You can only select two tiles that are of the same type (symbol) to remove from the board. These tiles must be adjacent either vertically or horizontally, with no other tiles obstructing them. The game typically has a time limit or a number of moves to remove all the tiles. Tile Sets: There are various tile sets with different symbols (such as flowers, seasons, and various animals). Some versions of the game also allow customization of the tile designs. Levels: The game can have multiple difficulty levels, which often involve more complex layouts or more tiles on the board. As you progress through levels, the number of tiles increases, or more complex patterns are introduced, making it more challenging to find matching pairs. Hints and Shuffling: Many versions of Original Mahjongg allow for hints, showing tiles that can be matched. If there are no more moves available or the game gets too difficult, players might be given the option to shuffle the tiles, giving them a new arrangement. Visuals and Sound: Graphics: The game features a grid layout with tiles arranged in a pyramid-like or stacked formation. The tiles are often decorated with traditional Chinese symbols, making the game visually distinct and culturally rich. Sound: The game may feature calming background music or sound effects to enhance the atmosphere, such as the sound of tiles being matched or shuffled. Game Progression: The game progresses by removing matching pairs of tiles, clearing the board. Once all tiles are removed, players win the round and can proceed to the next level, which will typically present a new, more complex layout. Some versions of the game include different types of challenges, such as a time limit or a limited number of moves to complete each level.

name: Orion Odyssey and the Search for the Magic Ankh
description: Orion Odyssey is a platforming game which seems to be heavily influenced by Captain Comic which was released only a few years earlier. The goal and story of the game (if any) are not immediately apparent, but it seems like you'll need to wander around and explore the alien world in order to eventually make it to a goal of some sort. The graphics and sounds are on par with Captain Comic but the controls could use some work.Orion Odyssey and the Search for the Magic Ankh is a DOS-based adventure game that was released in the early 1990s. It is an educational and puzzle-solving game set in an ancient Egyptian-inspired world, where players explore different environments to uncover mysteries, solve puzzles, and ultimately search for a magical artifact known as the Magic Ankh.

name: OSBIT
description: OSBIT is a platforming game, but only in a loose sense that would've been applicable back in 1988. Your goal is to progress through the levels, collecting disks and avoiding the baddies. You have very limited time, which is constantly ticking down. You also move in starts and stops, not by holding down the buttons, and have to expertly time tricky jumps in order to proceed. It's very difficult and seems nearly impossible! Granted, the cycles setting is my best guess, but it seems like a reasonable game speed, so good luck with this one!

name: Osmosis
description: Osmosis (apparently also sometimes called "Treasure Trove") is a solitaire variant played with a standard 52-card deck. I honestly didn't bother to learn the rules, but if you're interested in this game you probably already know how to play, or are at least willing to learn. The game itself (or the Osmosis Wikipedia page) provide an explanation of the rules. This version of the game uses graphics and the mouse for control, which seems superior to the other textmode version of Osmosis. The author Randy Rasa would later go on to create Solitaire Suite which includes Osmosis and a bunch of other solitaire games.

name: Osmosis Solitaire
description: Osmosis Solitaire (apparently also sometimes called "Treasure Trove") is a solitaire variant played with a standard 52-card deck. I honestly didn't bother to learn the rules, but if you're interested in this game you probably already know how to play, or are at least willing to learn. The game itself (or the Osmosis Wikipedia page) provide an explanation of the rules. This version of the game is text-based, but it seems to work reasonably well.Osmosis Solitaire is a DOS-based card game, part of the genre of solitaire games that was popular in the late 80s and early 90s. It is a variation of traditional solitaire, with a twist on the rules and gameplay mechanics, offering a unique take on the classic single-player card game.

name: Ossuary
description: Ossuary is a lovely CGA DOS roguelike RPG game published in 2020! Each of the 24 levels of the game are randomly generated each time you play, as are the starting stats of your character. Your goal is to delve the depths of the ossuary and kill the evil necromancer dwelling within. Along the way you'll battle enemies (mostly bats, early on) and collect weapons and other items. The in-game help lists the keys you'll need to navigate the ossuary and manage your inventory, but you'll likely need to consult the included ossuary.txt file for details on how the different game constructs work.

name: Out of this World (Another World)
description: DOSGames.com Review: Rating: 4.5 Out of this World (aka Another World) is a early polygon based action/adventure game which featured a distinctive artistic style and trial-and-error based gameplay which could be rather frustrating, yet the game was certainly memorable and entertaining. You play a scientist who has accidentally been sent to "another world" and must figure out what to do in order to survive. The side-view gameplay feels quite a bit like Prince of Persia, but the gameplay revolves more around simple puzzles. Unless you're using a walkthough, you will undoubtedly die many times as you attempt to figure out where to go and what to do.

name: Outburst - The Game of Topics
description: Outburst is a board game, originally developed in 1986, that seems similar to the still-popular Family Feud game show. A topic/category is shown, and the participant(s) must guess the top answers related to that topic. This text-mode DOS version allows two players to go head-to-head, or allows a single player to challenge the computer with varying difficulty settings. A sample topic is "PARTS OF A TACO" of which includes the shell, cheese, meat, etc. The game works pretty well, although it shows you the topic before the timer starts with an opportunity to pass, which allows you unlimited time to think of answers before starting the timer, so the timer is basically useless.

name: Outer Ridge
description: Outer Ridge is sort of a 3D interpretation of the classic Asteroids arcade game. You fly around in space and shoot nicely pre-rendered asteroids. You can also sometimes collect powerups. Once you've achieved the level objective, you just need to fly through the exit, and you'll be ready for the next stage. The 3D perspective is neat and visually impressive but despite the two radar screens, it's difficult to control and disorienting to watch.Outer Ridge is a DOS-based game, released in the early 1990s. It falls under the genre of action and puzzle-solving games, offering a mix of strategy and exploration in a science-fiction setting. The game focuses on space exploration and tasks players with navigating through different environments, often encountering enemies or obstacles while solving puzzles and completing missions.

name: Outer Space Arkanoid
description: Classic Arkanoid or Breakout game in HTML5. Shoot all bricks with the ball and keep the ball in play with your paddle. Move the paddle with the mouse or with your finger on Mobile devices.Outer Space Arkanoid is an HTML-based online game that offers a variation of the classic Arkanoid or Breakout style gameplay, set in a space-themed environment. In this game, players control a paddle to bounce a ball and break bricks or blocks, but with a sci-fi twist, possibly featuring outer space-themed backgrounds, obstacles, or power-ups.Paddle Control: The player controls a paddle (which may look like a spaceship, space station, or other space-themed object) that moves horizontally at the bottom of the screen. The paddle’s job is to bounce a ball that continuously moves upwards towards the blocks above. The player needs to catch and redirect the ball to break the blocks, and it may bounce off the sides of the screen depending on the angle. Blocks and Power-ups: The game features blocks or bricks that the player must destroy by making the ball hit them. Each block could represent a different challenge, and some might have special effects. Power-ups: As the ball hits certain blocks, it may trigger power-ups that help the player. Common power-ups include: Size increase/decrease: Making the paddle larger or smaller. Ball speed: Speeding up or slowing down the ball. Multi-ball: Splitting the ball into multiple balls to break more blocks at once. Laser or shield: Allowing the player to shoot lasers or gain temporary protection from the ball falling off. Levels and Difficulty: The game progresses through different levels, with each new level introducing a more complex arrangement of blocks, different block types (e.g., unbreakable blocks), and sometimes new obstacles like moving blocks or walls. Difficulty ramps up as the ball moves faster or the arrangement of blocks becomes more difficult to hit. Space Theme: Unlike classic Arkanoid, Outer Space Arkanoid adds a space-themed setting. This could include: Backgrounds with stars, planets, or galaxies. Special "space" blocks with unique powers or effects. Space-related obstacles or enemies that occasionally interfere with gameplay. Game Over and High Scores: Players continue to play until they run out of lives, which typically happens if they miss the ball a set number of times, causing the ball to fall off the screen. After losing all lives, the game ends, but players can try again to achieve a higher score. Scoring: Players earn points for breaking blocks and completing levels. Power-ups and special blocks might provide additional points or bonuses. The goal is to achieve the highest score possible while progressing through the levels.

name: Outfox
description: Outfox is a computerized version of the old "Fox and Hounds" board game, which was often played using a normal checkers/chess board. This version automates movement of the fox (the computer moves it, so it's one player only), greatly expands the board, and adds various obstacles to complicate matters. The goal is to use your twenty hounds to surround the fox on all eight sides before the fox reaches the bottom of the screen. This is difficult, especially since the fox can sometimes "kick" rocks (?) changing the layout of the map or even taking out one of the hounds. As with most of the author's games, it uses text mode.

name: Outland-A
description: Outland (or Outland=A) is a space-themed action game where the goal is simple: Shoot the alien ship (?) moving up and down on the right side of the screen. There is no timer or anything attacking you; your only danger is hitting the purple orb which is also moving up and down between you and your target. Other obstacles sometimes pop up in the way. That's about it. Minimal EGA graphics and PC speaker sounds. Not the most entertaining, but there is some strategy; moving your ship up and down also directs your shots, so you can aim them after firing.

name: Outlaw 97
description: Outlaw 97 is a visually-upgraded remake of the Atari 2600 game "Outlaw". Two players choose their fighters from a Street Fighter-style arrangement, and battle it out in an arena-style fight to the death. There are only three fighters available in the shareware version (eight in the full version): Sgt. Blade (military guy), TEX WACO (a sheriff), and Officer Wilbur (a police officer). It doesn't seem like your choice makes any difference in how the game plays, except the optional fatalities (which I think you only know if you register).

name: Overkill
description: Like shooting stuff? Try Overkill, aka "OverKill: The Six-Planet Mega Blast." Despite the name, it isn't at all gory. In fact, it's a space shooter in the tradition of Galaga and so many others. It features EGA graphics and SB sounds and music. The gameplay isn't extremely varied, but it has good control and can be fun to play. There are worse games that you could play ...Overkill is a DOS-based action game released in the early 1990s. It is a top-down, arcade-style shooter that features intense, action-packed gameplay with a focus on weaponry, combat, and survival. The game is typically set in a gritty, war-torn environment where players engage in fast-paced, violent battles.

name: OvO
description: from the screen to the ring to the pen to the king Yes. wheres my crown thats my bling

name: Oxyd
description: The goal of Oxyd is to roll your ball using your mouse and match up tiles to progress to the next level. The game controls quite well using the mouse although it takes some getting used to. The puzzles are not overly challenging although you'll need some quick reflexes to complete some of them. Also the group of levels offered in the shareware version is somewhat limited. Still, quite a well made game, with decent graphics. It's clear a lot of thought and work went into this one.Oxyd is a classic DOS puzzle game that was originally released in the early 1990s. The game combines elements of exploration, strategy, and puzzle-solving, where players control a ball and solve increasingly difficult puzzles. It is known for its challenging mechanics and minimalist design.

name: P-Robots
description: P-Robots was inspired by the similar game C-Robots which is similar but uses the C language instead of a Pascal-like language. The object is the same: Program the most lethal robot you can using the Pascal-inspired programming language, and then battle it against other robots to see who is king! You can see your robots battling against each other, but you can also run multiple matches in a row without visually seeing them to quickly process several battles automatically. Several example robots are included, and some can be pretty lethal!

name: P.E.G.S
description: BEZ P.E.G.S (an acronym of "Practically Everything Goes Somewhere") is a block-pushing game ala Sokoban with a twist. Pushing multiple of the same shape block together will cause unexpected results. Square and round pegs behave normally, but push two triangle pieces together and they become a block. Combine two plus-shaped pegs and you'll get to choose what kind of new peg is created. But don't try to push a square peg into a round peg, and watch out for pits! It's a simple but neat twist on the normal block-pushing game, and the game starts out slowly with easy levels so you can learn how to play.

name: P.O.D Wars
description: POD Wars is an interesting text-mode exploration/strategy/action hybrid game that doesn't actually seem to be balanced very well, gameplay-wise. The object is to explore different maps, tunneling through walls and locate the "metal Qzrn" using your POD (Personal Observational Droid). You first collect supplies from your ship, then proceed down to the map you've chosen. Press Spacebar to bring up a menu allowing you to perform various actions. The main issue seems to be that you aren't given enough resources to get very far in either of the two working maps, so your game will be over quite quickly. Unless of course I'm missing something which is quite possible, the included documentation is a bit short.

name: Pac
description: Pac is a Pac-Man with a few novel gameplay mechanics, which were actually implemented due to the limitations of the RDS Game-Maker GCS which was used to create it. Like the classic game, your goal is to collect all the dots in the maze and avoid the ghosts. Here instead of letting you eat the ghosts, the power pellets allow you to fire shots at them. The level also scrolls (in the signature janky GM way) to see the entire level. There are apparently many levels in this game all with different layouts but it will be difficult to see them since you only get a single life, so one hit and your game is done!

name: Pac Attack
description: Pac Attack is a remake / clone of the video game of the same name (Pac-Attack or Pac-Panic) originally published by Namco in 1993 for the SNES / Genesis platforms. This remake keeps the basic gameplay intact: Drop blocks and ghosts into the well. Try to make lines with the blocks; use the occasional Pac-Man (Pac-Men?) that drop to clear out some of the ghosts to make room for blocks. The game is presented with nice graphics and some sound effects and voices, but no music. There are two gameplay modes: Arcade-style and puzzle style. The game plays quite well and is a fun variant of the typical Tetris type games.

name: Pac Man
description: Pac-Man (Flash) is a web-based version of the classic arcade game Pac-Man, originally created by Namco in 1980. In the Flash version, the game mechanics and design are preserved but optimized for play on modern web browsers using Adobe Flash, which was a popular technology for browser games before being phased out.The gameplay of Pac-Man (Flash) follows the same mechanics as the original Pac-Man game: Objective: The player controls Pac-Man, a yellow, circular character that moves around a maze, eating dots (also known as pellets). The goal is to eat all the dots on the maze while avoiding being caught by four colored ghosts. There are also power pellets located in the corners of the maze. When eaten, these power pellets temporarily turn the ghosts blue, allowing Pac-Man to eat them for extra points. Maze Layout: The maze consists of a series of interconnected corridors with small dots scattered throughout. There are also larger power pellets at the four corners of the maze. The maze is set up so that Pac-Man must navigate through the corridors, collecting all the dots while avoiding the ghosts that chase him. Ghosts: Four ghosts pursue Pac-Man through the maze. Each ghost has a different behavior: Blinky (Red Ghost): Chases Pac-Man directly. Pinky (Pink Ghost): Tries to get in front of Pac-Man's movements. Inky (Cyan Ghost): Moves unpredictably based on the positions of Blinky and Pac-Man. Clyde (Orange Ghost): Alternates between chasing Pac-Man and wandering randomly. When Pac-Man is caught by a ghost, the player loses a life. Power Pellets: Eating a power pellet temporarily turns the ghosts blue, making them vulnerable. Pac-Man can eat these ghosts for extra points during this time. Power pellets are a key strategy in Pac-Man as they give the player a chance to clear the maze of ghosts temporarily. Levels and Progression: Pac-Man progresses through multiple levels, with each level becoming slightly more difficult. The speed of the ghosts increases as the game advances, and new maze layouts may appear. After completing a level by eating all the dots, the player moves on to the next level with a higher level of difficulty, and the game continues until all lives are lost. Scoring: Players earn points by eating dots, power pellets, and ghosts. Eating a regular dot gives 10 points. Eating a ghost after consuming a power pellet gives progressively higher points (200, 400, 800, and 1600 points for the first, second, third, and fourth ghosts eaten after consuming a power pellet). Eating fruit (which appears randomly in the maze) also gives bonus points. Lives: The player starts with a set number of lives (usually 3) and loses a life each time Pac-Man is caught by a ghost. The game ends when the player runs out of lives.

name: Pac Man Tree Top Token Game
description: Pac-Man Tree Top Token Game (Flash) is a fun and unique take on the classic Pac-Man franchise, presented in a Flash-based format. This Flash game was part of a series of games created around the Pac-Man brand, offering a new and different experience while maintaining the nostalgic charm of the original arcade game.Unlike the traditional maze-chase format of the original Pac-Man, Pac-Man Tree Top Token Game features a more platforming and puzzle-based gameplay. Here's how it works: Objective: In Pac-Man Tree Top Token Game, the main goal is to collect tokens scattered throughout the level. These tokens are usually located in trees or various structures within the environment. Players must navigate Pac-Man through a series of obstacles and challenges to reach and collect these tokens. Environment: The game is set in a vibrant, tree-filled environment, where Pac-Man moves between platforms and interacts with different objects. The design is colorful, and the levels are designed to feel like an adventure through a forest or a jungle setting. Collecting Tokens: Players must collect a certain number of Tree Top Tokens on each level. Tokens are typically placed in hard-to-reach areas that require the player to jump, move between different platforms, or solve small puzzles. The game focuses on exploration and strategic movement to ensure that Pac-Man can reach each token without falling into hazards or traps. Obstacles: The game features various obstacles that can slow Pac-Man down or cause him to lose a life. These include: Moving platforms: Players need to time their jumps to avoid falling. Enemies: Just like in the classic Pac-Man games, there are occasional enemies or creatures in the environment that Pac-Man must avoid. Hazards: Other environmental hazards such as spikes, gaps, or falling obstacles might be present. Power-ups: Power-ups might be available throughout the levels, offering temporary boosts or helping Pac-Man avoid enemies. These power-ups could give Pac-Man the ability to jump higher, move faster, or temporarily make him invincible. Levels: The game has multiple levels, and each one increases in difficulty. As players advance, they encounter more challenging obstacles and enemy types. Some levels may also introduce new gameplay mechanics, such as timed challenges or platforming sections that require perfect timing. End Goal: The game is typically level-based, and players must complete a series of levels by collecting all the tokens in each. Once the player collects all tokens in a level, they can progress to the next one, with higher levels offering increased difficulty and more complex puzzles.

name: Pac Maze
description: "Pac Maze" is an exciting maze escape game inspired by classic arcade games like Pac-Man. The goal is to navigate through a maze, collect all the stars, and escape through the exit. The game combines maze-solving, strategy, and quick reflexes, offering a fun and challenging experience. Game Description: Objective: Collect all the stars scattered throughout the maze to unlock the exit and escape. Gameplay: Players control a character (e.g., Pac-Man) that can move up, down, left, or right within the maze. The maze contains walls, open paths, stars, and an exit. Players must collect all the stars to unlock the exit and complete the level. Maze Layout: The maze is a grid-based layout with walls blocking certain paths. Stars are placed at specific locations, and the exit is initially locked. Some levels may include enemies or obstacles that move around the maze, adding to the challenge. Controls: Players use arrow keys or on-screen buttons to move the character. Progression: The game includes multiple levels, each with a unique maze layout and increasing difficulty. Later levels may introduce more complex mazes, additional enemies, or time limits. Special Features: Enemies: Some levels include enemies that chase the player, requiring quick thinking and strategy to avoid them. Power-Ups: Collect power-ups like speed boosts or temporary invincibility to help navigate the maze. Timer: Some levels may include a timer to add urgency to the gameplay.

name: Pac PC
description: He's a classic symbol (an icon, if you will) for video gaming ... and now you can play an almost arcade perfect version of the Pac-Man arcade game on your computer! In case you need a quick refresher: Pac-Man was one of the first hit arcade games where you collect dots and avoid ghosts in a maze. Pac PC is one of several terrific clones of the classic arcade game, including nearly identical sounds, graphics, and gameplay! The screen scrolls to follow the action. Very impressive indeed.Pac PC (DOS) is a fan-made clone of the classic arcade game Pac-Man that was designed for MS-DOS systems. This version follows the core mechanics of the original Pac-Man while offering a DOS-compatible version that could be run on older PCs, often as a way to enjoy the iconic game on systems that didn't support the original arcade or console versions.

name: Pac-Bar
description: A neat variant of the classic Pac-Man game. This version includes a couple of new gameplay elements, big levels and good EGA graphics. It seems quite challenging (at least for me!), although you DO receive more than the usual 3 lives. For one thing, there are no traditional power pellets (so that you can eat the ghosts). There are also some short dead-ends in the maze, and instead of fruit to eat, there are eyes bouncing around the levels.Pac-Bar (DOS) is a fan-made arcade game that combines the classic gameplay elements of Pac-Man with the mechanics of Breakout or Arkanoid. It was designed for MS-DOS systems, much like other fan-made clones and adaptations of popular games during the early days of personal computing.

name: Pac-Gal
description: Basic Pacman-style game done with only ASCII graphics (it was made in 1982 after all). Not much to say, will be useful for REALLY old computers or for nostalgia only. The # you're asked to enter at the beginning of the game relates to speed: 0=fastest, 30000=slowest ... however you'll still probably have to use either DOSBox or a slowdown program like MoSlo to make the game run at a reasonable speed regardless of the number that you choose if you're running it on modern PCs. (A reasonable value would be around the 2000-7000 range).

name: Pac-Maine
description: Pac-Maine is an obscure CGA oddity from 1988 which was distributed by the University of Maine at Fort Kent as a marketing tool for their computer science and IT programs. Coded by one of their professors, it's basically a Pac-Man clone like you would expect, although it's a bit clunkier than the average Pac-clone. You must eat all of the A's (representing good marks?) and avoid the ghosts which represent things which may derail your college career: Bad study habits, peer pressure, drinking, and drugs. It's an interesting early example of a promo game (complete a screen and you'll receive a congratulatory ad for the university) but not especially fun to play.

name: Pac-Man
description: Pac-Man (HTML) is a modern browser-based version of the classic arcade game Pac-Man, which can be played directly in a web browser without the need for any plugins or downloads. This version retains the core mechanics of the original game while being optimized for web technology, such as HTML5, CSS, and JavaScript, making it accessible on various devices and operating systems.Objective: The player controls Pac-Man, a yellow circle, in a maze filled with dots that must be eaten. The primary goal is to eat all the dots in the maze while avoiding four colored ghosts. The game progresses as the player clears the maze, moving on to the next level where the difficulty increases, with faster-moving ghosts and more complex mazes. Maze Layout: The maze remains similar to the original arcade version: a series of paths and corridors with dots scattered across them. The power pellets at the four corners of the maze give the player the ability to turn the ghosts blue and eat them for extra points. Ghosts: The four ghosts are: Blinky (Red Ghost): Chases Pac-Man directly. Pinky (Pink Ghost): Tries to predict Pac-Man's movements. Inky (Cyan Ghost): Moves unpredictably. Clyde (Orange Ghost): Moves randomly or follows Pac-Man at times. If Pac-Man is caught by a ghost, he loses a life. The game ends when all lives are lost. Power Pellets: Eating a power pellet temporarily turns the ghosts blue, allowing Pac-Man to eat them for extra points. Once the power pellet effect wears off, the ghosts return to their normal colors and chase Pac-Man again. Fruits: Like the original arcade game, fruits such as cherries, strawberries, and oranges occasionally appear in the maze. Collecting these fruits provides bonus points. Levels and Progression: The game has multiple levels, with the player clearing all the dots and power pellets in the maze to advance to the next stage. As levels increase, the speed of the ghosts becomes faster, and the game becomes more difficult. Lives and Scoring: The player starts with a set number of lives (usually 3) and loses one if caught by a ghost. Scoring is based on the collection of dots, power pellets, and fruit, as well as eating ghosts during the power pellet effect.

name: Pac-Man
description: Pac-Man (DOS) is a fan-made or unofficial version of the classic arcade game Pac-Man, designed to run on MS-DOS-based systems. While Pac-Man was originally developed by Namco in 1980 for arcades, over the years, many clones and adaptations of the game were made for various platforms, including MS-DOS, to allow players to enjoy the game on their home computers.The gameplay in Pac-Man (DOS) remains faithful to the original Pac-Man arcade game, with some fan-made versions attempting to improve or adapt it for MS-DOS. Here’s a breakdown of how it works: Objective: The player controls Pac-Man, a yellow, circular character who must navigate a maze, eating all the dots while avoiding four colored ghosts (Blinky, Pinky, Inky, and Clyde). The goal is to eat all the dots in the maze and move on to the next level, while avoiding the ghosts who try to catch Pac-Man. Maze Layout: The maze consists of corridors and open spaces where the dots are placed. Power pellets are located in the four corners of the maze. Eating a power pellet temporarily turns the ghosts blue, allowing Pac-Man to eat them for extra points. Ghosts: The four ghosts have different behaviors: Blinky (Red Ghost): Follows Pac-Man directly. Pinky (Pink Ghost): Tries to position itself ahead of Pac-Man, predicting his movement. Inky (Cyan Ghost): Moves unpredictably, influenced by Pac-Man's and Blinky’s position. Clyde (Orange Ghost): Alternates between chasing Pac-Man and wandering randomly. If a ghost touches Pac-Man, the player loses a life. The game ends when all lives are lost. Power Pellets: Eating a power pellet changes the behavior of the ghosts: they turn blue and become vulnerable. For a short time, Pac-Man can eat the ghosts, which gives extra points. Once the power pellet effect wears off, the ghosts return to their normal state. Fruit: Occasionally, fruits such as cherries, strawberries, or oranges appear in the maze. Collecting them provides additional points and rewards the player with bonus points. Levels and Progression: The game features an infinite number of levels, each becoming progressively harder as the ghosts move faster and the maze layout may vary slightly in some fan-made versions. The player continues to advance by clearing the maze of dots and power pellets. Lives and Scoring: The player starts with a set number of lives (typically 3), and each time a ghost catches Pac-Man, a life is lost. The game keeps track of the player's score, awarding points for eating dots, ghosts (when they are vulnerable), and fruit.

name: Pac-Maniac
description: Pac-Maniac (alternately referred to as simply "Champ Pacman" in the included docs) is a Pac-Man clone (it is NOT a clone of the similarly named Pac-Mania game) that preceeds CHAMProgramming's near perfect Pac-Em game. But this game, Pac-Maniac, plays like a horizontally stretched version of the classic pellet-muncher game. Also, in some ways it tries to be TOO arcade-like, with an unintuitive control structure: You have to use the function keys to do most things, like start the game. (Press F10 for the help menu.) So if you're looking for an experience that more exactly mirrors the arcade game and is much smoother to play, try Pac-Em.

name: Pacamaze
description: Pacamaze is a 3D Pac-man game, where instead of collecting power pellets, you collect ammo and can shoot the ghosts! It's an interesting idea, and although the engine is rather buggy, it does work well enough to play and enjoy. You are given both a mini-map (on screen at all times) showing the ghosts, as well as a full-maze map that you can also see the remaining dots you need to collect. Supposedly there is a end-game boss of some kind, but I didn't make it that far, so you'll need to play yourself to find out! Pretty impressive considering that the zip file is only 33k!

name: Packman
description: Packman is, as its name suggests, an overt Pac-Man clone. The playing field is horizontal rather than vertical, and the colors are uglier than its arcade counterpart, but it plays competently enough, at least for a game distributed for free in 1983. As in the original game, you control "Packman" and gobble dots while avoiding ghosts. You can gobble a power pellet to turn the tables and eat the ghosts. You move slower while gobbling pellets. Don't expect any fancy features or arcade-accuracy but it's a game that some people will remember from their childhood.

name: Packrat
description: AKA "The Pack Rat", this is a rather basic jumping game. Here you play the role of a rat who must run and jump through various scenes collecting items. The graphics are not bad (nice, but not flashy), but there's no sound (besides the annoying PC speaker which can be turned off) and the gameplay isn't extremely exciting. (But hey, it's only 50k!) It also includes a simple level editor, and a take-turns style uninteresting multiplayer mode.Packrat (DOS) is a classic, simple yet engaging puzzle game that was developed for DOS systems in the 1990s. It’s a puzzle game that involves arranging and packing various items into a limited space, which challenges the player’s spatial reasoning and planning skills.

name: Pacman Advanced
description: Pacman Advanced (Flash) is a modern twist on the classic Pac-Man game, designed to run in web browsers with Flash technology. It builds on the original Pac-Man formula by introducing new elements, power-ups, and advanced features, offering an enhanced experience while staying true to the nostalgic gameplay of the original arcade version.Objective: Similar to the classic Pac-Man, the player controls Pac-Man, who must navigate a maze, eat all the dots, and avoid being caught by the ghosts (Blinky, Pinky, Inky, and Clyde). The goal is to clear each level by eating all the dots in the maze and progressing to the next stage. Power-Ups and Advanced Features: Pacman Advanced introduces new power-ups and mechanics to expand the gameplay: Speed Boosts: Temporarily increase Pac-Man's speed to outrun the ghosts. Invisibility: At certain points, Pac-Man might become invisible, allowing him to avoid detection by the ghosts. Ghost Transformation: In some versions, eating specific power-ups can change the behavior of ghosts, making them act more predictably or even allowing Pac-Man to temporarily turn the tables and eat the ghosts (like in the original).
