name: Prince of Persia
description: Prince of Persia is a classic platforming game developed by Jordan Mechner. It premiered Jordan's use of the "rotoscoping" technique to digitize lifelike movements of the in-game characters. The game itself is a race against time since the clock is always ticking down, but moreso against all of the various traps and high falls in the dungeon which kill you just as much as the enemy characters that you will encounter. As an in-game text file included with the demo states: "It's like an Arabian Nights movie come to life... with you as the star!" The controls do take some getting used to, but they became standard for this sort of game, as also seen in the sequel Prince of Persia: The Shadow and the Flame, as well as other later games like Blackthorne or Out of this World. The graphics are indeed very appealing, as the movements of the characters and other in-game elements feel like they have real weight to them.

name: Prince of Persia 2: The Shadow and the Flame
description: "Prince of Persia 2: The Shadow and the Flame" is the sequel to the iconic Prince of Persia, developed by Jordan Mechner and released in 1993. This demo version offers a glimpse into the expanded world of the Prince, featuring the same running, jumping, and swordfighting action that made the original a classic. With its smooth rotoscoped animations, atmospheric music, and varied locations, the game builds on its predecessor’s success. However, its challenging one-hit deaths and precise controls can be frustrating for newcomers. Game Features: Gameplay Mechanics: Platforming and Combat: Players control the Prince as he navigates treacherous environments, jumps over gaps, and engages in sword fights with enemies. One-Hit Deaths: A single mistake can lead to death, requiring players to master timing and precision. Puzzle Solving: Solve environmental puzzles to progress through the levels. Levels and Challenges: Varied Locations: The demo features diverse settings, including palaces, dungeons, and rooftops, each with unique challenges. Progressive Difficulty: The game becomes increasingly challenging as players advance, with more complex traps and enemies. Visuals and Design: Rotoscoped Animations: The game uses the same rotoscoping technique as the original, resulting in smooth and realistic character movements. Detailed Environments: The levels are richly designed with atmospheric backgrounds and intricate details. Sound and Music: Sound Effects: Realistic sounds for sword clashes, footsteps, and environmental interactions, enhancing immersion. Background Music: Thematic music that complements the game’s adventurous and mysterious atmosphere. Controls: Keyboard Inputs: Precise controls for movement, jumping, and swordfighting, though they require practice to master. Intuitive Interface: The game’s interface is simple and easy to navigate, despite the challenging gameplay. Demo Limitations: Limited Content: The demo version includes only a portion of the full game, offering a taste of the expanded story and gameplay. Teaser Experience: Designed to showcase the game’s mechanics and atmosphere, encouraging players to explore the full version.

name: Princess Jewels
description: Match3 game with the Jewels of the Princess. Drop blocks down and combine 3 same jewels horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Change the order of the jewels with the arrow keys."Princess Jewels" is an engaging HTML puzzle game where players must match and collect sparkling jewels to complete levels. With its colorful graphics, relaxing gameplay, and intuitive controls, "Princess Jewels" offers a delightful experience for players of all ages. Perfect for fans of puzzle and matching games, it provides hours of brain-teasing fun. Game Features: Gameplay Mechanics: Jewel Matching: Players must match three or more identical jewels to clear them from the board. Chain Reactions: Create chain reactions by strategically matching jewels to clear large sections of the board. Special Jewels: Match four or more jewels to create special jewels with unique abilities, such as clearing entire rows or columns. Levels and Challenges: Progressive Difficulty: As players advance through levels, the jewel arrangements become more complex, and the objectives more challenging. Unique Objectives: Some levels have specific goals, such as clearing a certain number of jewels or achieving a target score. Visuals and Design: Colorful Graphics: The game features vibrant and detailed visuals, with sparkling jewel designs. Dynamic Animations: Smooth animations for jewel movements, matches, and chain reactions. Sound and Music: Catchy Music: Upbeat and engaging background music that complements the relaxing gameplay. Sound Effects: Satisfying sounds for matching jewels, activating special abilities, and completing levels. User Interface: Intuitive Controls: Simple mouse or touch controls for selecting and matching jewels. Responsive Design: Optimized for both desktop and mobile devices, ensuring a seamless experience across platforms. Score Tracking: High Scores: Track your highest scores and compete with friends or other players. Achievements: Unlock achievements for completing specific challenges or matching jewels quickly.

name: Princess Red Keyboard Warrior
description: Princess Red Keyboard Warrior is a short adventure game created for an online game-making contest #bitbitjam3. Created as a homage to the simple games of old (especially the ending screen) it does succeed, with its CGA graphics and PC speaker music. Gameplay is very simple and the game is short (you can probably finish it in 5mins) but it still has a retro-aesthetic about it that is nonetheless charming. Your princess character is given a standard quest, and then must battle monsters encountered in random battles along the way by quickly typing words as they appear on the screen. Full QBasic source code is included.

name: Prisoner
description: Prisoner DOS Game is a digital adaptation of the classic block-sliding puzzle genre, where the primary objective is to maneuver various blocks within a confined space to guide a special piece—referred to as the "prisoner"—to the exit on the opposite side of the board. The game follows the traditional mechanics of such puzzles, requiring players to strategically slide blocks horizontally or vertically to create a path for the prisoner to escape. Key Features: Single Layout: The game features only one predefined puzzle layout, which is typical for block-sliding puzzles. This limits its replayability, as the challenge remains the same each time you play. Objective: The goal is to move the blocks around the grid in such a way that the prisoner can reach the exit. This involves careful planning and spatial reasoning to avoid getting stuck. Advertisement Element: What makes this game particularly unique is its origin. It was created by the sysop (system operator) of The POWER Tower, a now-defunct BBS (Bulletin Board System) based in England. The game served as an advertisement for the BBS, and after playing, users were treated to a promotional message for The POWER Tower. Historical Context: The game is a snapshot of the early days of computer gaming and BBS culture, where sysops often created small programs or games to attract users to their systems. It reflects the creativity and community-driven nature of the BBS era. Gameplay Mechanics: Block Movement: Players can slide blocks in four directions (up, down, left, right) as long as there is space to move them. Prisoner Movement: The prisoner can only move when a clear path to the exit is created by rearranging the blocks. Puzzle Solving: Success requires logical thinking and patience, as the confined space and limited moves can make the puzzle quite challenging.

name: Professor Othello
description: Professor Othello is an Othello game. You play against the CPU only (no two player mode). There are no difficulty settings, you just try to beat the computer, which uses a "tree-pruning technique searching to a depth of 6 levels to find the best move". Keyboard controls are a bit unintuitive but simple using Spacebar to select the space and Enter to place your piece. I guess it works fine, the CPU seems to be making reasonable moves. Not sure why it's called "Professor" Othello since it doesn't teach you how to play or any strategies that might help you win.

name: PRogue
description: PRogue is a Roguelike game, inspired by the original Rogue, but the authors take considerable liberties with their re-interpretation of the game. Like the original, your quest is to recover a special item. There are no character classes here, you are a generic hero-type guy. And while many things are the same (text-mode randomly generated maps, many keyboard hotkeys to accomplish actions), there are many differences, like whenever you encounter an enemy, the view switches to a graphical mode with a drawing of your foe, and you simply repeatedly choose to (F)ight or (R)un. It seems like there is a decent amount of depth here, but it also seems quite difficult as I died quickly whenever I played.

name: Project X
description: Project X is a classic DOS game released in 1992 by Team17, a renowned developer known for their work on the Worms series. It is a side-scrolling shoot-'em-up (shmup) game that gained popularity for its challenging gameplay, vibrant graphics, and catchy soundtrack, which was composed by Allister Brimble. Gameplay: In Project X, players control a futuristic spacecraft tasked with battling waves of enemies, dodging obstacles, and defeating powerful bosses across multiple levels. The game features a variety of weapons and power-ups that can be collected to enhance the ship's firepower, such as lasers, homing missiles, and shields. The gameplay is fast-paced and requires quick reflexes and strategic use of power-ups to survive. Key Features: Multiple Levels: The game consists of several stages, each with unique environments, enemies, and a challenging boss at the end. Weapon Upgrades: Players can collect power-ups to upgrade their ship's weapons, including spread shots, homing missiles, and more. Difficulty: Project X is known for its high level of difficulty, which appeals to fans of challenging shoot-'em-ups. Graphics and Sound: The game features colorful, detailed graphics for its time and an iconic soundtrack that complements the action-packed gameplay. Two-Player Mode: The game supports a two-player cooperative mode, allowing friends to team up and tackle the alien forces together.

name: Prospector
description: Prospector is a single-screen (non-scrolling) action game that combines elements of Donkey Kong and other games, perhaps the original Mario Bros. The object is to collect all of the gold on the level while avoiding the enemies. The gold is positioned like the rivets supporting the scaffolding on the fourth level of the original Donkey Kong arcade game. However instead of just running over them, the Prospector must drop down and hang from the girder. While hanging he's safe from the enemies. He can also jump to avoid them, but he has no attacks. You can collect items that momentarily freeze the enemies. The main frustration is that your character has to be exactly positioned to collect the gold or go up/down ladders, which can be frustratingly twitchy. Graphics are average at best.

name: Protec
description: PROTEC is a fairly basic pinball simulation game. It includes only a single table, and simple graphics, with a technology/computers theme. There are Soundblaster sound effects and some simple MIDI music as well. The ball physics seem quite bouncy, so it'll take some getting used to. Make sure to run the game with the XT option (or use RUN.BAT) otherwise you won't be able to control one of the flippers! Overall it's a very average pinball game with the typical ramps, bumpers, etc, but it does work decently enough, despite the strange physics.

name: Proton
description: Proton is a sort of simple Lazer Tag type game where two teams of combatants shoot at each other trying to score points. The game works on a grid-based system which isn't the best model for this type of game. It's difficult to see where your opponents are, since only a small area of the map is shown. Whenever you get hit, your gun freezes and you can't shoot at anyone for a few seconds. Also after you register 5 hits, you must "clear" your gun by shooting the opponent's base. Overall it's an interesting game distributed for free in 1987 but the gameplay (as well as lack of a two player mode!) isn't very compelling.

name: Psionics
description: Psionics is a simple first-person perspective RPG game. You have been taken to the Nexus, a scientific research station in space, so that they can experiment on your psychic abilities. However, apparently you didn't see an attack coming on the space station, since you're awakened to dead bodies, mutated monsters, and calamity! Oh my! This plays like a simple first-person dungeon crawl, where you find items, and fight many mutated rats. Graphics are simple but workable, and sounds are the usual annoying PC speaker beeps. Not sure how long or in-depth this is, you'll need to keep playing to find out!

name: Pssst!
description: Pssst! was originally developed for the ZX Spectrum back in 1983. Ten years later, John Dow ported it to MS-DOS PCs and ... here it is! The object of the game is to protect a plant that is growing upwards from the bottom of the screen from bugs. You can grab various weapons from the sides and use them against the bugs; different tools kill different kinds. Once the plant grows to the top, you win the level and progress. The game looks the same as the ZX Spectrum original, with it's distinctive graphical style.Released in 1983 by Ultimate Play the Game (later known as Rare), Pssst! is a quirky and charming early computer game that combines elements of action and puzzle-solving. It’s a lesser-known gem from the early days of gaming, but it has a unique and memorable style. Gameplay: In Pssst!, you play as a robotic caretaker tasked with tending to a sentient plant. The plant is growing in a pot, and your goal is to keep it healthy and help it grow by protecting it from pests, providing water, and ensuring it gets enough sunlight. The game is played in a single-screen environment, and you must manage multiple tasks simultaneously. Pests: Insects and other creatures will try to attack the plant. You must zap them with your laser to keep them at bay. Watering: The plant needs water to grow. You must collect water droplets and bring them to the plant. Sunlight: The plant also needs sunlight, which you can direct toward it by positioning mirrors. The game becomes increasingly challenging as you progress, with more pests and faster-paced demands. Key Features: Unique Concept: The idea of nurturing a plant while defending it from pests was quite innovative for its time. Simple Controls: The game uses straightforward controls, making it easy to pick up and play. Charming Graphics: For an early 1980s game, Pssst! features colorful and whimsical visuals that stand out. Increasing Difficulty: As the plant grows, the game becomes more challenging, requiring quick reflexes and multitasking.

name: Psycho Pong
description: Psycho Pong is a two-player competitive Pong game with a twist. Or rather, a rotation. As you begin to play, the playing field begins to rotate 360 degrees. The longer you play, the faster it rotates. It's a somewhat impressive and definitely disorienting effect that makes the competition a lot more difficult and hectic than regular non-rotating Pong. That's all there is, though, as unfortunately this is an alpha version which was never fully finished. (What's here works fine though.)Psycho Pong is a unique and quirky take on the classic Pong game, which was one of the earliest video games ever created. While there isn’t a widely known DOS game specifically called Psycho Pong, the name suggests a chaotic or exaggerated version of Pong, possibly with added twists, power-ups, or surreal elements. If you’re referring to a specific DOS game by that name, it might be a lesser-known or fan-made title. However, I can provide some context and ideas based on the concept of a "Psycho Pong" game: What "Psycho Pong" Might Include: Chaotic Gameplay: The game could feature unpredictable ball movements, multiple balls, or obstacles that make the traditional Pong gameplay more intense and challenging. Power-Ups: Players might collect power-ups to gain advantages, such as larger paddles, faster movement, or the ability to temporarily freeze the opponent’s paddle. Surreal Visuals: The game could have trippy or psychedelic visuals, with flashing colors, distorted backgrounds, or bizarre themes. Multiplayer Madness: A "Psycho Pong" game might include a competitive or cooperative multiplayer mode with added chaos. Custom Rules: The game could introduce unconventional rules, such as paddles that change size, balls that split into multiple pieces, or goals that move around. Classic Pong vs. Psycho Pong: Classic Pong: A simple two-player game where players control paddles to hit a ball back and forth, trying to score points by getting the ball past the opponent. Psycho Pong: A more chaotic and exaggerated version of Pong, with added elements that make the gameplay faster, weirder, and more unpredictable.

name: Pub Darts
description: Pub Darts is a darts simulation game for one or more players. You can play a few different darts games (301, variations of 301, American Cricket, and Golf) against other human players or computer opponents. The dart throwing is basically tapping the spacebar to aim your throw on the board. It doesn't feel particularly fulfilling, perhaps partly because the bars don't seem to increase in a smooth and consistent way? In any case, you do get a lot of variety here and you can play on your own or against other opponents which is always a plus.

name: Pufftris
description: Pufftris plays like the original Tetris game, where you must carefully rotate and position falling pieces to complete horizontal lines. The main gimmick is that as you play, the dropzone will start swinging around, and as time passes it swings around more and more until it almost becomes nauseating to continue playing. (The authors themselves say "Don't blame be if you get seasick!".) Definitely a neat effect but hard to actually play! This game was apparently made for a Tetris-game competition of some sort and won second place.

name: Puffwort's Evil Scheme
description: Puffwort's Evil Scheme is a strange game which has at its core an important message. The entire game is a treatise against smoking cigarettes and why it's terrible for you. The documentation states it's intended for both older kids and adults to play. The game has you traveling to different spaces on a map, trying to convince people not to smoke by choosing one of two dialogue choices. Often you will need to play a minigame before arriving at your destination, which seem to be presented in text mode, or at least use mostly text characters. The game has a fantasy-themed plot (Puffwort is the baddie) which is detailed before you start the game.

name: Pulsar Flux
description: Pulsar Flux is a production-heavy platform shooting / adventure game, with impressive graphics and sound effects but confusing gameplay. I'm not sure about the story (and part of the disconnect may be that the game was created in Croatia where their first language was likely not English) but you play a robot who seems to need to collect parts scattered around a level to proceed. Your character sprite and other sprites are large, which looks impressive but makes control difficult. The detailed backgrounds also blend into your character making it a bit tough to discern what's going on (and what's an obstacle) at times.

name: Pulse
description: Pulse is an action/puzzle game with a unique and fast-paced twist on tile-matching mechanics. Let me break it down based on what you’ve shared: Gameplay Overview: In this version of Pulse, the player’s objective is to match colored tiles by aligning four of the same color. When matched, the tiles disappear and are replaced by a higher-value piece, which can be matched again for even more points. The twist is that the tiles are constantly moving around the screen, and the player must "attract" them to the desired position. This adds a layer of planning and dexterity to the game, as the board becomes increasingly chaotic with more tiles flying around. Key Features: Dynamic Tile Movement: Unlike traditional tile-matching games, the pieces in Pulse are in constant motion, making the gameplay more challenging and engaging. Attraction Mechanic: Players must strategically "attract" tiles to the correct position to create matches, adding a unique twist to the puzzle genre. Progressive Difficulty: As the game progresses, the board fills up with more tiles, and the pace increases, creating a frantic and exciting experience. High-Value Pieces: Matching tiles creates higher-value pieces, which can be matched again for greater rewards, encouraging strategic play. Fast-Paced Action: The combination of moving tiles and the need for quick decision-making makes Pulse a high-energy puzzle game. Why It Stands Out: This version of Pulse takes the familiar tile-matching formula and injects it with a dose of action and chaos. The moving tiles and attraction mechanic require players to think quickly and adapt to the ever-changing board, making it a refreshing and challenging take on the puzzle genre.

name: Pulsoid
description: Pulsoid is an Arkanoid-like game with high-res graphics and decent production values. It's unfortunately not that much fun to play, but still quite an interesting production overall. It's a remake or take-off of a C64 / ZX Spectrum game called Pulsoids. As mentioned, the graphics and sounds are nice, but the game feels a bit flimsy in the control department, and the balls always bounce at 45 degree angles so controlling its flow is mostly impossible. There are powerups to collect, however one of these is actually a power-down that instantly kills you and looks almost like the other powerups so you need to be careful. There are also a lot of ads and other unnecessary screens before and after you play a game.

name: Pune
description: Pune is a snake variant which offers simultaneous shared keyboard play for two players. (Up to 6 in the registered version.) Apparently based on an Amiga game called "Dune 3", Pune looks a lot like it. Your goal is to avoid crashing into your opponent's tail (or your own) while simultaneously attempting to get them to crash. You steer left and right by small degrees, so you are not just moving in the four cardinal directions. Your snake also leaves gaps in its tail, which allow other players a bit more opportunity to avoid being trapped. Overall it plays well, too bad only two players are allowed in the shareware version. Also too bad about those sound effects ... you may want to turn down the volume for this one ...

name: Puppy Puzzle
description: Remove the puppies. Click on groups of 2 or more of the same puppies. Reach the indicated goal.Puppy Puzzle is a delightful and charming puzzle game that can be implemented in HTML (along with CSS and JavaScript) for play in a web browser. The game typically involves arranging or matching pieces to complete a picture of adorable puppies. Here's a basic concept of how you could create a simple Puppy Puzzle game using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript: Game Concept: The player is presented with a scrambled image of a puppy divided into a grid (e.g., 3x3 or 4x4). The goal is to rearrange the pieces by dragging and dropping them into their correct positions to complete the picture.

name: Purple Dinosaur Massacre
description: Purple Dinosaur Massacre is a humorous and over-the-top DOS game that gained a cult following for its absurd premise and quirky gameplay. Released in 1993 by Palevich Entertainment, the game is a parody of the popular children’s television show Barney & Friends, featuring a purple dinosaur as the antagonist. The game is known for its dark humor, fast-paced action, and retro graphics. Gameplay: In Purple Dinosaur Massacre, the player takes on the role of a character tasked with eliminating waves of purple dinosaurs (clearly inspired by Barney). The gameplay is a mix of run-and-gun and shoot-'em-up mechanics, with the player navigating through various levels while fending off hordes of dinosaurs. Weapons: The player is equipped with a variety of weapons, including guns, explosives, and other unconventional tools of destruction. Enemies: The purple dinosaurs come in different forms, some of which are more aggressive or harder to defeat than others. Levels: The game features multiple levels, each with its own unique challenges and environments. Boss Fights: At the end of certain levels, the player faces off against larger, more powerful dinosaur bosses. Key Features: Dark Humor: The game’s premise and execution are intentionally absurd and humorous, appealing to players who enjoy satire and parody. Fast-Paced Action: The gameplay is intense and requires quick reflexes to survive the onslaught of dinosaurs. Retro Graphics: The game features pixelated, DOS-era graphics that add to its charm and nostalgic appeal. Variety of Weapons: Players can use a wide range of weapons to dispatch the dinosaurs, adding variety to the gameplay. Cult Classic Status: Despite its niche appeal, Purple Dinosaur Massacre has become a cult favorite among retro gaming enthusiasts.

name: Push Puzzle
description: Push and remove balls in this puzzle games. Click on the arrows to shoot a ball on the grid, a group of 4 or more of the same ball is removed. Remove all colored backgrounds.Push Puzzle is a classic puzzle game where the player must push blocks or objects to their designated targets. It’s a simple yet challenging game that can be easily implemented in HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. Below is a basic example of how you can create a Push Puzzle game for the web. Game Concept: The player controls a character (or cursor) that can push blocks around a grid. The goal is to move all the blocks onto their target positions. The challenge lies in planning moves carefully, as blocks can get stuck if pushed into corners or against walls.

name: Pusher
description: Pusher is a classic DOS puzzle game released in 1992 by Brady Games. It’s a sokoban-style game, where the player must push crates or boxes onto designated target spaces. The game is known for its challenging levels, simple yet addictive gameplay, and retro charm. Gameplay: In Pusher, the player controls a character (often represented by a smiley face or similar icon) who must push crates around a grid-based level. The goal is to move all the crates onto their target spots. The challenge lies in the fact that crates can only be pushed, not pulled, and they can get stuck if pushed into corners or against walls. Controls: The player moves the character using the arrow keys (or similar controls) to push crates. Levels: The game features a series of increasingly difficult levels, each with a unique layout. Restarting: If the player gets stuck, they can restart the level without penalty. Key Features: Sokoban-Style Gameplay: The game follows the classic sokoban formula, which has inspired many other puzzle games. Challenging Levels: The game starts simple but quickly ramps up in difficulty, requiring careful planning and strategy. Retro Graphics: The game features simple, pixelated graphics typical of early 1990s DOS games. Addictive Gameplay: The puzzle mechanics are easy to learn but hard to master, making the game highly replayable. How to Play: If you’re interested in playing Pusher, you can find it on retro gaming websites or DOS game archives. You’ll need a DOS emulator like DOSBox to run the game on modern systems. Similar Games: If you enjoy Pusher, you might also like: Sokoban: The original crate-pushing puzzle game that inspired Pusher. Boxxle: A sokoban-style game for the Game Boy. Chip’s Challenge: A puzzle game with a variety of challenges and mechanics.

name: Putt-Putt Goes to the Moon
description: Putt-Putt Goes to the Moon is a beloved children’s adventure game developed by Humongous Entertainment and released in 1993. It’s part of the Putt-Putt series, which features a cheerful, anthropomorphic car named Putt-Putt as the protagonist. This game is designed for young players and combines point-and-click gameplay with an engaging story, colorful graphics, and educational elements. Gameplay: In Putt-Putt Goes to the Moon, players guide Putt-Putt on a mission to help his friend Pep, the dog, who has accidentally been launched to the moon. The game is a point-and-click adventure, where players interact with the environment, solve puzzles, and complete tasks to progress the story. Exploration: Players explore various locations, including Putt-Putt’s neighborhood, a spaceship, and the moon. Puzzles: The game features simple, age-appropriate puzzles that encourage problem-solving and critical thinking. Mini-Games: There are fun mini-games and activities, such as repairing a spaceship and collecting moon rocks. Story-Driven: The game has a charming narrative that keeps players engaged from start to finish. Key Features: Child-Friendly Design: The game is designed for young children, with intuitive controls and easy-to-understand gameplay. Educational Value: The game subtly teaches problem-solving, logic, and basic science concepts (e.g., space travel). Colorful Graphics: The game features bright, cartoonish visuals that appeal to its target audience. Interactive Storytelling: Players feel like they’re part of the story, making choices that affect the outcome. Humorous and Wholesome: The game is filled with humor and positive messages, making it enjoyable for both kids and parents. How to Play: If you’d like to play Putt-Putt Goes to the Moon, you can find it on retro gaming websites or digital stores like GOG or Steam. The game runs on modern systems with the help of compatibility tools or emulators like ScummVM, which supports many classic Humongous Entertainment games.

name: Putt-Putt Joins the Parade
description: Putt-Putt Joins the Parade is the first in a long series of Putt-Putt games which are still being released over 20 years later. The game is an edutainment product in the "Junior Adventures" line that was popular in the 90's when it was first released, and continues to live on through re-releases on iOS, Android, and Steam. You play the titular car, Putt-Putt, who wants to join the parade. But first he must earn cash to pay for a car wash, among other assorted tasks. There are plenty of things for kids to click on which result in little animation / sound flourishes. The game is designed to use speech instead of text (good for younger players) so be sure to turn on your speakers.

name: Putty Squad
description: Putty Squad is a demo of a platforming game that unfortunately never seems to have seen a full-length release for DOS. The game, a sequel to the original Putty Squad, was released for SNES and Amiga, and much later remade and re-released for modern consoles like XBox 360 and Nintendo Switch. Anyways it's an interesting and zany platforming game where the object is to use your blob character to collect all of the scattered "Putties" (other blobs). You can punch as well as stretch out to grab things, drop down to levels below, etc. There are also plenty of objects to collect and interact with.

name: Puyo Puyo
description: Puyo Puyo is a popular puzzle game developed by Compile and first released in 1991 for the Game Boy handheld console. The game's unique blend of simple yet addictive gameplay has made it a beloved franchise among puzzle enthusiasts. Players are presented with a 3x3 grid of colored bubbles, and the objective is to clear the grid by making sets of three or four bubbles of the same color touch. When three bubbles of the same color touch, they are cleared from the grid, and when four bubbles of the same color touch, a special "sweep" is created that clears bubbles in a line. The game features a simple yet challenging formula, and its addictive nature has made it a staple of Nintendo consoles and a classic of the puzzle genre.

name: Puzzle Bobble
description: Puzzle Bobble (also known as Bust-a-Move) is a classic arcade puzzle game that was originally developed by Taito in 1994. While the game was initially released for arcades and consoles, it also became popular as a Flash game in the early 2000s. Flash versions of Puzzle Bobble were widely available on gaming websites and were known for their faithful recreation of the original gameplay. Gameplay: In Puzzle Bobble, the player controls a cannon at the bottom of the screen that shoots colored bubbles. The goal is to match three or more bubbles of the same color to clear them from the board. The game becomes progressively more challenging as the bubbles advance toward the bottom of the screen. Bubble Shooting: The player aims the cannon and shoots bubbles to match them with existing bubbles on the board. Matching: When three or more bubbles of the same color touch, they pop and are removed from the board. Chain Reactions: Clearing bubbles can cause others to fall, creating chain reactions for bonus points. Losing Condition: The game ends if the bubbles reach the bottom of the screen. Key Features of Flash Versions: Faithful Gameplay: Flash versions of Puzzle Bobble replicated the core mechanics of the original game. Simple Controls: Players could aim and shoot bubbles using the mouse, making it easy to play. Colorful Graphics: The Flash versions retained the vibrant, cartoonish visuals of the original game. Addictive Fun: The game’s simple yet challenging gameplay made it a favorite among casual gamers. How to Play Flash Puzzle Bobble: Since Adobe Flash is no longer supported, you can’t play Flash games directly in modern browsers. However, you can still enjoy Puzzle Bobble through the following methods: Flash Emulators: Use tools like Ruffle or Flashpoint to play Flash games offline. HTML5 Versions: Many websites have recreated Puzzle Bobble using HTML5, which works in modern browsers. Official Ports: Look for official versions of Puzzle Bobble on platforms like Steam, Nintendo Switch, or mobile app stores.

name: Puzzle Cube
description: Puzzle Cube Flash Game is a digital adaptation of the classic 3D puzzle that challenges players to solve the iconic Rubik's Cube. In this game, players can manipulate the cube by rotating its sides to match colors on each face. The gameplay mimics the physical cube, allowing users to twist and turn various sections to strategize their moves. Players can choose different difficulty levels, from beginner to advanced, depending on their familiarity with solving the cube. With a user-friendly interface and vibrant graphics, this flash game provides a great way to enjoy the Rubik's Cube experience online. Whether you're a seasoned cuber or a newcomer, the game offers an engaging way to test your problem-solving skills and improve your speed in solving the puzzle.

name: Puzzle Drop - Egypt
description: Drop pieces to solve the puzzle. Drop the pieces on the right spot.Puzzle Drop - Egypt is a puzzle game where players match falling blocks or tiles to clear them from the board. The game is themed around ancient Egypt, featuring symbols and visuals inspired by Egyptian culture. Below is a basic example of how you can create a simplified version of Puzzle Drop - Egypt using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. Game Concept: The player must match three or more identical tiles to clear them from the board. The tiles fall from the top of the screen, and the player can move and rotate them to create matches. The game ends if the tiles stack up and reach the top of the board.

name: Puzzle Drop - Space Adventure
description: Puzzle Drop - Space Adventure is a captivating and strategic puzzle game set in a space-themed environment. The goal is to drop shaped pieces into the correct spots to solve the puzzle. Players must carefully plan their moves to fit the pieces together perfectly, creating a complete image or filling the grid without gaps. It’s a fun and challenging game that combines spatial reasoning, problem-solving, and a touch of cosmic adventure. How to Play Puzzle Drop - Space Adventure: Objective: Drop the given pieces into the grid to fill it completely or recreate a specific image. Each piece must fit perfectly without overlapping or leaving gaps. Gameplay: Pieces of various shapes and sizes fall from the top of the screen. Use controls to rotate or move the pieces before dropping them into the grid. Place the pieces in the correct spots to complete the puzzle. Controls: Move Left/Right: Slide the piece horizontally to align it with the grid. Rotate: Spin the piece to fit into the available space. Drop: Release the piece to place it in the grid. Levels: The game starts with simple puzzles and gradually introduces more complex shapes and grids. Some levels may have obstacles or require you to recreate a specific space-themed image. Completion: The level is complete when all pieces are placed correctly, and the grid is filled or the image is recreated. Key Features of Puzzle Drop - Space Adventure: Space Theme: Enjoy cosmic visuals, including planets, stars, rockets, and galaxies. Strategic Gameplay: Requires careful planning and spatial awareness. Progressive Difficulty: Starts easy but becomes more challenging as you advance. Relaxing Yet Engaging: Combines calm gameplay with satisfying puzzle-solving.

name: Puzzle Fighting
description: Puzzle Fighting is unashamedly based on the Super Puzzle Fighter series of games by Capcom. The author mentions in the docs that he examined the Super Puzzle Fighter FAQ closely in order to mirror the original's rules as accurately as possible. Anyways the object of this game is to fill your opponent's screen with blocks, and you do so by collecting groups of same-colored stones into larger blocks, then destroying them with same-colored bombs. When you do so, more blocks will drop onto your opponent's screen.

name: Puzzle Fun-Pak
description: One of two "paks" of games released by the famous Apogee Software VERY early in their company's storied history (the other pack being the Adventure Fun-Pack), this collection contains 4 different games, of generally "okay" quality. Both packs were recently released by Apogee as freeware. The games contained in this collection are: Block Five: Apogee's take on the classic GO or Go-Moku game. Dolls: Select from three dolls (or multiple dolls) to dress up and customize. Clothing: Pick from five sets of male outfits and five sets of female outfits to style your dolls. Coloring Tools: Use fill tools to color in the dolls, outfits, and backgrounds, allowing for creative expression and personalization. Interactive Features: Voice Option: Enable the Voice option to make the dolls "talk," adding a playful and interactive element to the game. Creative Freedom: Combine different backgrounds, dolls, and outfits to create unique fashion scenes. Experiment with colors and designs to bring your creations to life. Key Features Six Backgrounds: A variety of settings to choose from for your fashion scenes. Three Dolls: Multiple dolls to dress up and customize. Ten Outfits: Five sets of male outfits and five sets of female outfits for diverse styling options. Coloring Tools: Fill tools to color in the dolls, outfits, and backgrounds. Voice Option: Enable the dolls to "talk" for added interactivity.

name: Radical Fishin'
description: Radical Fishin' is a fun, quirky action-arcade Flash game developed by Vlambeer, the same team behind Super Crate Box. It combines classic fishing mechanics with a ridiculous and over-the-top twist, making it a unique and memorable experience. The game offers a unique take on fishing, blending absurdity with arcade-style action. In Radical Fishin', instead of a traditional and relaxing fishing trip, you go for a wild, extreme fishing experience. It's a mixture of fishing, dodging obstacles, and launching fish into the air, all set to a fast-paced, retro-inspired backdrop. Fishing Line: At the start of each round, you drop your fishing line into the water, and as it descends, it catches fish that swim at various depths. The deeper you go, the more fish you catch. Fish come in different sizes, and some of them may be harder to catch than others. You’ll encounter a variety of fish, each with its own unique properties. Reel Back Up: After catching a bunch of fish, you need to reel yourself back to the surface. As you reel in the line, all the fish you’ve caught are launched into the air in an absurd and chaotic manner. The goal here is to control your character and dodge incoming obstacles while trying to maximize the number of fish you launch into the air. Avoiding sharks, bombs, and other enemies becomes key while you try to navigate your way to a bigger score. Upgrades: As you catch more fish, you earn money that can be used to purchase upgrades for your fishing gear. These upgrades can improve your fishing line's speed, effectiveness, and ability to catch more fish. Examples of upgrades include: Better fishing lines to catch larger fish more efficiently. Upgraded reels to help you pull in fish faster. Special hooks or tools that can attract more fish or reduce obstacles. Physics-Based Gameplay: The game is highly physics-driven, meaning the way fish move through the air and interact with one another is unpredictable. This randomness makes each round feel unique, and there’s a sense of fun chaos as you try to launch your catch back into the sky while avoiding obstacles. Obstacles and Hazards: The game isn't just about catching fish—it’s about surviving as well. As you reel yourself back up, you’ll need to dodge various obstacles like: Sharks that swim in your path and can damage you. Bombs that explode when you get too close, often knocking you back down into the water or causing you to lose a portion of your catch. Bubbles that might obscure your vision or mess with your line. The obstacles keep you on your toes, ensuring that the game never feels too easy. Levels and Progression: While Radical Fishin' doesn't have a traditional level structure, it features progressive difficulty. As you continue to catch more fish and earn upgrades, the hazards become more frequent and the fishing gets more challenging. Each time you upgrade your gear, you’re able to dive deeper into the water and catch more fish, but the danger level increases as well.

name: Radix: Beyond the Void
description: Radix: Beyond the Void is a 3D spaceship shooting game that draws inspiration from classics like Descent and Doom. Players pilot a spaceship through labyrinthine levels, engaging in fast-paced combat with enemies while navigating complex environments. While the level design may not match the polish of Descent, the game stands out with its impressive graphics (for its time), immersive sound effects, and unique control system that adds depth to the gameplay. Gameplay Overview Core Mechanics: Players control a spaceship in a fully 3D environment, navigating through tunnels, caves, and open areas. The game focuses on shooting enemies, dodging attacks, and completing objectives within each level. Combat: Engage in intense dogfights with enemy ships and turrets. Collect power-ups and weapons to enhance your ship’s capabilities. Movement and Controls: The ship’s movement is complex, requiring players to manage speed and direction. The ship can "strafe" (move side to side) in addition to moving forward, backward, and turning, adding a layer of strategy to navigation and combat. Level Design: Levels are maze-like and feature a mix of tight tunnels and open spaces. While the level design is functional, it may lack the refinement and variety seen in games like Descent. Key Features 3D Graphics: For its time, the game boasts impressive 3D visuals, with detailed environments and smooth rendering. Immersive Sound Effects: The sound design enhances the experience, with engine noises, weapon sounds, and explosions adding to the atmosphere. Unique Control System: The ship’s movement mechanics, including strafing and speed control, offer a challenging but rewarding gameplay experience. Power-Ups and Weapons: Collect upgrades to improve your ship’s firepower and survivability.

name: Raft Wars
description: Raft Wars is a turn-based strategy game where players control two brothers, Simon and his older brother, who must defend their treasure from greedy pirates and other enemies. Armed with tennis balls, grenades, and other weapons, players aim to defeat opponents by carefully calculating angles and power to hit their targets. The game’s humorous storyline, charming visuals, and challenging levels make it a memorable Flash game. Gameplay Overview Objective: Defeat all enemies on the opposing raft by launching projectiles at them. Protect your own raft and health while strategically taking out opponents. Turn-Based Mechanics: Players take turns with the enemy, aiming and shooting projectiles. Each turn requires careful calculation of angles and power to maximize damage. Weapons and Upgrades: Start with basic tennis balls and unlock more powerful weapons like grenades, rockets, and even a slingshot. Earn money by defeating enemies and use it to upgrade weapons or buy new ones. Levels and Enemies: The game features multiple levels, each with increasing difficulty and new enemy types. Enemies include pirates, ninjas, and even a giant baby, each with unique behaviors and attacks. Environment: The battlefield consists of two rafts floating on water, with obstacles like rocks and islands that can affect projectile trajectories. Key Features Humor and Storyline: The game’s lighthearted and humorous narrative adds charm to the gameplay. Weapon Variety: A wide range of weapons and upgrades keeps the gameplay fresh and exciting. Physics-Based Gameplay: Players must master angles and power to succeed, adding a layer of strategy. Challenging Levels: Increasing difficulty and unique enemies provide a satisfying challenge.

name: Raft Wars 2
description: Raft Wars 2 continues the humorous and strategic adventures of Simon and his older brother as they defend their treasure from a new wave of enemies. This turn-based strategy game combines physics-based gameplay with a quirky storyline, offering players more levels, weapons, and challenges than its predecessor. The game’s charm, accessibility, and increased depth make it a worthy follow-up to the original. Gameplay Overview Objective: Defeat all enemies on the opposing raft by launching projectiles at them. Protect your own raft and health while strategically taking out opponents. Turn-Based Mechanics: Players take turns with the enemy, aiming and shooting projectiles. Each turn requires careful calculation of angles and power to maximize damage. Weapons and Upgrades: Start with basic tennis balls and unlock more powerful weapons like grenades, rockets, and even a slingshot. Earn money by defeating enemies and use it to upgrade weapons or buy new ones. New weapons and upgrades are introduced, adding variety to the gameplay. Levels and Enemies: The game features multiple levels, each with increasing difficulty and new enemy types. Enemies include pirates, ninjas, and even a giant baby, each with unique behaviors and attacks. New levels and environments provide fresh challenges and visual variety. Environment: The battlefield consists of two rafts floating on water, with obstacles like rocks and islands that can affect projectile trajectories. New environmental elements and hazards are introduced to keep gameplay engaging. Key Features Humor and Storyline: The game’s lighthearted and humorous narrative adds charm to the gameplay. Weapon Variety: A wide range of weapons and upgrades keeps the gameplay fresh and exciting. Physics-Based Gameplay: Players must master angles and power to succeed, adding a layer of strategy. Challenging Levels: Increasing difficulty and unique enemies provide a satisfying challenge. New Content: Additional levels, weapons, and enemies expand on the original game’s content.

name: Ragdoll Avalanche
description: Ragdoll Avalanche is a physics-based platformer where players guide a floppy ragdoll character through a series of increasingly challenging and bizarre levels. The game’s humor, unpredictable physics, and creative level design make it a memorable and entertaining experience. Players must use their wits (and a bit of luck) to survive the chaos and reach the end of each level. Gameplay Overview Objective: Navigate the ragdoll character through each level to reach the goal. Avoid hazards like spikes, explosions, and falling objects while using the environment to your advantage. Physics-Based Mechanics: The ragdoll character moves in a floppy, unpredictable manner, adding a layer of challenge and humor to the gameplay. Players must manipulate the character’s limbs and momentum to overcome obstacles. Level Design: Levels are filled with creative and often absurd hazards, such as swinging axes, rolling boulders, and explosive barrels. Each level introduces new challenges and environmental elements to keep the gameplay fresh. Interactive Environment: Players can interact with objects in the environment, such as levers, switches, and platforms, to create paths or avoid dangers. The environment is often as much a hazard as it is a tool for progression. Humor and Chaos: The game’s humor comes from the ragdoll’s exaggerated physics and the slapstick situations players find themselves in. Unexpected events and chaotic level designs ensure that no two playthroughs are exactly the same. Key Features Physics-Based Gameplay: The ragdoll’s floppy movements and unpredictable physics create a unique and humorous experience. Creative Level Design: Each level is filled with imaginative hazards and challenges. Interactive Environment: Players can manipulate objects in the environment to progress or avoid dangers. Humor and Chaos: The game’s slapstick humor and chaotic events make it a fun and lighthearted experience.

name: Ragdoll Avalanche 2
description: Ragdoll Avalanche 2 continues the chaotic and humorous adventures of the floppy ragdoll character, offering players more levels, hazards, and opportunities for slapstick comedy. The game’s physics-based mechanics, creative level design, and absurd humor make it a worthy follow-up to the original. Players must navigate through increasingly bizarre and challenging levels, using their wits (and a bit of luck) to survive the chaos. Humor and Chaos: The game’s humor comes from the ragdoll’s exaggerated physics and the slapstick situations players find themselves in. name: Rage
description: Rage is a top-down shooter where players take on the role of a lone warrior battling against endless waves of enemies. The game’s fast-paced action, diverse arsenal of weapons, and challenging gameplay make it a thrilling experience. Players must survive as long as possible, using strategy and quick reflexes to fend off increasingly difficult enemies. Gameplay Overview Objective: Survive waves of enemies for as long as possible. Defeat enemies to earn points and unlock new weapons and power-ups. Combat Mechanics: Players can move in all directions and shoot at enemies using a variety of weapons. Weapons include pistols, shotguns, machine guns, and more, each with unique characteristics. Power-ups such as health packs, ammo, and temporary boosts can be collected to aid in survival. Enemies: Enemies come in various types, each with different behaviors and attack patterns. Waves become increasingly difficult, with more enemies and stronger variants appearing over time. Levels and Progression: The game features multiple levels, each with its own unique layout and enemy types. Players can unlock new weapons and upgrades as they progress, adding variety and strategy to the gameplay. Difficulty: The game is known for its high difficulty, requiring quick reflexes and strategic thinking to survive. Players must constantly move and adapt to the changing battlefield to avoid being overwhelmed. Key Features Fast-Paced Action: The game’s intense and fast-paced gameplay keeps players on their toes. Diverse Arsenal: A wide range of weapons and power-ups adds variety and strategy to the combat. Challenging Enemies: Various enemy types and increasingly difficult waves provide a satisfying challenge. Retro-Style Graphics: The game’s pixel art style and retro visuals add to its charm and nostalgic appeal.

name: Ragnarok
description: Ragnarok (also known as Valhalla in some regions) is a DOS-based roguelike role-playing game that stands out from its peers by using actual graphics instead of the traditional ASCII characters commonly found in other roguelikes. Developed in the late 1980s or early 1990s, Ragnarok offers a classic roguelike experience with procedurally generated content, challenging gameplay, and a focus on exploration, character progression, and survival. Ragnarok is a roguelike RPG that immerses players in a procedurally generated fantasy world filled with danger, treasure, and adventure. Inspired by Norse mythology, the game tasks players with exploring dungeons, battling monsters, and collecting powerful items to survive and grow stronger. Unlike many roguelikes of its time, Ragnarok uses graphical tiles instead of ASCII characters, making it more visually accessible while retaining the depth and complexity of the genre. Gameplay Overview Exploration: Players navigate through randomly generated dungeons, uncovering rooms, corridors, and hidden secrets. The gameworld is filled with monsters, traps, treasure, and other surprises. Character Progression: Players gain experience points by defeating enemies, which can be used to level up and improve their character’s stats. Character development is a key aspect of the game, with players customizing their abilities and playstyle. Combat: Combat is turn-based, requiring strategic thinking to defeat enemies while conserving resources. Players must manage their health, stamina, and equipment to survive increasingly difficult encounters. Items and Equipment: Players can find and collect a variety of items, including weapons, armor, potions, and magical artifacts. Equipment can be upgraded or swapped to improve the character’s effectiveness in combat. Permadeath: Like most roguelikes, Ragnarok features permadeath, meaning that if the player’s character dies, they must start over from the beginning. This adds tension and encourages careful decision-making. Randomization: The gameworld, including dungeons, enemies, and items, is randomly generated each time a new game is started, ensuring a unique experience with every playthrough. Key Features Graphical Tiles: Unlike many roguelikes, Ragnarok uses graphical tiles instead of ASCII characters, making it more visually appealing and accessible. Procedurally Generated Content: Randomly generated dungeons, enemies, and items ensure high replayability. Turn-Based Combat: Strategic, turn-based combat requires careful planning and resource management. Character Progression: Players can level up and customize their character’s abilities and equipment. Permadeath: The risk of permanent death adds tension and stakes to every decision.

name: Rags to Riches: The Financial Market Simulation
description: Rags to Riches is a simulation of being a stock broker, circa the early 90's. You start off with some cash, and you need to use your limited funds to buy investments and hire people to help you. By shrewdly investing, you can make lots of money and go on shopping trips to spend your $$$. This demo version gives you limited options (you can only hire a secretary and a pit runner) but you can get a taste of how the full game will play. (Tip: To hire your first employees, make sure J.E.A is selected on the Rolodex, then click the phone.

name: Raiden
description: The original "Raiden" is a classic vertical scrolling shooter game where players control a fighter jet, navigating through waves of enemy aircraft and ground units. The gameplay is fast-paced and emphasizes dodging enemy fire while shooting down foes and collecting power-ups to enhance weaponry. In a typical Flash adaptation of "Raiden," players would experience: Gameplay Mechanics: Players maneuver their jet up the screen, shooting at enemies and avoiding bullets. The game features various power-ups, such as upgraded weapons, speed boosts, and bombs. Levels and Bosses: The game is divided into levels, each culminating in a challenging boss battle. Each level has unique enemy patterns and environmental obstacles. Multiplayer Options: Some versions may allow for co-op play, letting two players team up against the enemy forces. Visuals and Sound: The graphics are often retro-inspired, with vibrant colors and classic 8-bit or 16-bit soundtracks that evoke nostalgia. If you’re interested in playing or discussing strategies, let me know!

name: RaidenX
description: "Raiden" is a classic vertical scrolling shooter game that originated in arcades in the early 1990s. If you're looking for flash versions of Raiden or similar shooting games, there are several fan-made adaptations available online. These usually retain the core gameplay elements: controlling a fighter jet, dodging enemy fire, and taking down waves of enemies. You can often find these games on various gaming websites that host Flash games, though keep in mind that many browsers have discontinued support for Flash. You might want to look for alternatives or remastered versions on platforms like Steam or other indie game sites. Are you looking for gameplay tips or recommendations for similar games?

name: Railway Mysteries
description: Find all the hidden objects in this Railway Mystery game. Click to find an object or difference.Railway Mysteries is an engaging hidden object puzzle game built using HTML5, making it accessible on both desktop and mobile browsers. Players step into the role of a detective aboard a vintage train, tasked with solving mysteries by finding hidden objects, uncovering clues, and piecing together the story. The game combines visual exploration, problem-solving, and story-driven gameplay to create an immersive and interactive experience. Gameplay Overview Objective: Explore beautifully illustrated scenes aboard a train to find hidden objects. Use the discovered items to solve puzzles and progress through the story. Hidden Object Mechanics: Each scene contains a list of objects that players must find within a cluttered environment. Objects are cleverly hidden, requiring keen observation and attention to detail. Puzzle Solving: Found objects are often used to solve puzzles or unlock new areas of the train. Puzzles range from simple item combinations to more complex logic challenges. Storyline: The game features a captivating narrative with twists and turns, keeping players engaged. Players interact with passengers, uncover secrets, and solve the overarching mystery. Progression: As players advance, the scenes and puzzles become more challenging. New areas of the train are unlocked, revealing more of the story and hidden objects. Key Features HTML5-Based: Playable directly in your browser without the need for downloads or plugins. Interactive Scenes: Beautifully illustrated, interactive environments to explore. Hidden Object Challenges: Find cleverly hidden items in cluttered scenes. Engaging Puzzles: Solve a variety of puzzles to progress through the story. Immersive Storyline: A captivating mystery narrative with multiple layers. Responsive Design: Optimized for both desktop and mobile devices.

name: Rainforest Jump
description: Rainforest Jump is an adrenaline-pumping platformer game where players navigate through the dense and dangerous rainforest. The goal is simple: move, jump, and survive! Avoid falling obstacles, dodge hazards, and leap over gaps to stay alive. With its vibrant visuals, challenging gameplay, and immersive rainforest setting, Rainforest Jump offers a thrilling experience for players of all ages. Gameplay Overview Objective: Control your character as they run through the rainforest. Jump over gaps, avoid falling obstacles, and dodge hazards to survive as long as possible. Movement and Controls: Use intuitive controls to move left, right, and jump. Timing is key—mistimed jumps or movements can lead to crushing defeat! Hazards and Obstacles: Watch out for falling logs, rolling boulders, and other rainforest dangers. The further you progress, the faster and more challenging the obstacles become. Survival: The game tests your reflexes and precision as you try to survive for as long as possible. Compete for high scores and challenge your friends to beat your record. Key Features Fast-Paced Gameplay: Quick reflexes and sharp timing are essential for survival. Vibrant Rainforest Setting: Immerse yourself in a lush, colorful rainforest environment. Simple Controls: Easy-to-learn mechanics make it accessible for all players. Increasing Difficulty: The game gets faster and more challenging as you progress. Endless Fun: Compete for high scores and see how long you can survive.

name: Raku Master
description: Raku Master is a tile-flipping puzzle game developed by Soleau Software, known for its clever mechanics and minimalist presentation. The goal of the game is simple yet challenging: flip all the red tiles to gray by selecting rows and flipping the tiles within them. With its strategic gameplay, quirky visuals, and increasing difficulty, Raku Master is perfect for puzzle enthusiasts who enjoy logical challenges. Gameplay Overview Objective: Flip all the red tiles on the grid to gray using the fewest moves possible. The game provides the minimum number of moves required to solve the puzzle, adding an extra layer of challenge. Mechanics: Select a row (horizontal, vertical, or diagonal) to flip all the tiles in that row to their opposite sides (red to gray or gray to red). Plan your moves carefully, as each flip affects multiple tiles and can complicate the puzzle. Difficulty: Puzzles start simple but become increasingly complex as you progress. The game tests your logical thinking and strategic planning skills. Presentation: The game features a minimalist design with a grid of tiles and a creepy floating eye (the "Raku Master") that watches over your progress. The visuals and graphical assets are typical of Soleau Software’s style, with a focus on functionality over flashiness. Key Features Strategic Gameplay: Requires careful planning and logical thinking to solve each puzzle. Multiple Row Directions: Flip tiles horizontally, vertically, or diagonally for varied gameplay. Minimum Move Challenge: The game tells you the minimum number of moves required, encouraging efficiency. Quirky Visuals: The "Raku Master" (a floating eye) adds a unique and slightly eerie charm to the game. Increasing Difficulty: Puzzles become more complex as you advance, keeping the game engaging.

name: Rally-Sport
description: Rally-Sport is a "cult classic" vector-graphics-based 3D rally racing game. It's technically impressive, and was created by a single developer. One of its big features is a track editor to make your own tracks (see the extra files to download it). The race begins, and you race one-on-one against the computer controlled car around the track. The graphics are impressive considering that no 3D card is necessary, however the demo/beta nature of the software is evident since there is not a lot of gameplay to go along with the admittedly gorgeous visuals (for a DOS game from 1996).

name: Rallyx
description: Rallyx is a clone of the classic Namco arcade game Rally-X. In the game you drive your car around collecting flags and avoiding enemy cars. There is a mini-map which you can glance at to see where the other cars currently are within the maze, but looking at it takes your attention away from your actual car which makes it tricky to use. If you are able to collect all the flags before losing all your lives (cars) you can progress to the next (very similar) stage. The game plays well enough and the graphics are passable although certainly not flashy.

name: Rampcube
description: Rampcube is a Klax-like game (released around the time that Klax became popular) which involves dropping differed color pieces down a grid. The main differences between this and Klax are that here you are trying to make cubes not lines, and the perspective is warped making it difficult to pay attention to where you're dropping the cubes. Seriously the perspective makes this game difficult to get used to, especially since you only have a limited amount of time to drop your piece before it's automatically dropped for you.

name: Ranadin
description: Ranadin is a turn-based RPG with an overhead perspective and CGA graphics, offering a straightforward yet challenging gameplay experience. Developed in the early days of PC gaming, the game focuses on exploration, survival, and treasure hunting in a dangerous fantasy world. While the mechanics are simple, the game’s difficulty lies in surviving the relentless attacks of monsters like skeleton warriors, which often make it hard to progress. With its retro charm and old-school RPG vibes, Ranadin is a nostalgic trip for fans of classic dungeon crawlers. Gameplay Overview Objective: Explore the game world, collect items and treasure, and try to survive as long as possible. The primary challenge is staying alive, as monsters like skeleton warriors can quickly overwhelm you. Turn-Based Mechanics: Players and enemies take turns moving and attacking on a grid-based map. Combat is straightforward, with basic attack and defense options. Exploration: Navigate through dungeons and other environments to find treasure, weapons, and other useful items. The game encourages exploration, but danger lurks around every corner. Survival: Monsters are relentless, and death can come quickly if you’re not careful. The game’s difficulty lies in managing resources and avoiding encounters with powerful enemies early on. Backstory: The game includes a backstory in the manual, but the focus is on gameplay rather than narrative. Players are free to explore and create their own adventures. Key Features Turn-Based Combat: Simple, grid-based combat mechanics. Overhead Perspective: Classic top-down view for exploration and movement. CGA Graphics: Colorful (for its time) and retro visuals that evoke the early days of PC gaming. Exploration and Survival: Focus on exploring the world, collecting treasure, and staying alive. High Difficulty: Monsters are tough, and survival is the main challenge.

name: Randzu
description: Randzu is a strategy board game for PC that brings the classic "5-in-a-row" concept to life. Similar to Gomoku, the game challenges two players to take turns placing pieces on a grid, aiming to create a line of five pieces of their own color. With multiple board sizes, adjustable difficulty levels, and the option to play against the computer or a friend, Randzu offers a simple yet deeply strategic experience for fans of abstract board games. Gameplay Overview Objective: Be the first to create a horizontal, vertical, or diagonal line of five pieces of your color on the board. Game Modes: Two-Player Mode: Play against a friend, taking turns to place pieces. Single-Player Mode: Play against the computer, with multiple difficulty levels to choose from. Board Sizes: Choose from three board sizes: 9x9, 15x15, or 21x21. Larger boards increase the complexity and strategic depth of the game. Controls: The game uses keyboard controls for placing pieces (mouse support is available only in the registered version). Players navigate the grid and place their pieces using intuitive keyboard commands. Strategy: While the rules are simple, the game requires careful planning, foresight, and tactical thinking to outmaneuver your opponent. Blocking your opponent’s moves while building your own line of five is key to winning. Key Features Classic 5-in-a-Row Gameplay: Simple rules with deep strategic possibilities. Multiple Board Sizes: Choose from 9x9, 15x15, or 21x21 grids to adjust the difficulty and complexity. Single-Player and Two-Player Modes: Play against the computer or challenge a friend. Adjustable Difficulty: Multiple AI difficulty levels for single-player mode. Keyboard Controls: Easy-to-use keyboard navigation for placing pieces.

name: Rapid Math
description: Train your Math skills in this rapid game. Type the correct answer.Rapid Math is an HTML-based calculation game designed to test and improve your math skills in a fun and engaging way. Perfect for players of all ages, the game challenges you to solve arithmetic problems quickly and accurately. With its simple interface, timed challenges, and increasing difficulty, Rapid Math is a great way to sharpen your mental math abilities while having fun. Gameplay Overview Objective: Solve as many math problems as possible within a given time limit. Answer correctly to earn points and progress to more challenging levels. Types of Problems: The game includes basic arithmetic operations: addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division. Problems range from simple to complex, depending on the difficulty level. Timed Challenges: Each round is timed, adding pressure and excitement to the gameplay. Quick thinking and accuracy are essential to achieve high scores. Difficulty Levels: The game starts with easy problems and gradually increases in difficulty as you progress. Higher levels introduce more complex calculations and shorter time limits. Scoring: Earn points for each correct answer. Compete for the highest score and challenge yourself to improve with each playthrough. Key Features HTML-Based: Play directly in your browser without the need for downloads or installations. Fast-Paced Gameplay: Timed challenges keep the game exciting and engaging. Multiple Operations: Practice addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division. Increasing Difficulty: Problems become more challenging as you advance. Score Tracking: Compete for high scores and track your progress.

name: Raptor: Call of the Shadows
description: Raptor: Call of the Shadows is a vertical scrolling shoot-'em-up game developed by Cygnus Studios and released in the early 1990s. Known for its stunning graphics (for its time) and Sound Blaster sound effects, the game offers a thrilling and addictive experience. Players take control of a fighter jet, blasting through waves of enemies, earning money, and upgrading their ship to become more powerful. With its fast-paced action, rewarding progression system, and retro charm, Raptor remains a beloved title among fans of the genre. Gameplay Overview Objective: Pilot your fighter jet through multiple levels, destroying enemies and avoiding their attacks. Complete missions and survive to the end of each level to progress. Combat: Engage in intense aerial combat, shooting down enemy planes, tanks, and other obstacles. Collect power-ups to enhance your ship’s weapons and abilities. Earning Money: Destroy enemies to earn cash, which can be used to purchase upgrades between levels. The more enemies you defeat, the more money you earn, incentivizing aggressive play. Upgrades: Spend your earnings on upgrades such as stronger weapons, shields, and special abilities. Customize your ship to suit your playstyle and tackle increasingly difficult levels. Levels and Difficulty: The game features multiple levels, each with unique enemies, bosses, and environments. Difficulty increases as you progress, requiring better strategy and upgraded equipment. Key Features Stunning Graphics: For its time, the game boasts impressive visuals with detailed sprites and vibrant environments. Sound Blaster Support: Immersive sound effects and music enhance the gameplay experience. Upgrade System: Earn money to buy upgrades, adding a layer of strategy and progression. Fast-Paced Action: Intense, non-stop shooting action keeps players on their toes. Retro Appeal: A classic shoot-'em-up that captures the essence of 90s arcade-style gaming.

name: RasterMind
description: Rastermind is a digital adaptation of the classic Mastermind board game, where players must deduce a hidden sequence of colors through logic and trial-and-error. The game challenges your problem-solving skills as you try to guess the correct combination of four colors within a limited number of attempts. While the game stays true to the mechanics of the original, its user interface can be a bit unclear, which adds an extra layer of challenge for players. Gameplay Overview Objective: Guess the hidden sequence of four colors within a limited number of attempts. Use the feedback from each guess to refine your strategy and solve the puzzle. Guessing Mechanics: Select four colors from a palette to make your guess. After submitting your guess, the game provides feedback using pegs: Green Peg: Indicates a correct color in the correct position. Blue Peg: Indicates a correct color but in the wrong position. Feedback System: If none of the colors in your guess are correct, no visual feedback is given, which can make the game more challenging. Use the feedback from each guess to eliminate possibilities and narrow down the correct sequence. User Interface: The interface is functional but not super intuitive. Players start at the top left, choose their colors, and press the Register Move button to submit their guess. The lack of feedback for incorrect guesses can be frustrating but adds to the game’s difficulty. Key Features Classic Mastermind Gameplay: A faithful digital version of the classic board game. Logical Deduction: Requires strategic thinking and problem-solving skills. Feedback System: Green and blue pegs provide clues to help you solve the puzzle. Challenging Interface: The unclear UI adds an extra layer of difficulty, making the game more rewarding for persistent players.

name: Ratillery
description: Ratillery is a turn-based artillery game that pays homage to classic "tank" games like Tank Wars, Scorched Earth, and Microsoft Gorillas. Players take turns aiming and firing their weapons, adjusting for angle, power, and wind to hit their opponent. With options for two-player battles, single-player against the computer, or even watching the computer play against itself, Ratillery offers a fun and strategic experience for fans of the genre. Additional features, like obstacles and hidden input values, add variety and challenge to the gameplay. Gameplay Overview Objective: Take turns firing at your opponent’s tank, adjusting your aim and power to land a direct hit. The first player to destroy their opponent wins the round. Turn-Based Mechanics: Players take turns adjusting their tank’s angle, power, and weapon type before firing. Wind speed and direction add an extra layer of strategy, requiring players to compensate for environmental factors. Game Modes: Two-Player Mode: Compete against a friend in a head-to-head battle. Single-Player Mode: Play against the computer, with adjustable difficulty levels. Computer vs. Computer: Watch the AI battle itself for fun or to learn new strategies. Additional Features: Obstacles: Some levels include hanging crates or other barriers that players must shoot around. Hidden Input Values: Enable this option to hide your input values (angle, power, etc.) from your human opponent, adding an extra layer of challenge. Weapons and Strategy: Choose from different weapons, each with unique properties and effects. Plan your shots carefully, as missed shots can leave you vulnerable to your opponent’s next move. Key Features Classic Artillery Gameplay: Inspired by beloved games like Tank Wars and Scorched Earth. Multiple Game Modes: Play against a friend, the computer, or watch the computer battle itself. Environmental Factors: Wind speed and direction affect your shots, requiring careful adjustments. Obstacles: Hanging crates and other barriers add complexity to the battlefield. Hidden Input Values: Keep your strategy secret from your opponent for a more challenging experience.

name: Ratmaz
description: Ratmaz is a simple first-person perspective maze game where the object is to find the exit before time runs out. You play a rat, and you're looking for the hole to escape the maze. That's about all there is to it. CGA graphics for the walls and a timer are shown on the screen, and there's also a mini-map of sorts, but it only shows where you actually move, not what you've seen, so it's not super useful since you can't waste time moving to every square in the maze. (I'm not sure of the status of this game, it possibly was originally sold, but there is no information in the game or online anywhere about it, or about the company that made it.

name: RatMaze1989
description: RatMaze is a text-mode action/maze game where players must navigate through a series of mazes, collecting stars while avoiding chasing rats. The game’s fast-paced gameplay and increasing difficulty make it a thrilling experience, even with its basic mechanics. With seven mazes to explore and only three lives to spare, RatMaze tests your speed, strategy, and ability to stay one step ahead of the relentless rats. Gameplay Overview Objective: Navigate through the maze and collect all the stars before the rats catch you. Avoid the rats (represented by X’s) to survive and progress to the next maze. Maze Navigation: Use the keyboard to move your character (represented by a symbol, e.g., @) through the maze. The maze layout is displayed in text mode, with walls, stars, and rats represented by simple characters. Rats: Rats chase you through the maze, and if they catch you, you lose a life. The rats’ movement is fast and relentless, adding tension to the gameplay. Mazes: The game features seven mazes, each with increasing difficulty. Later mazes have more complex layouts and faster rats, making survival a challenge. Lives: You start with three lives. If you lose all your lives, the game ends. The difficulty ramps up quickly, so seeing all seven mazes is no easy feat. Key Features Text-Mode Graphics: Simple, ASCII-based visuals that focus on gameplay rather than flashy graphics. Fast-Paced Gameplay: Quick movement and relentless rats keep the game exciting. Seven Mazes: Each maze offers a unique layout and increasing difficulty. Challenging Difficulty: With only three lives, the game requires skill and strategy to progress. Basic Mechanics: Easy to learn but hard to master, making it accessible yet rewarding.

name: Ravage
description: Ravage is a game that is seemingly heavily influenced by Raptor and Tyrian which appeared in 1994 and 1995, respectively. It's a vertical shooter with great graphics including parallax scrolling, pumping techno soundtrack, and decent sound effects. Your goal, as usual for shoot-em-ups, is to shoot everything and avoid getting shot! If you run out of lives, you'll need to start the level over again from the beginning. While no powerups appear during gameplay, you earn credits which can be used to purchase upgrades after each level, including more extra lives. Only two levels are available to play in the shareware version.

name: Ray Wars
description: Ray Wars is a vertical shooting game, sort of like Space Invaders, but a lot more pointless. You control a ship, and randomly aliens will appear on the screen. You must shoot them. Of course, they appear more quickly than you can destroy them, so your quest is futile from the start.
