description: "Vegetables Farm" is a delightful and colorful puzzle game where players must clear a farm full of vegetables by clicking on groups of three or more identical vegetables. The game combines elements of match-3 gameplay with a charming farm theme, making it both relaxing and challenging. The goal is to remove all vegetables from the farm by strategically matching them. Game Description: Objective: Clear the farm by clicking on groups of three or more identical vegetables. Gameplay: The farm is represented as a grid filled with various vegetables, such as carrots, tomatoes, potatoes, and cucumbers. Players click on groups of three or more adjacent vegetables of the same type to remove them. When a group is removed, the vegetables above fall down to fill the gaps, potentially creating new matches. Vegetable Types: The game features a variety of vegetables, each with its own unique color and design. Examples include carrots (orange), tomatoes (red), potatoes (brown), cucumbers (green), and more. Scoring: Players earn points for each group of vegetables they remove. Larger groups or chain reactions result in higher scores. Special Features: Power-Ups: Special vegetables or power-ups can be introduced to clear large areas or create explosive effects. Timer: Some levels may include a timer to add urgency to the gameplay. Levels: The game includes multiple levels, each with a unique layout and increasing difficulty.

name: Velcro Mind
description: Velcro Mind is a unique and original arcade-style game that stands out for its creative concept and vibrant visuals. The goal is to control a ship that grabs colored balls floating around the screen and delivers them to the correct colored hand on the side. While the premise may sound simple, the game's fast-paced action and colorful design make it an engaging and enjoyable experience. Featuring nice graphics and SoundBlaster-compatible sound effects, Velcro Mind is a hidden gem for fans of retro gaming and innovative mechanics. How to Play: Control Your Ship: Use the arrow keys or other controls to move your ship around the screen. Grab Colored Balls: Position your ship to grab floating balls of different colors. Deliver to Correct Hand: Take each ball to the corresponding colored hand on the side of the screen. Avoid Obstacles: Steer clear of enemies or hazards that can damage your ship or steal your balls. Score Points: Earn points by delivering balls quickly and accurately, aiming for a high score. Features: Original Concept: The game's unique mechanics set it apart from traditional arcade games. Colorful Graphics: Vibrant and eye-catching visuals enhance the gameplay experience. SoundBlaster Support: The game includes sound effects, though it lacks background music. Fast-Paced Action: The gameplay is quick and challenging, requiring precision and quick reflexes. Nostalgic Appeal: Perfect for fans of retro gaming and innovative arcade titles.

name: Vendetta
description: Vendetta is a shooting gallery style game where your goal is simple: Shoot all of the gangsters (?) that pop up into the many windows / doors / other areas that you can see. You'll need to watch the arrow near the top which indicates that a bad guy has popped up off the screen in that direction, then scroll over there with your mouse. That's about all there is to it; I don't know if there are levels or other gameplay elements, but I played for awhile and nothing else happened. The graphics are decent enough, but compared to something like Shooting Gallery this game won't hold your interest for very long. Also having to scroll the viewpoint with the mouse is janky and overly difficult, given that you don't have much time to react when a baddie pops up.

name: venge.io
description: Overview: Venge.io is an action-packed multiplayer shooter that immerses players in fast-paced combat across a variety of vibrant arenas. With a focus on skill-based gameplay, players engage in intense battles, utilizing an array of weapons and abilities to dominate their opponents. Gameplay Mechanics: Controls: Move using WASD or arrow keys, aim with the mouse, and shoot with left-click. Special abilities are activated with designated keys. Objective: Compete against other players in a battle to earn points by eliminating opponents. The player with the highest score at the end of the match wins. Weapons: Choose from a diverse selection of weapons, each with unique characteristics and playstyles. Players can find and upgrade weapons during matches. Abilities: Utilize special abilities to gain advantages in combat, such as speed boosts or defensive shields. Visuals and Audio: Venge.io features colorful, stylized graphics with dynamic environments that enhance the action. The animations are smooth, and the sound effects and music create an immersive atmosphere that keeps players engaged. Target Audience: This game appeals to fans of competitive shooters and action games, attracting both casual players and dedicated gamers looking for fast-paced multiplayer fun. Platforms: Venge.io is accessible in web browsers, allowing players to jump into matches on desktops, laptops, and even mobile devices. Conclusion: With its thrilling gameplay and engaging combat mechanics, Venge.io invites players to prove their skills in an exciting multiplayer arena. Can you rise to the top and claim victory over your rivals?

name: Vertrix
description: Vertrix is a vibrant and engaging DOS puzzle game that takes inspiration from the classic Columns and Tetris formulas, while adding its own unique twists to the genre. The gameplay revolves around matching falling 1x3 blocks to create sets of three or more identical colors. However, Vertrix expands on the traditional mechanics by allowing matches to be formed not only horizontally and vertically, but also diagonally and in box formations. This added complexity, combined with a wider variety of colors, makes the game both challenging and rewarding. Visually, Vertrix is appealing, with colorful graphics that enhance the gameplay experience. The inclusion of Soundblaster-compatible sound effects adds an extra layer of immersion, making the game feel more polished and dynamic. The two-player simultaneous mode is a standout feature, allowing players to compete head-to-head in a race to outmatch each other, adding a competitive edge to the puzzle-solving fun. For fans of Tetris, Columns, or puzzle games in general, Vertrix is a fantastic choice. Its blend of familiar mechanics and innovative features creates a fresh and enjoyable experience. Whether you're playing solo or challenging a friend, Vertrix offers hours of addictive gameplay. If you’re looking for a retro puzzle game with a bit of a twist, this one is definitely worth checking out!

name: Vex
description: "Vex" is an exciting platformer game that challenges players to navigate through a series of intricate levels filled with obstacles, traps, and enemies. Players control a stick figure character as they jump, slide, and climb through various environments, aiming to reach the end of each level while collecting gems and avoiding dangers. The gameplay is characterized by smooth controls and fast-paced action, allowing for fluid movement and precise maneuvers. Each level introduces new challenges, such as spikes, moving platforms, and tricky puzzles that test players' reflexes and problem-solving skills. With its minimalist graphics, engaging level design, and addictive gameplay, "Vex" offers a captivating experience for fans of platforming games, encouraging players to improve their skills and achieve high scores as they progress through increasingly challenging stages.

It is the sequel to the original Vex and builds upon its predecessor's success with more levels, improved mechanics, and enhanced visuals. Known for its fast-paced gameplay, precise controls, and difficult obstacles, Vex 2 has become a favorite among fans of skill-based platformers. While Flash games are no longer widely supported due to the discontinuation of Adobe Flash, Vex 2 remains a standout title in the genre. Key Features: Precise Platforming Mechanics: Players control a stick figure character and navigate through a series of increasingly difficult levels. The game requires precise timing, quick reflexes, and mastery of movement mechanics like running, jumping, sliding, and wall-climbing. Diverse Levels: Vex 2 features over 40 levels, each with unique obstacles, traps, and challenges. Levels are divided into acts, with each act introducing new mechanics and increasing difficulty. Challenging Obstacles: Players must avoid hazards such as spikes, saw blades, lasers, moving platforms, and more. The game is known for its high difficulty, requiring patience and practice to complete. Checkpoint System: Levels include checkpoints, allowing players to respawn at certain points instead of restarting the entire level. This system helps mitigate frustration while still maintaining a high level of challenge. Custom Level Editor: Vex 2 includes a level editor that allows players to create and share their own custom levels. This feature adds endless replayability and creativity to the game. Smooth Controls: The game features responsive and intuitive controls, which are essential for navigating the precise platforming challenges. Players can use both keyboard and mouse inputs for movement and actions. Minimalist Visuals: The game uses a simple, clean art style with a focus on gameplay rather than complex graphics. The stick figure character and level designs are easy to read, ensuring that players can focus on the challenges. Leaderboards: Players can compete for the fastest completion times on each level, adding a competitive element to the game.

name: Vex 3
description: Vex 3 is a fast-paced and challenging platformer game that tests your reflexes, timing, and problem-solving skills. Navigate through spikes, saw blades, moving platforms, and other hazards. Some levels require precise timing and quick reflexes to avoid enemies or complete sections. Challenges: Traps and obstacles become more complex as you progress. Enemies and moving hazards add to the difficulty. Limited checkpoints mean you may need to restart sections if you fail. High Difficulty: The game is known for being challenging, requiring patience and skill to master. Checkpoint System: Save your progress at checkpoints to avoid restarting the entire level.

name: Vexed
description: Vexed is a classic and intellectually stimulating puzzle game now available in HTML5, making it accessible on modern browsers and devices. The goal is to clear the board by moving similar blocks together, causing them to disappear. With its simple yet challenging mechanics, Vexed offers a satisfying and rewarding experience for puzzle enthusiasts. The game requires strategic planning and careful movement of blocks to ensure that all blocks are removed to advance to the next level. How to Play: Move Blocks: Drag blocks to an empty spot on the board to reposition them. Match Blocks: Move two or more identical blocks next to each other to make them disappear. Clear the Board: Strategically remove all the blocks to complete the level and advance to the next one. Plan Ahead: Think carefully about your moves, as some blocks may become stuck if you don’t clear them in the right order. Features: Classic Puzzle Gameplay: The game retains the timeless mechanics of the original Vexed, offering a nostalgic yet fresh experience. HTML5 Compatibility: Playable on modern browsers and devices without the need for additional plugins. Increasing Difficulty: Each level introduces new challenges and more complex layouts, keeping the gameplay engaging. Relaxing Yet Challenging: The game is perfect for unwinding while still providing a satisfying mental challenge.

name: Vexed Zoobies
description: Vexed Zoobies is a challenging and strategic puzzle game that tasks players with moving and matching similar blocks to remove them from the board. Here's a detailed description of the game: Gameplay Mechanics: Objective: The primary goal is to remove all blocks from the board by moving and matching similar blocks together. The game is won when the entire board is cleared. Block Movement: Dragging Blocks: You can drag blocks to an empty spot to move them. The blocks can only move in the direction of the empty spot if the path is clear. Matching Blocks: When two or more similar blocks are moved next to each other, they are matched and removed from the board. Game Flow: Initial Setup: The game starts with a grid filled with various blocks. Some spots may be empty, providing opportunities for moving blocks. Moving and Matching: Drag blocks to empty spots to create matches of similar blocks. When blocks are matched, they are removed, and new blocks may fall into place, potentially creating new matches. Clearing the Board: Continue moving and matching blocks until the entire board is cleared. Level Progression: The game is divided into levels, each with increasing difficulty. As you progress, the grids become more complex, and the number of blocks increases, requiring more strategic thinking and planning. Hints and Assistance: Hints: If you get stuck, the game may offer hints to show possible moves or highlight blocks that can be matched. Undo: Some versions of the game might include an undo feature, allowing you to reverse your last move and try a different strategy. Visuals and Sound: Graphics: The game features clean, high-quality graphics with detailed block designs and a user-friendly interface. The blocks and grid are visually distinct, making it easy to track movements and plan strategies. Soundtrack: The background music is calming and fitting for a puzzle game, with sound effects like the "click" of moving blocks and the "ding" of matching blocks enhancing the overall experience.

name: VGA Jigsaw
description: VGA Jigsaw is the aesthetically improved "sequel" to PC Jigsaw, also released by Alive Software. The premise is the same: An image gets scrambled, and you have to figure out how to put it back together using your mouse to swap pieces around. A count of the number of swaps you make is kept, and at the end you'll see how good (or bad) you were at reassembling the puzzle. Like its predecessor, this game only includes five images (the registered version allows you to use your own PCX/GIF images) but this VGA version has five difficulty levels rather than only three. It also of course has improved color depth due to its 320x200, 256 color mode, and it has MIDI music too. (It also supports higher resolution modes, if you have the patience to get them working. I did not.) The full version of the game is still available to buy from Alive Software in their Puzzles Bundle.

name: VGA Sharks
description: VGA Sharks is a simple and straightforward action game developed by Alive Software (now Alivesoft). In this game, players take on the role of a diver tasked with collecting various marine creatures and safely returning them to a shark-proof cage. The challenge lies in avoiding sharks and other hazards while gathering as many creatures as possible. Despite its simplistic gameplay, basic graphics, and unremarkable sound design, VGA Sharks gained a fair amount of recognition upon its original release. While it may not stand out as a groundbreaking title, it offers a nostalgic and casual gaming experience for those who enjoy retro action games. Key Features: Marine Creature Collection: The primary objective is to collect marine creatures scattered throughout the underwater environment and bring them back to the shark-proof cage. Shark Avoidance: Sharks patrol the waters, and players must avoid them while collecting creatures. Getting caught by a shark ends the game. Simple Controls: The game features easy-to-learn controls, typically involving movement and an action button to collect creatures. This makes it accessible to players of all skill levels. Basic Graphics and Sound: The visuals and sound effects are quite basic, even for the time of its release. The graphics are functional but lack detail, and the sound design is minimal. Nostalgic Appeal: Despite its simplicity, VGA Sharks has a certain nostalgic charm, especially for those who played it during its original release. Casual Gameplay: The game is easy to pick up and play, making it suitable for quick gaming sessions or casual players.

name: VGA Tron
description: VGA Tron is one of many interpretations of the classic TRON type game (aka Nibbles, aka Snake, etc) that was popular in arcades, then in DOS thanks to QBasic, then again on early mobile phones thanks to Snake. VGA Tron follows the same formula, allowing up to four human players or computer opponents to compete simultaneously. After each round, the layout of the playing field will change so that you will need to pay attention to the layout of the walls. You are also given a limited number of weapons that you can use against your competitors. The graphics here (while proudly VGA of course) are nothing special. Also the computer opponents don't put up much of a challenge; they tend to self-distruct rather quickly, so try to find some human opponents instead.

name: VGATetris
description: VGATetris is a straightforward and no-frills version of the classic Tetris game, presented in VGA graphics. The game stays true to the original formula: blocks fall, and you must rotate and place them to form complete horizontal lines, which are then removed from the playing field. While the game lacks advanced options or customization, it delivers a solid and enjoyable Tetris experience. The only notable control quirk is that it requires a numeric keypad with NUM LOCK turned on. If you're looking for a simple and classic Tetris experience, VGATetris is a great choice. How to Play: Start the Game: Begin playing as blocks (tetrominoes) fall from the top of the screen. Move and Rotate Blocks: Use the numeric keypad to move blocks left and right (4 and 6), rotate them (8), and drop them quickly (2). Form Complete Lines: Arrange the blocks to create solid horizontal lines without gaps. Clear Lines: When a line is complete, it disappears, and you earn points. Avoid Stacking: If the blocks stack up to the top of the screen, the game ends. Features: Classic Tetris Gameplay: The game retains the timeless mechanics of Tetris, making it easy to pick up and play. VGA Graphics: The visuals are clean and crisp, offering a retro yet polished look. Simple Controls: The numeric keypad is used for all actions, though it requires NUM LOCK to be on. No Frills: The game focuses purely on the Tetris experience, without additional modes or options. Nostalgic Appeal: Perfect for fans of retro gaming and classic puzzle games.

name: VGAWHEEL
description: VGAWHEEL is a VGA version of Wheel of Fortune. You and up to two other players can take turns spinning the wheel and guessing letters before trying to solve the puzzle. (There are no CPU opponents so if you play single player, you'll be the only one playing.) You can also of course buy vowels, and lose all your cash for the round if you hit the Bankrupt area on the wheel. The game includes a total of 1000 puzzles and you can edit or add your own as well. Some of the puzzles are a bit obscure and US-centric (ex, in the screenshot) and of course if you were born after this game was released in 1990 you may not remember many of them, but the game itself works well and as noted above has a LOT of puzzles to solve.

name: Vigilance on Talos V
description: Vigilance on Talos V is an obscure Metroid-esque action/platformer set in a sci-fi world where everything is out to kill you! You're a mercenary, and the Xenos have kidnapped your daughter! Use your guns to get her back! The graphics and sounds here are decent enough, and the gameplay takes obvious cues from Metroid. Even in the way you shoot open convex-shaped doors to open them, or can transform into a ball referred to as a "Saturn Ball". Missiles, energy tanks, yup they're all here. So it should be fun? The controls are not bad but feel a bit touchy. Enemies pop out suddenly and are hard to kill.

name: Viking Siege
description: Viking Siege is a PC version of the ancient board game "Hnefatafl" aka "Viking Chess". It looks a little like chess, but plays very differently. There are a different number of pieces on each side, and only one king. The white side tries to move the king off the board, while the black side tries to surround and capture the king. There is a full tutorial included in the program (press F5 at the menu) so you can get the full rules there. You can play against the PC, or against a human opponent. It seems like a pretty decent version of the board game!

name: Viking Tiles
description: Viking Tiles is a captivating tile-matching game set in the world of Norse mythology and Viking adventures. The goal is to clear the board by removing pairs of identical tiles that are on top of the stack and not blocked by other tiles. With its Viking-themed design and strategic gameplay, it’s a fun and challenging experience for puzzle enthusiasts. How to Play Viking Tiles: Objective: Remove all tiles from the board by matching pairs of identical tiles. Only tiles that are on top of the stack and not blocked by other tiles can be selected. Gameplay: The board is filled with Viking-themed tiles, such as helmets, shields, ships, runes, and axes. Look for pairs of identical tiles that are free (not covered by other tiles). Click or tap on two matching tiles to remove them from the board. Rules: Only two identical tiles that are free can be matched and removed. Tiles are considered free if they have no tiles covering them. The game ends when all tiles are cleared or no more moves are possible. Themes and Visuals: The game features a Viking-inspired design, with rich, detailed graphics and atmospheric sound effects. Tiles are adorned with symbols and imagery from Norse mythology, adding to the immersive experience. Hints and Shuffle: If you get stuck, use the hint button to highlight a possible match. Some versions of the game allow you to shuffle the tiles to create new matching opportunities. Key Features of Viking Tiles: Viking Theme: Immersive visuals and designs inspired by Norse mythology. Classic Tile-Matching Gameplay: Simple mechanics with a strategic twist. Relaxing Yet Challenging: Perfect for unwinding while exercising your brain. Progressive Difficulty: Starts easy but becomes more complex as you advance.

name: Vikings: Fields of Conquest
description: Vikings: Fields of Conquest is a turn-based strategy title with a medieval flair. This demo version allows you to play up to 7 turns from the full game. This may prove difficult because this game is not intuitive at all to play, and there is no included manual. Maybe this was because it's technically a sequel to the game "Kingdoms of England" and they figured fans of the original would already sorta know how to play? Anyways, it's the Internet age and you can look stuff up if you want. The game looks decent enough, has a variety of soldier types (swordsmen, archers, crossbowmen, pikemen, etc) and probably has a lot of decent content for turn-based strategy fans who are willing to take the time to learn to play.

name: Vintage Vexed
description: Vintage Vexed is a classic and challenging puzzle game that tests your strategic thinking and problem-solving skills. The goal is to clear the board by moving similar blocks together, causing them to disappear. With its retro-inspired design and progressively difficult levels, Vintage Vexed offers a satisfying and nostalgic experience for puzzle enthusiasts. How to Play: Move Blocks: Drag blocks to an empty spot on the board to reposition them. Match Blocks: Move two or more identical blocks next to each other to make them disappear. Clear the Board: Strategically remove all the blocks to complete the level and advance to the next one. Plan Ahead: Think carefully about your moves, as some blocks may become stuck if you don’t clear them in the right order. Features: Retro Design: The game features a vintage-inspired aesthetic, giving it a nostalgic and timeless feel. Increasing Difficulty: Each level introduces new challenges and more complex layouts, keeping the gameplay engaging. Simple Mechanics: Easy-to-understand rules make the game accessible, while the strategic depth provides a satisfying challenge. Relaxing Yet Challenging: With no time limits, you can take your time to plan your moves and enjoy the puzzle-solving process.

name: Vinyl Goddess From Mars
description: The scantily clad and mildly provocative Vinyl Goddess from Mars will, for many gamers, bring to mind one of the early Epic Megagames heroines, Jill of the Jungle. The comparison is apt, because the rumor is that this game was originally intended to be a sequel to the Jill of the Jungle games but was cancelled by Epic and released by another company under another name. Overall it plays mostly like the Jill games but not as well. Despite its decent graphics and music, it doesn't feel as polished as the original games.

name: Viper
description: Viper is a very simple text-mode shmup from 1986. You face wave after wave of enemy ships, and you blast 'em while avoiding their shots. That's pretty much it, but thankfully the author created some sweet-looking text-mode graphics for your ship and the enemy ships, each which are comprised of several characters. There are animations when your ship takes a hit, and then when it gets hit a second time and explodes. The enemy ships also have simple animations. It adds a lot to the game's charm. Later waves get more difficult as you progress, and with only three lives, you may not get far!

name: Viper2004
description: Viper is a fairly basic Snake / Nibbles clone. The goal is to eat the various "treasures" that appear, while avoiding crashing into your own ever-growing tail or walls. That's pretty much it. You get to choose the speed of the game, and it interestingly allows you to add additional length to your tail while playing (press F7, or Shift-F7 to add 100 tail links at once ...) but other than that, not much else to it. Average graphics and some sound card effects. (Note: Although the game says "Registered version do not distribute" etc, this is the file that is/was available on the PLBM official website, so it seems like at some point it was released for free.)

name: Virus Killer
description: Virus Killer is a strange and ambiguous yet still somewhat intriguing game. The goal is to wipe out all of the viruses that have infected a PC. You do this by driving around a maze-like circuit board type area, killing viruses and repairing / activating "memory locations" on the walls. The instructions are not very clear and the way you navigate is confusing, yet the game looks quite decent (for 1989!) and there seems to be decent depth. It seems too difficult to hit the viruses during the little mini-game that plays out when you try to remove them, but otherwise basically playable once you get the controls sorted out; maybe you'll be more willing than I am to spend the time to figure out what exactly all of these gauges and stuff actually mean!

name: Visual Star Trek
description: Visual Star Trek (sometimes called VTrek after its executable file's name) is a strategy game in the style of other Star Trek-inspired games like EGA Trek and Turbo Trek. Your goal is to destroy the Klingons, and you do so by traveling around and fighting 'em, while occasionally mining planets and getting repairs and such. There is no included documentation and this is NOT my kind of game so I am not going to go through the trial-and-error process of learning it, but from what I've read it's highly regarded within this niche subgenre, partially due to its mouse-based controls and general UI. Try watching the Ancient DOS Games review of Visual Star Trek for some gameplay help.

name: Vitetris
description: Vitetris is a great implementation of the classic Tetris game in "terminal" mode, ie, text mode. It offers a fast and clean interface with many options, and no-nonsense Tetris gameplay. You can play one player or two player mode, and each player can even set their gameplay options individually. This is a great version of the original text mode Tetris to play if you enjoy a text-mode aesthetic or just want a classic-style Tetris game with plenty of options that you can set so that it plays just how you like it.

name: ViVi Vicious Viper
description: ViVi is a Snake / Nibbles clone where the object is to gobble up all of the edible items on the screen while avoiding the poisonous / dangerous objects. As is common for snake games, your snake's tail grows every time you eat an item. The graphics are basic but not objectionable and your snake controls pretty well, as long as your PC isn't too fast and/or DOSBox cycles aren't set too high. There are a total of 50 levels in the game and the difficulty ramps up as you progress so you'll be hard pressed to make it all the way to the end! (The game's included documentation is in German but it isn't needed to play. Press Spacebar to start the game.)

name: Vlak
description: Vlak (which means "train" in Czech) is a fun and straightforward take on the classic Snake or Nibbles gameplay formula. While the game is not in English, its intuitive mechanics make it easy to pick up and play. The objective is to collect gems scattered across each level, which causes your tail to grow longer, and then find the exit to progress. Despite its average graphics and minimal sound design, Vlak delivers a solid and enjoyable experience for fans of retro puzzle games. If you’re looking for a simple yet addictive game, this one is worth a try. Key Features: Snake-Inspired Gameplay: The core gameplay is reminiscent of the classic Snake or Nibbles games, where you control a growing tail and must navigate through levels to collect items. Gem Collection: The primary objective is to collect gems scattered throughout each level. Each gem you collect makes your tail grow longer, adding to the challenge. Level Progression: After collecting all the gems, you must find the exit to advance to the next level. The levels increase in difficulty as you progress. Simple Controls: The controls are easy to learn, typically involving arrow keys or similar inputs to move your character. This makes the game accessible to players of all skill levels. Average Graphics and Minimal Sound: The visuals are functional but not particularly impressive, and the sound design is minimal. The focus is on gameplay rather than presentation. Non-English Interface: While the game is in Czech, the intuitive mechanics and straightforward objectives make it easy to play without understanding the language.

name: Volcano Hunter
description: Volcano Hunter is a port of a TRS-80 game from 1984. Therefore it's rather primitive in many ways, like its use of monochrome, blocky graphics with barely any animation. But there is surprising depth here, given the age of the game. The object is to collect all of the fuel tanks that are spread across the game's 200+ screens. To do so, you must run, jump, and bomb your way around the various screens, avoiding enemies and natural obstacles. Including falling off the edge of platforms! One online review notes that "anything kills you," which is not too far off the mark. Thankfully you start with seven lives, and you'll need 'em! Not exceptionally fun to play these days but definitely an interesting relic from the past.

name: Volvo Road Rally
description: Similar to other promotional games released to promote a product, most notably Ford Simulator, the goal of this advertainment product (is that a word?) is to get you to buy a Volvo. This digital brochure from 1991 explains many details about Volvo cars, but also includes the Volvo Road Rally game. Unlike the aforementioned Ford Simulator, you don't actually get to drive the car. Rather you guide your car around roads on a map, visiting Volvo dealerships and playing simple puzzle games to get points. Not sure what all of that has to do with buying a Volvo but I guess the longer you get people staring at your company's materials, the better, right?

name: Vortex
description: Vortex is a unique and minimalist text-mode action/strategy game for DOS. Despite its simple presentation, the game offers a challenging and engaging experience as players attempt to contain tornadoes by strategically picking up and dropping blocks. The randomness of the tornadoes' movements and their ability to move blocks add an element of unpredictability, making the game both difficult and addictive. Key Features: Gameplay: The goal is to contain tornadoes by placing blocks around them. Players can pick up and drop blocks, carrying up to three at a time. The challenge lies in predicting the tornadoes' movements and positioning blocks effectively to trap them. Movement and Safety: Players are safe from tornadoes if they are carrying at least one block or are stationary. If a tornado touches the player while they are empty-handed and moving, it’s game over. Tornado Behavior: Tornadoes move randomly around the screen and can also push blocks out of the way, adding an extra layer of difficulty. This unpredictability forces players to think quickly and adapt their strategies on the fly. Text-Mode Graphics: The game uses ASCII characters to represent the player, blocks, and tornadoes. While this might seem primitive, it adds to the game’s charm and keeps the focus on strategy and quick thinking. Controls: The controls are simple and keyboard-based, allowing players to move around the screen, pick up blocks, and drop them with ease. Strengths: Unique Concept: The idea of containing tornadoes with blocks is creative and sets the game apart from more traditional action or strategy titles. Challenging Gameplay: The random movement of the tornadoes and their ability to move blocks make the game difficult and rewarding to master. Minimalist Design: The text-mode graphics and straightforward mechanics keep the game accessible and easy to pick up, while the strategic depth ensures it remains engaging.

name: Vox Populi Vox Dei
description: Vox Populi Vox Dei is a narrative-driven puzzle adventure Flash game developed by Johan Peitz and released in 2010. The title is Latin for "The voice of the people is the voice of God," and the game centers around themes of control, society, and free will, exploring philosophical ideas through a simple yet thought-provoking gameplay experience. Basic Movement and Interaction: The game has grid-based movement, where you move The Citizen around a grid and interact with objects or other characters to manipulate the environment. The core gameplay mechanic involves solving puzzles by interacting with people in the game. Crowds of people are spread across each level, and your goal is to influence them to get past obstacles or gain new abilities. Crowd Dynamics: A key element of the gameplay is group dynamics. As you move through the game, you’ll encounter crowds of people who hold different ideas or opinions. You can join these groups or change their opinions by interacting with them, affecting how they behave. This means you might need to lead certain groups, merge them, or break them up to achieve your goals. Groups may have different behaviors based on their opinions—some will follow you, some will be hostile, and some may ignore you. Manipulating these crowds is a puzzle in itself, and you'll need to experiment with different actions to progress. Voice Mechanic: The game’s title, "Vox Populi Vox Dei," reflects the power of the voice of the people. As The Citizen, you can harness the power of the crowd's collective will, which allows you to speak and influence others in various ways. Some levels require you to amplify the influence of a crowd in order to break barriers or open paths to new areas. This mechanic symbolizes the power of collective action and mob mentality, where the combined voice of the crowd is greater than any single individual's.

name: voxiom.io
description: Voxiom.io is an engaging multiplayer voxel-based game that combines elements of building, crafting, and combat in a vibrant 3D environment. Players can explore, gather resources, and engage in battles with others, all while creating their own structures. Game Overview: Objective: Players aim to survive and thrive in a blocky world by collecting resources, crafting items, and battling other players to become the strongest. Gameplay Mechanics: Resource Gathering: Players can mine various materials from the environment, including wood, stone, and ores, which are essential for crafting tools and building structures. Building and Crafting: Using the collected resources, players can create tools, weapons, and shelters, allowing for both defensive and offensive strategies. Combat: Players can engage in PvP battles against other players using crafted weapons and tactics, adding an exciting competitive element to the gameplay. Features: Multiplayer Interaction: The game emphasizes player interaction, with the ability to team up with friends or compete against others in real-time. Customizable Environments: Players can shape the world around them, building unique structures and bases that reflect their style and strategy. Vibrant Graphics: The game features colorful, voxel-style graphics that create a lively and inviting atmosphere. Visuals and Sound: Voxiom.io offers bright, blocky visuals reminiscent of sandbox games, along with sound effects and music that enhance the immersive experience. Voxiom.io is popular for its blend of exploration, crafting, and combat, making it a favorite among fans of sandbox and multiplayer games looking for a fun and dynamic online experience.

name: Voyage to the Planet Earth
description: Voyage to the Planet Earth only barely fits into the category of "game" but it's so cool that I couldn't help including it here, hoping that it gets some wider recognition. It's sort of like Google Earth, but made in text-mode (with a few edited characters) in 1993 in DOS. Yes it's as wild as it sounds. You can see the map of the earth depicted in 3D on a globe, and you can rotate and zoom it however you want. You can also switch to a "political map" view which shows the different countries and even city locations as you zoom in. It does include a game where you have to find a city using the latitude and longitude, so there's that if you want to play it. But really it's more of an interesting toy to play with, definitely worth checking out.

name: VVVVVV Demo
description: VVVVVV Demo is a Flash demo of the full VVVVVV game, which was originally created by Terry Cavanagh, a well-known indie game developer. VVVVVV is a critically acclaimed platformer known for its challenging mechanics, minimalistic art style, and a unique twist on the classic gravity-based movement. The Flash demo was an early version of the game that allowed players to experience the core mechanics before the full game was released. Gravity Flipping: The core mechanic of VVVVVV is that the player controls Captain Viridian, who can flip gravity. Instead of jumping, you press a button to flip the direction of gravity, causing Viridian to switch between walking on the floor and the ceiling. This makes for a completely different type of platforming experience. The flip is instantaneous, and the change in gravity affects everything, including the player's movement, enemies, and platforms. It requires quick reflexes and precision to navigate obstacles. Puzzle and Platforming: Levels in VVVVVV are full of traps, spikes, and other deadly obstacles that require careful gravity manipulation to overcome. The game’s levels are designed with increasing difficulty, and often the puzzles require not just skill, but careful planning and thinking ahead. No Traditional Jumping: The most notable feature of VVVVVV is the lack of a traditional jump button. Instead, the player’s ability to switch gravity is the main tool for moving through the levels, making every platforming section a unique challenge compared to other platformers. Challenging Levels: The difficulty in VVVVVV is high, with precise timing needed to avoid spikes, enemy creatures, and other hazards. Each level is designed to be difficult but rewarding, with no hand-holding or checkpoints. The game was designed with a retro style and a lot of "trial-and-error" gameplay, similar to old-school platformers. Simple Controls: The game is controlled using the arrow keys (or WASD keys on a keyboard), where the left and right arrows are used to move Viridian horizontally, and the up or down arrow (depending on the version) flips gravity. This simple control scheme makes the game easy to pick up, but difficult to master. Retro Aesthetic: VVVVVV uses a retro-inspired, pixel-art style with a vibrant color palette. The game’s aesthetic is simple but effective, with blocky character designs and a focus on clear, easy-to-read visuals.

name: Wacky Wheels
description: Wacky Wheels is a kart racing game for PC that draws heavy inspiration from Super Mario Kart, offering a similar style of gameplay with its own quirky twist. While it may not reach the same level of polish as its Nintendo counterpart, it’s a fun and nostalgic title for fans of retro racing games. Here’s a detailed look at what makes Wacky Wheels a memorable, if imperfect, kart racing experience: Key Features: Kart Racing Gameplay: The game features fast-paced kart racing across a variety of tracks, complete with power-ups, obstacles, and competitive AI opponents. Animal Characters: Instead of Mario and friends, Wacky Wheels features a cast of anthropomorphic animal characters, each with their own unique kart and personality. Power-Ups and Weapons: Like Mario Kart, the game includes power-ups and weapons that can be used to gain an advantage or hinder opponents. Examples include missiles, oil slicks, and speed boosts. VGA Graphics and Sound: The game boasts colorful VGA graphics and catchy sound effects, giving it a vibrant and lively atmosphere. However, the frame rate can be choppy, which affects the overall smoothness of the gameplay. Track Variety: The game includes a selection of tracks with different themes and layouts, providing variety and replayability. Multiplayer Mode: Wacky Wheels supports multiplayer racing, allowing you to compete against friends on the same computer. This adds to the fun and replay value. Nostalgic Appeal: For retro gaming enthusiasts, Wacky Wheels is a nostalgic trip back to the early days of PC gaming and kart racing. Gameplay: Objective: Race against AI opponents or friends to finish first in a series of kart races. Controls: Use the keyboard or joystick to steer, accelerate, and brake. Collect power-ups and use them strategically to gain an edge. Tracks: Navigate through themed tracks filled with twists, turns, and hazards. Power-Ups: Pick up items like missiles, oil slicks, and shields to outmaneuver your opponents.

name: Wall Pipe
description: Wall Pipe is one of many Pipedream / Pipemania / Oilswell type games released by Soleau Software. This game plays pretty much the same as the games previously mentioned: Lay out pieces of pipe so that the oil continues to flow. You're given 30 seconds before the oil starts moving. The interface is a bit confusing to me: You need to click the mouse to select the next piece, which then disappears, so you'd better remember what type of piece you're placing. I also encountered a weird bug: The clock continues to tick down while you're in the options menu, but the game apparently only checks when the clock hits 0 while you're in the actual game. So the clock ticked below 0 while I was in the options, and was at -5 when I returned to the game. The oil never flowed and I had to quit the game! Other than the weird bug and the confusing interface design choice, it does work, but there are better Pipedream clones out there, several from Soleau itself.

name: Wall Street Raider
description: Wall Street Raider (full name "Wall $treet Raider - The Corporate Takeover Game / Simulation") is a financial business simulation game for 2-5 players where the object is to take $1billion and turn it into ... an even bigger fortune, I guess! To do so you'll invest in companies and try to maximize your investments. The author attended Harvard so I guess he knows what he's talking about with business stuff. There are a LOT of menus and things to do in this text-based game, which was first created in 1986 and continues to receive updates to this day, albeit in a Windows remake first released in 2001. Check out the modern game at www.wallstreetraider.com/ if you like the old DOS version!

name: Wallpaper Connect
description: Wallpaper Connect is a visually stunning and relaxing mahjong-style puzzle game that combines the classic tile-matching gameplay with beautiful wallpaper designs. The goal is to connect pairs of identical wallpaper tiles by drawing paths with no more than two 90-degree angles. As you clear the board, you’ll reveal intricate and artistic wallpaper patterns, making the game both a mental challenge and a visual treat. How to Play: Match Tiles: Find and connect two identical wallpaper tiles to remove them from the board. Path Rules: The connecting line between the tiles can have no more than two 90-degree angles. If the path requires more angles, the tiles cannot be matched. Clear the Board: Strategically remove all the tiles to complete the level and reveal the full wallpaper design. Plan Ahead: Think carefully about your moves, as some tiles may become blocked if you don’t clear them in the right order. Features: Beautiful Wallpaper Designs: The game features a variety of stunning wallpaper patterns, making each level a visual delight. Unique Pathing Rules: The restriction on the number of angles adds a strategic challenge, requiring players to think carefully about their connections. Multiple Levels: The game offers a variety of levels with increasingly complex layouts, keeping the gameplay fresh and engaging. Relaxing Gameplay: With its calming visuals and soothing soundtrack, Wallpaper Connect is perfect for unwinding and enjoying a peaceful puzzle-solving experience.

name: Wanderer
description: This is the graphical version of the original Wanderer game; the original was made by Steve Shipway in 1988. See the extra files for the original ASCII version. Like the original text-mode game, Wanderer is a Boulderdash derivative where the object is to collect the diamonds and avoid the hazards before making your way to the exit. There are a whole bunch of dangerous levels here to explore, each with the signature loved/hated boulder falling/rolling physics. There are many different obstacles here and you will need some careful planning, and likely some trial and error, to beat all of the levels.

name: Wanderer1988
description: Wanderer is a Boulderdash-like game where you explore a large playing field trying to collect treasure, kill monsters, and avoid dying. The game follows Boulderdash-like rules for how the boulders fall, which fans of the original game should enjoy and those who dislike those mechanics should despise. Graphically the game's sprites do their job but they're not much to look at. There's also a textmode you can choose instead. There are a total of 60 (!) levels so there's plenty of gameplay if you enjoy this sort of game and want to see what future levels have to offer.

name: War of the Mages
description: War of the Mages is a text-mode turn-based strategy game with a fantasy theme. You start the game by choosing the number of players, and setting a bunch of options that will determine how the game plays. Turns progress through a series of menus where you direct your troops, conquer cities, and perform other actions to gain control of enough cities to win the game. The included documentation (WM32.DOC) seems to be required reading in order to know how the game should be played, so it will take some commitment if you want to try this one, hope you enjoy navigating menus. One unique aspect is that it seems to allow you to specify an unlimited number of players (I tried 99 at it let me do it) so if you happen to have 98 friends around who want to play a DOS strategy game from 1989 ...

name: War Tank Rush
description: "War Tank Rush" is an exhilarating flash game that puts players in command of a powerful tank in a fast-paced combat scenario. Your mission is to navigate through enemy territory, engaging in intense battles while avoiding enemy fire and obstacles. As you drive your tank forward, you'll face waves of enemy tanks, turrets, and other military units. The gameplay emphasizes quick reflexes and strategic movement, allowing players to dodge attacks while launching their own. Collect power-ups to upgrade your tank’s weapons and armor, enhancing your firepower and survivability. The game features a variety of levels with increasing difficulty, each set in dynamic environments that keep the action fresh. With vibrant graphics, explosive sound effects, and addictive gameplay, "War Tank Rush" delivers an adrenaline-fueled experience where only the strongest will survive. Can you lead your tank to victory?

name: War1993
description: War-8}! is a strangely-named Tank Wars / Scorched Earth / Gorillas type two-player war game. The author named it that way to differentiate it from other "war" named games and also because it looks like a smiley face ... Anyways there are some differences here between this and other similar tank games. First, each player gets five tanks, all of which must be destroyed for the opposing player to win. (Only one tank gets to shoot per player per turn.) Second, you can choose from one of three different weapons each turn, each with different properties. Third, setting shot angle, power, and sometimes fuel level is done using active, moving gauges, so it requires good timing as well as careful planning.

name: Warbots
description: Warbots is a robot battle game where you use your credits to assign different attributes to your robot, then write code to guide its actions. It's similar to many other similar games like C-Robots, AT-Robots, and other programming games. This game does support graphics for the robot battles, and they fight each other on a relatively small grid that places random obstacles in their way. The game comes with a few sample robots included, most of which don't seem too deadly. Worth a look if you enjoy programming type games!

name: Warcraft
description: In a "Warcraft" flash game, fights typically involve strategy, unit management, and tactical decision-making. Here’s a strategy guide to help you excel in such a game: 1. Understand Unit Types Familiarize yourself with different units and their strengths and weaknesses (e.g., melee vs. ranged, ground vs. air). Use this knowledge to counter enemy units effectively. 2. Resource Gathering Start by collecting resources quickly. Focus on gathering gold and lumber to build and upgrade your army. 3. Build a Balanced Army Create a diverse army composition. Include melee units for frontline combat, ranged units for support, and spellcasters for versatility. 4. Positioning and Terrain Use the map’s terrain to your advantage. Position your ranged units on higher ground for increased damage and visibility. 5. Upgrade Your Units Invest in upgrades as soon as possible. Improved units can make a significant difference in battle. 6. Use Spells Wisely Pay attention to your hero’s abilities. Use them strategically to turn the tide of battle, especially during key moments. 7. Micro-Management Control units individually for better positioning and focus fire. Retreat damaged units to heal and regroup. 8. Scout Enemy Positions Send out scouts to gather intel on enemy movements. Knowing where the enemy is can help you plan your attacks better. 9. Plan Your Attacks Timing is crucial. Attack when the enemy is vulnerable or distracted. Consider ambush tactics for surprise attacks. 10. Retreat Strategically If a fight isn’t going well, don’t hesitate to pull back. Regroup and heal your units before re-engaging. By employing these strategies, you can improve your chances of success in "Warcraft" flash games and enjoy a more rewarding gaming experience!

name: Warcraft 2: Tides of Darkness
description: Blizzard's follow-up sequel to their successful Warcraft: Orcs & Humans RTS game was immensely successful, and people still continue to play it today. Warcraft II continues the same style as its predecessor, but adds numerous features and innovations which make it a superior game to the original. Again you choose to play as either the humans or the orcs, and battle against the other. You can play against a human opponent over a local network or the Internet, or you can play against the computer. The graphics are detailed and well drawn, and the sound effects and music are classic ("Zug zug!"). This shareware version (I would've called it a demo but it clearly says shareware on the title screen) includes six unique maps not found in the full game, as well as one demo multiplayer map. Truly a modern classic game and definitely worth trying for RTS fans.

name: Warcraft: Orcs & Humans
description: This demo version of the full game gives you a taste of what the original entry into the Warcraft series of games was like. "Orcs & Humans" (or simply Warcraft I) came before Warcraft II and Warcraft 3 and while it has its merits, it is generally surpassed by later entries in the series in most ways. Still, it was the first real-time fantasy strategy game from Blizzard. This game will still be fun for fans of the genre, and those interested in the origins of their addiction since it served as the prototype for Blizzard's later more well-known games.

name: Warehouse Hidden Differences
description: Warehouse Hidden Differences is an exciting and fast-paced spot-the-difference game set in a bustling warehouse environment. The goal is to find all four differences between two seemingly identical images within a time limit. With its detailed visuals, challenging gameplay, and time pressure, it’s a perfect game for players who enjoy observation and quick thinking. How to Play Warehouse Hidden Differences: Objective: Find all four differences between two warehouse-themed images. Click on the differences within the time limit to complete the level. Gameplay: The screen displays two similar images side by side. Carefully compare the images to spot the differences. Click on the differences in one of the images to mark them as found. Controls: Click/Tap: Select and mark the differences. Zoom: Some versions allow you to zoom in for a closer look at the images. Levels: The game features multiple levels, each with a unique set of images and differences. As you progress, the differences become more subtle, and the time limit may decrease. Time Limit: Each level has a time limit, adding an extra layer of challenge. You must find all four differences before time runs out. Key Features of Warehouse Hidden Differences: Warehouse Theme: Detailed and immersive warehouse environments. Spot-the-Difference Gameplay: Fun and challenging searches for subtle differences. Time Pressure: Adds excitement and urgency to the gameplay. Progressive Difficulty: Starts easy but becomes more complex as you advance.

name: Warp Shot
description: Warp Shot is a fast-paced, physics-based Flash game that combines elements of puzzle-solving and precision shooting. Developed by Nitrome, a well-known creator of Flash games, Warp Shot challenges players to navigate a ball through a series of obstacles by strategically warping it through portals. The game is known for its colorful visuals, clever level design, and addictive gameplay. While Flash games are no longer widely supported due to the discontinuation of Adobe Flash, Warp Shot remains a memorable title in the puzzle-action genre. Key Features: Portal-Based Gameplay: Players control a ball that can be warped through portals to navigate levels. The goal is to guide the ball to the exit by strategically placing portals and using physics to overcome obstacles. Physics-Based Mechanics: The game relies on realistic physics to simulate the movement of the ball. Players must account for momentum, gravity, and angles to successfully complete levels. Challenging Obstacles: Levels are filled with hazards such as spikes, moving platforms, lasers, and more. Each level introduces new challenges, requiring players to think creatively and adapt their strategies. Colorful and Pixelated Visuals: Warp Shot features Nitrome's signature pixel art style, with vibrant colors and charming animations. The visuals are simple yet appealing, adding to the game's overall charm. Intuitive Controls: Players use the mouse to aim and shoot portals, making the controls easy to learn but difficult to master. The game requires precision and timing to place portals effectively. Level Progression: The game features a series of increasingly difficult levels, each with unique layouts and obstacles. Players must complete each level to unlock the next, providing a sense of progression and accomplishment. Replayability: Players can replay levels to improve their performance or achieve faster completion times. The game encourages experimentation with different strategies to find the most efficient path.

name: Wasp Solitaire
description: Wasp Solitaire is a challenging and strategic card game that requires players to place all cards in order from King to Ace. Here's a detailed description of the game: Gameplay Mechanics: Objective: The primary goal is to arrange all cards in descending order from King to Ace within each column. The game is won when all cards are successfully placed in the correct order. Card Movement: Open Cards: Only the open (face-up) cards at the bottom of each column can be moved. Movement Rules: An open card can be moved to another column if it is the same color and one rank higher than the card at the bottom of the target column. For example, a red 7 can be placed on a black 8. Game Flow: Initial Setup: The game starts with a tableau of cards arranged in several columns. Some cards are face-up, and some are face-down. The face-down cards are revealed as the face-up cards above them are moved. Moving Cards: Click on an open card to select it, then click on another column to move it, provided the move follows the rules. The goal is to create sequences of cards in descending order within each column. Completing Sequences: Continue moving cards to create descending sequences until all cards are arranged from King to Ace in each column. Level Progression: The game is divided into levels, each with increasing difficulty. As you progress, the initial card arrangements become more complex, requiring more strategic thinking and planning. Hints and Assistance: Hints: If you get stuck, the game may offer hints to show possible moves or highlight cards that can be moved. Undo: Some versions of the game might include an undo feature, allowing you to reverse your last move and try a different strategy.

name: Wasteland Rebels
description: Wasteland Rebels is a text-based simulation game based on the world of Macross (aka Robotech) where you are the pilot of a ship that fights other ships from the opposing side in the war. Everything happens through descriptive text that you react to by choosing from the options presented, like do you fight or flee, or do you attack using your missiles or laser weapons. There doesn't seem to be a tremendous amount of depth but if you are fan of this genre and are interested to see what kind of random events occur, it might be worth trying. (Unfortunately I can't find a version that includes documentation so we don't know more about the author, shareware registration cost, or other details.)

name: Water Pouring Puzzle
description: Water Pouring Puzzle is a brain-teasing and strategic puzzle game that challenges players to measure and pour water between cups to achieve a specific goal amount. Here's a detailed description of the game: Gameplay Mechanics: Objective: The primary goal is to measure and pour water between cups to achieve the exact goal amount in one of the cups. The game is won when the desired amount of water is successfully measured. Cups and Water: Cups: The game features cups of different sizes, each with a specific capacity. Players must use these cups to measure the correct amount of water. Pouring Water: Players can pour water from one cup to another. The amount of water poured depends on the capacity of the cups involved. Game Flow: Initial Setup: The game starts with a set of cups, each containing a certain amount of water. The goal is to achieve a specific amount in one of the cups. Pouring: Click on a cup to select it, then click on another cup to pour water from the first cup to the second. The pouring action continues until the first cup is empty or the second cup is full. Achieving the Goal: Continue pouring water between cups until one of the cups contains the exact goal amount. Level Progression: The game is divided into levels, each with increasing difficulty. As you progress, the number of cups and the complexity of the pouring tasks increase, requiring more strategic thinking and planning. Hints and Assistance: Hints: If you get stuck, the game may offer hints to show possible pouring sequences or highlight the next move. Undo: Some versions of the game might include an undo feature, allowing you to reverse your last move and try a different pouring sequence. Visuals and Sound: Graphics: The game features clean, high-quality graphics with detailed cup designs and a user-friendly interface. The water and cups are visually distinct, making it easy to track the amount of water in each cup. Soundtrack: The background music is calming and fitting for a puzzle game, with sound effects like the "pour" of water and the "ding" of achieving the goal enhancing the overall experience.

name: Water Sort
description: Water Sort is a relaxing yet challenging puzzle game where players sort colored liquids into tubes to ensure each tube contains only one color. The game requires careful planning, logical thinking, and patience to solve increasingly complex puzzles. It’s a visually satisfying and mentally stimulating game that’s perfect for players of all ages. How to Play Water Sort: Objective: Sort the colored water so that each tube contains only one color. Complete all levels by organizing the liquids correctly. Setup: A set of tubes is displayed, each containing a mix of colored liquids. Some tubes may be empty, providing space to move liquids around. Gameplay: Tap on a tube to select the liquid at the top, then tap on another tube to pour the liquid into it. You can only pour liquids into a tube if: The destination tube has enough space. The top liquid in the destination tube matches the color of the liquid you’re pouring. Continue sorting the liquids until each tube contains only one color. Challenges: The number of tubes and colors increases as you progress, making the puzzles more complex. Limited moves or space can add to the difficulty. Some levels may include obstacles, such as locked tubes or unmovable liquids. Winning: Successfully sort all the liquids so that each tube contains only one color to complete the level. Key Features of Water Sort: Simple Mechanics: Easy to learn but increasingly challenging as you progress. Relaxing Gameplay: The smooth, flowing liquids and calming colors make it a soothing experience. Strategic Thinking: Requires planning and foresight to solve the puzzles efficiently. Progressive Difficulty: Starts with simple puzzles and gradually introduces more complex challenges.

name: Waterfall - Hidden Stars
description: Waterfall - Hidden Stars is a serene and visually stunning hidden object game set in breathtaking waterfall landscapes. The goal is to find all the hidden stars scattered across the images. With its calming atmosphere, beautiful visuals, and engaging gameplay, it’s a perfect game for players who enjoy exploration and relaxation. How to Play Waterfall - Hidden Stars: Objective: Find all the hidden stars in each waterfall-themed scene. Click on the spots where you find a star to mark them. Gameplay: Each level features a detailed image of a waterfall and its surrounding environment. Look for hidden stars cleverly blended into the scenery. Click on the stars to mark them as found. Controls: Click/Tap: Select and mark the hidden stars. Zoom: Some versions allow you to zoom in for a closer look at the scene. Levels: The game features multiple levels, each with a unique waterfall scene and set of hidden stars. As you progress, the scenes become more intricate, and the stars harder to find. Hints: If you’re stuck, use the hint button to reveal the location of a hidden star. Hints are limited, so use them wisely! Key Features of Waterfall - Hidden Stars: Waterfall Theme: Stunning and tranquil scenes featuring cascading waterfalls and lush landscapes. Hidden Object Gameplay: Fun and challenging searches for cleverly concealed stars. Beautiful Graphics: Immersive and detailed visuals that bring the waterfall environments to life. Relaxing Yet Engaging: Perfect for unwinding while exercising your observation skills.

name: Waterputer
description: Waterputer is an interesting Pipedreams / Pipemania type game that adds the element of gravity to change up the game. Like the aforementioned games, the goal is to connect all of the pipes so the water can flow through them, but the twist here is that the water flows down from the top, and the goal is to fill all of the boxes. This turns out to be rather difficult, as you must note only rotate single boxes at a time, but also four boxes at once to change their positions, since not all boxes have the same connections. It's an interesting concept and plays well once you get the hang of it (press 'H' for in-game help) but it's also quite challenging, at least for me, and it's a bit too difficult to tell which connections each square has; the graphics could have been clearer. Still, an interesting concept.

name: Watman
description: Watman is a DOS-based remake of the 1986 Batman game originally released for the ZX Spectrum and other older computers. This updated version features improved graphics, an isometric perspective, and a nostalgic yet challenging gameplay experience. While the controls can be tricky to master, the game offers a fun and engaging adventure for fans of retro gaming and the Caped Crusader. Here’s a closer look at what makes Watman a unique and enjoyable game: Gameplay Overview: In Watman, you step into the boots of Batman on a mission to rescue Robin by collecting seven batcraft parts scattered across a series of levels. The game combines exploration, puzzle-solving, and action in an isometric perspective: Objective: Your goal is to find and collect all seven batcraft parts hidden throughout the levels. Once you’ve gathered all the parts, you can rescue Robin and complete the game. Isometric Perspective: The game uses an isometric view, which adds a unique visual style but can make movement and navigation a bit challenging at first. Controls: The controls are initially difficult to get used to, but they can be redefined from the main menu to suit your preferences. Movement is grid-based, requiring precise inputs to navigate the environment. Enemies and Hazards: Each level is filled with enemies and obstacles that you must avoid or defeat to progress. Batman can punch enemies, but it’s often better to avoid confrontation and focus on collecting the batcraft parts. Puzzle Elements: Some levels require you to solve puzzles or find keys to unlock doors and access new areas.

name: Weapon
description: Weapon is an intense and immersive first-person defense game set against the backdrop of the Middle East conflicts. Players take on the role of a soldier tasked with defending a downed Black Hawk helicopter that carries vital intelligence. The game combines strategic planning, fast-paced action, and weapon customization, offering a thrilling and challenging experience. With its realistic setting, diverse weapon options, and high-stakes gameplay, Weapon is perfect for fans of tactical shooters and defense games. How to Play: Defend the Helicopter: Protect the downed Black Hawk helicopter from waves of enemy attacks. Use your weapons and strategic positioning to neutralize threats. Buy and Upgrade Weapons: Earn points or currency by defeating enemies and use it to purchase and upgrade a variety of weapons, including rifles, shotguns, sniper rifles, and explosives. Customize Loadouts: Experiment with different weapon configurations to find the most effective setup for each wave of enemies. Survive Waves: Each wave increases in difficulty, with more enemies and stronger attacks. Plan your defenses carefully to survive. Complete Objectives: Protect the helicopter and its vital intelligence until rescue arrives or the mission is complete. Features: First-Person Perspective: The game offers an immersive first-person view, putting you right in the action. Realistic Setting: Set in the Middle East conflicts, the game features authentic environments and high-stakes scenarios. Weapon Customization: Buy, upgrade, and customize a wide range of weapons to suit your playstyle and adapt to different challenges. Strategic Gameplay: Plan your defenses, manage resources, and prioritize targets to survive increasingly difficult waves. High-Stakes Action: The combination of fast-paced combat and strategic planning creates a thrilling and engaging experience.

name: Weave Lines
description: Weave Lines is a visually engaging and mentally stimulating puzzle game where the objective is to recreate a specific pattern or image by weaving lines in the correct way. Players must manipulate lines on a grid to match the target design shown at the top of the screen. The game requires careful observation, spatial reasoning, and patience to solve each level. How to Play Weave Lines: Objective: Recreate the top image (target pattern) exactly by weaving the lines on the grid below. Gameplay: The screen displays a target image made of interwoven lines at the top. Below it, there is a grid with lines that can be moved, rotated, or adjusted. Your task is to manipulate the lines on the grid to match the target image. Controls: Drag and Drop: Move lines around the grid. Rotate: Twist lines to change their direction. Connect: Ensure lines intersect or weave in the same way as the target image. Levels: The game starts with simple patterns and gradually increases in complexity. Later levels may include more lines, intricate weaves, or additional challenges. Completion: Once the grid matches the target image exactly, the level is complete, and you can move on to the next puzzle. Key Features of Weave Lines: Visual Puzzles: Focuses on recreating intricate line patterns. Relaxing Yet Challenging: Combines calm gameplay with mental stimulation. Progressive Difficulty: Starts easy but becomes more complex as you advance. Minimalist Design: Clean and intuitive interface with a focus on the puzzles.

name: Weenie Golf
description: Weenie Golf is a simple mini-golf type game where you ... need to hit a ball into a hole. You can only hit the ball in one of the four cardinal directions, then adjust the power of your shot. There are obstacles on the courses like water, gopher holes, chocolate pudding, and teleportation boxes. (?) Two full courses are included (the course labeled "EASY" is actually the difficult course, and the default course is easy?!) with the promise of MORE if you register. Graphics are bare-bones but the simple gameplay makes this one sort of relaxing to play.

name: Weird Island
description: Weird Island is a first-person point-and-click adventure game that lives up to its name with a quirky and bizarre storyline. The plot revolves around inheriting an island (which, unsurprisingly, turns out to be very weird) and exploring it to uncover its secrets. Along the way, you’ll encounter strange characters, obscure puzzles, and plenty of oddities that make the game stand out. With its decent graphics and point-and-click interface, Weird Island offers a unique and humorous adventure for fans of the genre. If you’re looking for a game that’s equal parts puzzling and peculiar, this one’s worth a visit—just be prepared for some truly weird shenanigans. Key Features: First-Person Perspective: The game is played from a first-person perspective, immersing you in the strange and surreal world of the island. Point-and-Click Interface: The intuitive point-and-click controls make it easy to interact with the environment, solve puzzles, and progress through the story. Quirky and Bizarre Plot: The story begins with inheriting an island, but things quickly take a turn for the weird. Expect plenty of humor, odd characters, and unexpected twists. Obscure Puzzles: The game features a variety of puzzles, many of which are unconventional and require creative thinking to solve. Be prepared for some head-scratching moments! Decent Graphics: The visuals are well-done for the time, with detailed environments and character designs that enhance the game’s quirky atmosphere. Weird Stuff: From strange objects to bizarre encounters, the island is full of oddities that keep the adventure interesting and unpredictable.

name: Wesp
description: WESP is a classic puzzle game originally developed in German, where the objective is to step on every square of a grid to remove it from the playing field. The game features a large number of puzzles, each requiring careful planning and strategic movement to solve. While the graphics and presentation are very basic, the gameplay is engaging and challenging, making it a solid choice for puzzle enthusiasts. However, the controls can be slightly unintuitive, especially for players without a numeric keypad. Key Features: Gameplay: The goal is to step on every square of a grid to clear it. Players must navigate the grid using specific movement rules, ensuring they don’t get trapped or miss any squares. Each level presents a new grid layout, increasing in complexity as the game progresses. Movement Mechanics: The game uses a unique control scheme: Numbered Arrow Keys (1-9): Move one square at a time in the corresponding direction. Regular Arrow Keys: Move two squares at a time, hopping over one square in the process. This dual movement system adds a layer of strategy, as players must decide when to use single steps and when to hop. Puzzle Variety: The game includes many puzzles, each with a different grid layout and challenge. This variety keeps the gameplay fresh and engaging. Basic Graphics: The visuals are simple and functional, with a focus on the grid and the player’s movements. While not visually impressive, they serve their purpose well. Controls: The controls can be tricky to master, especially for players without a numeric keypad. The dual movement system requires some practice to use effectively. Strengths: Challenging Puzzles: The game offers a wide range of puzzles that require careful planning and strategic thinking, making it a satisfying experience for puzzle fans. Unique Movement System: The combination of single-step and hopping movements adds depth and complexity to the gameplay. Replayability: With many puzzles to solve, the game provides plenty of content to keep players engaged.

name: WetSpot 2
description: WetSpot 2 is similar to the classic game Pengo (or clones like Pango) where the object is to kick around blocks to squash your enemies. Your goal is to squash all of the foes in the level, and after collecting the fruit or other bonuses that they drop, you automatically move on to the next level. The graphics in this game are pleasing and there are a total of 50 levels to complete. The controls are responsive and the game is fun to play. Additional levels can be found as well, and there is a level editor available to create your own levels! It's impressive that this was programmed in QuickBasic.

name: Whack the Moles
description: Whack the Moles is a fun and fast-paced typing game where the goal is to type words quickly to "whack" moles before they disappear. The game tests your typing speed, accuracy, and reflexes as you try to keep up with the moles popping up on the screen. It’s a great way to improve your typing skills while having a blast! How to Play Whack the Moles: Objective: Type the words displayed below each mole to whack it before it disappears. Score points for each mole you successfully whack. Gameplay: Moles pop up from holes on the screen, each with a word displayed below it. Type the word exactly as it appears to whack the mole. If you type the word correctly, the mole is whacked, and you earn points. If you’re too slow or make a mistake, the mole escapes. Controls: Type: Use your keyboard to type the words below the moles. Enter: Press Enter after typing a word to submit it (in some versions). Levels: The game starts with slow-moving moles and simple words. As you progress, moles appear faster, and the words become longer or more complex. Scoring: Points are awarded for each mole you whack. Bonus points may be given for typing words quickly or in succession. Key Features of Whack the Moles: Typing Practice: Great for improving typing speed and accuracy. Fast-Paced Action: Keeps you on your toes as moles pop up quickly. Fun and Engaging: Combines the excitement of whacking moles with the challenge of typing. Desktop Only: Designed for keyboard use, making it perfect for desktop play.

name: Whack Your Boss
description: Find all 17 ways to whack your boss in this violent interactive animation created using Flash. These were published about 1 year prior to the Great Recession of 2008. Their popularity fueled multiple remakes in different scenarios. No when. No want. No worry.

name: Whack Your PC
description: Whack Your PC is a humorous and cathartic Flash game that allows players to take out their frustrations on a virtual computer. Developed as a parody of the frustrations people often feel with their technology, the game provides a fun and exaggerated way to "punish" a malfunctioning PC. Players use various tools to smash, burn, and destroy a computer in increasingly creative ways. While Flash games are no longer widely supported due to the discontinuation of Adobe Flash, Whack Your PC remains a memorable and entertaining title for its humor and interactive destruction. Key Features: Destruction Gameplay: Players are given a variety of tools and weapons to destroy a virtual computer. Tools include hammers, chainsaws, fire, explosives, and more, each causing unique damage. Humor and Satire: The game pokes fun at common computer problems, such as crashes, slow performance, and viruses. The exaggerated destruction and over-the-top reactions add to the comedic appeal. Interactive Environment: The computer reacts dynamically to the player's actions, with parts breaking off, sparks flying, and smoke rising. Each tool creates a different visual and auditory effect, making the destruction feel satisfying. Progressive Unlocks: Players start with basic tools and unlock more destructive options as they progress. New tools and upgrades keep the gameplay fresh and engaging. Simple Controls: The game uses intuitive mouse controls, allowing players to easily select tools and interact with the computer. The straightforward mechanics make it accessible to players of all ages. Cathartic Experience: The game provides a safe and humorous outlet for venting frustrations with technology.
